ex_ZSXCIA.description: Dumbbell Straight Arm Twisting Sit-Up is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

ex_VUMAIL.name: Dumbbell Straight Leg Russian Twist
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended straight just off the floor, and hold a dumbbell with both hands close to your chest. Lean back slightly to engage your core, keeping your back straight.
Rotate your torso to the right, moving the dumbbell towards the floor beside your right hip while keeping your legs extended just off the floor.
Rotate your torso back to the center, bringing the dumbbell back to center.
Continue rotating your torso to the left, moving the dumbbell towards the floor beside your left hip. Return to the center. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, alternating sides.
tips: Avoid leaning back too far to prevent strain on your lower back.
Exhale as you twist to each side and inhale as you return to the center.
Keep your legs extended and together to maintain stability.
ex_VUMAIL.description: Dumbbell Straight Leg Russian Twist is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors, Shoulders.

ex_IXG7PO.name: Dumbbell Suitcase Crunch
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs extended vertically and your feet together. Hold a dumbbell with both hands above your chest and extend your arms toward your legs.
Engage your core and lift your head, shoulders, and upper back while reaching the dumbbell toward your feet.
Pause briefly at the top and contract your abdominal muscles while keeping your legs raised and still.
Slowly lower your upper back toward the floor while maintaining the vertical leg position, then repeat.
tips: Keep your arms extended and the dumbbell securely held with both hands.
Keep your lower back controlled against the floor as you lower your torso.
Avoid swinging your arms or using momentum to complete the crunch.
Exhale as you crunch upward and inhale as you lower your upper body.
ex_IXG7PO.description: Dumbbell Suitcase Crunch is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors, Obliques, Shoulders.

ex_3VLS4K.name: Dumbbell v-Up
instructions: Begin by lying flat on your back with your legs extended straight and holding a dumbbell with both hands extended on the floor, arms fully extended.
Simultaneously lift your legs, upper body and dumbbell off the floor, bringing your legs and arms together to form a V-shape.
Reach the dumbbell towards your feet, keeping your arms and legs as straight as possible.
Slowly lower your legs, upper body and dumbbell back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Maintain straight arms and legs to maximize the effectiveness of the exercise.
Exhale as you lift into the V-up position and inhale as you lower back down.
Avoid jerking or using momentum; perform the movement in a controlled manner.
ex_3VLS4K.description: Dumbbell v-Up is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

ex_LB2CS7.name: Elbow Push Plank Up
instructions: Begin in a forearm plank position with your elbows directly under your shoulders and your body forming an arch line from your head to your heels.
Push through your forearms to lift your elbows a few inches off the floor, keeping your fists on the floor.
Keep pressing through your forearms to raise your hips off the floor until your torso is straight, maintaining the plank position.
Lower your hips back down to the floor, followed by your elbows, returning to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Perform the exercise on a non-slip surface to prevent your forearms from slipping.
Ensure your elbows remain under your shoulders to maintain proper form and prevent strain.
Move slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
ex_LB2CS7.description: Elbow Push Plank Up is an intermediate single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

ex_YCZNRN.name: Elbow-Up and Down Dynamic Plank
instructions: Begin in a forearm plank position with your elbows directly under your shoulders and your body forming a straight line from your head to your heels.
Lift your elbows a few inches off the floor, keeping your forearms off the floor and fists on the floor.
Place your right hand on the floor, followed by your left hand, pushing your body up into a high plank position with your arms fully extended.
Lower your right hand back to the floor, followed by your left hand, returning to the starting position. Repeat the movement, alternating which arm you start with each time.
tips: Focus on steady breathing, exhaling as you push up and inhaling as you lower down.
Avoid rotating your hips; keep them level to increase core stability.
Perform the exercise on a non-slip surface to prevent your forearms and hands from slipping.
ex_YCZNRN.description: Elbow-Up and Down Dynamic Plank is an intermediate single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

ex_IQMNN7.name: Exercise Ball Body Saw
instructions: Begin in a plank position with your forearms resting on an exercise ball and your body forming a straight line from your head to your heels.
Engage your core and slowly roll the ball a few inches away from your body.
Reverse the motion by rolling the ball closer to your forearms.
Continue the rolling motion for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining a straight body line throughout.
tips: Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you move forward and inhaling as you move back.
Avoid allowing your lower back to arch; keep your spine in a neutral position.
Use a properly inflated exercise ball to ensure stability and control during the movement.
ex_IQMNN7.description: Exercise Ball Body Saw is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a stability ball, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

ex_R5DWNE.name: Exercise Ball Sit Ups
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart, leaning back so the ball supports your lower back and hips. Place your hands behind your head.
Engage your core and lift your upper body until vertical to the floor, performing a sit-up while keeping your chin slightly tucked and your back straight.
Lower your upper body back down to the starting position with control, maintaining tension in your core.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your lower back remains in contact with the exercise ball to support your spine and prevent injury.
Move slowly and with control to avoid using momentum and to maximize muscle engagement.
Focus on steady breathing, exhaling as you lift your upper body and inhaling as you lower it.
Avoid pulling on your neck with your hands if they are placed behind your head; instead, use your core muscles to lift.
ex_R5DWNE.description: Exercise Ball Sit Ups is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a stability ball, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

ex_KU6NUL.name: Flat Knee Raise
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor. Place your hands lightly behind your head, and rest your head and shoulders against the floor.
Engage your core and lift both feet together, drawing your knees toward your chest while maintaining the bend in your legs.
Continue raising your knees until they are positioned above your abdomen, gently tilting your pelvis toward your ribs without lifting your upper back.
Slowly lower both legs until your feet return to the floor, maintaining control throughout the descent, then repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Support your head lightly without pulling on your neck with your hands.
Draw both knees upward together without swinging or using momentum.
Lower your feet slowly and touch the floor lightly before beginning the next repetition.
Exhale as you draw your knees toward your chest and inhale as you lower your feet.
ex_KU6NUL.description: Flat Knee Raise is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors, Obliques.

ex_ZGLLSA.name: Flutter Kicks
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs extended and your arms at your sides, palms facing down. Place your hands under your hips for added support if needed.
Lift your legs off the floor a few inches, keeping them straight and close together.
Quickly alternate kicking your legs up and down in a small, controlled motion, engaging your core throughout the movement.
Continue the flutter kicks for the desired duration, maintaining a steady and controlled pace. Lower your legs back to the floor to complete the exercise.
tips: Move your legs in a controlled manner to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Focus on steady breathing, exhaling as you kick your legs and inhaling as you maintain the movement.
Avoid letting your lower back arch off the floor; keep it pressed down to prevent strain.
Adjust the height of your kicks to suit your fitness level and comfort, starting with smaller kicks and increasing the range of motion as you build strength.
ex_ZGLLSA.description: Flutter Kicks is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

ex_MIK6BT.name: Hanging Knee Raises
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with your hands shoulder-width apart, palms facing forward or towards each other. Allow your body to hang straight with your feet off the floor.
Engage your core and, keeping your legs together, bend your knees and lift them towards your chest.
Raise your knees as high as comfortably possible, aiming to bring them towards your chest.
Slowly lower your legs back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid swinging your body; use controlled movements to lift and lower your legs.
Focus on steady breathing, exhaling as you lift your knees and inhaling as you lower them.
Ensure your grip on the bar is secure to prevent slipping.
ex_MIK6BT.description: Hanging Knee Raises is an intermediate single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

ex_LTMBLJ.name: Hanging Oblique Knee Raise
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, arms straight and shoulders engaged.
Brace your core and raise both knees up and across toward one shoulder.
Pause at the top, feeling the side of your waist contract.
Lower your legs with control without swinging, then repeat toward the other side.
tips: Pull your shoulders down away from your ears to protect them.
Move slowly; momentum takes the work away from your obliques.
ex_LTMBLJ.description: Hanging Oblique Knee Raise is an intermediate single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors, Forearms.

ex_MIUOFV.name: Heel Touches
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart. Position your arms along your sides with your palms facing down.
Lift your shoulders slightly off the floor, engaging your core and keeping your neck relaxed.
Reach your right hand towards your right heel, bending your torso to the side. Return to the center and then reach your left hand towards your left heel.
Alternate sides in a controlled manner, maintaining the contraction in your core throughout the exercise. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Move slowly and with control to maximize the effectiveness of the exercise and prevent injury.
Focus on steady breathing, exhaling as you reach towards your heel and inhaling as you return to the center.
Ensure your lower back remains pressed into the floor to prevent strain.
ex_MIUOFV.description: Heel Touches is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

ex_REWQH2.name: High Cable Kneeling Crunch
instructions: Attach a rope handle to a high pulley on a cable machine. Kneel down facing the machine, holding the rope handles with both hands, and position them close to your head.
Keep your back straight and engage your core muscles to pull the rope down by crunching your torso towards your knees, bringing your elbows towards your thighs.
Just before your elbows touch your thighs, return to the starting position with control, keeping the tension on the cable.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your knees are firmly planted on the floor for stability.
Keep your hips stable and avoid using momentum.
Exhale as you crunch down and inhale as you return to the starting position.
ex_REWQH2.description: High Cable Kneeling Crunch is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abdominals, Hip Flexors.

ex_2COS4W.name: High Knee Twist
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your arms raised to shoulder height in front of you, palms facing down.
Lift your right knee towards your left elbow while simultaneously twisting your torso to the right, engaging your core.
Return to the starting position, then lift your left knee towards your right elbow while twisting your torso to the left.
Alternate sides in a controlled manner, maintaining a steady rhythm. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Twist your torso and lift your knee simultaneously to engage both your abs and obliques.
Move smoothly and with control to avoid straining your back or hips.
Ensure your movements are balanced and controlled to prevent injury.
ex_2COS4W.description: High Knee Twist is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors, Quadriceps.

ex_APBYYG.name: High Resistance Band Kneeling Crunch
instructions: Attach a resistance band to a high anchor point. Kneel down facing the anchor point, holding the handles of the resistance band with both hands, bend your arms at 90 degrees to bring your hands close to your face, palms facing each other.
Pull the resistance band down by crunching your torso towards your knees, bringing your elbows towards your thighs.
Slowly return to the starting position with control, keeping the tension on the band.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your knees are firmly planted on the floor for stability.
Keep your hips stable and avoid using momentum.
Exhale as you crunch down and inhale as you return to the starting position.
ex_APBYYG.description: High Resistance Band Kneeling Crunch is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abdominals, Hip Flexors.

ex_YCVDUM.name: Medicine Ball Hold the World
instructions: Sit on the floor holding a medicine ball with both hands and bend your knees.
Lean your torso back and lift both feet until your shins are nearly parallel to the floor.
Extend your arms straight upward, holding the ball over your head while balancing on your hips.
Hold the position for the desired duration, then lower the ball and your feet with control.
tips: Keep your chest lifted without collapsing backward.
Brace your core to keep your torso and legs steady.
Keep your arms straight and the ball aligned with your shoulders.
Inhale and exhale steadily without holding your breath.
ex_YCVDUM.description: Medicine Ball Hold the World is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a medicine ball, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Obliques, Shoulders, Quadriceps.

ex_PVBAU4.name: Hollow Hold
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs extended and your arms stretched overhead.
Engage your core and lift your shoulders and legs off the floor, keeping your lower back pressed into the floor. Your body should form a slight curve with your arms and legs elevated.
Hold this position, maintaining tension in your core and keeping your lower back flat against the floor.
Continue to hold the position for the desired duration, then slowly lower your shoulders and legs back to the starting position.
tips: Ensure your shoulders and legs are lifted at the same height to create a balanced position.
Focus on steady breathing, inhaling through your nose and exhaling through your mouth to help maintain focus and endurance.
If the full hollow hold is too challenging, you can modify the position by bending your knees or keeping your arms by your sides.
Avoid straining your neck; keep it relaxed and in line with your spine.
ex_PVBAU4.description: Hollow Hold is an intermediate single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors, Quadriceps.

ex_R4V3B7.name: Jack Knives
instructions: Lie flat on your back with your legs extended and your arms stretched on your sides.
Simultaneously lift your upper body and legs towards each other, reaching your hands towards your feet. Engage your core to lift both your torso and legs.
Try to touch your hands to your feet at the top of the movement, forming a "V" shape with your body.
Slowly lower your upper body and legs back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: If the full movement is too challenging, modify by bending your knees slightly.
Focus on steady breathing, exhaling as you lift your body and inhaling as you lower it.
Ensure your lower back remains pressed into the floor during the movement to prevent strain.
ex_R4V3B7.description: Jack Knives is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

ex_7JE7AW.name: Kettlebell Situp Press
instructions: Begin by lying on your back with your legs straight on the floor, holding a kettlebell with both hands at your chest.
Lift your upper body off the floor until it is vertical to the floor, and then press the kettlebell overhead by extending your arms.
Lower the kettlebell back close to your chest.
Slowly lower your upper body back to the starting. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions
tips: Use a controlled motion to lift and lower your upper body, avoiding any jerky movements.
Engage your core throughout the movement to maintain control and stability.
Choose a moderate weight for the kettlebell to ensure proper form and control.
ex_7JE7AW.description: Kettlebell Situp Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Triceps, Core.

ex_RPBZX4.name: L Sit Hold
instructions: Place your hands on parallel bars, dip handles or the floor next to your hips.
Press down to lift your body, locking your elbows and pushing your shoulders down.
Raise your straight legs in front of you until they are parallel to the floor, forming an L shape.
Hold the position for the set time while breathing steadily, then lower with control.
tips: Point your toes and squeeze your thighs together to keep your legs straight.
Bend your knees (tuck sit) if you can't yet hold straight legs.
ex_RPBZX4.description: L Sit Hold is an advanced multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Shoulders, Quadriceps.

ex_C4JOYB.name: Landmine Hollow Hold
instructions: Lie on your back with the landmine bar beside you and hold the end of the bar above your chest with both hands.
Press your lower back into the floor and lift your shoulders and straight legs off the ground.
Keep your arms extended, holding the bar steady over your chest in the hollow position.
Hold for the set time while breathing steadily, then lower your legs and shoulders with control.
tips: Your lower back must stay flat on the floor; raise your legs higher if it arches.
Keep your chin slightly tucked.
ex_C4JOYB.description: Landmine Hollow Hold is an intermediate single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors, Shoulders.

ex_IS3DIP.name: Landmine Kneeling Twist
instructions: Kneel facing the landmine and hold the end of the bar at chest height with both hands, arms extended.
Brace your core and keep your hips facing forward.
Rotate your torso to bring the bar down in an arc toward one hip.
Return through the centre with control and continue to the other side.
tips: Let the movement come from your torso, not your arms.
Keep your glutes tight so your hips stay square.
ex_IS3DIP.description: Landmine Kneeling Twist is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abdominals, Shoulders.

ex_4S3XGO.name: Landmine Oblique Twist
instructions: Stand facing the landmine with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold the end of the bar at chest height with both hands.
Extend your arms and brace your core.
Rotate your torso and pivot your back foot to swing the bar in an arc down toward one hip.
Bring the bar back over the top with control and repeat to the other side.
tips: Keep your arms long and the movement smooth.
Pivot your feet so your lower back doesn't twist under load.
ex_4S3XGO.description: Landmine Oblique Twist is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abdominals, Shoulders, Glutes.

ex_MQBBAP.name: Landmine Russian Twist
instructions: Sit on the floor beside the landmine with your knees bent and heels on the ground.
Hold the end of the bar with both hands above your chest and lean back slightly with a straight back.
Rotate your torso to lower the bar toward the floor on one side.
Bring it back over the top with control and lower it to the other side.
tips: Keep your chest open; don't round your back.
Lift your feet off the floor to make it harder.
ex_MQBBAP.description: Landmine Russian Twist is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abdominals, Hip Flexors.

ex_AXAZ2A.name: Leg Lift Circles
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs extended and your arms at your sides, palms facing down.
Lift both legs off the floor, about a foot above the floor, keeping your legs straight and your core engaged.
Begin to draw small circles in the air with both legs moving together in a controlled and steady motion. Perform the circles in one direction for a set number of repetitions.
Switch directions and draw circles with both legs in the opposite direction for the same number of repetitions. Lower your legs back to the starting position.
tips: Keep your legs as straight as possible to maximize the stretch and engagement in your hip flexors and quadriceps.
Perform the exercise on a comfortable, non-slip surface to prevent discomfort or injury.
If you find it difficult to keep your legs straight, you can start with smaller circles and gradually increase the size as you build strength and flexibility.
ex_AXAZ2A.description: Leg Lift Circles is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Adductors, Abductors.

ex_MQITYL.name: Leg Raises (Straight Legs)
instructions: Position yourself on a captain's chair, supporting your body weight with your forearms on the arm pads and your back against the backrest. Let your legs hang straight down.
Engage your core and keep your legs straight. Lift both legs together while keeping them straight.
Raise your legs until they are parallel to the floor or as high as you can comfortably go, maintaining control throughout the movement.
Slowly lower your legs back down to the starting position without swinging. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid swinging your legs or using momentum; focus on controlled movements to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you lift your legs and inhaling as you lower them.
Ensure your arms and shoulders remain stable to support your body weight effectively.
ex_MQITYL.description: Leg Raises (Straight Legs) is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors, Quadriceps.

ex_IE2V7X.name: Long Arm Crunches
instructions: Lie flat on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart. Extend your arms straight in line with your head, keeping them close to your ears, and hands crossed over each other.
Engage your core and lift your upper body off the floor, with your arms following your torso line, until it forms a 45-degree angle with the floor.
Hold the top position for a moment, squeezing your abdominal muscles.
Slowly lower your body back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your arms straight and aligned with your ears to ensure proper form and avoid straining your neck.
Press your lower back firmly into the floor throughout the exercise to prevent lower back strain.
Use a comfortable, non-slip exercise mat to provide cushioning and prevent slipping during the movement.
ex_IE2V7X.description: Long Arm Crunches is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Obliques.

ex_MZPVIA.name: Long Lever Plank
instructions: Start in a forearm plank, then walk your elbows forward so they are in front of your shoulders.
Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Brace your core hard and squeeze your glutes.
Hold the position for the set time while breathing steadily.
tips: The further your elbows are in front, the harder it gets.
Don't let your hips sag or your lower back arch.
ex_MZPVIA.description: Long Lever Plank is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Glutes.

ex_JC2RR4.name: Lying Abs Resistance Band
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Attach the resistance band to a low anchor point behind your head and hold the handles with both hands, keeping your arms bent and handles close to your head.
Curl your upper body, bringing your elbows towards your knees while lifting your back off the floor.
Slowly lower your upper body back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you curl your torso up and inhale as you lower it back down.
Keep your feet flat on the floor for better stability.
Focus on engaging your abdominal muscles throughout the movement.
ex_JC2RR4.description: Lying Abs Resistance Band is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abdominals, Hip Flexors.

ex_BFIXSW.name: Lying Leg Raise
instructions: Lie flat on your back with your legs extended and your arms at your sides, palms facing down firm on the floor.
Engage your core muscles and press your lower back into the floor.
Keeping your legs straight, lift them up towards the ceiling until they are perpendicular to the floor.
Slowly lower your legs back to the starting position with control, stopping just before they touch the floor. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you lift your legs up and inhale as you lower them back down.
Keep your legs as straight as possible for maximum effectiveness.
Focus on engaging your abdominal muscles throughout the movement.
ex_BFIXSW.description: Lying Leg Raise is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abdominals, Hip Flexors, Lower Back.

ex_K7YI3X.name: Med Ball Half Kneeling Wood Choppers
instructions: Kneel on one knee with the other foot flat in front, holding a medicine ball with both hands.
Start with the ball beside your hip on the side of the down knee.
Rotate your torso and lift the ball diagonally across your body to above the opposite shoulder.
Return along the same path with control, then switch sides after the set.
tips: Keep your hips facing forward and squeeze the glute of the down leg.
Move with control; let your torso, not your arms, do the work.
ex_K7YI3X.description: Med Ball Half Kneeling Wood Choppers is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a medicine ball, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abdominals, Shoulders, Glutes.

ex_77DGNG.name: Med Ball Toe Touches
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs raised straight toward the ceiling.
Hold a medicine ball with both hands above your chest, arms straight.
Curl your shoulders off the floor and reach the ball up toward your toes.
Lower your shoulders with control and repeat.
tips: Keep your lower back pressed into the floor.
Exhale as you reach up.
ex_77DGNG.description: Med Ball Toe Touches is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a medicine ball, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Obliques.

ex_XPOVTT.name: Medicine Ball Chest Throw With Abs
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent, facing a partner or a wall, holding a medicine ball at your chest.
Curl up into a sit-up and, as you rise, throw the ball forcefully from your chest.
Catch the ball, or receive it back from your partner, at chest height.
Lower your back to the floor with control and repeat.
tips: Brace your core before each throw.
Use a ball you can throw with full speed and good form.
ex_XPOVTT.description: Medicine Ball Chest Throw With Abs is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a medicine ball, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Triceps, Shoulders.

ex_3JXJTO.name: Medicine Ball Rotational Throw
instructions: Stand side-on to a wall about an arm's length away, feet shoulder-width apart, holding a medicine ball at your hip.
Load by rotating your torso away from the wall and bending your knees slightly.
Drive from your legs and hips and rotate explosively to throw the ball into the wall.
Catch the rebound, reset and repeat, then switch sides.
tips: Pivot your back foot so the power comes from your hips.
Keep your arms relaxed; they guide the ball, the core throws it.
ex_3JXJTO.description: Medicine Ball Rotational Throw is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a medicine ball, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abdominals, Shoulders, Glutes.

ex_AVUCVN.name: Middle Crunches
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs extended straight on the floor and your arms straight by your sides, palms facing the floor.
Curl your abdomen, raising your upper back off the floor, while simultaneously lifting your legs straight up towards the ceiling and raise your arms towards your feet.
Just before your hands and feet touch, lower your upper back, legs and arms back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you lift your upper back, legs and arms up, and inhale as you lower them back down.
Keep your legs as straight as possible for maximum abdominal activation.
Focus on engaging your abdominal muscles throughout the movement.
ex_AVUCVN.description: Middle Crunches is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors, Lower Back.

ex_A2YN6Y.name: Mountain Climber
instructions: Begin in a plank position on your toes and hands, with your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Bend your right knee and bring it towards your right elbow and stop when your knee is close to the elbow.
Return to the starting plank position, then repeat the movement on the opposite side.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure you keep your movements smooth and controlled to maintain form and avoid injury.
Maintain a steady breathing pattern, exhaling as you bring your knee towards your elbow and inhaling as you return to the plank position.
Keep your shoulders stable and your core engaged throughout the exercise to enhance effectiveness.
ex_A2YN6Y.description: Mountain Climber is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

ex_GIB3D5.name: Oblique Crunch
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Place your hands behind your head, keeping your elbows wide.
Engage your core muscles and lift your upper back off the floor, rotating your abdomen to raise your right elbow towards the ceiling.
Squeeze your obliques at the top of the movement and slowly lower your upper back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides to work the opposite oblique.
tips: Exhale as you lift and rotate your upper body, and inhale as you lower it back down.
Avoid pulling on your neck with your hands; let your abs do the work.
Focus on engaging your oblique muscles throughout the movement.
ex_GIB3D5.description: Oblique Crunch is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abdominals, Hip Flexors.

ex_SJGWKT.name: Over Head Weight Sit Up
instructions: Begin by lying flat on your back with your legs slightly bent and your feet together. Hold a weight plate with both hands, extending your arms straight above your chest.
Engage your core muscles and lift your upper body off the floor into a sitting position while keeping the weight extended straight up.
As you sit up, ensure your back remains straight and your chest is lifted, bringing your torso to an upright position.
Lower your upper body back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your core engaged throughout the entire movement to maintain stability and proper form.
Avoid using momentum to lift your upper body; focus on using your abdominal muscles to perform the sit-up.
Exhale as you sit up and inhale as you lower back down.
ex_SJGWKT.description: Over Head Weight Sit Up is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.

ex_IOTZ4Q.name: Over Weight Ab Crunch
instructions: Begin by lying on your back with your legs straight on the floor close together. Hold a dumbbell with both hands, keeping your arms bent and behind your head, close to the floor.
Engage your core muscles and lift your torso off the floor while bending your knees and raising them to your chest, and bringing the dumbbell close to your knees.
Lower your body back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you crunch up and inhale as you lower back down.
Start with a lighter weight to master the form before progressing to heavier weights.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and avoid injury.
ex_IOTZ4Q.description: Over Weight Ab Crunch is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.

ex_3LYFMW.name: Plank Cross Knee Drive
instructions: Begin in a plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your body forming a straight line from head to heels. Engage your core.
Lift your right knee and drive it towards your left elbow and straighten your leg, twisting your torso slightly to the left as you do so.
Return your right leg to the starting plank position.
Repeat the movement with your left knee, driving it towards your right elbow. Alternate sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your core engaged throughout the exercise to maintain stability and support your lower back.
Move slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Focus on steady breathing, exhaling as you drive your knee towards your elbow and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
ex_3LYFMW.description: Plank Cross Knee Drive is an intermediate single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Hip Flexors.

ex_CMYW3B.name: Plank Jack
instructions: Begin in a plank position with your elbows directly under your shoulders and your body forming a straight line from head to heels. Engage your core.
Jump your feet out to the sides, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, while keeping your upper body stable.
Quickly jump your feet back together to return to the starting plank position.
Continue jumping your feet in and out for the desired number of repetitions or duration.
tips: Move quickly but with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Maintain a neutral head position, looking slightly ahead of your hands, to keep your neck aligned with your spine.
Ensure your body stays in a straight line, avoiding sagging hips or raised buttocks.
ex_CMYW3B.description: Plank Jack is an intermediate single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Hip Flexors, Quadriceps.

ex_JJLXOF.name: Plank Knee Tucks
instructions: Begin in a plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your body forming a straight line from head to heels.
Quickly jump both knees towards your chest, landing with both feet flat on the floor beneath you.
Immediately jump your feet back to the starting plank position.
Continue jumping your feet in and out for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Use controlled, explosive movements to quickly bring your knees to your chest and return to plank position.
Ensure your shoulders remain directly over your wrists to maintain alignment and reduce strain on your shoulders.
Keep your hips level throughout the movement to maintain proper form and avoid sagging or raising your hips.
ex_JJLXOF.description: Plank Knee Tucks is an intermediate single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Hip Flexors, Quadriceps.

ex_2KM4MA.name: Plank Reach Through
instructions: Begin in a side plank position on your right side with your right elbow supporting your body, your left arm raised vertically towards the ceiling, and your body forming a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your left arm, reaching it under and across your torso while slightly lowering your hips.
Return your left arm to the starting position, lifting your hips back to the straight line.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the left side and repeat the movement with your right arm.
tips: Engage your core throughout the exercise to maintain stability and support your lower back.
Ensure your supporting arm or elbow is directly under your shoulder to maintain proper alignment and reduce strain.
Keep your hips stable and aligned with your body, avoiding excessive rotation.
Focus on steady breathing, exhaling as you reach under your torso and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
ex_2KM4MA.description: Plank Reach Through is an intermediate single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.

ex_6JOB6L.name: Plank on Elbows
instructions: Begin by lying face down on the floor. Place your elbows directly under your shoulders and your forearms flat on the floor, parallel to each other.
Engage your core and lift your body off the floor, forming a straight line from your head to your heels. Your elbows and toes should support your body weight.
Hold this position, keeping your core tight and your body straight. Avoid letting your hips sag or rise too high.
Maintain the plank position for the desired amount of time, focusing on your form and breathing steadily.
tips: Engage your core throughout the exercise to maintain stability and support your lower back.
Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels, avoiding any sagging or lifting of the hips.
Keep your shoulders directly above your elbows to maintain proper alignment and reduce strain on your shoulders.
ex_6JOB6L.description: Plank on Elbows is an intermediate single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Lower Back.

ex_2VZPV4.name: Plate Hollow Hold
instructions: Lie on your back holding a weight plate with both hands, arms extended above your chest.
Press your lower back into the floor and lift your shoulders and straight legs off the ground.
Keep the plate steady above you in the hollow position.
Hold for the set time while breathing steadily, then lower with control.
tips: Raise your legs higher if your lower back starts to arch.
Keep your chin slightly tucked.
ex_2VZPV4.description: Plate Hollow Hold is an intermediate single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors, Shoulders.

ex_DUNBYZ.name: Plate Pinch Grip Side Bend
instructions: Stand tall and pinch a weight plate in one hand at your side, fingers on one face and thumb on the other.
Place the other hand on your hip or behind your head.
Bend sideways toward the plate as far as you comfortably can, keeping your hips still.
Return to upright by contracting the opposite side of your waist, then switch sides after the set.
tips: Bend straight to the side; don't lean forward or back.
The pinch grip also trains your fingers and forearm.
ex_DUNBYZ.description: Plate Pinch Grip Side Bend is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms, Core.

ex_3TXREU.name: Plate Russian Twist
instructions: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and heels on the ground, holding a weight plate at your chest.
Lean back slightly with a straight back.
Rotate your torso to bring the plate to one side of your hips.
Rotate back through the centre to the other side and repeat.
tips: Lift your feet to make it harder.
Turn your shoulders, not just your arms.
ex_3TXREU.description: Plate Russian Twist is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abdominals, Hip Flexors.

ex_2NQGBT.name: Plate Situp
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat, holding a weight plate on your chest.
Brace your core and curl your torso up until you are sitting upright.
Pause at the top.
Lower your back to the floor with control and repeat.
tips: Anchor your feet under something if they lift.
Don't pull with your neck; lead with your chest.
ex_2NQGBT.description: Plate Situp is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors, Obliques.

ex_W3IP6L.name: Plate Standing Twist
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold a weight plate at chest height with your arms slightly bent.
Brace your core and keep your hips facing forward.
Rotate your torso to one side.
Return through the centre with control and rotate to the other side.
tips: Keep the movement controlled; don't swing the plate.
Extending your arms further makes it harder.
ex_W3IP6L.description: Plate Standing Twist is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abdominals, Shoulders.

ex_W4UFSB.name: Plate Wood Chopper
instructions: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width, holding a weight plate with both hands.
Start with the plate above one shoulder, arms extended.
Rotate and squat slightly as you bring the plate diagonally down across your body to the outside of the opposite knee.
Reverse the movement back up to the starting position, then switch sides after the set.
tips: Pivot your feet to protect your lower back.
Keep your back flat as you reach down.
ex_W4UFSB.description: Plate Wood Chopper is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abdominals, Shoulders, Quadriceps.

ex_WTTOIG.name: Raised Leg Crunch
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs straight, vertical to the floor. Place your hands behind your head with your elbows pointing outwards.
Engage your core and lift your shoulders off the floor, bringing your chest towards your knees.
Hold the top position for a moment, squeezing your abdominal muscles.
Lower your shoulders back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid pulling on your neck with your hands; instead, use your abdominal muscles to lift your shoulders.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you lift your shoulders and inhaling as you lower them.
Keep your lower back pressed against the floor to prevent strain and maintain proper form.
Perform the exercise on a comfortable, non-slip surface to ensure safety and reduce discomfort.
ex_WTTOIG.description: Raised Leg Crunch is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Obliques.

ex_ZUPFRA.name: Resistance Band Lying Bent Knee Raise
instructions: Attach the resistance loop band to a low anchor point and lie on your back with your knees bent and feet touching together. Wrap the other end of the loop resistance band over your feet. Place your arms on the floor by your sides.
Keep both legs straight and a few inches off the floor.
Slowly bend your knees and bring your legs up until your thighs are perpendicular to the floor and for a 90 degree.
Straighten your legs to the starting position with control and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on engaging your abdominals throughout the movement.
Avoid lifting your lower back off the floor; keep it pressed down for the duration of the exercise.
Maintain a slight bend in your knee if necessary to reduce strain.
ex_ZUPFRA.description: Resistance Band Lying Bent Knee Raise is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors, Quadriceps.

ex_AWMUZ2.name: Reverse Ab Wheel Rollout
instructions: Begin in a plank position with your hands on the floor, arms straight, and the ab roller set under your feet. Your legs should be straight back, forming a straight line from head to heels.
Engage your core and slowly roll the ab roller towards your hands, keeping your legs straight. Continue rolling until your thighs are vertical to the floor.
Hold the position briefly, ensuring your core is tight and your back is straight.
Roll the ab roller back to the starting position with control, maintaining a straight line with your body. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily, exhaling as you roll the roller towards your hands and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
Avoid arching your back; maintain a neutral spine to prevent strain on your lower back.
Start with a small range of motion if you are new to this exercise, gradually increasing the distance as you build strength.
Perform the exercise on a stable, non-slip surface to ensure safety and prevent slipping.
ex_AWMUZ2.description: Reverse Ab Wheel Rollout is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a wheel roller, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Quadriceps.

ex_B6KPZX.name: Reverse Crunch With Kick Out
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Place your arms by your sides with palms facing down for stability.
Lift your legs off the floor, bending your knees at a 90-degree angle so that your thighs are perpendicular to the floor and your calves are parallel to the floor.
Extend your legs straight out in front of you, keeping them off the floor to perform a kick-out.

Bend your knees back to the starting position and engage your core to lift your hips off the floor, curling your knees towards your chest. Lower your hips back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid using momentum to lift your hips; focus on using your abdominal muscles.
Perform the exercise on a comfortable, non-slip surface to ensure safety and reduce discomfort.
Keep your head and shoulders relaxed on the floor to avoid straining your neck.
ex_B6KPZX.description: Reverse Crunch With Kick Out is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Obliques.

ex_FXY3GL.name: Reverse Crunch
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Place your arms by your sides with palms facing down for stability.
Lift your legs off the floor, bending your knees at a 90-degree angle so that your thighs are perpendicular to the floor and your calves are parallel to the floor.
Engage your core and lift your hips off the floor, curling your knees towards your chest. Focus on using your abdominal muscles to lift your hips.
Slowly lower your hips back to the starting position, keeping your knees bent at a 90-degree angle. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid using momentum to lift your hips; focus on using your abdominal muscles.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you lift your hips and inhaling as you lower them back down.
Keep your head and shoulders relaxed on the floor to avoid straining your neck.
ex_FXY3GL.description: Reverse Crunch is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Obliques.

ex_SVCY4S.name: Reverse Plank
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs straight and hands behind your hips, fingers pointing toward your feet.
Press through your hands and heels to lift your hips until your body forms a straight line.
Squeeze your glutes and keep your chest open.
Hold the position for the set time, then lower with control.
tips: Don't let your hips drop.
Keep your neck in line with your body; look up rather than letting your head hang back.
ex_SVCY4S.description: Reverse Plank is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Shoulders, Triceps.

ex_UW4CWN.name: Russian Twist With Medicine Ball
instructions: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and heels on the ground, holding a medicine ball at your chest.
Lean back slightly with a straight back.
Rotate your torso to bring the ball beside one hip.
Rotate back through the centre to the other side and repeat.
tips: Lift your feet to make it harder.
Keep your chest open and turn your shoulders.
ex_UW4CWN.description: Russian Twist With Medicine Ball is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a medicine ball, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abdominals, Hip Flexors.

ex_OVG34C.name: Russian Twist
instructions: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Lean back slightly so that your torso forms a V-shape with your thighs.
Clasp your hands together in front of your chest.
Rotate your torso to the right, bringing your hands opposite your right hip.
Rotate back through the center and to the left, bringing your hands opposite your left hip. Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Move your torso, not just your arms, to ensure you are engaging your oblique muscles.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you rotate to each side and inhaling as you return to the center.
Keep your back straight and avoid hunching your shoulders to maintain proper form.
ex_OVG34C.description: Russian Twist is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abdominals, Hip Flexors.

ex_L6W26Y.name: Scissors Kick
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs extended and your arms by your sides, palms facing down.
Lift both legs off the floor a few inches, keeping them straight.
Alternately cross your legs over each other in a scissor-like motion. Move your right leg over your left leg and then switch, bringing your left leg over your right leg.
Continue alternating legs in a controlled manner for the desired number of repetitions or duration.
tips: Ensure your lower back remains pressed against the floor to avoid strain and maintain proper form.
Move your legs slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Perform the exercise on a comfortable, non-slip surface to ensure safety and reduce discomfort.
Avoid letting your legs drop too low, which could increase strain on your lower back.
ex_L6W26Y.description: Scissors Kick is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Obliques, Hip Flexors.

ex_73OEJX.name: Seated Floor Crunches
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended straight out in front of you, forming an L-shape with your torso.
Place your hands behind your head without pulling on your neck, elbows facing outwards.
Engage your core and bend your torso towards your thighs, performing a crunch while keeping your legs straight.
Bring your torso back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid pulling on your neck with your hands; use your abdominal muscles to lower your torso.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you lift your torso and inhaling as you lower it back down.
Keep your legs straight and flat on the floor to maintain stability during the exercise.
ex_73OEJX.description: Seated Floor Crunches is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Obliques.

ex_HRSPUD.name: Seated Flutter Kicks
instructions: Sit on a bench with your legs extended straight out in front of you. Lean back slightly, supporting yourself by gripping the sides of the bench.
Lift both legs off the bench a few inches, keeping them straight.
Begin the flutter kicks by alternately raising and lowering your legs in a scissor-like motion, moving your right leg up while your left leg moves down and vice versa.
Continue the flutter kicks for the desired number of repetitions or duration, keeping your core engaged and your movements controlled.
tips: Keep your back straight and avoid rounding your shoulders to maintain proper form.
Perform the exercise on a stable, non-slip bench to ensure safety and prevent slipping.
If you are new to this exercise, start with a smaller range of motion and gradually increase it as you build strength.
ex_HRSPUD.description: Seated Flutter Kicks is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors, Obliques.

ex_CKUPB7.name: Seated V Up
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended straight in front of you and your arms placed on the floor slightly behind you for support.
Engage your core and lift your torso off the floor, bringing your knees towards your chest to form a V shape with your body.
Hold the top position for a moment, squeezing your abdominal muscles.
Lower your legs and torso back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily, exhaling as you lift into the V position and inhaling as you lower back down.
Avoid using momentum to lift your legs and torso; focus on using your abdominal muscles.
Keep your back straight and avoid rounding your shoulders to maintain proper form.
ex_CKUPB7.description: Seated V Up is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

ex_RQPJ2F.name: Side Plank Oblique Crunch
instructions: Begin in a side plank position on your right side, with your legs extended straight and stacked on top of each other. Prop yourself up on your right elbow, keeping your elbow directly under your shoulder. Place your left hand on your hip.
Engage your core and lift your hips off the floor, forming a straight line from your head to your feet.
Lower your hips towards the floor without touching it, then raise them back up to the starting position, squeezing your obliques at the top.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other side and perform the exercise on your left side.
tips: Keep your core engaged throughout the exercise to maintain balance and stability.
Move your hips slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you lift your hips and inhaling as you lower them.
ex_RQPJ2F.description: Side Plank Oblique Crunch is an intermediate single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Core, Shoulders.

ex_ICALYP.name: Side Plank
instructions: Lie on your right side with your legs extended straight and stacked on top of each other. Prop yourself up on your right elbow, keeping your elbow directly under your shoulder.
Engage your core and lift your hips off the floor, forming a straight line from your head to your feet.
Hold the position for the desired duration, keeping your body straight and your core tight.
Slowly lower your hips back to the starting position with control. Repeat on the other side by lying on your left side and following the same steps.
tips: Ensure your elbow is directly under your shoulder to support your upper body.
Focus on keeping your head in line with your spine to prevent neck strain.
Maintain a straight body line, avoiding any sagging or lifting of the hips.
Perform the exercise on a comfortable, non-slip surface to ensure safety and reduce discomfort.
ex_ICALYP.description: Side Plank is an intermediate single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.

ex_AETH3T.name: Situps
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart. Place your hands behind your head.
Engage your core and lift your upper body off the floor, curling your chest towards your knees.
Continue to lift your torso until you are in a sitting position with your chest close to your knees.
Slowly lower your upper body back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your core engaged throughout the exercise to maximize muscle engagement and support your lower back.
Move your body slowly and with control to avoid using momentum and to prevent injury.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you lift your torso and inhaling as you lower it back down.
ex_AETH3T.description: Situps is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

ex_PA4MIJ.name: Spider Plank
instructions: Begin in a standard plank position with your forearms on the floor, elbows directly under your shoulders, and your body forming a straight line from head to heels. Engage your core and keep your feet hip-width apart.
Lift your right foot off the floor and bring your right knee towards your right elbow, keeping your hips level and your core tight.
Return your right foot to the starting position, maintaining a stable plank position.
Repeat the movement with your left leg, bringing your left knee towards your left elbow. Continue alternating legs for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you bring your knee towards your elbow and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
Focus on keeping your hips level and avoiding excessive torso rotation.
Use a mat to cushion your forearms and feet for added comfort.
ex_PA4MIJ.description: Spider Plank is an intermediate single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Glutes, Hip Flexors.

ex_6DZQW5.name: Standing Ab Wheel Rollout
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding an ab wheel with both hands. Engage your core and maintain an upright posture.
Bend at your hips and knees to lower the ab wheel to the floor in front of your feet. Keep your arms extended and your back straight.
Slowly roll the ab wheel forward, extending your body into a plank position. Ensure your core remains tight and your back stays straight throughout the movement.
Roll the ab wheel back towards your feet, bending at your hips and knees to return to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and reduce injury risk.
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you roll out and inhaling as you return.
Keep your back straight and avoid sagging or arching your lower back.
ex_6DZQW5.description: Standing Ab Wheel Rollout is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a wheel roller, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Back, Hip Flexors.

ex_GOW3GK.name: Standing Cable Oblique Twist
instructions: Stand sideways to a cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart. Attach a handle to a mid-pulley and grasp it with both hands. Bend your arms at 90 degrees and keep your elbows close to your torso sides.
Engage your core and keep your arms stationary as you twist your torso away from the machine, pulling the handle across your body.
Twist until your shoulders are turned 90 degrees from the machine, feeling the stretch in your oblique muscles.
Slowly return to the starting position with control, keeping your arms straight. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
tips: Use your oblique muscles to twist, not your arms, hips, or legs.
Keep your feet planted firmly on the floor.
Adjust the cable machine weight to a challenging but manageable level.
ex_GOW3GK.description: Standing Cable Oblique Twist is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Core, Lower Back, Glutes.

ex_MI4V5R.name: Standing Oblique Crunch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, placing your hands behind your head with your elbows flared out to the sides. Engage your core and maintain an upright posture.
Lift your right knee towards your right elbow while simultaneously bending your torso to the right to bring your elbow and knee closer together.
Return to the starting position by lowering your right leg and straightening your torso.
Repeat the movement on the left side, lifting your left knee towards your left elbow. Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily: exhale as you crunch to the side and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Ensure your standing leg remains slightly bent to maintain balance.
Keep your back straight and avoid leaning forward or backward during the exercise.
ex_MI4V5R.description: Standing Oblique Crunch is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abdominals, Hip Flexors, Shoulders.

ex_SHM5HG.name: Star Crunches
instructions: Lie flat on your back with your arms and legs extended out to form an "X" shape. Keep your core engaged and your lower back pressed into the floor.
Crunch your abdominal muscles to lift your shoulders and legs off the floor and lift your arms and legs towards each other, reaching your hands towards your ankles.
Lower your arms and legs back to the starting position with control.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily: exhale as you lift your arm and leg, and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Focus on using your abdominal muscles to lift your arms and legs off the floor.
Use a mat to provide cushioning and support for your back.
ex_SHM5HG.description: Star Crunches is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors, Shoulders, Quadriceps.

ex_WVLOEL.name: Suspension Trainer With Grips Abdominal Fallout
instructions: Adjust the suspension trainer handles to about waist height. Stand in front of the hanging handles with your feet shoulder-width apart and grasp the handles with your palms facing down.
Engage your core and lean forward, allowing your arms to extend overhead while maintaining a straight body line from head to heels.
Lower your body until your arms are fully extended above your head, feeling the tension in your core.
Pull your body back to the starting position by pulling your arms back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily: exhale as you lean forward and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Adjust the length of the suspension trainer straps to increase or decrease the difficulty of the exercise.
Keep your arms straight and avoid bending your elbows during the movement.

ex_4QNJIN.name: Dumbbell Alternating Pendlay Row
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand. Bend your knees and hinge forward at your hips until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor, allowing both arms to hang straight beneath your shoulders, resting the dumbbells on the floor.

ex_XQHZ5Y.name: Dumbbell Bent Arm Pullover
instructions: Lie perpendicular on a bench with only your upper back supported and your hips slightly lowered. Hold a dumbbell with both hands above your chest, keeping your elbows slightly bent.

Pull the dumbbell back to the starting position with a controlled motion, keeping your elbows slightly bent. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Ensure your shoulders and upper back remain in contact with the bench throughout the exercise.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
ex_XQHZ5Y.description: Dumbbell Bent Arm Pullover is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

ex_OHJYRP.name: Dumbbell Bent-Over Reverse Row
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip (palms facing towards you). Bend at your hips and knees to lower your torso until it is nearly parallel to the floor, keeping your back straight.

Pull the dumbbells towards your torso, leading with your elbows and keeping them close to your body. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
Lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with a controlled motion. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Breathe out as you pull the dumbbells towards your torso and breathe in as you lower them back down.
Ensure your elbows remain close to your body throughout the exercise to protect your joints.
ex_OHJYRP.description: Dumbbell Bent-Over Reverse Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Biceps.

ex_KLHF6Q.name: Dumbbell Bent-Over Row
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip (palms facing each other). Bend at your hips and knees to lower your torso until it is nearly parallel to the floor, keeping your back straight.

Pull the dumbbells towards your torso, leading with your elbows and keeping them close to your body. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
Lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with a controlled motion. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Breathe out as you pull the dumbbells towards your torso and breathe in as you lower them back down.

ex_NBDKOU.name: Dumbbell Goblet Good Morning
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and hold a dumbbell vertically against your chest with both hands. Keep your knees slightly bent and your core engaged.
Push your hips back and hinge your torso forward while keeping the dumbbell close to your chest and your back straight.
Lower your torso until it is nearly parallel to the floor or until you feel a comfortable stretch in your hamstrings.
Drive your hips forward to return to the upright position, then repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Keep your spine neutral and avoid rounding your lower back.

ex_PWRY3Y.name: Dumbbell Hammer Grip Incline Bench Two Arm Row
instructions: Adjust an incline bench to a 45-degree angle. Lie face down on the bench with your feet firmly on the floor. Hold a dumbbell in each hand using a hammer grip (palms facing each other).
Let your arms hang straight down toward the floor, fully extended, with your elbows slightly bent.
Pull the dumbbells towards your torso by bending your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid using momentum; perform the movement in a slow and controlled manner.
Exhale as you pull the dumbbells towards your torso and inhale as you lower them.
Keep your feet firmly planted on the floor for stability.
ex_PWRY3Y.description: Dumbbell Hammer Grip Incline Bench Two Arm Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Biceps.

ex_EPZI6D.name: Dumbbell Incline Row
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 45-degree angle and lie chest-first against it, allowing your arms to extend opposite your chest with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing down.
Row both dumbbells backward by bending your elbows and pulling them towards your sides.
Return the dumbbells back to the starting position with control, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Ensure your wrists remain straight and aligned with your forearms.
Select a weight that allows for proper form and control throughout the exercise.
ex_EPZI6D.description: Dumbbell Incline Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps.

ex_KKWYIA.name: Dumbbell Knee Lawnmower Row
instructions: Begin in a wide stance with one foot pointing forward and the other pointing to the side. Bend your knees, lean forward, brace your free hand on your thigh, and hold the dumbbell between your legs with an overhand grip.
Pull the dumbbell toward your abdomen while keeping your torso still, rotating your hand from an overhand grip to an underhand grip as your elbow moves upward and backward.
Pause briefly at the top and squeeze your back muscles while keeping your hips and shoulders steady.
Lower the dumbbell with control while rotating your hand back to an overhand grip, then repeat before switching sides.

Pull the dumbbell toward your abdomen while keeping your elbow close to your body.
Keep your working shoulder down and avoid shrugging as you row.
Exhale as you pull the dumbbell upward and inhale as you lower it.
ex_KKWYIA.description: Dumbbell Knee Lawnmower Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Forearms, Core.

ex_BLGRVH.name: Dumbbell One Arm Row (Rack Support)
instructions: Stand facing a dumbbell rack, placing your left hand on the rack for support. Hold a dumbbell in your right hand with a neutral grip, arm extended down.

Pull the dumbbell upward towards your hip, bending your elbow and keeping it close to your body, focusing on squeezing your back muscles.
Lower the dumbbell back to the starting position with control, fully extending your arm. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.

ex_ANUKTF.name: Dumbbell Pendlay Row
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand using a neutral grip. Bend your knees and hinge forward until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor, with the dumbbells hanging below your shoulders.

Keep your torso still and avoid using momentum to lift the weights.

ex_ANUKTF.description: Dumbbell Pendlay Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Forearms, Lower Back.

ex_FWHORK.name: Dumbbell Pullover (Bent Arm)
instructions: Begin by lying on a flat bench, with your feet flat on the floor. Hold a dumbbell with both hands, palms pressed against the underside of the plates, arms extended straight above your chest.

Pull the dumbbell back over your chest by contracting your chest and lats, following the same arc as you lowered it.

ex_Q6DJYQ.name: Dumbbell Pullover on Floor
instructions: Begin by lying flat on your back on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat. Hold a dumbbell with both hands, palms pressed against the underside of the plates, arms extended straight above your chest.

ex_XTURBN.name: Dumbbell Pullover

ex_EBBZNB.name: Dumbbell Renegade Row
instructions: Begin in a plank position with your feet hip-width apart and each hand holding a dumbbell, arms fully extended, and body forming a straight line from head to heels.
Lift your right hand off the floor, rowing the dumbbell towards your right hip by bending your elbow and keeping your arm close to your body.

ex_UA3FUQ.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
