instructions: Lie with your upper back supported on a flat bench, your knees bent, and your feet firmly on the floor. Lift your hips and hold a kettlebell with both hands above your chest, using a neutral grip.
Keep your arms slightly bent and slowly lower the kettlebell behind your head.
Lower until you feel a comfortable stretch through your mid-back while keeping your hips raised.
Pull the kettlebell back above your chest with control, then repeat.
tips: Keep your hips raised throughout the entire exercise.
Avoid arching your lower back as the kettlebell lowers.
Lower the kettlebell behind your head in a smooth, controlled arc.
Inhale as you lower the kettlebell and exhale as you raise it.
ex_76DSPU.description: Kettlebell Pullover is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Triceps, Shoulders.

ex_PUQHOR.name: Kettlebell Row
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart, bend your knees, and hinge forward with your back straight. Hold a kettlebell in each hand using a neutral grip and let your arms hang down.
Pull both kettlebells toward the sides of your abdomen, driving your elbows upward and backward close to your body.
Pause briefly at the top and squeeze your back muscles while keeping your torso still.
Lower both kettlebells with control until your arms are extended, then repeat.
tips: Maintain the same torso position throughout each repetition.
Keep your elbows close to your body as you row.
Pull the kettlebells toward your abdomen rather than your shoulders.
Exhale as you pull and inhale as you lower.
ex_PUQHOR.description: Kettlebell Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Biceps, Forearms.

ex_TVKVSC.name: Kettlebell Single Arm Row
instructions: Stand in a wide stance with your right foot forward and your left leg slightly back. Bend your knees slightly, lean forward, rest your right arm on your right thigh, and hold the kettlebell in your left hand with a neutral grip.
Let your left arm hang toward the floor with your palm facing inward.
Pull the kettlebell toward the left side of your abdomen, driving your elbow back close to your body.
Lower the kettlebell with control until your arm is extended, then repeat before switching sides.
tips: Keep your chest up and your torso still during each repetition.
Keep your working elbow close to your body as you pull.
Fully extend your arm at the bottom without rounding your back.
Exhale as you pull and inhale as you lower.
ex_TVKVSC.description: Kettlebell Single Arm Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Forearms, Core.

ex_62I7TY.name: Kettlebell Sumo Deadlift
instructions: Place a kettlebell on the floor between your feet. Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart and your toes pointed slightly outward.
Hinge at your hips and bend your knees to lower your body, reaching down to grasp the kettlebell handle with both hands, keeping your back straight and chest up.
Push through your heels to lift the kettlebell off the floor, extending your hips and knees simultaneously.
Lower the kettlebell back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your knees track over your toes to prevent knee strain.
Maintain a wide stance with toes pointed slightly outward.
Use a weight that allows you to maintain proper form throughout the exercise.
ex_62I7TY.description: Kettlebell Sumo Deadlift is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Lower Back.

ex_7XFDEN.name: Double Kettlebell Sumo Deadlift High Pull
instructions: Place two kettlebells on the floor between your feet. Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart and your toes pointed slightly outward.
Hinge at your hips and bend your knees to lower your body, reaching down to grasp the kettlebell handles, one in each hand, keeping your back straight and chest up.

Push through your heels to lift the kettlebells off the floor, extending your hips and knees simultaneously. As you reach the standing position, pull the kettlebells upward towards your chin by bending your elbows and keeping them pointed outward.
Lower the kettlebells back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back straight and avoid rounding your shoulders.
Exhale as you lift the kettlebell and perform the high pull, inhale as you lower it.
Push through your heels to maximize power and stability.
ex_7XFDEN.description: Double Kettlebell Sumo Deadlift High Pull is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Upper Back, Lower Back.

ex_GQS2GR.name: Kipping Pull Up
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Start a rhythmic swing by pushing your chest through your arms, then pulling your legs forward.
At the front of the swing, drive your hips up and pull hard with your arms to bring your chin over the bar.
Push away from the bar as you descend and flow straight into the next swing.
tips: Learn strict pull-ups first; kipping puts more stress on the shoulders.
Keep your core tight to control the swing.
ex_GQS2GR.description: Kipping Pull Up is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Upper Back, Abdominals.

ex_7BV2QA.name: Land Mine Row
instructions: Straddle the landmine bar facing away from the anchor, or stand beside it, and hinge at your hips with a flat back.
Grip the bar just below the plates, with a V-handle or both hands.
Row the bar toward your chest by driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades.
Lower the bar with control until your arms are straight and repeat.
tips: Keep your back flat and your hips still throughout.
Pull toward your lower chest, not your neck.
ex_7BV2QA.description: Land Mine Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Rear Shoulders, Lower Back.

ex_WOHHFY.name: Landmine Romanian Deadlift
instructions: Stand facing the landmine and hold the end of the bar with both hands at hip height.
With a slight bend in your knees, hinge at your hips and push them back as you lower the bar along your legs.
Stop when you feel a stretch in your hamstrings, keeping your back flat.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall and squeeze your glutes at the top.
tips: The movement is a hip hinge, not a squat.
Keep the bar close to your body.
ex_WOHHFY.description: Landmine Romanian Deadlift is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Forearms.

ex_A6QRLF.name: Lat Pull Down Close Grip
instructions: Sit at the lat pulldown machine with your feet flat on the floor and knees secured under the pads. Grasp the bar with both hands just closer than shoulder-width apart, and your arms fully extended above you.
Pull the bar down towards your upper chest by bending your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together, keeping your back straight.
Hold the contraction for a second, then slowly return the bar to the starting position with control, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back straight and avoid leaning backward excessively.
Focus on engaging your back muscles throughout the movement.
Exhale as you pull the bar down and inhale as you return to the starting position.
ex_A6QRLF.description: Lat Pull Down Close Grip is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Shoulders, Upper Back.

ex_E7C3C2.name: Lat Pull Down Normal Grip
instructions: Sit at the lat pulldown machine with your feet flat on the floor and knees secured under the pads. Grasp the bar with both hands, just wider than shoulder-width apart, and your arms fully extended above you.
Pull the bar down towards your upper chest by bending your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together, keeping your back straight.
Hold the contraction for a second, then slowly return the bar to the starting position with control, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back straight and avoid leaning backward excessively.
Focus on engaging your back muscles throughout the movement.
Exhale as you pull the bar down and inhale as you return to the starting position.
ex_E7C3C2.description: Lat Pull Down Normal Grip is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Shoulders, Upper Back.

ex_STL56E.name: Lat Pull Down Wide Grip
instructions: Sit at the lat pulldown machine with your feet flat on the floor and knees secured under the pads. Grasp the bar with both hands, wider than shoulder-width apart, and your arms fully extended above you.
Pull the bar down towards your upper chest by bending your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together, keeping your back straight.
Hold the contraction for a second, then slowly return the bar to the starting position with control, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back straight and avoid leaning backward excessively.
Focus on engaging your back muscles throughout the movement.
Exhale as you pull the bar down and inhale as you return to the starting position.
ex_STL56E.description: Lat Pull Down Wide Grip is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Shoulders, Upper Back.

ex_7JTA7H.name: Lawnmower Row
instructions: Stand in a split stance with one hand on your front thigh or a bench, holding a dumbbell in the other hand.
Hinge forward with a flat back and let the dumbbell hang below your shoulder.
Pull the weight up and back toward your hip, rotating your torso slightly as you would starting a lawnmower.
Lower the weight with control and repeat, then switch sides.
tips: Lead with your elbow and keep it close to your body.
Keep the rotation small and controlled.
ex_7JTA7H.description: Lawnmower Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Rear Shoulders, Obliques.

ex_PHIUMX.name: Lying Back Extension
instructions: Begin by lying face down on the floor with your legs extended straight behind you and your hands placed behind your head, elbows out to the sides.
Engage your core and glutes, then lift your upper torso off the floor, keeping your neck in a neutral position and your lower body relaxed on the floor.
Hold the top position for a moment, squeezing your lower back muscles.
Slowly lower your upper torso back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your neck in a neutral position to avoid straining it.
Perform the exercise on a comfortable, non-slip surface to prevent discomfort or injury.
If you find it challenging to lift your upper torso, you can start with smaller movements and gradually increase the range of motion as you build strength.
ex_PHIUMX.description: Lying Back Extension is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Hamstrings.

ex_XKJ7XS.name: Plate Alternating Deadstop Row
instructions: Place two weight plates on the floor and hinge over them with a flat back, knees slightly bent.
Grip one plate and row it up toward your hip.
Lower it back to the floor and let it come to a full stop.
Row the other plate and keep alternating.
tips: Each rep starts from a dead stop, so don't bounce the plate.
Keep your torso still as you pull.
ex_XKJ7XS.description: Plate Alternating Deadstop Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Rear Shoulders, Forearms.

ex_ZOOWPD.name: Plate Glute Bridge to Pullover
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, holding a weight plate above your chest with both hands.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips into a glute bridge.
Holding the bridge, lower the plate behind your head with slightly bent arms until you feel a stretch in your lats.
Pull the plate back over your chest, then lower your hips and repeat.
tips: Keep your ribs down while the plate moves overhead.
Squeeze your glutes throughout the bridge.
ex_ZOOWPD.description: Plate Glute Bridge to Pullover is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Chest, Triceps.

ex_MMGDUN.name: Plate Good Morning
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and hold a weight plate against your chest.
With a slight bend in your knees, hinge forward from your hips with a flat back.
Lower your torso until it is close to parallel with the floor, or until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
Drive your hips forward to return to standing.
tips: Keep your back flat; don't round it to go lower.
Push your hips back rather than bending your knees more.
ex_MMGDUN.description: Plate Good Morning is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes.

ex_ZEORHY.name: Plate Pinch Grip Deadlift
instructions: Stand over two weight plates and pinch one in each hand by its rim, fingers on one face and thumb on the other.
Hinge at your hips and bend your knees with a flat back.
Drive through your feet to stand up tall, holding the plates at your sides.
Lower them back down with control by hinging at your hips.
tips: The pinch grip limits the weight, so this is mainly a grip and posture drill.
Keep your shoulders back and chest up.
ex_ZEORHY.description: Plate Pinch Grip Deadlift is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Quadriceps, Traps.

ex_TVAVLM.name: Plate Pinch Grip Row
instructions: Pinch a weight plate in one hand and hinge forward with a flat back, supporting yourself on a bench or your thigh with the other hand.
Let the plate hang below your shoulder.
Row the plate up toward your hip by driving your elbow back.
Lower it with control and repeat, then switch sides.
tips: Keep the plate from swinging.
Squeeze your shoulder blade at the top.
ex_TVAVLM.description: Plate Pinch Grip Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Forearms, Rear Shoulders.

ex_NKOK6S.name: Prone Bench Row Barbell Pronated Grip
instructions: Lie chest-first on an incline bench, holding a barbell with a pronate grip (palms facing down) and your hands placed shoulder-width apart. Extend your arms straight down towards the floor.
Pull the barbell towards your upper abdomen by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement, ensuring the barbell reaches close to the bench.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position with control, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on pulling with your back muscles rather than your arms.
Exhale as you pull the barbell up and inhale as you lower it.
Use a weight that allows you to maintain proper form throughout the exercise.
ex_NKOK6S.description: Prone Bench Row Barbell Pronated Grip is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Shoulders.

ex_XPXPJN.name: Prone Bench Row Barbell Reverse Grip
instructions: Lie chest-first on an incline bench, holding a barbell with a reverse grip (palms facing up) and your hands placed shoulder-width apart. Extend your arms straight down towards the floor.
Pull the barbell towards your abdomen by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement, ensuring the barbell reaches close to the bench.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position with control, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on pulling with your back muscles rather than your arms.
Exhale as you pull the barbell up and inhale as you lower it.
Keep your elbows close to your body to maximize back muscle engagement.
ex_XPXPJN.description: Prone Bench Row Barbell Reverse Grip is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Shoulders.

ex_ZTLQTU.name: Prone Bench Row Dumbbells Pronated Grip
instructions: Lie chest-first on an incline bench, holding a dumbbell in each hand with a reverse grip (palms facing down), and your arms extended straight down towards the floor.
Pull the dumbbells towards your abdomen by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement, ensuring the dumbbells reach the sides of your torso.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on pulling with your back muscles rather than your arms.
Exhale as you pull the dumbbells up and inhale as you lower them.
Use a weight that allows you to maintain proper form throughout the exercise.
ex_ZTLQTU.description: Prone Bench Row Dumbbells Pronated Grip is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Shoulders.

ex_C2277G.name: Prone Bench Row Dumbbells Supinated Grip
instructions: Lie chest-first on an incline bench, holding a dumbbell in each hand with a supinate grip (palms facing up), and your arms extended straight down towards the floor.
Pull the dumbbells towards your abdomen by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement, ensuring the dumbbells reach the sides of your torso.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on pulling with your back muscles rather than your arms.
Exhale as you pull the dumbbells up and inhale as you lower them.
Use a weight that allows you to maintain proper form throughout the exercise.
ex_C2277G.description: Prone Bench Row Dumbbells Supinated Grip is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Shoulders.

ex_U6J6WY.name: Prone Bench Row Dumbbells
instructions: Lie chest-first on an incline bench, holding a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip (palms facing each other), and your arms extended straight down towards the floor.
Pull the dumbbells towards your abdomen by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement, ensuring the dumbbells reach the sides of your torso.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on pulling with your back muscles rather than your arms.
Exhale as you pull the dumbbells up and inhale as you lower them.
Use a weight that allows you to maintain proper form throughout the exercise.
ex_U6J6WY.description: Prone Bench Row Dumbbells is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Shoulders.

ex_UPWQ2O.name: Pull Up Normal Grip
instructions: Stand beneath a pull-up bar and grasp it with an overhand grip (palms facing away from you), hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Engage your back muscles and pull yourself up towards the bar by bending your elbows.
Continue pulling until your chin is above the bar, focusing on contracting your back muscles.
Lower yourself back to the starting position in a controlled manner, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Use a full range of motion, fully extending your arms at the bottom and pulling up until your chin is above the bar.
Focus on engaging your back muscles, particularly the latissimus dorsi, to perform the pull-up effectively.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you pull up and inhaling as you lower yourself down.
Avoid using momentum to swing your body; maintain a controlled movement throughout the exercise.
Perform the exercise on a stable, secure pull-up bar to ensure safety.
ex_UPWQ2O.description: Pull Up Normal Grip is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.

ex_D3NEEI.name: Pull Up Wide Grip (Front View)
instructions: Stand beneath a pull-up bar and grasp it with an overhand grip (palms facing away from you), hands wider than shoulder-width apart.
Engage your back muscles to pull yourself up towards the bar by bending your elbows.
Continue pulling until your chin is above the bar, focusing on contracting your back muscles.
Lower yourself back to the starting position in a controlled manner, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Use a full range of motion, fully extending your arms at the bottom and pulling up until your chin is above the bar.
Focus on engaging your back muscles, particularly the latissimus dorsi, to perform the pull-up effectively.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you pull up and inhaling as you lower yourself down.
Avoid using momentum to swing your body; maintain a controlled movement throughout the exercise.
Perform the exercise on a stable, secure pull-up bar to ensure safety.
ex_D3NEEI.description: Pull Up Wide Grip (Front View) is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.

ex_R7DQBA.name: Push Pull Chair Over Head Pull
instructions: Sit tall on the machine chair, or a cable seat, and take the overhead handles with your arms extended.
Brace your core and keep your chest up.
Pull the handles down toward your shoulders by driving your elbows down and back.
Return the handles overhead with control and repeat.
tips: Lead with your elbows, not your hands.
Avoid leaning back to finish the rep.
ex_R7DQBA.description: Push Pull Chair Over Head Pull is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Upper Back, Rear Shoulders.

ex_YSXKKX.name: Resistance Band - Cable Row
instructions: Attach a resistance band to a sturdy anchor point at chest height. Kneel on one knee with the opposite leg forward, foot flat on the ground.
Hold the band handles with both hands, arms extended forward, and palms facing down.
Pull the band handles towards your chest by bending your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together at the end of the movement.
Return to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired repetitions.
tips: Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together at the peak of the row to maximize back activation.
Adjust the resistance band tension or your kneeling position for an appropriate challenge.
Avoid shrugging your shoulders; keep them down and relaxed.
ex_YSXKKX.description: Resistance Band - Cable Row is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Biceps.

ex_VLPTFC.name: Resistance Band Cross Body Single Straight Arm Supinated Pulldown
instructions: Attach the resistance band to a high anchor point in front of you, on your left side. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handle with your right hand, palm facing up.
Extend your right arm straight opposite the left side of your head, keeping your arm straight.
Pull the handle down across your body towards your right hip until fully extended by your side and slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other side.
tips: Exhale as you pull the band down and inhale as you release it back up.
Focus on pulling with your back muscles rather than your arm for better engagement.
Ensure your hips stay square and stable, avoiding any twisting motion.
ex_VLPTFC.description: Resistance Band Cross Body Single Straight Arm Supinated Pulldown is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.

ex_QLD2NH.name: Resistance Band Floor Hyperextension
instructions: Lie face down on the floor with a loop resistance band over your ankles and another loop resistance band over your forearms. Extend your arms forward and keep your legs straight.
Engage your core and glutes, and lift your chest and legs off the floor simultaneously, spreading your legs apart against the resistance of the band.
Squeeze your lower back muscles at the top of the movement, keeping your arms and legs straight.
Slowly lower your chest and legs back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your neck in a neutral position to avoid straining it.
Focus on engaging your lower back and glute muscles throughout the movement.
Exhale as you lift your chest and legs and inhale as you lower them back down.
ex_QLD2NH.description: Resistance Band Floor Hyperextension is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Shoulders.

ex_XDCLOS.name: Resistance Band Kneeling Cross Body Single Straight Arm Supinated Pulldown
instructions: Attach the resistance band to a high anchor point in front of you, on your left side. Kneel on the floor on your right knee and your left foot flat on the floor, holding the handle with your right hand, palm facing up.
Extend your right arm straight opposite the left side of your head, keeping your arm straight.
Pull the handle down across your body towards your right hip until fully extended by your side and slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other side.
tips: Exhale as you pull the band down and inhale as you release it back up.
Focus on pulling with your back muscles rather than your arm for better engagement.
Ensure your hips stay square and stable, avoiding any twisting motion.
ex_XDCLOS.description: Resistance Band Kneeling Cross Body Single Straight Arm Supinated Pulldown is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.

ex_PQHOBE.name: Resistance Band Lying Hyperextension Abduction
instructions: Lie face down on the floor with your arms crossed under your head, resting your forehead on your arms. Place a loop resistance band around your thighs, just above your knees. Keep your legs extended and feet together.
Engage your core and glutes to lift your legs straight off the floor while resting your head on your arms.
While lifting your legs, spread them wide apart against the band's resistance, keeping your legs straight.
Slowly bring your legs back together while lowering them to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired repetitions.
tips: Focus on engaging your glutes and hip abductors throughout the movement.
Exhale as you lift and open your legs, and inhale as you bring them back together and lower them.
Keep your core engaged throughout the exercise to maintain stability and protect your lower back.
ex_PQHOBE.description: Resistance Band Lying Hyperextension Abduction is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Core.

ex_2ICQ6F.name: Reverse Grip Lat Pull Down
instructions: Sit at a lat pulldown machine with your feet flat on the floor and knees secured under the pads. Grasp the bar with an underhand grip (palms facing you) at shoulder-width apart, arms fully extended above you.
Engage your core and keep your back straight. Lean back slightly to create a natural arch in your lower back.
Pull the bar towards your upper chest, bringing your elbows down to your sides while squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Slowly return the bar to the starting position with control, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you pull the bar down and inhale as you return it to the starting position.
Avoid using momentum or swinging your body to lift the weight.
Keep your wrists straight and avoid letting them bend backward.
ex_2ICQ6F.description: Reverse Grip Lat Pull Down is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Forearms.

ex_YOLNXY.name: Seated Cable Row v Bar Machine
instructions: Sit on the cable row machine with your feet secure on the foot platform. Grasp the V bar with both hands.
Sit upright with your back straight, extending your arms fully in front of you.
Pull the V bar towards your abdomen by bringing your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Slowly extend your arms back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired repetitions.
tips: Keep your back straight throughout the exercise to avoid strain.
Engage your core to maintain stability and proper posture.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and reduce the risk of injury.
ex_YOLNXY.description: Seated Cable Row v Bar Machine is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Shoulders, Biceps.

ex_S77EWV.name: Seated Normal Grip Row Machine
instructions: Sit on a bench facing a row machine with a straight back and your feet placed on the footrests.
Hold the rod above your knees with an overhand grip of your hands while keeping your arms straight.
Pull the cable towards your chest by bending your arms and taking your elbows past your back.
Return to the initial position and repeat.
ex_S77EWV.description: Seated Normal Grip Row Machine is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Rear Shoulders.

ex_X53SCA.name: Seated Resistance Band - Cable Rows
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs fully extended and feet together, anchoring the resistance band around the soles of your feet. Hold the handles with both hands, arms extended forward, palms facing each other.
Keep your back straight, chest up, and core engaged to stabilize your body.
Pull the handles towards your torso by bending your elbows, keeping your arms close to your body. Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together at the peak of the movement.
Slowly extend your arms back to the starting position, maintaining control over the resistance band. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back straight and avoid slouching to maintain proper form.
Engage your core to prevent any rocking or unnecessary movement during the exercise.
Use a controlled motion to pull and release the resistance band, avoiding jerking movements.
ex_X53SCA.description: Seated Resistance Band - Cable Rows is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Biceps, Core.

ex_XDMKWD.name: Seated Row Machine Rows
instructions: Sit on the machine with your chest against the pad, or your feet on the platform, and grab the handles.
Sit tall with your shoulders down and arms extended.
Pull the handles toward your torso, driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Return the handles with control until your arms are straight and repeat.

ex_HZIWID.name: Arm Double Crossover

instructions: Stand tall with your back straight and feet shoulder-width apart.

ex_NMDP23.name: Arm Pulses
instructions: Stand tall with your back straight and feet shoulder-width apart.

ex_YV3UTR.name: Arms Lateral Raise and Rotation Up
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder width apart, arms at your sides, and a slight bend in your elbows.
Raise your arms laterally until they reach shoulder height while rotating your shoulders so your palms face upward (supinated).
Rotate your arms at the shoulder joint so that your palms face down.

ex_UJNEDE.name: Arms Up and Down
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart. Extend your right arm straight up overhead and your left arm straight down by your side.
Simultaneously lower your right arm while raising your left arm, keeping both arms straight, until your right arm is down by your side and your left arm is overhead.

instructions: Sit on the Assault AirBike's seat and adjust it to a comfortable height. Place your feet on the pedals and your hands on the handles.
Begin pedaling at a moderate pace. Simultaneously, push and pull the handles back and forth in a coordinated motion with your legs.
Gradually increase your pedaling speed and the intensity of your arm movements to achieve a fast pace.

instructions: Sit on the seat of the Assault AirBike and adjust it to a comfortable height. Place your feet on the pedals and your hands on the handles.
Begin pedaling at a steady, moderate pace. Simultaneously, push and pull the handles back and forth in a coordinated motion with your legs.

ex_2OHCJX.name: Back Lever
instructions: Start by hanging on a bar with your arms extended overhead, hands placed shoulder-width apart, and your palms facing forward.
Pull yourself up until your head is facing the floor and your legs are overhead.
Pass your legs under the bar and align your body in a straight line from head to toe and parallel to the floor.
Hold this position for a suitable duration.
tips: Focus on engaging your core and glutes to maintain a straight line from head to heels.
Ensure your grip on the bar is firm and secure to provide stability and prevent slipping.
Breathe steadily and evenly to help maintain the hold and reduce tension.
ex_2OHCJX.description: Back Lever is an advanced multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Arms.

ex_DJP3OC.name: Balance Board Lateral Squat
instructions: Stand on the balance board with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Shift your weight to one side and bend at the knees and hips to perform a squat, keeping your core engaged to maintain balance.
Return to the starting position and shift your weight to the other side, performing a squat on the opposite side.
Continue alternating sides in a controlled, rhythmic manner.
tips: Keep your knees aligned with your toes to prevent strain on your joints.
Engage your core muscles to maintain stability and support your lower back.
Focus on a point in front of you to help maintain balance and control.
ex_DJP3OC.description: Balance Board Lateral Squat is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the balance category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

ex_DRYKLS.name: Ball Slams
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart while holding a medicine ball with both hands over your head.
Forcefully slam the ball straight into the ground, while pulling your hips back and bending your knees.
Retrieve the ball from the ground, return to the starting position and repeat with controlled, powerful repetitions.
tips: Engage your core before initiating each slam.Generate power from your hips and legs rather than using only your arms.
Keep your back neutral and avoid rounding your spine during the slam.
Perform each repetition with maximum power while maintaining proper technique.

ex_DRYKLS.description: Ball Slams is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a stability ball, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Chest, Hamstrings.

ex_6JZVPR.name: Band Squat Row
instructions: Securely loop a resistance band around a sturdy anchor point, at the hip level. Standing with legs at shoulder width, grip the other end of the resistance band palms facing down.
Begin the exercise in a squat position, keeping your chest up and your arms fully extended in front of you.
Stand up explosively, while pulling the band with your arms toward your torso, bringing your elbows to your sides.
Lower your body to a squat position, extending your arms forward. Repeat the movement for the desired amount of repetitions.
tips: Keep your torso upright and avoid rounding your lower back or leaning forward during the movement.
Drive through the heels of your feet, focusing on your quads and glutes.
Keep your elbows tucked in when pulling the band near your torso, avoid flaring your elbows.
Exhale during the explosive part of the movement, inhale while slowly returning to the starting position.
ex_6JZVPR.description: Band Squat Row is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Shoulders, Hamstrings.

ex_F6PPB4.name: Barbell Jump Shrug
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, bend at your hips and knees to grip the barbell with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Hold the barbell against your thighs.
Begin the exercise by hinging at the hips, lowering the barbell to knee level, then explosively extend your hips and knees and lightly jump off the floor, while shrugging your shoulders.
Allow the barbell to rise naturally from the momentum without pulling it with your arms.
Land softly with your knees slightly bent, absorb the impact, and reset before performing the next repetition.
tips: Keep your arms straight throughout the entire movement.
Generate power from your hips and legs rather than your shoulders.
Maintain a neutral spine, keep your chest up and brace your core before each repetition.
Exhale during the explosive jump and inhale as you reset.
ex_F6PPB4.description: Barbell Jump Shrug is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the traps (back). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Forearms, Core.

ex_EVQXXG.name: Basketball Shot Jump
instructions: Start in a squat position with your feet shoulder-width apart and your hands mimicking holding a basketball.

ex_EVQXXG.description: Basketball Shot Jump is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Hamstrings.

ex_FZAE32.name: Battle Rope Alternating Arm Waves
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and hold the ends of the battle ropes with a neutral grip. Lean your torso forward, bend your knees slightly and brace your core.

ex_AYIHPX.name: Battle Rope Double Arm Slams

ex_THT2K6.name: Bear Crawls
instructions: Start on all fours with your hands under your shoulders, your knees under your hips, and your knees slightly off the floor.
Move one hand and the opposite foot forward at the same time while keeping your hips level.

ex_ZXMIBV.name: Bent Over Twist

Bend forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and your knees slightly bent, until your torso is parallel to the floor.
Twist your torso to one side, bringing one end of the bar towards the ceiling.

ex_FK7SLZ.name: Body Slide

ex_X2KDDW.name: Bodyweight Knee Thrust
