instructions: Stand in a boxing stance with your feet shoulder-width apart, left foot forward, and hands up in a guard position near your chin.
Rotate your hips and shoulders, extending your right arm forward in a straight line to throw a cross.
Quickly retract your right arm back to the guard position.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your non-punching hand up to protect your face and maintain a balanced stance.
Engage your core to generate power and maintain stability.
Rotate your back foot and hips to add power to the cross.
ex_VR3EMX.description: Boxing Right Cross is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Upper Back.

ex_5WOVZW.name: Boxing Right Hook
instructions: Stand in a boxing stance with your feet shoulder-width apart, left foot forward, and hands up in a guard position near your chin.
Rotate your hips and shoulders, bringing your right arm in a horizontal arc to throw a hook.
Quickly retract your right arm back to the guard position.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your non-punching hand up to protect your face and maintain a balanced stance.
Engage your core to generate power and maintain stability.
Focus on rotating your hips and shoulders to add power to the hook.
ex_5WOVZW.description: Boxing Right Hook is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Upper Back.

ex_AFSWAS.name: Boxing Right Uppercut
instructions: Stand in a boxing stance with your feet shoulder-width apart, left foot forward, and hands up in a guard position near your chin.
Bend your knees slightly and rotate your hips and shoulders, bringing your right fist upward in a rising arc to throw an uppercut.
Quickly retract your right arm back to the guard position.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your non-punching hand up to protect your face and maintain a balanced stance.
Engage your core to generate power and maintain stability.
Focus on driving the punch from your legs and hips to add power to the uppercut.
ex_AFSWAS.description: Boxing Right Uppercut is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Upper Back.

ex_BXUN5B.name: Brisk Walking (360 Degree View)
instructions: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart and your arms relaxed by your sides.
Begin walking at a brisk pace, ensuring that you take quick, short steps.
Swing your arms naturally with each step, allowing them to move opposite to your legs for balance.
Maintain this brisk pace for the desired duration or distance.
tips: Keep your core engaged to maintain good posture and stability.
Focus on a heel-to-toe motion with each step to ensure proper walking mechanics.
Breathe steadily and rhythmically to support your pace and endurance.
ex_BXUN5B.description: Brisk Walking (360 Degree View) is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Hip Flexors.

ex_3IUL7E.name: Brisk Walking (45 Degree View)
instructions: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart and your arms relaxed by your sides.
Begin walking at a brisk pace, ensuring that you take quick, short steps.
Swing your arms naturally with each step, allowing them to move opposite to your legs for balance.
Maintain this brisk pace for the desired duration or distance.
tips: Keep your core engaged to maintain good posture and stability.
Focus on a heel-to-toe motion with each step to ensure proper walking mechanics.
Breathe steadily and rhythmically to support your pace and endurance.
ex_3IUL7E.description: Brisk Walking (45 Degree View) is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Hip Flexors.

ex_6HNXZ6.name: Burpee To Pull-Up
instructions: Stand under a pull-up bar.
Squat down, place your hands on the floor and jump your feet back into a plank, then jump them back in.
Jump up to grab the bar and pull your chin over it.
Lower yourself, drop down and go straight into the next burpee.
tips: Land softly from the jump before the pull-up.
Use a band on the bar if the pull-up is too hard.
ex_6HNXZ6.description: Burpee To Pull-Up is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Quadriceps, Biceps.

ex_KZNF47.name: Burpees
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Squat down and place your hands on the floor in front of your feet.
Jump your feet back into a plank, then jump them back in toward your hands.
Explode up into a jump, reaching your arms overhead, and land softly into the next rep.
tips: Keep your core tight in the plank so your hips don't sag.
Step back instead of jumping to make it easier.
ex_KZNF47.description: Burpees is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Chest, Shoulders.

ex_3CJYM3.name: Butt Kick With Row
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms extended in front of you, palms facing down.
Bend your right knee to bring your heel towards your buttocks while simultaneously pulling your elbows back to perform a rowing motion.
Return to the starting position and repeat the movement with your left leg, bringing your left heel towards your buttocks while pulling your elbows back.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions or duration.
tips: Keep your upper body upright to maintain proper form and avoid leaning forward.
Perform the rowing motion with controlled movements, squeezing your shoulder blades together as you pull your elbows back.
Ensure each butt kick is high enough to effectively engage the hamstrings.
ex_3CJYM3.description: Butt Kick With Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Calves, Shoulders.

ex_OAA5CB.name: Butt Kick (Slow)
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms relaxed by your sides.
Begin by jogging in place, lifting your heels towards your buttocks with each step.

Alternate lifting your right and left heels in a quick, continuous motion, keeping your knees pointing down. Swing your arms naturally with each step, allowing them to move opposite to your legs for balance.
Maintain a steady pace for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your upper body upright and avoid leaning forward to maintain proper form.
Engage your core to support balance and stability throughout the exercise.
Focus on a quick, light motion with each heel lift to effectively engage your hamstrings.
ex_OAA5CB.description: Butt Kick (Slow) is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Glutes.

ex_HUKEPY.name: Butt Kick
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms relaxed by your sides.
Begin by jogging in place, lifting your heels towards your buttocks with each step.

Alternate lifting your right and left heels in a quick, continuous motion, keeping your knees pointing down. Swing your arms naturally with each step, allowing them to move opposite to your legs for balance.
Maintain a steady pace for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your upper body upright and avoid leaning forward to maintain proper form.
Engage your core to support balance and stability throughout the exercise.
Focus on a quick, light motion with each heel lift to effectively engage your hamstrings.
ex_HUKEPY.description: Butt Kick is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Glutes.

ex_A64QEB.name: Cable Twisting Overhead Press
instructions: Stand sideways to the cable machine with your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, knees bent at almost 90 degrees and hips pushed back.
Grasp the handle, attached at hip height, with the hand closest to the machine, keeping it close to your shoulder. Place your other hand on your hip.
Twist your torso away from the machine while pushing the handle sideways and straight across your torso, straightening your legs to a standing position as you press the handle.
Slowly return to the starting semi-squat position with control, bringing the handle back to your shoulder. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
tips: Use a lighter weight to ensure proper form and gradually increase the resistance as you get stronger.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and reduce injury risk.
Exhale as you twist and press the handle across your torso, and inhale as you return to the starting position.
ex_A64QEB.description: Cable Twisting Overhead Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Triceps, Legs.

ex_RKQTGI.name: Cardio Lunge
instructions: Begin in a lunge position with your right leg forward and left leg back, ensuring your right knee is aligned over your ankle and your left knee is just above the floor. Bend both arms at your sides.
Explosively push off your left foot, bringing it forward in a small step while pushing your right leg slightly backwards.
Immediately return your left foot back to the starting lunge position.
Continue the explosive movement, maintaining a steady, rhythmic pace. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions or duration, then switch legs.
tips: Ensure your front knee stays aligned with your toes to avoid putting unnecessary strain on your knee.
Perform the movement with a controlled pace to maximize cardiovascular benefits and prevent injury.
Use your arms to help balance and stabilize your movements.
Focus on the explosive movement of the back leg to engage your glutes and hamstrings.
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, inhaling as you bring your leg forward and exhaling as you return to the lunge position.
ex_RKQTGI.description: Cardio Lunge is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

ex_5SK25O.name: Celebratory Hip Thrust
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms extended straight up in the air.
Simultaneously bend your elbows and thrust your arms downwards to your hips while thrusting your hips forward.
Return to the initial position with your arms extended overhead and your hips back in the starting position.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Perform the movement with a controlled pace, focusing on the coordinated motion of your arms and hips.
Use the downward thrust of your arms to help generate momentum for the hip thrust.
Keep your feet firmly planted on the floor to maintain stability.
ex_5SK25O.description: Celebratory Hip Thrust is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

ex_6TIMF5.name: Chest Fly Side Step
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart, arms bent at 90 degrees, and your elbows open wide at shoulder height.
Step your right foot out to the side, bending your right knee slightly as you bring your elbows together in front of you until they are close together and back.
Return to the starting position by stepping your left foot out to the side while repeating the fly motion with your arms.
Repeat the movement alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Ensure your arms remain bent at the elbows throughout the chest fly motion.
Focus on squeezing your chest muscles as you bring your elbows together in front of you.
ex_6TIMF5.description: Chest Fly Side Step is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.

ex_5FF6V4.name: Chest Pull Back
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart and leaning slightly forward at the hips. Bend your arms in front of your chest with your palms facing each other, lightly squeezing to activate your chest.
Perform a rowing motion with your right arm by pulling it back, bending your elbow, and squeezing your shoulder blade towards your spine.
Return your right arm to the starting position, keeping your left arm steady and engaged in front of your chest.
Repeat the rowing motion for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on squeezing your shoulder blade towards your spine to maximize the engagement of you back muscles.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to avoid using momentum and to ensure proper muscle activation.
Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears to avoid unnecessary strain.
Ensure your chest remains open and engaged by maintaining light tension between your palms.
ex_5FF6V4.description: Chest Pull Back is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Biceps.

ex_2B5QFV.name: Chest Raise and Rotate
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart, arms bent at 90 degrees, with forearms parallel to the floor, elbows squeezed to the sides.
Perform a semi-circular motion by rotating your arms upwards and outwards until your forearms are vertical to the floor and your upper arms are at shoulder level.
Reverse the motion, bringing your arms back to the starting position with your forearms parallel to the floor.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on maintaining a 90-degree bend in your elbows throughout the exercise to ensure proper form.
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, inhaling as you lift your arms and exhaling as you lower them.
Maintain a slight bend in your knees to support your lower back and enhance balance.
ex_2B5QFV.description: Chest Raise and Rotate is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Biceps.

ex_NS5NI5.name: Circle Elbow Arm
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart. Extend your arms out to the sides at shoulder level, keeping them straight.
Bend your arms at the elbows, bringing your fingers to touch your shoulders on the same side, keeping your elbows pointing outwards.
Begin to make small circular motions with your elbows, moving them forward, up, back, and down in a controlled manner.
Continue circling your elbows for the desired number of repetitions, then reverse the direction of the circles and repeat.
tips: Focus on making smooth and controlled movements to maximize muscle activation and avoid straining your joints.
Perform the movement slowly to maintain control and improve shoulder mobility.
Ensure your shoulders remain down and away from your ears to avoid unnecessary strain.
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, maintaining a consistent rhythm.
ex_NS5NI5.description: Circle Elbow Arm is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms, Chest.

ex_CP7APK.name: Clap Jack
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet together and your arms extended by your sides at shoulder level.
Simultaneously jump your feet out to the sides to a wide stance while bringing your arms straight in front of you and clapping your hands together at chest level.
Jump your feet back together and bring your arms back to your sides to return to the starting position.
Repeat the movement continuously for the desired number of repetitions or duration.
tips: Ensure your knees are slightly bent during the jumps to absorb impact and protect your joints.
Breathe rhythmically throughout the exercise, exhaling as you jump out and clap, and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
Focus on maintaining a consistent rhythm and avoiding excessive arm or leg movements to maximize efficiency.
ex_CP7APK.description: Clap Jack is an advanced multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Hamstrings.

ex_PCKGXC.name: Control Balance
instructions: Lie down on your back, raise your legs towards the head, and hold your feet by extending your arms overhead.
Release your right leg and take it upward until it becomes vertical to the floor.
Place your free hand on your left calf and maintain balance.
Hold for a while, return to the starting position, and repeat.
tips: Perform the movement with control, especially when lifting and lowering your legs, to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Ensure your shoulders remain on the floor and avoid straining your neck.
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you lift your leg and inhaling as you lower it.
Use a mat or soft surface to support your back and prevent discomfort during the exercise.
ex_PCKGXC.description: Control Balance is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the balance category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Hamstrings.

ex_CWRVQD.name: Corner Touch
instructions: Begin standing with your body turned to the left side in a semi-lunge position, your left leg bent, and your right leg extended behind you lightly bent. Extend your right arm upward and your left arm downward to your side.

Engage your core and rotate your body on your feet, turning to face the opposite side. As you rotate, lower your right arm and raise your left arm, so that your left arm is now upward and your right arm is downward to your side.
Repeat the movement, alternating sides, and performing the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on using a controlled motion when rotating your body to avoid straining your back.
Ensure you stay in place as you rotate, using a controlled motion to maintain balance and stability.
Ensure your movements are smooth and deliberate to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you rotate and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
ex_CWRVQD.description: Corner Touch is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Core, Lower Back.

ex_YV4NND.name: Crawl With Sled Drag
instructions: Attach a light sled to a harness or belt around your waist.
Get on your hands and feet in a bear-crawl position with your knees just off the floor.
Crawl forward, moving opposite hand and foot together, dragging the sled behind you.
Continue for the set distance with your back flat.
tips: Keep your hips level and low.
Take small, controlled steps.
ex_YV4NND.description: Crawl With Sled Drag is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a sled machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Glutes, Triceps.

ex_3QWVXL.name: Criss Cross Arms Lift
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms extended straight in front of you at your hip height, palms facing inwards.
Cross your right arm over your left arm at the wrists and then cross your left arm over your right arm.
Repeat the crossing movement until your hands are opposite your head.
Lower your arms back to your hip level by crossing them down.
tips: Focus on using your shoulder muscles to lift and lower your arms, maintaining a controlled motion throughout.
Perform the movement with control to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Ensure your shoulders remain down and away from your ears to avoid unnecessary strain.
ex_3QWVXL.description: Criss Cross Arms Lift is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Core.

ex_LALP4M.name: Criss Cross Elbow to Knee
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart and your hands placed behind your head, elbows pointing out to the sides.
Engage your quadriceps and perform a light jump, crossing your legs in mid-air, and land with your feet crossed and immediately lightly jump back to the starting position.
Lift your right knee towards your left elbow while twisting your torso to bring your left elbow towards your right knee.

Return to the starting position, perform another light jump crossing your legs, and repeat the movement on the opposite side by lifting your left knee towards your right elbow. Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on using your abdominal muscles to twist your torso and lift your knee, maintaining a controlled motion throughout.
Perform the movement with control, especially during the jumps and twists, to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you twist and lift your knee and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
ex_LALP4M.description: Criss Cross Elbow to Knee is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Shoulders.

ex_PEQC7X.name: Criss Cross Jack
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet wide apart and your arms extended straight out to the sides at shoulder level.
Engage your quadriceps and perform a light jump, crossing your legs in mid-air while simultaneously bringing both arms straight in front of your chest.
Land with your legs crossed and your arms in front of your chest.
Immediately jump again to return to the starting position with your feet wide apart and your arms extended to the sides at shoulder level. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on using your leg, chest and shoulder muscles to perform the jumps and crosses, maintaining a controlled motion throughout.
Perform the movement with control, especially during the jumps, to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you cross your legs and arms and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
ex_PEQC7X.description: Criss Cross Jack is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abdominals, Glutes.

ex_MTCH6P.name: Criss Cross Jump
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet wide apart and your arms bent out to the sides at shoulder level and hands facing each other.
Engage your quadriceps and perform a light jump, crossing your legs in mid-air while simultaneously crossing both arms in front of your chest.
Land with your legs crossed and your arms in front of your chest.

Immediately jump again to return to the starting position with your feet wide apart and your arms bent out to the sides at shoulder level and hands facing each other. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on using your leg, chest and arm muscles to perform the jumps and crosses, maintaining a controlled motion throughout.
Perform the movement with control, especially during the jumps, to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Ensure your shoulders remain down and away from your ears to avoid unnecessary strain.
ex_MTCH6P.description: Criss Cross Jump is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Abdominals, Glutes.

ex_UWAA37.name: Decline Shoulder Tap
instructions: Begin by placing your feet on a bench and positioning your hands on the floor shoulder-width apart. Your body should be in a decline position with your feet elevated.
Engage your core and ensure your body forms a straight line from your head to your heels.
Lift your right hand off the floor and tap your left shoulder, lightly rotate your hips according to the tap side.
Return your right hand to the floor and repeat the movement with your left hand, tapping your right shoulder. Continue alternating for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your core engaged throughout the exercise to maintain a straight body line and avoid sagging your hips.
Avoid letting your shoulders sag; keep them stable and aligned with your hands.
Use a stable bench to prevent any movement or slipping during the exercise.
ex_UWAA37.description: Decline Shoulder Tap is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Core.

ex_WTHMVM.name: Diagonal Opens
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, arms bent at the elbows, elbows facing outwards, and hands close to your chest.
Slide your right hand over your left forearm, both arms in an opposite diagonal direction while keeping the elbows bent.
Return your hands to the starting position and repeat the movement by sliding your left hand over your right forearm, extending in the opposite diagonal direction.
tips: Ensure your movements are smooth and controlled to maintain tension and focus on muscle engagement.
Focus on maintaining a rhythmic breathing pattern, inhaling as you extend and exhaling as you return to the start position.
Maintain a slight tension in your core throughout the exercise to help stabilize your upper body.
ex_WTHMVM.description: Diagonal Opens is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Arms.

ex_BO7WV2.name: Diagonal Punch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, and hands in a guard position near your face.
Rotate your torso to the right, and extend your right arm in a diagonal punch across your body.
Return your right hand to the starting position as you rotate your torso back to center.
Repeat the motion with your left arm, rotating your torso to the left to execute a diagonal punch across your body.
tips: Keep your hands up and elbows slightly bent when not punching to protect your face and maintain balance.
Rotate your hips and shoulders fully with each punch to maximize power and engage your core muscles.
Practice the punches slowly at first to ensure proper technique before increasing speed and power.
Exhale sharply with each punch to increase force and stabilize your core.
ex_BO7WV2.description: Diagonal Punch is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Arms.

ex_WBQWX5.name: Double Kettlebell Sled Push
instructions: Place two kettlebells on the sled and grip the sled handles.
Lean into the sled at about 45 degrees with your arms extended.
Drive forward with powerful steps through the balls of your feet.
Keep pushing for the set distance.
tips: Brace your core and keep your back flat.
Drive your knees forward.
ex_WBQWX5.description: Double Kettlebell Sled Push is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a sled machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Hamstrings, Shoulders.

ex_F2CVCZ.name: Double Knee Drive
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, both arms bent and raised by your sides.
Lift your right knee towards your chest while rotating your torso to the right, bringing your left elbow to touch your right knee twice.
Lower your right leg back to the starting position and return your torso to face forward.

Repeat the movement on the opposite side by lifting your left knee towards your chest, rotating your torso to the left, and bringing your right elbow to touch your left knee twice. Continue alternating sides.
tips: Keep your upper body upright and avoid leaning too far forward or backward to maintain balance and proper form.
Engage your core muscles to stabilize your body and enhance the rotational movement.
Focus on a steady, rhythmic breathing pattern, exhaling as you bring your knee and elbow together.
ex_F2CVCZ.description: Double Knee Drive is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Obliques.

ex_HBM44T.name: Double Punch Front Leg Lift
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your hands in fists near your sides with closed fists.
Simultaneously punch forward with both arms while lifting your right leg slightly bent at the knee to about waist height.
Return your arms and right leg to the starting position.
Immediately repeat the movement, this time lifting your left leg while simultaneously punching forward with both arms. Continue alternating leg lifts with each set of punches.
tips: Ensure your punches are strong and controlled, extending fully without locking your elbows.
Maintain a slight bend in the lifted leg to reduce strain and enhance control during the movement.
Focus on a steady, rhythmic breathing pattern, exhaling as you punch and lift your leg, and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
ex_HBM44T.description: Double Punch Front Leg Lift is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Arms.

ex_C7DMDE.name: Downward Dog Sprint
instructions: Begin with your hands shoulder width apart and your feet hip width apart. Walk your feet backward until your body forms an inverted V shape with your hips lifted toward the ceiling.
Keeping your hands firmly planted, flex one knee lifting your foot off the floor while the opposite leg remains extended.
Return your foot to the starting position, then immediately drive the opposite leg in the same way.
Continue alternating legs in a smooth, controlled sprinting motion while keeping your hips elevated and your upper body stable.
tips: Lift each knee toward your chest without rounding your upper back.
Maintain your hips high throughout the exercise instead of shifting into a plank position.
Engage your core to minimize movement through your torso.
Inhale as you return your foot to the floor and exhale as you drive your knee forward.
ex_C7DMDE.description: Downward Dog Sprint is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Triceps, Hamstrings.

ex_NPKUP7.name: Dumbbell Curl Press Extend
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder width apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand by your sides using an underhand grip.
Curl both dumbbells while keeping your elbows close to your sides and your upper arms still.
Press the dumbbells overhead, then bend your elbows to lower the dumbbells behind your head. Extend your elbows to raise them overhead again.
Lower the dumbbells to shoulder height, then slowly extend your elbows to return them to your sides and repeat.
tips: Keep your elbows close to your torso during the curl, and upper arms beside your head and as still as possible during the triceps extension.
Use a manageable weight that allows smooth transitions between every part of the exercise.
Press the dumbbells directly overhead without leaning backward.
Exhale during the curl, press, and elbow extension, and inhale during each controlled lowering phase.
ex_NPKUP7.description: Dumbbell Curl Press Extend is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms, Upper Back, Core.

ex_MCQ62P.name: Dumbbell Iron Cross
instructions: Begin in a squat position with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand. Extend your arms in front of your chest, keeping the dumbbells close together and your palms facing each other.
Keep your back straight as you start to stand up. As you rise, simultaneously open your arms out to your sides, extending them at shoulder level, forming a "T" shape with your body.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring your arms are fully extended to the sides and parallel to the floor, with your palms facing forward.
Bring your arms back in front of your chest while returning to the squat position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Use a slow and controlled motion to maximize muscle engagement and prevent momentum from taking over.
Keep your wrists straight and aligned with your forearms throughout the movement.
Start with lighter weights to ensure proper form before progressing to heavier dumbbells.
ex_MCQ62P.description: Dumbbell Iron Cross is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_CDDGQB.name: Dumbbell Low Windmill
instructions: Stand with your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in your left hand. Extend your left arm down, and raise your right arm straight up overhead.

Engage your core and hinge at your hips, bending your left knee slightly while keeping your right leg straight. Lower the dumbbell toward your left foot, keeping your back flat and left arm extended upward.
Rotate your torso slightly to follow the movement of the dumbbell. Lower the dumbbell as close to the floor as you can while maintaining proper form.
Reverse the motion by pushing through your left foot and straightening your torso back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
tips: Ensure your back remains flat and avoid rounding your spine during the movement.
Maintain a slight bend in your left knee while keeping your right leg straight.
Focus on a controlled movement, avoiding any jerky or rapid motions.
ex_CDDGQB.description: Dumbbell Low Windmill is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Lower Back.

ex_QQCJ26.name: Dumbbell Pullover Hip Extension on Exercise Ball
instructions: Begin by lying with your back on an exercise ball, feet flat on the floor, and knees bent at 90 degrees. Hold a dumbbell with both hands, palms pressed against the underside of the plates, arms extended straight above your chest.
Lower your hips towards the floor by bending your knees, while simultaneously lowering the dumbbell in an arc over your head until your upper arms are in line with your torso.
Extend your hips back to the starting position by squeezing your glutes and lifting your hips, while simultaneously pulling the dumbbell back over your chest by contracting your chest and lats.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement to avoid joint strain.
Ensure your back is firmly supported on the exercise ball.
Avoid lowering the dumbbell too far behind your head to prevent shoulder strain.
ex_QQCJ26.description: Dumbbell Pullover Hip Extension on Exercise Ball is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

ex_YHIDTF.name: Dumbbell Single Arm Overhead Carry
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in your right hand. Press the dumbbell overhead until your arm is fully extended.
Walk forward in a straight line for the desired distance, keeping the dumbbell steady overhead.
Once you've covered the desired distance, carefully lower the dumbbell back to your shoulder and switch to your left hand. Repeat the movement with your left arm overhead.
tips: Maintain a steady and controlled pace while walking.
Ensure your arm is fully extended with your wrist straight.
Avoid leaning or tilting your torso to one side.
ex_YHIDTF.description: Dumbbell Single Arm Overhead Carry is an intermediate multi-joint compound loaded carry exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Core.

ex_DHL33Z.name: Dumbbell Swing
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and hold a dumbbell vertically with both hands between your legs, keeping your arms extended.
Push your hips backward and bend your knees as you swing the dumbbell between your legs while maintaining a straight back.
Drive your hips forward and straighten your legs to swing the dumbbell upward until your arms reach approximately shoulder height.
Allow the dumbbell to descend with control, hinge your hips backward as it passes between your legs, and continue for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Generate the upward movement by driving your hips forward rather than lifting primarily with your arms.
Keep your spine neutral and avoid rounding your back during the downward swing.
Control the dumbbell as it travels between your legs instead of allowing it to pull you forward.
Inhale as the dumbbell swings downward and exhale as you drive your hips forward.
ex_DHL33Z.description: Dumbbell Swing is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Lower Back, Core.

ex_TG2Y6Z.name: Dumbbell Burpee
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand. Lower the dumbbells to the floor as you squat down, placing them shoulder-width apart.
Jump your feet back into a plank position, keeping your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Jump your feet back towards the dumbbells, landing in a squat position. As you stand up, lift the dumbbells off the floor.
Jump up explosively, extending your arms overhead with the dumbbells. Land softly and immediately lower the dumbbells back to the floor to start the next repetition.
tips: Land softly on your feet to minimize impact on your joints.
Keep your feet hip-width apart for stability during the plank and jump phases.
Start with lighter weights to get comfortable with the movement, then gradually increase the weight.
ex_TG2Y6Z.description: Dumbbell Burpee is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Core, Chest, Triceps.

ex_ZE2EKK.name: Dynamic Leg Swing
instructions: Stand next to a wall or sturdy object, using your right hand to support yourself and left hand on your hip. Position your feet hip-width apart.
Swing your left leg forward and backward in a controlled, yet dynamic motion while lightly rotating your hips. Keep your leg straight but not locked at the knee.
Allow the movement to be fluid, swinging your leg as high forward and backward as your flexibility allows.
After completing the desired number of repetitions, switch sides and repeat the movement with your right leg while supporting yourself with your left hand.
tips: Keep the swinging leg straight, but avoid locking the knee to reduce strain on the joint.
Perform the swings in a controlled manner to maximize the stretch and avoid any sudden jerks.
Focus on smooth, fluid movements, gradually increasing the range of motion as your muscles warm up.
ex_ZE2EKK.description: Dynamic Leg Swing is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Glutes.

ex_FVBGYU.name: Elbow-Extension
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder width apart, your arms resting beside your body, and your palms facing forward.
Keep your upper arms close to your torso and bend both elbows until your forearms are approximately parallel to the floor with your palms facing up.
Contract your triceps and straighten both elbows, lowering your hands toward your sides while keeping your shoulders and upper arms still.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Move only through your elbows without swinging your shoulders.
Straighten your arms fully without forcefully locking your elbows.
Keep your upper arms close to your torso throughout the movement.
Exhale as you extend your elbows and inhale as you bend them.
ex_FVBGYU.description: Elbow-Extension is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Forearms.

ex_MWLS5R.name: Fast Feet
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, and your arms at your sides.
Quickly alternate lifting your feet off the floor, moving them up and down rapidly as if running in place, but without moving forward.
Keep your core engaged and maintain a slight bend in your knees to stay light on your feet.
Continue the rapid foot movement for the desired duration, maintaining a steady and controlled pace.
tips: Stay on your forefeet to maintain quick, light movements.
Use your arms for balance, allowing them to move naturally as your feet move.
Focus on quick, controlled movements to maximize speed and effectiveness.
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, inhaling through your nose and exhaling through your mouth.
ex_MWLS5R.description: Fast Feet is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Hip Flexors.

ex_YJBSVB.name: Front Lever Raise to Hold
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, your arms straight, and your legs together.
Engage your core and raise your legs and torso together until your body is parallel to the floor.
Keep your arms and legs straight as you hold the horizontal position.
Slowly lower your body back to the hanging position, then repeat.
tips: Keep your body straight from your shoulders to your feet.
Keep your elbows fully extended throughout the movement.
Avoid swinging or using momentum.
Exhale as you raise your body and inhale as you lower it.
ex_YJBSVB.description: Front Lever Raise to Hold is an advanced single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back, Hip Flexors.

ex_XP4LD4.name: Front Lever Raise
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, your arms straight, and your legs together.
Engage your core and raise your legs and torso together while keeping your body straight.
Continue lifting past horizontal until your feet rise above the bar.
Lower your body with control until you return to the hanging position, then repeat.
tips: Keep your arms straight throughout the movement.
Keep your core engaged during the lowering phase.
Avoid swinging or using momentum.
Exhale as you raise your body and inhale as you lower it.
ex_XP4LD4.description: Front Lever Raise is an advanced single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back, Hip Flexors.

ex_QUBT5G.name: Gorilla Walk
instructions: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width and squat down until you can place your hands on the floor in front of you.
Place your hands on the floor and shift your weight onto them.
Hop or step your feet forward to land outside your hands.
Repeat, moving forward in a low, gorilla-like stance.
tips: Keep your hips low and your back flat.
Land softly.
ex_QUBT5G.description: Gorilla Walk is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Core, Hamstrings.

ex_DTFINU.name: Gym Elliptical Machine Fast Speed
instructions: Step on the elliptical machine and place your feet securely on the pedals. Grip the handles with both hands for stability.
Begin moving your legs in a smooth, elliptical motion, coordinating with the handles as they move back and forth. Start at a moderate pace to get comfortable with the movement.
Gradually increase your speed to a fast pace, maintaining a smooth and controlled motion with both your legs and arms.
Continue pedaling and moving the handles at a fast pace for the desired duration.
tips: Breathe steadily and deeply to maintain oxygen flow during the exercise.
Focus on using both your legs and arms to distribute the effort evenly and prevent early fatigue.
Adjust the resistance level if needed to provide a challenging but manageable workout.
ex_DTFINU.description: Gym Elliptical Machine Fast Speed is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with an elliptical machine, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Shoulders, Upper Back.

ex_34KFNM.name: Gym Elliptical Machine Normal Speed
instructions: Step on the elliptical machine and place your feet securely on the pedals. Grip the handles with both hands for stability.
Begin moving your legs in a smooth, elliptical motion, coordinating with the handles as they move back and forth. Start at a moderate pace to get comfortable with the movement.
Maintain a consistent, moderate speed, ensuring smooth and controlled movements with both your legs and arms.

ex_UQ5ZC5.name: Gym Elliptical Machine Sprint Speed
instructions: Step on the elliptical machine and place your feet securely on the pedals. Grip the handles with both hands for stability.
Begin moving your legs in a smooth, elliptical motion, coordinating with the handles as they move back and forth. Start at a moderate pace to get comfortable with the movement.
Gradually increase your speed to a sprint pace, maintaining a fast, explosive rhythm with smooth, controlled movements.
Continue pedaling and moving the handles at a sprint pace for the desired duration.

ex_UQ5ZC5.description: Gym Elliptical Machine Sprint Speed is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with an elliptical machine, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Shoulders, Upper Back.

ex_DQVPAC.name: Gym Rowing Machine Fast Speed
instructions: Sit on the rowing machine with your feet securely strapped into the footrests, knees bent, and hands grasping the handle with an overhand grip.
Push through your legs to extend your knees and drive your body backward, keeping your arms straight until your legs are almost fully extended.
Just before your legs are fully extended, pull the handle towards your lower chest by bending your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Reverse the motion by extending your arms forward first, then bending your knees to return to the starting position. Repeat the motion at a fast pace for the desired duration.
tips: Keep your back straight and avoid rounding your spine throughout the exercise.
Use a moderate resistance level to ensure proper form and gradually increase the resistance as you get stronger.
Exhale as you pull, and inhale as you return to the starting position.
ex_DQVPAC.description: Gym Rowing Machine Fast Speed is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a rowing machine, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Shoulders, Arms.

ex_AORJKI.name: Gym Rowing Machine Normal Speed
instructions: Sit on the rowing machine with your feet securely strapped into the footrests, knees bent, and hands grasping the handle with an overhand grip.
Push through your legs to extend your knees and drive your body backward, keeping your arms straight until your legs are almost fully extended.
Just before your legs are fully extended, pull the handle towards your lower chest by bending your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Reverse the motion by extending your arms forward first, then bending your knees to return to starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions or time.

ex_Y7C572.name: Gym Rowing Machine Sprint Speed
instructions: Sit on the rowing machine with your feet securely strapped into the footrests, knees bent, and hands grasping the handle with an overhand grip.
Push through your legs to extend your knees and drive your body backward, keeping your arms straight until your legs are almost fully extended.

Reverse the motion by extending your arms forward first, then bending your knees to return to the starting position. Repeat the motion at a sprint pace for the desired duration.

ex_MWDVEM.name: Half Burpees
instructions: Begin in a high plank position with your hands placed directly under your shoulders and your body forming a straight line from head to heels.
Quickly jump your feet forward towards your hands, landing with your heels on the floor in a squat position.
Immediately jump your feet back to return to the high plank position, keeping your body straight and your core engaged.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining a quick and controlled pace.
tips: Focus on steady breathing, exhaling as you jump your feet forward and back, and inhaling as you hold the plank position.
Ensure your hands are placed directly under your shoulders in the plank position to maintain proper form and prevent strain.
