ex_CVYAVU.name: Hand Stand Hold
instructions: Begin in a handstand with your hands shoulder width apart, your arms straight, and your legs extended overhead.
Press firmly through your palms and shoulders to keep your body lifted.
Engage your core and glutes while keeping your body as straight as possible.
Hold the position for the desired duration.
tips: Spread your fingers wide and press through your entire palms.
Keep your elbows straight without allowing your arms to bend.
Look toward the floor between your hands without lifting your head excessively.
Inhale and exhale steadily throughout the hold.
ex_CVYAVU.description: Hand Stand Hold is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Core, Forearms.

ex_3PRWNP.name: Headstand
instructions: Place your forearms on the floor and clasp your hands behind your head, resting the crown of your head on the floor. Lift your hips and extend your legs together behind you.
Bend both knees and draw them toward your chest as you stack your hips above your shoulders.
Straighten both legs upward until your body forms a vertical line, then pause briefly.
Bend your knees, lower them toward your chest, and extend your legs behind you to return to the starting position.
tips: Press firmly through your forearms to reduce pressure on your head and neck.
Engage your core to control the raising and lowering phases.
Practise near a wall until you can maintain balance safely.
Exhale as you raise your legs and inhale as you lower them.
ex_3PRWNP.description: Headstand is an advanced multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Forearms, Hip Flexors.

ex_RE5CUP.name: Heavy Bag Sled Drag
instructions: Attach the sled to a rope or strap and hold it in both hands, or attach it to a harness.
Face away from the sled and lean slightly forward.
Walk or run forward with powerful strides, dragging the sled behind you.
Continue for the set distance.
tips: Keep your chest up and drive through your legs.
Keep tension on the rope; don't jerk it.
ex_RE5CUP.description: Heavy Bag Sled Drag is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a sled machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves, Forearms.

ex_P6L7T7.name: High Knees
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your arms at your sides.
Begin by lifting your right knee towards your chest as high as possible while simultaneously swinging your left arm forward.
Quickly switch to lift your left knee towards your chest while swinging your right arm forward, mimicking a running motion.
Continue to alternate knees rapidly, maintaining a steady rhythm and engaging your core. Repeat for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
tips: Lift your knees as high as possible while maintaining proper form and balance.
Move quickly but with control to maximize cardiovascular benefits and prevent injury.
Ensure your movements are balanced and coordinated to avoid straining your muscles.
ex_P6L7T7.description: High Knees is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

ex_QKBWCB.name: Indoor Cycling Spinbike Sprint
instructions: Set the saddle so your knee is slightly bent at the bottom of the pedal stroke.
Warm up at an easy pace.
Add moderate resistance and pedal as fast as you can for the sprint interval.
Recover at an easy cadence, then repeat the sprints.
tips: Stay seated with a stable upper body.
Keep enough resistance that you don't bounce in the saddle.
ex_QKBWCB.description: Indoor Cycling Spinbike Sprint is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a stationary bike, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Glutes, Calves.

ex_43XBWE.name: Indoor Cycling Spinbike
instructions: Set the saddle so your knee is slightly bent at the bottom of the pedal stroke.
Hold the handlebars lightly and keep your back neutral.
Pedal at a steady cadence, adjusting the resistance to your target effort.
Keep a smooth, circular pedal stroke for the set time.
tips: Push down and pull up through the whole stroke.
Don't grip the handlebars too tightly.
ex_43XBWE.description: Indoor Cycling Spinbike is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a stationary bike, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Glutes, Calves.

ex_J4HSRB.name: Jogging
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your arms relaxed by your sides. Engage your core and maintain an upright posture.
Begin jogging by taking short, quick steps, lifting your knees slightly higher than walking pace.
Swing your arms naturally with each step, keeping them bent at a 90-degree angle.
Maintain a steady, comfortable pace and continue jogging for the desired duration or distance.
tips: Gradually increase your jogging duration and intensity to build endurance and strength.
Breathe steadily and rhythmically to maintain oxygen flow during the jog.
Stay hydrated and take breaks if needed, especially during longer jogging sessions.
ex_J4HSRB.description: Jogging is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Hip Flexors, Core.

ex_A3KBQL.name: Jump Rope Alternating Foot
instructions: Stand with your feet together, holding a jump rope with the handles in each hand. Position the rope behind you, ready to swing it over your head.
Swing the rope over your head and, as it passes under your feet, lift one foot off the floor, quickly followed by the other foot, allowing the rope to pass beneath both feet in succession.
Continue to alternate feet with each jump, lifting one foot after the other, maintaining a steady rhythm and keeping your jumps low and controlled.
Repeat the movement for the desired duration or number of repetitions, ensuring a smooth and continuous motion.
tips: Focus on quick, controlled movements, keeping your jumps low to minimize impact on your joints.
Use your wrists to swing the rope, rather than your arms, to maintain a smooth and efficient motion.
Wear supportive footwear to protect your feet and ankles during the exercise.
ex_A3KBQL.description: Jump Rope Alternating Foot is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with a rope, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings.

ex_BXNAXW.name: Jump Rope Basic Jump
instructions: Stand with your feet together, holding a jump rope with the handles in each hand. Position the rope behind you, ready to swing it over your head.
Swing the rope over your head and, as it passes under your feet, jump with both feet simultaneously, keeping your jumps low to the floor.
Land softly on your forefeet and immediately swing the rope over your head again for the next jump.
Continue jumping at a steady rhythm, maintaining a smooth and continuous motion for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on quick, controlled movements, keeping your jumps low to minimize impact on your joints.
Use your wrists to swing the rope, rather than your arms, to maintain a smooth and efficient motion.
Wear supportive footwear to protect your feet and ankles during the exercise.
ex_BXNAXW.description: Jump Rope Basic Jump is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with a rope, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings.

ex_TFQCHN.name: Jump Rope Double Bounce
instructions: Stand with your feet together, holding a jump rope with the handles in each hand. Position the rope behind you, ready to swing it over your head.
Swing the rope over your head and, as it passes under your feet, perform a small jump, landing on your forefeet.
Immediately perform a second smaller bounce while keeping the rope in motion and preparing for the next swing.
Continue with the double bounce rhythm, maintaining a smooth and controlled motion for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on quick, controlled movements, keeping your jumps low to minimize impact on your joints.
Use your wrists to swing the rope, rather than your arms, to maintain a smooth and efficient motion.
Wear supportive footwear to protect your feet and ankles during the exercise.
ex_TFQCHN.description: Jump Rope Double Bounce is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with a rope, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings.

ex_3JIUBU.name: Jumping Jack
instructions: Stand with your feet together and your arms at your sides.
Jump your feet out to the sides while simultaneously raising your arms overhead, forming an "X" shape with your body.
Quickly jump back to the starting position with your feet together and your arms at your sides.
Repeat the movement for the desired duration or number of repetitions, maintaining a steady rhythm.
tips: Maintain a slight bend in your knees throughout the exercise to absorb impact and reduce strain on your joints.
Keep your movements light and quick to enhance cardiovascular benefits.
Engage your shoulders and back muscles when raising your arms to ensure full range of motion.
Keep your gaze forward and your head in a neutral position to maintain alignment.
ex_3JIUBU.description: Jumping Jack is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Shoulders.

ex_ILQJJT.name: Kettlebell Single Arm Clean and Press
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and the kettlebell placed on the floor between your feet. Bend your knees and hinge at your hips to grab the kettlebell with your right hand.

Explosively extend your hips and knees to lift the kettlebell off the floor and swing it up to shoulder height. As the kettlebell rises, rotate your wrist to catch it in a rack position with your elbow bent and close to your body.
Press the kettlebell overhead by extending your right arm fully, keeping your wrist straight and aligned with your shoulder.
Lower the kettlebell back to the rack position with control, then return it to the starting position on the floor. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the left hand.
tips: Use your hips and legs to generate power for the clean.
Use an appropriate weight to maintain proper form and control.
Keep your wrist straight and aligned with your forearm during the press.
ex_ILQJJT.description: Kettlebell Single Arm Clean and Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Core.

ex_NLWVUN.name: Kettlebell Single Leg Glute Bridge Pullover
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, holding a kettlebell with both hands extended straight on the floor. Extend your right leg upwards bent at 90 degrees.

Press through your left heel to lift your hips off the floor, forming a straight line from your shoulders to your left knee. Simultaneously, extend the kettlebell overhead with both arms, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Lower your hips back to the floor while bringing the kettlebell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to your left leg extended and perform the same motion.
tips: Lower the kettlebell and your hips in a controlled manner to prevent any sudden movements or loss of balance.
Focus on squeezing your glutes at the top of the bridge for maximum activation.
Inhale as you lower your hips and the kettlebell, and exhale as you lift them.
ex_NLWVUN.description: Kettlebell Single Leg Glute Bridge Pullover is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Shoulders, Triceps.

ex_ZE75TH.name: Kettlebell Sled Drag
instructions: Place a kettlebell on the sled and attach a rope or strap to it.
Face the sled and walk backward, or face away and walk forward, holding the strap.
Drag the sled with steady, powerful steps.
Continue for the set distance with your core braced.
tips: Keep your chest up.
Walking backward targets the quadriceps more.
ex_ZE75TH.description: Kettlebell Sled Drag is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a sled machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves, Forearms.

ex_FFI6YK.name: Kettlebell Snatch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and a kettlebell between your feet.
Hinge at your hips and grab the handle with one hand.
Swing the kettlebell back between your legs, then drive your hips forward and pull it straight up close to your body.
Punch your hand through as the bell flips onto your forearm, locking out overhead; lower it back into the next swing.
tips: Keep the bell close to avoid it slamming your forearm.
Power comes from your hips, not your arm.
ex_FFI6YK.description: Kettlebell Snatch is an advanced multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Traps, Core.

ex_QHFWYC.name: Kettlebell Strict Press
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in your right hand, close to the front of your shoulder. The kettlebell should rest against the back of your wrist, with your palm facing inward and your elbow close to your body facing down.
Press the kettlebell directly overhead by extending your arm upward, keeping your wrist straight.
Lower the kettlebell back to the starting position with control, returning it to shoulder height.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the left hand and perform the exercise on the other side.
tips: Maintain a neutral wrist position to avoid strain.
Avoid using momentum; focus on a slow, controlled press.
Exhale as you press the kettlebell up and inhale as you lower it.
ex_QHFWYC.description: Kettlebell Strict Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Upper Chest.

ex_JMVTUC.name: Kettlebell Sumo Deadlift High Pull
instructions: Place a kettlebell on the floor between your feet. Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart and your toes pointed slightly outward.
Hinge at your hips and bend your knees to lower your body, reaching down to grasp the kettlebell handle with both hands, keeping your back straight and chest up.

Push through your heels to lift the kettlebell off the floor, extending your hips and knees simultaneously. As you reach the standing position, explosively pull the kettlebell upward towards your chin by bending your elbows and keeping them pointed outward.
Lower the kettlebell back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Use a weight that allows you to maintain proper form throughout the exercise.
Push through your heels to maximize power and stability.
Ensure your knees track over your toes to prevent knee strain.
ex_JMVTUC.description: Kettlebell Sumo Deadlift High Pull is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Upper Back, Lower Back.

ex_L5AR3Q.name: Kettlebell Swing (45 Degree View)
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly outward. Place a kettlebell vertically on the floor between your feet. Bend at your hips and knees to reach forward and grab the kettlebell with both hands, interlocking your fingers.
Hinge at your hips to swing the kettlebell back between your legs, allowing a slight bend in your knees.

Drive through your hips, extending them forcefully to swing the kettlebell forward and up to shoulder height. Allow the momentum to carry the kettlebell upwards, keeping your arms straight but not locked.
As the kettlebell begins to descend, hinge at your hips again to let it swing back between your legs, preparing for the next repetition. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Use the power from your hips, not your arms, to generate the swing.
Keep your back straight and avoid rounding your shoulders.
Exhale as you swing the kettlebell up, inhale as it swings back down.
ex_L5AR3Q.description: Kettlebell Swing (45 Degree View) is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Lower Back.

ex_D6WO2Q.name: Kettlebell Swing
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly outward. Place a kettlebell on the floor between your feet. Bend at your hips and knees to reach forward and grab the kettlebell with both hands, keeping your back straight and chest up.
Hinge at your hips to swing the kettlebell back between your legs, allowing a slight bend in your knees.

Drive through your hips, extending them forcefully to swing the kettlebell forward and up to shoulder height. Allow the momentum to carry the kettlebell upwards, keeping your arms straight but not locked.
As the kettlebell begins to descend, hinge at your hips again to let it swing back between your legs, preparing for the next repetition. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Use the power from your hips, not your arms, to generate the swing.
Keep your back straight and avoid rounding your shoulders.
Exhale as you swing the kettlebell up, inhale as it swings back down.
ex_D6WO2Q.description: Kettlebell Swing is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Lower Back.

ex_FAE567.name: Kettlebell Thruster
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in each hand at shoulder level, palms facing inward. Keep your elbows close to your.
Lower into a squat by bending your hips and knees until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Push through your heels to stand back up while simultaneously pressing the kettlebells overhead. Fully extend your arms at the top of the movement.
Lower the kettlebells back to shoulder level as you prepare for the next repetition. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you press the kettlebells overhead, inhale as you lower into the squat.
Choose an appropriate weight to maintain control throughout the exercise.
Keep your wrists straight and aligned with your forearms.
ex_FAE567.description: Kettlebell Thruster is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Core.

ex_DZOF34.name: Kettlebell Turkish Get Up
instructions: Lie on your back holding a kettlebell straight above your shoulder, with the knee on the same side bent.
Roll onto your opposite forearm, then hand, keeping the bell locked out overhead.
Lift your hips, sweep your straight leg under you into a kneeling position, and stand up.
Reverse every step with control back to lying down.
tips: Keep your eyes on the kettlebell.
Learn the movement with a light weight or no weight first.
ex_DZOF34.description: Kettlebell Turkish Get Up is an advanced multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Quadriceps, Triceps.

ex_KTVII2.name: Kettlebell Walkover Pushup
instructions: Start in a push-up position with one hand on a kettlebell handle and the other on the floor.
Do a push-up.
Move your hands so the other hand goes onto the kettlebell, walking over it.
Do another push-up and keep alternating.
tips: Keep your body in a straight line.
Make sure the kettlebell is stable before putting weight on it.
ex_KTVII2.description: Kettlebell Walkover Pushup is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Shoulders, Core.

ex_OB6WUR.name: Kettlebell Windmill
instructions: Press a kettlebell overhead with one arm and turn your feet about 45 degrees away from that side.
Keeping your eyes on the bell, push your hips out to the side of the raised arm.
Hinge and slide your free hand down the inside of your front leg toward the floor.
Return to standing by driving your hips back under you, keeping the bell locked out.
tips: Keep your top arm vertical throughout.
Only go as low as your hamstrings allow.
ex_OB6WUR.description: Kettlebell Windmill is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Glutes, Core.

ex_3KDBOZ.name: Kipping Handstand Push-Up
instructions: Kick up into a handstand against a wall with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Lower your head to the floor or a pad, then bring your knees down toward your chest.
Kick your legs up explosively while pressing hard with your arms to lock out.
Lower with control and repeat.
tips: Master strict handstand push-ups and wall handstands first.
Use a pad under your head.
ex_3KDBOZ.description: Kipping Handstand Push-Up is an advanced multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Chest, Core, Hip Flexors.

ex_P65PJZ.name: Landmine Alternating Lunge and Twist
instructions: Stand facing the landmine and hold the end of the bar at chest height with both hands.
Step back into a reverse lunge.
In the lunge, rotate your torso to bring the bar toward the side of your front leg.
Rotate back, stand up and repeat on the other leg.
tips: Keep your front knee over your foot.
Rotate from your torso, not your hips.
ex_P65PJZ.description: Landmine Alternating Lunge and Twist is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Shoulders, Core.

ex_R7C3BI.name: Landmine Alternating Lunge to Chest Press
instructions: Stand facing the landmine and hold the end of the bar at your chest with both hands.
Step back into a reverse lunge.
As you lower, press the bar forward and up until your arms are straight.
Bring the bar back to your chest, stand up and repeat with the other leg.
tips: Keep your torso upright in the lunge.
Brace your core during the press.
ex_R7C3BI.description: Landmine Alternating Lunge to Chest Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps, Hamstrings.

ex_JW3PJR.name: Landmine Rotational Lift to Press
instructions: Stand side-on to the landmine and hold the end of the bar beside your hip with both hands.
Squat slightly and rotate toward the bar.
Drive from your legs and rotate your torso to lift the bar across your body.
Press it overhead on the opposite side, then reverse with control.
tips: Pivot your back foot as you rotate.
Power comes from your legs and hips.
ex_JW3PJR.description: Landmine Rotational Lift to Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Quadriceps, Triceps.

ex_RM34EZ.name: Lateral Sled Drag
instructions: Attach a rope or strap to the sled and stand side-on to it, holding the strap.
Bend your knees into a quarter squat.
Step sideways away from the sled, dragging it with each step.
Continue for the set distance, then switch to lead with the other side.
tips: Stay low and don't cross your feet.
Keep your torso upright.
ex_RM34EZ.description: Lateral Sled Drag is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a sled machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Adductors, Core.

ex_MBC6VK.name: Low Box Lateral Runner
instructions: Stand beside a low box or step.
Step one foot onto the box.
Quickly run sideways over the box, switching feet with each step.
Continue moving side to side for the set time.
tips: Stay on the balls of your feet.
Keep your steps quick and light.
ex_MBC6VK.description: Low Box Lateral Runner is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Abductors, Adductors.

ex_JVTAFN.name: Low Box Quick Feet
instructions: Stand facing a low box or step.
Tap one foot onto the box, then the other, in quick succession.
Keep alternating taps as fast as you can with control.
Continue for the set time.
tips: Stay on the balls of your feet.
Pump your arms to keep the rhythm.
ex_JVTAFN.description: Low Box Quick Feet is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Glutes.

ex_QUJO3Y.name: Low Rotational Med Ball Chops (Quarter Squat, Rotating Med Ball Left and Right Across Core)
instructions: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width in a quarter squat, holding a medicine ball at chest height.
Rotate your torso to bring the ball down to the outside of one hip.
Rotate back across your body, keeping the ball low as it rides across your core to the other hip.
Continue alternating sides in a smooth, controlled rhythm.
tips: Stay in the quarter squat throughout.
Pivot your feet slightly to protect your knees.
ex_QUJO3Y.description: Low Rotational Med Ball Chops (Quarter Squat, Rotating Med Ball Left and Right Across Core) is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a medicine ball, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abdominals, Quadriceps, Glutes.

ex_2ZPRBJ.name: Low Sled Push
instructions: Grip the sled at the low handles, arms extended.
Lean forward so your torso is nearly parallel to the floor with a flat back.
Drive the sled forward with short, fast steps through the balls of your feet.
Keep pushing for the set distance.
tips: Keep your hips low and your back flat.
Drive your knees forward.
ex_2ZPRBJ.description: Low Sled Push is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a sled machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Hamstrings, Shoulders.

ex_JMYQDX.name: Lying Neck Curls
instructions: Lie on your back on a bench with your head and neck past the end.
Let your head lower gently back until it is in line with the bench.
Tuck your chin and slowly curl your head up toward your chest.
Lower it back with control and repeat.
tips: Move slowly with no jerking.
Start with bodyweight only; add a towel-wrapped plate only when this is easy.
ex_JMYQDX.description: Lying Neck Curls is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the levator scapulae (neck). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category.

ex_STUWNJ.name: Lying Neck Extension
instructions: Lie face down on a bench with your head and neck past the end.
Let your head lower gently toward the floor.
Slowly lift your head back until it is in line with your spine.
Lower it with control and repeat.
tips: Don't lift your head beyond a neutral line.
Move slowly and without weight at first.
ex_STUWNJ.description: Lying Neck Extension is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the levator scapulae (neck). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Traps.

ex_P2TNLI.name: Lying on Side Arm Circle Warm Up
instructions: Lie on your side with your knees bent and both arms extended in front of you at chest height.
Lift your top arm and draw a large circle over your head and behind you.
Let your chest open and your eyes follow your hand as the arm goes behind you.
Bring the arm back to the start and repeat, then switch sides.
tips: Keep your knees together and on the floor.
Move slowly through the full range.
ex_P2TNLI.description: Lying on Side Arm Circle Warm Up is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Upper Back.

ex_LDDUJW.name: Major Groups Muscle Body
instructions: Stand tall with your back straight, arms by your side, and feet shoulder-width apart.
ex_LDDUJW.description: Major Groups Muscle Body is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category.

ex_F5MG3H.name: Med Ball Jumping Jacks
instructions: Stand with your feet together, holding a medicine ball at your chest.
Jump your feet out wide while pressing the ball overhead.
Jump your feet back together as you bring the ball back to your chest.
Repeat at a steady pace.
tips: Land softly on the balls of your feet.
Use a light ball.
ex_F5MG3H.description: Med Ball Jumping Jacks is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a medicine ball, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Calves, Quadriceps.

ex_RQC2YJ.name: Med Ball Side Wall Slams
instructions: Stand side-on to a wall about an arm's length away, holding a medicine ball at your hip.
Rotate away from the wall to load.
Rotate explosively and throw the ball into the wall at hip to chest height.
Catch the rebound and repeat, then switch sides.
tips: Pivot your back foot so your hips drive the throw.
Use a ball made for wall throws.
ex_RQC2YJ.description: Med Ball Side Wall Slams is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a medicine ball, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abdominals, Shoulders, Glutes.

ex_ZN35XE.name: Med Ball Slam Burpees
instructions: Stand holding a medicine ball overhead.
Slam the ball to the floor in front of you.
Place your hands on the ball or the floor, jump your feet back into a plank, then jump them back in.
Pick up the ball, stand and lift it overhead into the next rep.
tips: Use a slam ball that doesn't bounce.
Keep your back flat when you pick up the ball.
ex_ZN35XE.description: Med Ball Slam Burpees is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a medicine ball, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Abdominals, Quadriceps.

ex_KDPSRW.name: Monkey Bar Swings
instructions: Hang from the first bar of a monkey bar set with both hands.
Swing your body slightly and reach one hand forward to the next bar.
Shift your weight and swing the other hand forward to the following bar.
Continue across the bars, keeping your shoulders engaged.
tips: Use your hips to create a gentle swing.
Keep a firm grip and active shoulders.
ex_KDPSRW.description: Monkey Bar Swings is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Shoulders, Core.

ex_GLTCX5.name: Mountain Climber Jumps
instructions: Start in a high plank with your hands under your shoulders.
Jump one foot forward toward your hands, with the other leg extended behind.
Switch legs in mid-air so the opposite foot lands forward.
Keep switching quickly while holding your hips level.
tips: Keep your shoulders over your hands.
Don't let your hips bounce up.
ex_GLTCX5.description: Mountain Climber Jumps is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Quadriceps, Chest.

ex_3L3TC5.name: Overhead Med Ball Throw
instructions: Stand facing a wall or open space, holding a medicine ball overhead.
Bend slightly at the knees and hips and take the ball back behind your head.
Throw the ball forward explosively with your arms and core.
Catch the rebound or retrieve the ball and repeat.
tips: Brace your core so your lower back doesn't overextend.
Release the ball at head height.
ex_3L3TC5.description: Overhead Med Ball Throw is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a medicine ball, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Lats, Chest.

ex_IYXUNP.name: Pike Alternating Opposite Hip Taps
instructions: Start in a pike position, hips high, with your hands and feet on the floor.
Shift your weight onto one hand.
Reach the other hand back to tap the opposite hip or ankle.
Return the hand to the floor and alternate sides.
tips: Keep your hips high and still.
Move slowly to stay balanced.
ex_IYXUNP.description: Pike Alternating Opposite Hip Taps is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Triceps.

ex_DMXHYJ.name: Pike Individual Alternating Arm Reaches
instructions: Start in a pike position, hips high, with your hands and feet on the floor.
Shift your weight onto one hand.
Reach the other arm forward in line with your head.
Return it to the floor and alternate arms.
tips: Keep your hips high and level.
Press the floor away with the supporting hand.
ex_DMXHYJ.description: Pike Individual Alternating Arm Reaches is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Hamstrings.

ex_YSNZMU.name: Pike Jacks Feet Kicking in and Out
instructions: Start in a pike position, hips high, with your hands and feet on the floor.
Jump your feet out wide.
Jump them back together.
Keep repeating while your hands stay planted.
tips: Keep your hips high and your arms straight.
Land softly on the balls of your feet.
ex_YSNZMU.description: Pike Jacks Feet Kicking in and Out is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Core, Hamstrings, Abductors.

ex_XHEGTK.name: Pike Shoulder Taps
instructions: Start in a pike position, hips high, with your hands and feet on the floor.
Lift one hand and tap the opposite shoulder.
Place the hand back down and tap with the other hand.
Keep alternating with your hips still.
tips: Widen your feet for more stability.
Move slowly and with control.
ex_XHEGTK.description: Pike Shoulder Taps is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Hamstrings.

ex_3NDFCI.name: Plank Individual Arm Reach
instructions: Start in a high plank with your hands under your shoulders and feet hip-width apart.
Brace your core and lift one arm straight forward.
Hold briefly without letting your hips rotate.
Place the hand back down and switch arms.
tips: Widen your feet if you lose balance.
Keep your hips level.
ex_3NDFCI.description: Plank Individual Arm Reach is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abdominals, Obliques.

ex_J4NUM6.name: Plank IYTW
instructions: Start in a high plank with your feet slightly wider than hip-width.
Lift one arm straight overhead in line with your body (I), then return it.
Lift it diagonally (Y), then out to the side (T), returning to the floor each time.
Bend the elbow and pull it back (W), then repeat the sequence with the other arm.
tips: Keep your hips steady throughout.
Squeeze your shoulder blade with each position.
ex_J4NUM6.description: Plank IYTW is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Core, Shoulders.

ex_QEBXRP.name: Plank Lunges
instructions: Begin in a plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your body forming a straight line from head to heels.
Bring your right knee forward and place your right foot outside your right hand, keeping your left leg extended straight back.
Return your right foot to the plank position.
Repeat the movement with your left knee, bringing your left foot forward to place it outside your left hand. Alternate sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Move your leg slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you bring your foot forward and inhaling as you return to the plank position.
Ensure your body stays in a straight line, avoiding sagging hips or raised buttocks.
ex_QEBXRP.description: Plank Lunges is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Glutes.

ex_53JS6N.name: Plank Pushup
instructions: Start in a forearm plank.
Place one hand on the floor and press up, then the other, until you are in a high plank.
Lower back to one forearm, then the other.
Alternate the leading arm each rep.
tips: Keep your hips from rocking.
Widen your feet for more stability.
ex_53JS6N.description: Plank Pushup is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Chest.

ex_HT4AQ5.name: Plate Overhead Carry
instructions: Hold a weight plate overhead with both hands, arms locked out.
Brace your core and stand tall.
Walk forward with steady, controlled steps.
Continue for the set distance or time, then lower the plate with control.
tips: Keep your ribs down; don't arch your lower back.
Keep the plate directly over your head.
ex_HT4AQ5.description: Plate Overhead Carry is an intermediate multi-joint compound loaded carry exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Traps, Upper Back.

ex_PXRRHA.name: Pull Sled or Dog Sled Push
instructions: Grip the sled handles with your arms extended.
Lean forward with a flat back.
Drive the sled forward with powerful steps.
Continue for the set distance.
tips: Brace your core.
Keep your steps short and fast.
ex_PXRRHA.description: Pull Sled or Dog Sled Push is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a sled machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Hamstrings, Shoulders.

ex_DS7NMW.name: Pushup to Renegade Row
instructions: Start in a high plank holding a dumbbell in each hand on the floor.
Do a push-up.
At the top, row one dumbbell to your hip, then lower it.
Row the other dumbbell, then go into the next push-up.
tips: Widen your feet to stop your hips from rotating.
Use hex dumbbells so they don't roll.
ex_DS7NMW.description: Pushup to Renegade Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Lats, Core.

ex_G73O5O.name: Rebounder High Knee Runs
instructions: Stand in the middle of a rebounder trampoline.
Run on the spot, driving your knees up toward hip height.
Pump your arms in rhythm with your legs.
Keep going for the set time.
tips: Stay in the centre of the mat.
Stand tall.
ex_G73O5O.description: Rebounder High Knee Runs is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Core.

ex_2YSJOF.name: Rebounder Knee Jumps
instructions: Stand in the middle of a rebounder trampoline.
Bounce, then jump and bring both knees up toward your chest.
Land softly with bent knees.
Repeat in a steady rhythm.
tips: Use your arms to help the jump.
Land in the centre of the mat.
ex_2YSJOF.description: Rebounder Knee Jumps is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Abdominals, Glutes.

ex_A3ECUY.name: Rebounder Knee Pushes
instructions: Kneel beside a rebounder and place your hands on the mat in a kneeling push-up position.
Lower your chest toward the mat.
Press up quickly using the rebound of the mat.
Repeat in a steady rhythm.
tips: Keep a straight line from head to knees.
Keep your elbows at about 45 degrees.
ex_A3ECUY.description: Rebounder Knee Pushes is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Shoulders, Core.

ex_BVGSGK.name: Rebounder Light Jumps
instructions: Stand in the middle of a rebounder trampoline with your feet hip-width apart.
Bounce gently, keeping your feet close to the mat.
Keep your knees soft and your core engaged.
Continue for the set time.
tips: A good warm-up; keep it easy.
Stay in the centre of the mat.
ex_BVGSGK.description: Rebounder Light Jumps is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Core.

ex_RL4FRN.name: Rebounder in & Out From Ground
instructions: Stand next to a rebounder.
Step or jump onto the mat, bounce once, and step or jump back to the ground.
Alternate the lead foot.
Continue for the set time.
tips: Make sure the rebounder is stable.
Land softly each time.
ex_RL4FRN.description: Rebounder in & Out From Ground is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Core.

ex_JMAEIV.name: Rebounder in & Out Jacks
instructions: Stand in the middle of a rebounder with your feet together.
Bounce your feet out wide.
Bounce them back together.
Repeat in a steady rhythm, adding arm swings if you like.
tips: Keep your knees soft.
Stay in the centre of the mat.
ex_JMAEIV.description: Rebounder in & Out Jacks is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Adductors, Shoulders.

ex_NZNTQJ.name: Resistance Band Pull Apart
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a loop resistance band with both hands. Your arms should be extended straight in front of you at shoulder height, and your palms should be facing down.
Pull the resistance band apart by moving your arms out to your sides, squeezing your shoulder blades together, and keeping your arms straight.
Slowly return your arms to the starting position with control, maintaining tension in the band.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your arms straight throughout the exercise, maintaining a slight bend in your elbows.
Maintain a neutral wrist position to prevent strain.
Focus on engaging your upper back and shoulder muscles throughout the movement.
ex_NZNTQJ.description: Resistance Band Pull Apart is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Rotator Cuff.

ex_S35PX6.name: Resistance Band Shoulder Adduction
instructions: Attach one end of a resistance band to a sturdy anchor point at a high height. Stand with your left side facing the anchor point, holding the other end of the band with your right hand.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart. Extend your right arm straight out to the side parallel to the floor, palm facing down.
Pull the band towards your body, bringing your right hand close to your hip, keeping your arm straight.
Slowly return your right arm to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the left side.
tips: Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and reduce injury risk.
Exhale as you pull the band across your body and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Use a resistance band that provides enough tension to challenge your muscles without compromising form.
ex_S35PX6.description: Resistance Band Shoulder Adduction is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_GDBY34.name: Resistance Band Standing External Rotation
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and place a loop resistance band around your wrists. Keep your elbows bent at 90 degrees and close to your sides, with your forearms parallel to the floor and pointing forward.
Rotate your shoulders outwards by pulling the resistance band apart while keeping your elbows fixed at your sides.
Slowly return your forearms to the starting position with control, maintaining tension in the band.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and reduce shoulder injury risk.
Exhale as you rotate your forearms outward and inhale as you return them to the starting position.
Keep your elbows fixed at your sides to ensure proper form.
ex_GDBY34.description: Resistance Band Standing External Rotation is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.

ex_LFN3Y5.name: Resistance Band Standing Single Arm Shoulder Extension
instructions: Attach one end of a resistance band to a sturdy anchor point at hips height. Stand facing the anchor point and hold the other end of the band in your right hand.
Extend your right arm up, pointing to the anchor point, with your palm facing down.
Pull the band backward, keeping your arm straight, and until it reaches parallel to your side.
