ex_IRCG6V.name: Tyre Flip
instructions: Squat down in front of a large tyre and grip under its edge with your chest close to it.
Drive through your legs and hips to lift the tyre.
As it rises, step forward and push it over with your hands or knee.
Reset and repeat.
tips: Lift with your legs, not your back.
Keep your arms straight during the initial lift.
ex_IRCG6V.description: Tyre Flip is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a tire, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Chest, Triceps.

ex_76VKU7.name: Tyre Hammering
instructions: Stand in front of a tyre holding a sledgehammer, feet shoulder-width apart.
Swing the hammer up over one shoulder.
Bring it down forcefully onto the tyre, bending your knees as you strike.
Control the rebound and repeat, switching sides regularly.
tips: Slide your top hand down the handle as you strike.
Keep your back flat.
ex_76VKU7.description: Tyre Hammering is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a hammer, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abdominals, Lats, Forearms.

ex_LIIIQB.name: Unilateral Box Jump - Bilateral Deceleration
instructions: Stand on one leg in front of a box.
Jump onto the box from one leg.
Land on both feet, absorbing the landing with bent knees and hips.
Step down and repeat, alternating the take-off leg.
tips: Land softly and quietly.
Choose a box height you can land on in control.
ex_LIIIQB.description: Unilateral Box Jump - Bilateral Deceleration is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Hamstrings.

ex_WMS2M5.name: Unilateral Box Jump
instructions: Stand on one leg in front of a low box.
Bend your standing knee and swing your arms back.
Jump onto the box, landing softly on the same leg.
Step down and repeat, then switch legs.
tips: Start with a very low box.
Land with your knee over your toes.
ex_WMS2M5.description: Unilateral Box Jump is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Hamstrings, Core.

ex_BMR65W.name: Unilateral Front Plank
instructions: Start in a forearm plank with your body in a straight line.
Lift one leg a few inches off the floor.
Hold without letting your hips rotate or sag.
Switch legs after the set time.
tips: Squeeze the glute of the raised leg.
Keep your hips square to the floor.
ex_BMR65W.description: Unilateral Front Plank is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Shoulders.

ex_27CLBI.name: Unilateral Jumps
instructions: Stand on one leg with a slight bend in the knee.
Hop forward or straight up on the same leg.
Land softly, absorbing the landing.
Repeat, then switch legs.
tips: Stick each landing before the next hop.
Use your arms for balance.
ex_27CLBI.description: Unilateral Jumps is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Core.

ex_GEOIFW.name: Unilateral Plank
instructions: Start in a high plank.
Lift one arm and the opposite leg off the floor.
Hold the position with your hips level.
Return and switch sides.
tips: Widen your supporting base if you lose balance.
Keep your neck in line with your spine.
ex_GEOIFW.description: Unilateral Plank is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Shoulders.

ex_BTFG7L.name: Walking Fast
instructions: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart and your arms relaxed by your sides.
Step forward with your right foot, rolling through the heel to the ball of your foot while swinging your left arm forward and right arm back.
Push off with your right foot, quickly bringing your left foot forward to step, swinging your right arm forward and left arm back. Increase your pace while maintaining control.
Continue this alternating pattern, maintaining a brisk and consistent stride. Repeat for the desired distance or time.
tips: Maintain a brisk pace that challenges you but allows you to walk efficiently.
Wear comfortable, supportive shoes to prevent injury and enhance your walking experience.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid tensing your upper body.
ex_BTFG7L.description: Walking Fast is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Core, Lower Back, Hip Flexors.

ex_NDJWZQ.name: Walking
instructions: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart and your arms relaxed by your sides.
Step forward with your right foot, rolling through the heel to the ball of your foot while swinging your left arm forward and right arm back.
Push off with your right foot, bringing your left foot forward to step, swinging your right arm forward and left arm back.
Continue this alternating pattern, maintaining a natural stride and rhythm. Repeat for the desired distance or time.
tips: Swing your arms naturally in opposition to your legs to help with balance and momentum.
Maintain a steady and comfortable pace that allows you to walk efficiently.
Wear comfortable, supportive shoes to prevent injury and enhance your walking experience.
ex_NDJWZQ.description: Walking is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Core, Lower Back, Hip Flexors.

ex_QODDMW.name: Archer Push Up
instructions: Start in a push-up position with your hands placed wider than shoulder-width apart and your body forming a straight line from head to heels.
Bend your right elbow to lower your chest towards your right hand while keeping your left arm extended straight to the side.
Push back up to the starting position.
Bend your left elbow to lower your chest towards your left hand while keeping your right arm extended straight to the side. Continue alternating sides.
tips: Ensure your shoulders and hips stay level to avoid any imbalance during the movement.
Use a slow and steady breathing pattern, exhaling as you push up and inhaling as you lower down.
Keep your gaze slightly forward to maintain a neutral spine and avoid neck strain.
ex_QODDMW.description: Archer Push Up is an advanced multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.

ex_XBHMWC.name: Assisted Weighted Push Up
instructions: Position yourself in a high plank position with your hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, your feet together, and your body forming a straight line from head to heels. Have your partner place a weight plate on your upper back.
Lower your body towards the floor by bending your elbows, until your chest nearly touches the floor.
Push through your palms to straighten your arms and return to the starting position, maintaining a controlled and steady movement. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Maintain a straight line from head to heels to ensure proper form.
Exhale as you push up and inhale as you lower your body.
Ensure the weight plate is securely placed on your upper back for safety.
ex_XBHMWC.description: Assisted Weighted Push Up is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Shoulders, Core.

ex_RIFIVJ.name: Band Pallof Press
instructions: Attach a resistance band to a sturdy anchor point at chest height. Stand perpendicular to the anchor point, holding the handle of the band with both hands close to your chest.
Push the band straight out in front of you, extending your arms fully and squeezing your chest muscles at the peak of the movement.
Slowly return your hands to your chest, maintaining control.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
tips: Maintain an upright posture and avoid leaning towards or away from the anchor point.
Engage your core to resist the rotational pull of the band.
Adjust the band’s tension or your distance from the anchor for an appropriate challenge.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you push the band forward and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
ex_RIFIVJ.description: Band Pallof Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

ex_QOM5NS.name: Band Single Arm Pec Fly
instructions: Attach a resistance band to a sturdy anchor point at chest height. Stand facing away from the anchor point, holding the handle of the band in your working hand with your arm extended out to the side, palm facing forward.
Keep your feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, and your chest engaged.
Pull the band in an arc motion, bringing your hand towards the center of your chest.
Slowly return your arm to the starting position. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
tips: Engage your core to stabilize your body and prevent unnecessary movement.
Use a controlled motion to pull and return the band, preventing any jerking movements.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you pull the band across your body and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
Keep your elbow slightly bent throughout the movement to avoid joint strain.
ex_QOM5NS.description: Band Single Arm Pec Fly is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Biceps.

ex_XVTIBC.name: Barbell Bench Press Decline
instructions: Set a decline bench at a suitable angle and lie down on it with your feet secured under the foot pads. Grip the barbell with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and unrack the barbell by extending your arms fully. Lower the barbell slowly and with control to your lower chest, keeping your elbows at a 90-degree angle to your body.
Press the barbell back up to the starting position by extending your arms fully, focusing on using your chest muscles.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then carefully rack the barbell back onto the bench press rack.
tips: Keep your feet secured under the foot pads to maintain stability and prevent sliding.
Engage your core to maintain a stable and strong torso throughout the movement.
Lower the barbell slowly and with control to prevent injury and maximize muscle engagement.
ex_XVTIBC.description: Barbell Bench Press Decline is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

ex_IN3YDK.name: Barbell Incline Bench Press (Front View)
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 45 degree angle and lie down on it with your feet flat on the floor. Grip the barbell with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and unrack the barbell by extending your arms fully. Lower the barbell slowly and with control to your upper chest, keeping your elbows at a 45-degree angle to your body.
Press the barbell back up to the starting position by extending your arms fully, focusing on using your chest muscles.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then carefully rack the barbell back onto the bench press rack.
tips: Keep your feet flat on the floor to maintain stability and support your lower back.
Engage your core to maintain a stable and strong torso throughout the movement.
Lower the barbell slowly and with control to prevent injury and maximize muscle engagement.
ex_IN3YDK.description: Barbell Incline Bench Press (Front View) is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

ex_SAWOOH.name: Barbell Bench Press
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor. Grip the barbell with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, and position the bar directly above your chest.
Engage your core and unrack the barbell by extending your arms fully. Lower the barbell slowly and with control to your chest, keeping your elbows at a 90-degree angle to your body.
Press the barbell back up to the starting position by extending your arms fully, focusing on using your chest muscles.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then carefully rack the barbell back onto the bench press rack.
tips: Keep your feet flat on the floor to maintain stability and support your lower back.
Engage your core to maintain a stable and strong torso throughout the movement.
Lower the barbell slowly and with control to prevent injury and maximize muscle engagement.
ex_SAWOOH.description: Barbell Bench Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

ex_KT263D.name: Barbell Close Grip Bench Press
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor. Grip the barbell with your hands placed closer than shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the barbell by extending your arms fully. Lower the barbell slowly and with control to your lower chest, keeping your elbows facing away from your body.
Press the barbell back up to the starting position by extending your arms fully, focusing on using your triceps and chest muscles.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then carefully rack the barbell back onto the bench press rack.
tips: Maintain a controlled pace to ensure that you're using muscle strength rather than momentum.
Keep your feet flat on the floor to maintain stability and support your lower back.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you press the barbell up and inhaling as you lower it back down.
ex_KT263D.description: Barbell Close Grip Bench Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

ex_F7SLDU.name: Barbell Floor Chest Press
instructions: Lie on your back on the floor with your feet flat on the floor. Grip a barbell with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, and hold the barbell directly above your chest with your arms bent, elbows on the floor.
Engage your core and slowly press the barbell up until your arms are straight over your chest.
Lower the barbell back to the starting position by bending your arms fully, focusing on using your chest muscles.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Lower the barbell slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Ensure your elbows are at a 45-degree angle to your body to reduce shoulder strain.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you press the barbell up and inhaling as you lower it down.
ex_F7SLDU.description: Barbell Floor Chest Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

ex_M7AGNQ.name: Barbell Hooklying Bench Press Close Elbows
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with your knees bent, feet resting on the bench, and grasp the barbell with a grip slightly narrower than shoulder width. Position the bar above your chest with your elbows tucked close to your sides.
Lower the barbell slowly toward the lower chest while keeping your elbows close to your torso.
Press the barbell upward by extending your elbows until your arms are fully straight above your chest.
Pause briefly at the top, slowly return to the starting position. Repeat while maintaining control throughout the movement.
tips: Keep your core engaged to stabilize your body on the bench.
Keep your elbows tucked in and maintain a neutral wrist position throughout the lift.
Press the bar vertically while keeping it balanced over your chest, while squeezing your triceps, and lower the bar under control, avoiding bouncing the weight off your chest.
Exhale as you press the bar upward and inhale as you lower it.
ex_M7AGNQ.description: Barbell Hooklying Bench Press Close Elbows is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Serratus Anterior, Forearms.

ex_CBEOLQ.name: Barbell Incline Bench Press

anatomical: Clavicular Head of the Pectoralis Major

instructions: Lie on an incline bench set at a 45 degree angle. Grip the barbell with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, and hold the barbell directly above your chest with your arms fully extended.
Slowly lower the barbell to your upper chest, keeping your elbows at a 45-degree angle to your body.
Press the barbell back up to the starting position by extending your arms fully, focusing on using your chest.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then carefully rack the barbell back onto the bench press rack.
tips: Breathe steadily, exhaling as you press the barbell up and inhaling as you lower it down.
Maintain a firm grip on the barbell to ensure control and proper alignment.
Use a spotter if lifting heavy weights to ensure safety.
ex_CBEOLQ.description: Barbell Incline Bench Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

ex_WSQD5N.name: Barbell JM Bench Press
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor, holding a barbell with your hands shoulder-width apart. Your arms should be fully extended above your chest.
Lower the barbell by bending your elbows and bringing it down towards your chest.
When the barbell is just above your chest, move it toward your head and stop when the barbell is just overhead and move it back to above the chest.

Push it back up to the starting position by extending your elbows, focusing on using your triceps. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then carefully rack the barbell back onto the bench press rack.
tips: Focus on the triceps by keeping your elbows slightly tucked in and not flaring out too much.
Lower the barbell slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Maintain a strong grip on the barbell to ensure control and proper alignment.
ex_WSQD5N.description: Barbell JM Bench Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Shoulders.

ex_ZEFSDD.name: Barbell Landmine Chest Press
instructions: Stand facing the free end of the landmine barbell with your feet shoulder width apart and hold the end of the bar at chest height using both hands. Keep your elbows slightly in front of your body and brace your core.
Press the bar upward until your arms are fully extended while maintaining a stable, upright posture.
Pause briefly at the top while keeping your shoulders down and your chest engaged.
Slowly lower the bar back to chest level under control and repeat.
tips: Press the bar in its natural arc rather than trying to move it straight overhead.
Keep your elbows slightly tucked instead of flaring them outward.
Keep your core engaged and chest up, avoid leaning backward.
Exhale as you press the bar upward and inhale as you return.
ex_ZEFSDD.description: Barbell Landmine Chest Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Serratus Anterior, Core.

ex_NAG72H.name: Barbell Larsen Bench Press
instructions: Lie flat on a bench with your legs fully extended in front of your body and hold the barbell with a grip wider than shoulder width.
Keep your core tight and slowly lower the barbell to the middle of your chest while keeping your legs raised.
Pause briefly with the barbell lightly touching your chest.
Press the barbell back up until your arms are straight, then repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your legs fully extended and off the floor throughout the exercise, while engaging your core for stability.
Keep your wrists straight and stacked over your forearms.
Press the barbell in a smooth, controlled path over your chest and lower the weight slowly with control.
Inhale as you lower the barbell and exhale as you press it up.
ex_NAG72H.description: Barbell Larsen Bench Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abdominals, Shoulders, Forearms.

ex_DA7LYB.name: Barbell Pullover to Triceps Extension
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor. Hold a barbell with an overhand grip (palms facing the barbell), hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Extend your arms so the barbell is directly above your chest.
Bend your elbows and lower the barbell in an arc motion behind your head. Lower the barbell until you feel a stretch in your chest and lats.
Reverse the motion by pulling the barbell back over your chest, then extend the barbell straight up by extending your arms fully.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily, inhaling as you lower the barbell and exhaling as you press it back up.
Use a weight that allows for proper form and control throughout the exercise to prevent strain or injury.
Ensure a firm grip on the barbell to maintain control and proper alignment.
ex_DA7LYB.description: Barbell Pullover to Triceps Extension is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Shoulders.

ex_63QTUM.name: Barbell Reverse Close Grip Bench Press
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor. Hold a barbell with a reverse grip (palms facing back) and hands placed shoulder-width apart. Position the barbell directly above your chest with your arms fully extended.
Slowly lower the barbell towards your chest by bending your elbows. Keep your elbows close to your body throughout the movement.
Lower the barbell just before touching your chest, then push the barbell back up to the starting position by extending your arms fully.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your elbows close to your body to ensure proper form and prevent shoulder strain.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Ensure a firm grip on the barbell to maintain control and proper alignment.
ex_63QTUM.description: Barbell Reverse Close Grip Bench Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

ex_EZ4JV4.name: Barbell Reverse Grip Bench Press
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor. Hold a barbell with a reverse grip (palms facing back) and hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Position the barbell directly above your chest with your arms fully extended.
Slowly lower the barbell towards your chest by bending your elbows. Keep your elbows close to your body throughout the movement.
Allow the barbell to lightly touch your chest, then push the barbell back up to the starting position by extending your arms fully.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your elbows close to your body to ensure proper form and prevent shoulder strain.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Ensure a firm grip on the barbell to maintain control and proper alignment.
ex_EZ4JV4.description: Barbell Reverse Grip Bench Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

ex_C2MIKW.name: Barbell Spoto Press
instructions: Lie flat on a bench with your feet firmly on the floor and hold the barbell above your chest with a shoulder width grip.
Lower the barbell slowly until it is just above your chest without allowing it to touch.
Pause briefly for 1 - 2 seconds while keeping the barbell steady above your chest.
Press the barbell back to the starting position with control and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your shoulder blades pulled back and pressed into the bench, and your feet firmly planted on the floor for stability.
Maintain a straight bar path over your chest throughout the movement.
Keep the barbell just above your chest without letting it touch to maintain tension on the triceps. Pause briefly at the bottom of each repetition before pressing upward.
Inhale as you lower the barbell and exhale as you press it upward.
ex_C2MIKW.description: Barbell Spoto Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Core.

ex_IELJPF.name: Barbell Wide Bench Press
instructions: Lie flat on a bench with your feet firmly planted on the floor. Hold a barbell with an overhand grip (palms facing forward), hands placed wider than shoulder-width apart. Position the barbell directly above your chest with your arms fully extended.
Slowly lower the barbell to your chest by bending your elbows, keeping them at a 45-degree angle to your body.
Once the barbell lightly touches your chest, push the barbell back up to the starting position by extending your arms fully.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your chest up and shoulders retracted throughout the movement to maximize chest engagement.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you press the barbell up and inhaling as you lower it back down.
Keep your feet firmly planted on the floor for stability and support.
ex_IELJPF.description: Barbell Wide Bench Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

ex_MHNB2F.name: Bodyweight Standing Fly
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms extended out to the sides, bent at 90 degrees, elbows at shoulder height.
Bring your arms together in front of your body until your forearms meet.
Open your arms back out to the sides to return to the starting position.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your movements are smooth and controlled to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears to avoid tension.
Focus on squeezing your chest muscles as you bring your arms together to enhance muscle activation.
ex_MHNB2F.description: Bodyweight Standing Fly is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_6K7N3T.name: Bodyweight Svend Press
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your hands pressed together close to your chest, elbows bent.
Extend your arms straight out in front of you, keeping your hands pressed together.
Bring your hands back to your chest, bending your elbows to return to the starting position.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Maintain a firm press of your hands together to engage your chest muscles throughout the exercise.
Keep your core engaged to maintain stability and balance.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
ex_6K7N3T.description: Bodyweight Svend Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Shoulders.

ex_KHTWIP.name: Cable Bench Fly Press
instructions: Lie on a flat bench positioned between two cable machines, with the cables set at a low position. Grasp the handles with your arms bent and hands close to your chest sides.
Press the handles upward in an arc motion over your chest, extending your arms upward.
Lower the handles back down to the starting position, stopping when your hands are close to your chest sides.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you press the handles up and inhale as you lower them back down.
Ensure your back remains flat against the bench and avoid arching your spine.
Focus on the contraction of your chest muscles as you press the handles up.
ex_KHTWIP.description: Cable Bench Fly Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

ex_SNXE7T.name: Cable Core Palloff Press
instructions: Stand sideways to a cable machine with your feet shoulder width apart and hold the handle with both hands at chest level.
Press the handle straight forward until your arms are fully extended while resisting the cable's pull.
Pause briefly with your arms extended and keep your torso stable without rotating.
Bring the handle back to your chest with control and repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching sides.
tips: Keep your torso upright and avoid rotating during the movement.
Brace your core before pressing the handle forward.
Maintain a slight bend in your knees for better stability.
Inhale as you bring the handle toward your chest and exhale as you press it forward.
ex_SNXE7T.description: Cable Core Palloff Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Forearms.

ex_MJ6GZE.name: Cable Fly Machine Mid
instructions: Set both pulleys at chest height and stand in the middle holding a handle in each hand.
Step forward with a slight bend in your elbows and your arms open to the sides.
Bring the handles together in front of your chest in a wide arc.
Return slowly to the stretched position and repeat.
tips: Keep the elbow angle fixed throughout.
Squeeze your chest when the handles meet.
ex_MJ6GZE.description: Cable Fly Machine Mid is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Front Shoulders.

ex_DZK6MR.name: Cable Low Fly
instructions: Stand in the center of a cable machine with the pulleys set at a low position. Grasp the handles with your palms facing forward and arms extended down out to your sides. Position your feet shoulder-width apart and slightly staggered for stability.
Stand upright with your back straight. Bring the handles together in front of your body in a wide arc, keeping a slight bend in your elbows and palms should face upwards.
Slowly return the handles to the starting position with control, maintaining the slight bend in your elbows.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on the contraction of your chest muscles as you bring the handles together.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and reduce the risk of injury.
Exhale as you bring the handles together and inhale as you return them to the starting position.
ex_DZK6MR.description: Cable Low Fly is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Biceps.

ex_PES5PV.name: Cable Lying Fly
instructions: Lie on a flat bench between a dual crossover machine and your feet flat on the floor. Grasp the handles with your palms facing up and arms extended to the sides at chest level.
Raise the handles over your chest in a wide arc motion, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Return to the starting position by lowering the handles out to your sides in a wide arc motion.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on the contraction of your chest muscles as you bring the handles together.
Start with a lighter weight to ensure proper form and gradually increase the resistance as you build strength.
Make sure the bench is stable and positioned securely between the cable machines.
ex_PES5PV.description: Cable Lying Fly is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps.

ex_IJ3PRE.name: Cable Machine High to Low
instructions: Stand in the center of a cable machine with the pulleys set at a high position. Grasp the handles with your palms facing forward and arms extended down out to your sides. Position your feet shoulder-width apart and slightly staggered for stability.
Stand upright with your back straight. Bring the handles together in front of your body in a wide arc, keeping a slight bend in your elbows and palms should face upwards.
Slowly return the handles to the starting position with control, maintaining the slight bend in your elbows.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on the contraction of your chest muscles as you bring the handles together.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and reduce the risk of injury.
Exhale as you bring the handles together and inhale as you return them to the starting position.

ex_HWADG7.name: Push Up and Rotation
instructions: Begin in a plank position with your hands placed shoulder-width apart and your feet together. Your body should form a straight line from head to heels.

ex_MLXWWY.name: Smith Machine Press Incline
instructions: Position an incline bench under the smith machine. Adjust the bench so that the barbell is at chest height when lying on the bench.
Lie on the incline bench with your feet flat on the floor. Grip the barbell with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the barbell and lower it to your chest until it slightly touches it.
Press the barbell back to the starting position, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily, exhaling as you press the barbell up and inhaling as you lower it down.
Ensure your feet are firmly set on the floor for balance and support.
Focus on using your chest muscles to press the weight, avoiding excessive strain on your shoulders.
ex_MLXWWY.description: Smith Machine Press Incline is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a smith machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

ex_GTJLVY.name: Suspension Trainer With Grips Chest Fly
instructions: Adjust the suspension trainer handles to about waist height. Stand facing away from the anchor point with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handles with your palms facing each other.
Engage your core and lean forward, extending your arms straight to the sides to form a T-shape. Your body should be in a straight line from head to heels.
Slowly bring your hands together in front of your chest by squeezing your chest muscles, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Return to the starting position by allowing your arms to extend back to the sides with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily: exhale as you bring your hands together and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Focus on using your chest muscles to bring your hands together, avoiding excessive use of your arms.
Keep your core tight to maintain a straight body line and avoid sagging your hips.
ex_GTJLVY.description: Suspension Trainer With Grips Chest Fly is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a suspension trainer, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back, Core.

ex_RN6PM7.name: Suspension Trainer With Grips Decline Push-Up
instructions: Adjust the suspension trainer handles to about knee height. Place your feet in the handles, ensuring they are secure, and assume a plank position with your hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width apart on the floor.
Engage your core, keeping your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Bend your elbows and lower your chest towards the floor, keeping your elbows at a 45-degree angle to your body.
Push through your hands to return to the starting position, straightening your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily: exhale as you push up and inhale as you lower down.
Focus on using your chest and triceps muscles to push yourself up, avoiding excessive use of your shoulders.
Ensure your feet are securely placed in the suspension trainer handles to prevent slipping.
ex_RN6PM7.description: Suspension Trainer With Grips Decline Push-Up is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a suspension trainer, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Shoulders, Core.

ex_PMQWU3.name: Suspension Trainer With Grips Push-Up to Side Plank
instructions: Adjust the suspension trainer handles to about knee height. Place your feet in the handles and assume a push-up position with your hands placed directly under your shoulders, arms fully extended, and body in a straight line from head to heels.
Perform a push-up by bending your elbows and lowering your chest towards the floor while keeping your body straight.
Push back up to the starting position and rotate your body to the right as you reach the top, extending your right arm towards the ceiling to enter a side plank position.
Return to the push-up position and repeat the movement, rotating to the left for the side plank. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Perform the exercise on a non-slip surface to avoid slipping.
Focus on smooth transitions between the push-up and side plank for fluid motion.
Maintain even breathing to help keep your movements controlled and steady.
ex_PMQWU3.description: Suspension Trainer With Grips Push-Up to Side Plank is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a suspension trainer, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Upper Back.

ex_QGABHG.name: Suspension Trainer With Grips Reverse Push-Up
instructions: Adjust the suspension trainer handles close to the floor. Grasp the handles with an underhand grip (palms facing forward) and position your body in a straight line, feet together and arms fully extended.
Engage your core and maintain a straight line from your head to your heels.
Lower your chest towards the handles by bending your elbows, keeping your body straight and elbows close to your sides.
Press through your hands to extend your arms and return to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Perform the movement with a steady and controlled tempo to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Breathe steadily: exhale as you push up and inhale as you lower your body.
Ensure your wrists are under your shoulders to maintain proper alignment.
ex_QGABHG.description: Suspension Trainer With Grips Reverse Push-Up is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a suspension trainer, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Abdominals, Upper Back.

ex_DJICIK.name: Svend Press Decline Bench
instructions: Lie on a decline bench with your feet secured under the foot pads and your back firmly against the bench. Hold a weight plate with both hands, pressing your palms against the flat sides of the plate at chest level with your fingers pointing up.
Engage your chest and press the weight plate straight out in front of you by extending your arms.
Squeeze your chest muscles as you press the plate outward until your arms are fully extended.
Slowly bring the plate back to your chest with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on pressing through your chest, not your shoulders, to emphasize chest muscle activation.
Choose a weight that challenges you but allows you to maintain proper form.
Avoid locking your elbows completely at the top of the movement to keep tension on the chest muscles.
ex_DJICIK.description: Svend Press Decline Bench is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

ex_QKFLTP.name: Wide Push Ups Bodyweight
instructions: Begin in a plank position with your hands placed wider than shoulder-width apart and your feet together. Your body should form a straight line from head to heels.
Engage your chest and lower your body towards the floor by bending your elbows, keeping them at a 90-degree angle to your body.
Lower your chest until it is just above the floor.
Push through your hands to raise your body back to the starting position, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your elbows at a 90-degree angle to your body to maximize chest and triceps engagement and reduce shoulder strain.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you push up and inhaling as you lower yourself.
Keep your head aligned with your spine to avoid straining your neck.
ex_QKFLTP.description: Wide Push Ups Bodyweight is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

ex_MNYYC6.name: Barbell Standing Back Wrist Curl
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell behind your back with an overhand grip (palms facing backward), hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Your arms should be fully extended, and the barbell should rest against your glutes.
Flex your wrists to curl the barbell upward, bringing the barbell toward your forearms.
Hold the contraction at the top for a moment, squeezing your forearm muscles.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position by extending your wrists. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid using your arms or shoulders to lift the barbell; focus on your wrist movement.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you curl the barbell up and inhaling as you lower it back down.
Use a weight that allows for proper form and control throughout the exercise to prevent strain or injury.
ex_MNYYC6.description: Barbell Standing Back Wrist Curl is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

ex_YK3JNI.name: Barbell Wrist Curl Wide Legs
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet spread wide apart, holding a barbell with an underhand grip (palms facing up), hands placed shoulder-width apart. Rest your forearms on the edge of the bench, allowing your wrists to hang over the edge.
Start with your wrists extended so the barbell is lowered as much as possible.
Curl the barbell upward by flexing your wrists, lifting the barbell as high as possible while keeping your forearms stationary on your thighs.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position by extending your wrists. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your forearms stationary on your thighs to isolate your wrist flexors.
Avoid using your elbows to lift the barbell; focus on your wrist movement.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you curl the barbell up and inhaling as you lower it back down.
ex_YK3JNI.description: Barbell Wrist Curl Wide Legs is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

ex_LZYAGB.name: Barbell Wrist Curl on Knees
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor, holding a barbell with an underhand grip (palms facing up), hands placed shoulder-width apart. Rest your forearms on your thighs, allowing your wrists to hang over the edge.
Start with your wrists extended so the barbell is lowered as much as possible while maintaining control.
Curl the barbell upward by flexing your wrists, lifting the barbell as high as possible while keeping your forearms stationary on your thighs.

ex_GVORBD.name: Barbell Wrist Extension on Knees
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor, holding a barbell with an overhand grip (palms facing down), hands placed shoulder-width apart. Rest your forearms on your thighs, allowing your wrists to hang over the edge.
Start with your wrists relaxed so the barbell hangs as much as possible.
Extend the barbell upward by extending your wrists, raising the barbell as far as possible while keeping your forearms stationary on your thighs.
Slowly bring the barbell back to the starting position by relaxing your wrists. Repeat for the desired repetitions.
tips: Keep your forearms stationary on your thighs to isolate your wrist extensors.

ex_GVORBD.description: Barbell Wrist Extension on Knees is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

ex_ABE3NP.name: Cable Wrist Curl
instructions: Sit on a bench facing the cable machine with a straight bar attached to the low pulley. Grasp the bar with both hands using an underhand grip (palms facing up), hands shoulder-width apart.
Rest your forearms on your thighs with your wrists just beyond your knees, allowing the bar to hang down.
Curl the bar upwards by flexing your wrists, bringing the bar towards your forearms.
Slowly lower the bar back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your forearms stationary on your thighs throughout the exercise.
Focus on squeezing your forearms at the top of the movement.
Exhale as you curl the bar up and inhale as you lower it back down.
ex_ABE3NP.description: Cable Wrist Curl is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps.

ex_HWKRRW.name: Cable Wrist Extension
instructions: Stand sideways, facing away from a low cable pulley and hold the handle with one hand using an underhand grip. Bend your elbow to approximately 90 degrees and keep it tucked against your side with your forearm stationary.
Extend your hand at the wrist joint, moving your hand downward while keeping the rest of your arm still. Pause for 1 - 2 seconds.
Curl the weight by flexing at the wrist joint, bringing your hand upward. Pause for 1 - 2 seconds.
Slowly lower your hand back to the starting position with control and repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching sides.
tips: Keep your elbow tucked against your side throughout the exercise.
Move only at your wrist while keeping your forearm still.
Use a controlled range of motion without forcing your wrist beyond a comfortable position.
Inhale as you lower your hand and exhale as you raise it.
ex_HWKRRW.description: Cable Wrist Extension is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Core.

ex_BJSSAP.name: Dumbbell Lying Pronation Rotation on Floor
instructions: Lie on your side on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat. Support your head with the lower hand. Hold a dumbbell in the top hand with your elbow resting on your side, bent at a 90-degree angle, and your palm facing your head.
Slowly rotate your forearm, turning your palm down toward the knees while keeping your upper arm and elbow stationary.
Rotate your forearm back to the starting position with control, ensuring the movement is smooth and steady. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.
tips: Keep your upper arm and elbow stable throughout the exercise.
Avoid using excessive weight to ensure proper form and prevent strain on the wrist and elbow.
Focus on a slow and controlled rotation to maximize muscle engagement.
ex_BJSSAP.description: Dumbbell Lying Pronation Rotation on Floor is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

ex_M5HGRE.name: Dumbbell One Arm Reverse Wrist Curl
instructions: Sit on a bench with your forearm resting on your thigh, palm facing down, holding a dumbbell with an overhand grip (palm facing down).
Allow your wrist to extend downward so that the dumbbell hangs towards the floor, keeping your forearm stationary.
Curl the dumbbell upward as high as possible by flexing your wrist, focusing on engaging your forearm muscles.
Lower the dumbbell back to the starting position with control, fully extending your wrist. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.
tips: Keep your forearm stable and only move your wrist.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to avoid using momentum.
Focus on using your forearm muscles to lift the weight.
ex_M5HGRE.description: Dumbbell One Arm Reverse Wrist Curl is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps.

ex_54YGVO.name: Dumbbell One Arm Seated Neutral Wrist Curl
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor. Hold a dumbbell in your right hand with a neutral grip.
Place your right forearm on your right thigh, allowing your wrist to extend beyond your knee. Keep your left hand resting on your left thigh for support.
Curl the dumbbell upward by flexing your wrist, squeezing your forearm muscles at the top of the movement.
Lower the dumbbell back to the starting position with control, extending your wrist. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Use a controlled motion to avoid using momentum.
Maintain a neutral grip throughout the exercise.
ex_54YGVO.description: Dumbbell One Arm Seated Neutral Wrist Curl is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category.

ex_HZ77C6.name: Dumbbell Over Bench Reverse Wrist Curl
instructions: Kneel on the floor in front of a bench, placing both forearms over the bench while holding a dumbbell with an overhand grip (palm facing down).

Curl the dumbbells upward by flexing your wrists, lifting the weight as high as possible while keeping your forearms flat on the bench.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position, fully extending your wrists. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your forearms pressed firmly against the bench to isolate the wrist movement.
Use a controlled motion to lift and lower the dumbbells, avoiding any jerking movements.
Avoid using your shoulder or upper arm to lift the weight.
ex_HZ77C6.description: Dumbbell Over Bench Reverse Wrist Curl is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

ex_H6IHNH.name: Alternate Heel Touch Side Kick Squat
instructions: Stand tall with your back straight, arms by your side, and feet shoulder-width apart.
Lower your hips by bending one of your knees while sliding the opposite leg outward on the floor, and touch your heel with your hands.
Return to the initial position, and do the same while bending your other knee and sliding the opposite leg.

instructions: Stand tall with your back straight and your feet shoulder-width apart.

instructions: Sit or lie with your legs straight.

ex_DMTESX.name: Assisted Bulgarian Split Squat
instructions: Stand facing away from an elevated box and place your right foot on it. Hold onto a stable bar or support in front of you with your right hand. Keep your chest upright and your front foot flat on the floor.
Lower your body by bending your front knee and hip until your back knee is close to the floor.
Pause for a second at the bottom and push through the heel of your front foot to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired repetitions, then switch legs and repeat.
tips: Use the support only for balance, not to pull yourself up.

ex_HNO7AO.name: Assisted Pistol Squats
instructions: Stand upright while holding onto a sturdy equipment with both hands for balance. Extend one leg straight forward and keep it off the floor while the other leg remains on the floor.
Lower yourself slowly by bending the standing leg at the hip and knee, keeping your chest up and your extended leg straight in front of you.
Descend until your glutes are close to your heel and then push through the heel of your planted foot to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired repetitions, then switch legs and repeat.
tips: Lower yourself slowly and avoid collapsing at the bottom of the squat to avoid injury.
Extend your non-working leg fully in front of you and keep it parallel to the floor.

ex_WBL2CK.name: Back and Forward Leg Swings
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and use a nearby support (such as a squat cage, wall or a chair) for balance.
Swing your right leg forward and backward in a controlled, rhythmic manner.
After completing the desired number of swings with your right leg, switch to your left leg and repeat the movement.

Ensure your upper body remains upright and avoid leaning forward or backward.

ex_DLXF5O.name: Ball Headlock Squat
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold an exercise ball to your side with one arm wrapped around it as if in a headlock. Extend the opposite arm in front of you for balance.

Descend until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor and then push through your heels to return to the starting position.

ex_DSC6CJ.name: Band Cross Abduction
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and place the resistance band under both feet, crossing the band in front of you. Hold the handles of the band in opposite hands with arms hanging in front of your hips.
Keeping your right leg straight, lift it sideways away from your body until your leg is fully extended to the side.
Slowly lower your leg back to the starting position with control, keeping tension in the band.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the left leg.
tips: Ensure the resistance band is securely placed under your feet and properly crossed to avoid slipping.
Keep your upper body stationary and avoid leaning to the side.

ex_UBUZZY.name: Band Hip Adduction
instructions: Secure one end of the resistance band to a stable anchor and attach the other end around the ankle closest to the anchor.

Sweep the banded leg inward across the front of your body while keeping your torso upright and your movement controlled.
Slowly return your leg to the starting position without letting the band pull it back, then repeat before switching sides.
tips: Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning to either side.
Maintain a slight bend in your supporting knee for better stability. Keep the working leg straight or slightly bent throughout the movement.

instructions: Stand a few feet in front of a bench or elevated surface, facing away from it. Place your right foot behind you on the bench, with the top of your foot resting on the surface.
Position your left foot firmly on the floor, a comfortable distance in front of the bench.
Lower your body by bending your left knee and hip, keeping your torso upright, until your left thigh is parallel to the floor.
Push through your left heel to return to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
tips: Keep your front knee aligned with your toes to avoid putting unnecessary strain on your knee.
Focus on driving through the heel of your front foot to engage your glutes and quadriceps effectively.
Maintain a slight forward lean to help with balance and ensure proper form throughout the exercise.
ex_PUHV27.description: Bodyweight Bulgarian Split Squat (Left, Side View) is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

ex_XGGRBT.name: Burpee Squat
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms at your sides, ready to begin the movement.
Lower your body into a squat position and place your hands on the floor in front of you.
Step your right foot back, then your left foot, to land in a plank position, keeping your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Step your right foot forward, then your left foot, to return to the squat position, then stand up and repeat.
tips: Start with a moderate pace to master the form, then gradually increase your speed as you become more comfortable with the movement.
Engage your core to maintain stability and support your lower back throughout the exercise.
Focus on keeping your knees aligned with your toes during the squat to prevent unnecessary strain on your joints.
ex_XGGRBT.description: Burpee Squat is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

ex_FA7MZR.name: Cable Assisted Inverse Leg Curl
instructions: Kneel on the seat of a cable pulldown machine with both legs secured under the thigh pads. Face away from the machine and hold the cable bar behind your neck with both hands.
Lean forward to straighten your legs until your torso is almost parallel to the floor.
Slowly return to the starting position by bringing your upper body back up, bending at the knees.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and reduce the risk of injury.
Avoid using momentum; focus on the controlled contraction of your hamstrings.
Exhale as you straighten your legs and inhale as you return to the starting position.
ex_FA7MZR.description: Cable Assisted Inverse Leg Curl is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Lower Back, Abdominals.

ex_W5BUVQ.name: Cable Calve Raise
instructions: Stand facing a low cable pulley with a straight bar attachment, with your feet hip-width apart, holding the bar in front of your hips with both hands.
Push through your forefeet to raise your heels as high as possible.
Pause for a second at the peak of the movement and then slowly lower your heels back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired repetitions.
tips: Focus on moving only at the ankles to isolate your calves.
Keep your knees slightly bent and avoid locking them out to minimize knee stress.
Hold the top position for a second to maximize contraction.
ex_W5BUVQ.description: Cable Calve Raise is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shins.

ex_NN32EP.name: Cable Goblet Squat
instructions: Stand upright facing the cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a bar attachment with both hands at chest level with elbows facing the floor.
Begin squatting by bending your hips and knees, descend into a deep squat until your thighs are parallel to the ground or lower.
Push through your heels to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired repetitions.
tips: Keep your elbows pointed down and tucked in to stabilize the bar during the squat.
Engage your core to protect your lower back and maintain balance.
Ensure your knees track in line with your toes as you descend.
ex_NN32EP.description: Cable Goblet Squat is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves, Lower Back.

ex_C67LID.name: Cable Hamstring Curl
instructions: Attach an ankle strap to a low pulley and secure it around your working ankle, then stand upright facing the machine and hold onto a stable surface or clasp your hands together for balance.
Keep your upper body stationary and your knees aligned as you slowly bend your working knee, curling your foot up toward your glutes.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, focusing on squeezing your hamstring.
Lower your foot back down to the starting position with control and repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching legs.
tips: Squeeze your hamstring at the top of the curl for peak contraction.
Adjust the weight appropriately to maintain proper form throughout the set.
Maintain a slight bend in your standing leg for better stability.
ex_C67LID.description: Cable Hamstring Curl is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Calves.

ex_IZFMME.name: Cable Individual Glute Kickbacks
instructions: Attach an ankle strap to a low pulley on a cable machine and secure it around one ankle. Stand facing the machine and hold onto the handles or frame for support while keeping your torso leaning slightly forward.
Engage your core and shift your weight onto the stationary leg while slightly bending the knee of the supporting leg.
Extend the strapped leg straight back in a controlled motion, squeezing your glute at the top without hyperextending your lower back.
Slowly return your leg to the starting position without letting the weight stack touch, and repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching sides.
tips: Perform each repetition with slow and controlled motion to maximize glute engagement.
Avoid swinging your leg or using momentum to lift the weight.
Focus on squeezing the glute at the top of the movement for better muscle activation.
ex_IZFMME.description: Cable Individual Glute Kickbacks is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Core, Lower Back.

ex_IXSEH2.name: Cable Narrow Chair Stand-Up
instructions: Attach a rope to the low pulley on the machine. Grasp the end of the rope in each hand and bring it close to your chest.Feet close together, flat on the floor, knees bent at a 90-degree angle.
Push through your heels and extend your legs to stand up, keeping the handles close to your chest.
Slowly lower yourself back down to the seated position, controlling the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on pushing through your heels to engage your glutes and quads effectively.
Exhale as you stand up and inhale as you sit back down.
Ensure your back remains straight and avoid rounding your spine.
ex_IXSEH2.description: Cable Narrow Chair Stand-Up is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Core.

ex_RWAX66.name: Cable Pull Through
instructions: Stand in the middle of a cable pulley machine with a rope attached at a low position. Hold the handles between your thighs with your back facing the machine, and the cables extending back.
Spread your feet just wider than shoulder-width, lean forward, bending at the hips and knees into a semi-squat position, while keeping your back straight and your arms extended.
Extend your hips forward to straighten your body, pushing the handles with your thighs.
Return to the starting semi-squat position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid using your lower back to lift; the movement should come from your hips.
Focus on engaging your glutes and hamstrings as you extend your hips.
Exhale as you extend your hips forward and inhale as you return to the starting position.
ex_RWAX66.description: Cable Pull Through is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Core.

ex_NZP66U.name: Cable Single Leg Deadlift
instructions: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley and stand facing the cable while holding the bar with both hands. Shift your weight onto your right leg, keeping it bent at 90 degrees.
Slightly bend your standing knee and hinge at the hips to lower your torso to the floor.
Once your torso is nearly parallel to the floor. Drive through your standing leg to return to the starting position
Lower your foot to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired repetitions, switch legs, and repeat.
tips: Maintain a neutral spine throughout the entire movement to avoid lower back strain.
Keep your hips square to the floor and avoid rotating your torso as you hinge forward.
Engage your core to help stabilize your balance during the single-leg movement.
ex_NZP66U.description: Cable Single Leg Deadlift is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Abdominals.

ex_LOMBEH.name: Cable Split Squat
instructions: Stand in front of a low pulley cable machine with a bar attached and grab it with both hands using an overhand grip. Take a step back into a split stance with one foot forward and one foot behind.
Hold the bar extended along the cable and keep your torso upright.
Lower your body by bending both knees until your thigh is parallel to the floor. Push through your front heel to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired repetitions.
tips: Keep your front knee aligned with your ankle throughout the movement.
Lower yourself slowly to avoid unnecessary strain on the knee joint.
Avoid locking out the knees at the top to keep muscles under tension.
ex_LOMBEH.description: Cable Split Squat is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings.

ex_G5UV6X.name: Calf Raise Clap
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms extended out to the sides at shoulder level.
Lift your heels off the floor as high as possible while simultaneously bringing your arms forward to clap, keeping them straight.
Lower your heels back to the floor and return your arms to the starting position.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your head up and eyes forward to maintain proper alignment and balance.
Squeeze your calf muscles fully at the top of the movement for maximum benefit.
Focus on keeping your arms straight and level with your shoulders throughout the exercise to maintain proper form.
ex_G5UV6X.description: Calf Raise Clap is an advanced single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Shoulders.

ex_WFO5IM.name: Calf Raise From Deficit With Chair Supported
instructions: Stand on the edge of a raised platform or step, with your heels hanging off the edge, and hold onto a chair for support.
Position your feet hip-width apart, ensuring your toes are firmly on the platform.
Slowly raise your heels as high as possible, engaging your calf muscles and lifting your body.
Lower your heels back down past the edge of the platform to feel a stretch in your calves. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Use the chair for balance but avoid leaning on it heavily to ensure your legs are doing the work.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Ensure your heels drop below the platform to achieve a full range of motion and stretch.
ex_WFO5IM.description: Calf Raise From Deficit With Chair Supported is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps.

ex_I6VEL7.name: Calf Raise Leg Press Machine
instructions: Sit on the leg press machine and position your feet shoulder-width apart on the higher portion of the footplate with your toes pointing up.
Press the footplate by extending your legs and keeping a slight bend in your knees.
Push through your forefeet to raise the footplate as much as possible, squeezing your calf muscles.
Slowly lower your forefeet down to the starting position. Repeat for the desired repetitions.
tips: Keep your legs slightly bent throughout the exercise to avoid placing stress on your knees.
Focus on a full range of motion, pushing your forefeet as much as possible for deep muscle activation.
Exhale as you raise your heels and inhale as you lower them back down.
ex_I6VEL7.description: Calf Raise Leg Press Machine is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Quadriceps.

ex_K3Z4SI.name: Calf Raise With Wall Support
instructions: Stand facing a wall with your feet hip-width apart. Place your hands on the wall at shoulder height for support.
Position your feet flat on the floor, ensuring they are parallel to each other.
Slowly raise your heels as high as possible, lifting your body and engaging your calf muscles.
Lower your heels back to the floor in a controlled manner. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on lifting your heels fully and pausing briefly at the top of the movement to maximize muscle activation.
Use the wall for balance but ensure your legs are doing the work.
Keep your knees slightly bent to reduce strain on your joints.
ex_K3Z4SI.description: Calf Raise With Wall Support is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps.

ex_67BLPO.name: Calf Raise on Hack Squat Machine
instructions: Stand on the hack squat machine with your shoulders under the pads and your feet hips-width apart on the foot platform, with your toes pointing forward and your heels hanging off the edge.
Extend your legs to release the safety handles, keeping a slight bend in your knees.
Push through your forefeet to raise your heels as high as possible, squeezing your calf muscles at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your legs slightly bent throughout the exercise to avoid placing stress on your knees.
Focus on a full range of motion, lowering your heels as much as possible for a deep muscle activation.
Exhale as you raise your heels and inhale as you lower them back down.
ex_67BLPO.description: Calf Raise on Hack Squat Machine is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Quadriceps.

ex_CMIZIB.name: Chair Back Lunge Left Resistance Band
instructions: Attach one end of a resistance band to a sturdy chair or similar support and the other end to your left ankle. Stand facing the chair with your right foot firmly planted on the floor.

Step back with your left foot, keeping your right foot in place, and lower your body into a lunge position by bending both knees, ensuring your right knee is directly above your right ankle and your left knee is hovering just above the floor.
Push through your right heel to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
tips: Use a lighter resistance band if needed to ensure proper form and gradually increase the resistance as you get stronger.
Focus on keeping your front knee aligned over your ankle to avoid putting excess strain on your knee joint.
Maintain balance by keeping your hands steady and holding the chair.
ex_CMIZIB.description: Chair Back Lunge Left Resistance Band is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

ex_6OLOT4.name: Chair Elevated Single Leg Glute Bridge
instructions: Lie on your back with your left heel placed on the edge of a chair, your right leg extended bent up towards the ceiling.
Position your arms by your sides with your palms facing down for stability.
Engage your core and glutes to lift your hips off the floor.
Hold the position briefly at the top, squeezing your glutes, then slowly lower your hips back to the floor. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
tips: Ensure your heel remains firmly on the chair to provide a stable base for the movement.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.

instructions: Lie on your back with both heels placed on the edge of a chair, legs bent at a 90-degree angle.
Position your arms by your sides with your palms facing down for stability.
Engage your core and glutes, then lift your hips off the floor.
Hold the position briefly at the top, squeezing your glutes, then slowly lower your hips back to the floor. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your heels remain firmly on the chair to provide a stable base for the movement.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.

ex_NEKYLZ.name: Chair Frog Feet Elevated Glute Bridge Bodyweight
instructions: Lie on your back with your heels placed on the edge of a chair, legs bent, and the soles of your feet touching each other in a frog position.
Position your arms by your sides with your palms facing down for stability.
Engage your core and glutes to lift your hips off the floor until your body forms a straight line from your shoulders to your knees.
Hold the position briefly at the top, squeezing your glutes, then slowly lower your hips back to the floor. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your heels remain firmly on the chair to provide a stable base for the movement.
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you lift your hips and inhaling as you lower them.
Focus on squeezing your glutes at the top of the movement to enhance muscle engagement.
