ex_EJDZBD.name: Clamshell
instructions: Lie on your side with your legs stacked, knees bent at about 90 degrees, and your hips aligned. Rest your head on your bottom arm and place your top hand on your hip for support.
Keep your feet together and your core engaged.
Raise your top knee upward as far as possible without rotating your hips or lifting your feet off each other. Pause briefly at the top of the movement.
Lower your knee back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
tips: Keep your hips stacked and avoid rolling your body backward as you lift your knee.
Engage your core throughout to stabilize your torso.
Use slow, controlled movements to maintain constant tension on the muscles.
ex_EJDZBD.description: Clamshell is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hips.

ex_H7PJWO.name: Clap Curtsy Squat
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms extended straight overhead, palms facing each other.
Step your right foot behind and across your left leg, bending both knees to lower into a curtsy squat while simultaneously lower your hands in circular motion to your sides.
Push through your left heel to return to the starting position, extending your right leg back to shoulder-width apart and bringing your arms back overhead and clap them together.
Repeat the movement on the opposite side. Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on keeping your chest lifted and your back straight to avoid leaning forward.
Perform the movement slowly and with control, especially when lowering into the curtsy squat, to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Ensure your front knee stays aligned with your front foot and does not extend past your toes.
ex_H7PJWO.description: Clap Curtsy Squat is an advanced multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Adductors.

ex_MSJMSA.name: Cossack Squat
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart and your toes pointing slightly outward.
Shift your weight to your right leg, bending your right knee while keeping your left leg straight. Lower your hips towards the floor, ensuring your right knee tracks over your right toes.

Push through your right heel to return to the starting position, then repeat the movement on the left side by shifting your weight to your left leg and bending your left knee. Alternate sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on maintaining an upright chest and straight back to ensure proper form and prevent injury.
Perform the movement with control, especially when shifting your weight and lowering your hips, to maximize muscle activation.
Ensure your knee tracks over your toes during the squat to avoid unnecessary strain on your joints.
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you descend and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
ex_MSJMSA.description: Cossack Squat is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Adductors, Calves.

ex_AZPTR7.name: Counterbalanced Skater Squat
instructions: Stand tall on your right foot, curl your left leg to 90 degrees, and extend your arms forward.
Lower your hips while bending your right knee, lean forward, and maintain balance by moving your left thigh backward.
Hold this position for a while, return to the initial position, and repeat.
tips: Keep your core engaged throughout the exercise to maintain stability and balance.
Focus on maintaining an upright chest and straight back to ensure proper form and prevent injury.
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you lower into the squat and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
Ensure your knee tracks over your toes during the squat to avoid unnecessary strain on your joints.
ex_AZPTR7.description: Counterbalanced Skater Squat is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Adductors, Calves.

ex_WLBOEH.name: Crossed Arms Front Leg Kick
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms crossed in front of your chest.
Engage your core and lift your right leg straight in front of you to perform a front kick, keeping your leg as straight as possible.
Lower your right leg back to the starting position.
Immediately lift your left leg to perform a front kick, keeping your arms crossed and your core engaged. Continue alternating legs for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on maintaining an upright posture, avoiding leaning back or forward as you kick.
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you kick and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
Ensure your kicks are performed with a controlled motion, avoiding any jerky movements.
ex_WLBOEH.description: Crossed Arms Front Leg Kick is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abdominals.

ex_B7C44T.name: Curtsy Lunge Bodyweight
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet hip-width apart and your hands on your hips or by your sides.
Step your right leg behind and across your left leg, bending both knees to lower into a curtsy lunge. Your front knee should be aligned with your front ankle.
Push through your left heel to return to the starting position.
Repeat the movement on the opposite side, stepping your left leg behind and across your right leg. Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your torso upright throughout the exercise to maintain balance and proper form.
Ensure your front knee does not extend beyond your toes to protect your knees from strain.
Focus on pushing through your heel as you return to the starting position to engage your glutes.
ex_B7C44T.description: Curtsy Lunge Bodyweight is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Adductors.

ex_OBNLUO.name: Curtsy Lunge Slide With Towel
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet hip-width apart and place a towel under your right foot.
Slide your right foot behind and across your left leg, bending both knees to lower into a curtsy lunge. Your front knee should be aligned with your front ankle.
Push through your left heel to return to the starting position, sliding your right foot back to the original position.
Complete the desired number of repetitions on one side, then switch the towel to the other foot and repeat the movement with the opposite leg.
tips: Perform the movement with control to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Ensure your front knee does not extend beyond your toes to protect your knees from strain.
Focus on pushing through your heel as you return to the starting position to engage your glutes.
Use a smooth surface to ensure the towel slides easily and reduces friction.
ex_OBNLUO.description: Curtsy Lunge Slide With Towel is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Adductors.

ex_QJZE7N.name: Curtsy Lunges Resistance Band
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and place a resistance band under your left foot. Hold the handles of the band with both hands either at shoulder height or by your abdomen sides.
Step your right leg behind and across your left leg, while bending both knees to lower into a lunge.
Push through your left heel to return to the starting position, bringing your right leg back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides to work the other leg.
tips: Keep your chest up and your back straight to maintain proper form.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and reduce injury risk.
Exhale as you push back to the starting position and inhale as you lower into the lunge.
ex_QJZE7N.description: Curtsy Lunges Resistance Band is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Hamstrings.

ex_W5HOH5.name: Curtsy Squat
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet hip-width apart and your hands on your hips or by your sides.

Step your right leg behind and across your left leg, bending both knees to lower into a curtsy squat. Your front knee should be aligned with your front ankle, and your back knee should point towards the floor.
Push through your left heel to return to the starting position.
Repeat the movement on the opposite side, stepping your left leg behind and across your right leg. Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Perform the movement with control to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Ensure your front knee does not extend beyond your toes to protect your knees from strain.
Focus on pushing through your heel as you return to the starting position to engage your glutes.
ex_W5HOH5.description: Curtsy Squat is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Adductors.

ex_KEBPPP.name: Diagonal Lunge
instructions: Stand with your feet together, arms extended outwards at shoulder level.

Step diagonally forward with your right foot, planting it at a 45-degree angle. As you lower into a lunge, rotate your torso to the right and lean down to touch your right foot with your left hand, keeping your left leg straight.
Press through your right heel and rotate back to center as you return to the starting position.
Repeat the movement with your left leg, stepping diagonally forward, rotating left, and touching your left foot with your right hand.
tips: Maintain your arms extended at shoulder level throughout the exercise to help with balance and increase the workout intensity.
Rotate your torso smoothly and keep your movements controlled to avoid any jerky motions that might cause injury.
Ensure that your lunging knee does not extend past your toes to protect your knee joint.
ex_KEBPPP.description: Diagonal Lunge is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Core, Adductors.

ex_UXAISB.name: Donkey Calf Raise
instructions: Stand on the edge of a step with your heels hanging off, placing your forefeet securely on the step.
Lean forward and reach down to hold onto a bench in front of you for stability, keeping your back straight and hips aligned with your feet.
Press down through your forefeet to elevate your heels as high as possible, fully contracting your calf muscles.
Slowly lower your heels below the level of the step to maximize the stretch in your calves before the next lift.
tips: Ensure your grip on the bench is secure to maintain balance and focus the effort on your calves.
Keep your back flat and avoid rounding your shoulders to prevent unnecessary strain on your back.
Emphasize the upward and downward movements equally to enhance muscle growth and strength in your calves.
Maintain a slow, controlled pace to increase the intensity of the muscle contraction and effectiveness of the exercise.
ex_UXAISB.description: Donkey Calf Raise is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings.

ex_AXQ7WG.name: Donkey Kicks Bodyweight
instructions: Begin on all fours in a tabletop position with your knees hip-width apart on the floor, hands under your shoulders, and your back flat.
Keeping your knee bent at a 90-degree angle, lift your right leg up towards the ceiling, driving your heel upward as if pushing against the sky.
Push your leg up until your thigh is in line with your body and your foot is above your knee.
Lower your leg slowly back to the starting position without letting your knee touch the floor. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions before switching to the left leg.
tips: Ensure your movements are controlled and deliberate to maximize glute activation and minimize momentum.
Keep your neck and spine in a neutral position by gazing down at the floor.
Avoid swinging your leg or using jerky movements; the power should come from your glutes and not from momentum.
ex_AXQ7WG.description: Donkey Kicks Bodyweight is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings.

ex_JXUIHM.name: Double Jump Squat
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your hands close together in front of your torso. Lower into a squat position by bending your knees and hips, keeping your chest up and your weight in your heels. Stand back up to the starting position.
Immediately lower into a squat again and then explosively jump up from the squat.
Land softly on your feet after the jump, repeat the sequence.
tips: Keep your chest up and back straight throughout the movement to maintain proper form and avoid injury.
Perform the jumps in a fluid motion, transitioning smoothly between the squats and jumps.
Focus on landing softly to reduce impact on your joints.
ex_JXUIHM.description: Double Jump Squat is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

ex_55EGD4.name: Dumbbell Bar Grip Sumo Squat
instructions: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly outward. Hold a dumbbell vertically with both hands, like holding a bar, in front of your hips.
Push your hips back and bend your knees to lower yourself until your thighs are parallel to the floor, keeping the dumbbell in line with your chest.
Push through your heels to return to the starting position, straightening your legs and squeezing your glutes at the top. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your knees follow the direction of your toes to avoid placing unnecessary stress on your joints.
Breathe in as you lower into the squat and breathe out as you push back up.
Maintain a slow and controlled movement to maximize muscle engagement and stability.
ex_55EGD4.description: Dumbbell Bar Grip Sumo Squat is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Adductors, Hamstrings.

ex_OCBV4W.name: Dumbbell Bench Squat
instructions: Stand with your back facing a bench with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Lower yourself into a squat by bending your knees and hips, keeping your chest up and back straight, until your thighs are parallel to the floor and your buttocks lightly touch the bench.
Push through your heels to stand back up to the starting position, fully extending your hips and knees.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining proper form throughout.

Breathe in as you lower into the squat and exhale as you push back up to the starting position.
Use a controlled, steady pace to maximize muscle engagement and maintain balance.
ex_OCBV4W.description: Dumbbell Bench Squat is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

ex_RI44M2.name: Dumbbell Bulgarian Box Split Squat
instructions: Stand a few feet, back first in front of a box, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your arms hanging by your sides. Place the top of one foot on the box behind you.
Lower your body by bending your front knee until your front thigh is parallel to the floor and your back knee is hovering just above the floor.
Push through your front heel to return to the starting position, keeping your back straight and core engaged.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs and repeat the movement on the other side.
tips: Start with a lighter weight to master the technique before progressing to heavier weights.
Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning forward or arching your back during the movement.

ex_RI44M2.description: Dumbbell Bulgarian Box Split Squat is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

Push through your front heel to return to the starting position, keeping your back straight and core engaged.

ex_VGZEAC.name: Dumbbell Farmer Walks
instructions: Begin by standing upright with a dumbbell in each hand, arms fully extended at your sides, and palms facing inward. Ensure your feet are hip-width apart.

ex_HPXEOD.name: Dumbbell Feet Elevated Figure Four Glute Bridge
instructions: Lie on your back and place the heel of one foot on an elevated surface. Cross your opposite ankle over the supporting thigh and hold a dumbbell securely across your hips.

ex_CSMIYU.name: Dumbbell Figure Four Glute Bridge

Lower your hips back to the starting position with control.

ex_CSMIYU.description: Dumbbell Figure Four Glute Bridge is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps.

ex_MTJFFU.name: Dumbbell Figure Four Hip Thrust
instructions: Sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench and place a dumbbell across your hips. Bend your knees and place your feet flat on the floor, then cross one ankle over the opposite knee in a figure four position.
Press through the heel of your grounded foot to lift your hips upward in a swift motion, extending your hips until your torso forms a straight line from your shoulders to your bent knee.

ex_HIZEYZ.description: Dumbbell Hip Thrust (Version 2) is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Quadriceps.

ex_JSAJGA.name: Dumbbell Hip Thrust
instructions: Sit on the floor with your upper back resting against a bench, knees bent, and feet flat on the floor. Hold a dumbbell with each hand across your hips.
Press through your heels to lift your hips upward until your body forms a straight line from your shoulders to your knees.
Hold the top position for a moment, ensuring your glutes are fully contracted.
Lower your hips back down to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Press through your heels to maximize glute activation.
Avoid arching your lower back; maintain a neutral spine.
Focus on squeezing your glutes at the top of the movement.
ex_JSAJGA.description: Dumbbell Hip Thrust is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Quadriceps.

ex_UXDJRO.name: Dumbbell Jumping Squat
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand by your sides. Keep your chest up, shoulders back, and core engaged.
Lower yourself into a squat position by bending your knees and hips, keeping your back straight and the dumbbells close to your body.
Explosively push through your heels to jump straight up into the air, extending your legs and keeping the dumbbells by your sides.
Land softly on your forefeet. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your knees track over your toes during the squat and landing phases to avoid strain on your joints.
Use a controlled motion when landing to minimize impact on your joints.
Keep your chest lifted and your back straight to maintain proper posture.
ex_UXDJRO.description: Dumbbell Jumping Squat is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

ex_NHCJYC.name: Dumbbell Kneeling Hold to Stand Clean Grip
instructions: Begin in a kneeling position on both knees with a dumbbell in each hand, held with a neutral grip (palms facing each other) at shoulder height.

Engage your thighs and bring one foot forward, planting it flat on the floor to form a 90-degree angle with your knee. Press through the planted foot to stand up, bringing your other foot forward to meet it, standing upright.
Lower back into the kneeling position by stepping one foot back and lowering the knee to the floor, followed by the other knee, returning to the starting position.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, alternating the leading leg if preferred.
tips: Ensure your front knee is aligned with your ankle to avoid undue stress on the joint.
Move smoothly and controlled, focusing on engaging your glutes and quadriceps during the transition.
Use a weight that allows for proper form and control throughout the exercise.
ex_NHCJYC.description: Dumbbell Kneeling Hold to Stand Clean Grip is a beginner multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Lower Back.

ex_HP4ZT3.name: Dumbbell Kneeling Squat
instructions: Begin in a kneeling position with both knees on the floor, torso straight upright from knees to shoulders. Holding a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip (palms facing each other) at shoulder height.
Bend your knees further pushing your hips backward to sit back onto your heels, keeping your torso upright.
Push your hips forward and squeeze your glutes to return to the starting position.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining a controlled motion throughout.
tips: Squeeze your glutes as you push your hips forward to maximize muscle activation.
Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning forward during the movement.
Use a controlled motion to avoid putting strain on your knees.
ex_HP4ZT3.description: Dumbbell Kneeling Squat is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Lower Back.

ex_52QG4I.name: Dumbbell Lunge Alternating on the Spot
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand by your sides.

Take a step forward with your right foot and lower your body into a lunge position by bending both knees. Your right knee should be directly above your right ankle, and your left knee should hover just above the floor.
Push through your right heel to return to the starting position.
Repeat the movement with your left leg, alternating legs with each repetition.
tips: Ensure your front knee does not extend past your toes to avoid strain on the knee joint.
Maintain a steady and controlled pace to ensure proper form and balance.
Exhale as you push back to the starting position and inhale as you lower into the lunge.
ex_52QG4I.description: Dumbbell Lunge Alternating on the Spot is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

ex_3GFDTD.name: Dumbbell Lunge Pulse
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand by your sides.

Take a step forward with your right foot and lower your body into a lunge position by bending both knees. Your right knee should be directly above your right ankle, and your left knee should hover just above the floor.
From the lunge position, pulse up and down by slightly raising and lowering your body a few inches for 2-3 pulses. Keeping the movement controlled and small.
Push through your right heel to return to the starting position. Repeat the movement with your left leg, alternating legs with each set.
tips: Ensure your front knee does not extend past your toes to avoid strain on the knee joint.
Maintain a steady and controlled pace to ensure proper form and balance.
Exhale as you push back to the starting position and inhale as you lower into the lunge.
ex_3GFDTD.description: Dumbbell Lunge Pulse is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

ex_B25IDP.name: Dumbbell Lunge to Overhead Press
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height with your palms facing each other.

Step forward with your right foot and lower your body into a lunge position by bending both knees while simultaneously pressing the dumbbells overhead until your arms are fully extended. Your right knee should be directly above your right ankle, and your left knee should hover just above the floor.
Push through your right heel to return to the starting position while lowering the dumbbells back to shoulder height.
Repeat the movement with your left leg, alternating legs with each set.
tips: Ensure your front knee does not extend past your toes to avoid strain on the knee joint.
Keep a steady and controlled pace to ensure proper form and balance.
Exhale as you press the dumbbells overhead and inhale as you lower them back down.
ex_B25IDP.description: Dumbbell Lunge to Overhead Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Triceps, Calves.

ex_KIEEMI.name: Dumbbell Narrow Stance Squats
instructions: Stand with your feet close together, about hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with your palms facing your body.
Begin the squat by pushing your hips back and bending your knees to lower your body, keeping the dumbbells at your sides.
Lower yourself until your thighs are parallel to the floor or as low as you can comfortably go while maintaining proper form.
Push through your heels to stand back up, straightening your legs and returning to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your weight is evenly distributed through your feet, especially your heels, to activate your glutes and quadriceps.
Breathe in as you lower into the squat and breathe out as you push back up.
Keep your knees in line with your toes to avoid excessive strain on your knees.
ex_KIEEMI.description: Dumbbell Narrow Stance Squats is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

ex_5B3BOU.name: Dumbbell Offset Squat
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and hold a dumbbell against your shoulder with a neutral grip. Extend your opposite arm forward at shoulder height for balance.
Push your hips back and bend your knees to lower into a squat while keeping your chest lifted and your torso facing forward.
Lower until your thighs are approximately parallel to the floor, or as far as you can while keeping your heels down and your knees aligned with your toes.
Press through your heels to stand upright, then repeat for the desired number of repetitions before holding the dumbbell on the opposite side.
tips: Brace your core to prevent your torso from leaning toward the weighted side.
Keep your hips and shoulders level without twisting your body.
Distribute your weight evenly across your heels and the middle of your feet.
Inhale as you lower into the squat and exhale as you return to standing.
ex_5B3BOU.description: Dumbbell Offset Squat is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Core, Obliques.

ex_W3R4LA.name: Dumbbell Overhead Lunge
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand. Extend your arms fully overhead with your palms facing each other.
Step forward with your right foot, lowering your hips until both knees are bent at approximately 90 degrees. Your back knee should hover just above the floor.
Push through your front heel to return to the starting position, maintaining the dumbbells overhead throughout the movement.
Alternate legs and repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Maintain a controlled motion to prevent any wobbling or loss of balance.
Avoid leaning forward; keep your torso upright throughout the exercise.
Inhale as you step forward and lower into the lunge, and exhale as you push back to the starting position.
ex_W3R4LA.description: Dumbbell Overhead Lunge is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Hamstrings.

ex_PTPIDX.name: Dumbbell Press Squat
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell with both hands close to your chest.
Lower your body into a squat position by bending your knees and hips. Make sure your thighs are parallel to the floor and your knees do not go past your toes.
At the bottom of the squat, stay in position and press the dumbbell forward in front of your chest twice by extending your arms fully, then bring it back to your chest.
Push through your heels to stand up and return to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your knees track over your toes and avoid letting them cave inward.
Ensure the dumbbell moves in a straight line in front of your chest.
Use a weight that allows you to perform the exercise with proper form.
ex_PTPIDX.description: Dumbbell Press Squat is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Triceps, Chest.

ex_DK66CL.name: Dumbbell Rear Lunge From Step
instructions: Stand on a step with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand by your sides with your arms fully extended.
Step your right foot back off the step and lower your body into a lunge position, keeping your left knee over your left ankle and lowering your right knee towards the floor.
Just before your right knee touches the floor, push through your left heel to return to the starting position on the step, bringing your right foot forward to stand up straight.
Repeat the movement with your left leg stepping back off the step. Alternate legs for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Maintain equal weight distribution between your front and back legs.
Avoid letting your back knee touch the floor.
Ensure your front knee does not go past your toes to avoid undue stress on the knee joint.
ex_DK66CL.description: Dumbbell Rear Lunge From Step is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

ex_DG2PCE.name: Dumbbell Rear Lunge
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand by your sides with your arms fully extended.
Step your right foot back and lower your body into a lunge position, keeping your left knee over your left ankle and lowering your right knee towards the floor.
Just before your right knee touches the floor, push through your left heel to return to the starting position, bringing your right foot forward to stand up straight.

ex_DG2PCE.description: Dumbbell Rear Lunge is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

ex_ICW4BA.name: Dumbbell Reverse Lunge on the Spot
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand by your sides, palms facing your body.
Take a step backward with your right foot, lowering your body until your left thigh is parallel to the floor and your right knee is just above the floor.
Push through your left heel to return to the starting position, bringing your right foot back to meet your left.
Repeat the movement with your left leg, alternating legs for the desired number of repetitions.

Make sure your front knee does not extend past your toes to avoid putting strain on the knee joint.
Maintain a steady, controlled motion to ensure proper form and balance.
ex_ICW4BA.description: Dumbbell Reverse Lunge on the Spot is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

ex_LXRUDI.name: Dumbbell Reverse Lunges Pulses
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand by your sides, palms facing your body.
Take a step backward with your right foot, lowering your body until your left thigh is parallel to the floor and your right knee is just above the floor.
Perform two small pulses by slightly raising and lowering your body while maintaining the lunge position.
Push through your left heel to return to the starting position, bringing your right foot back to meet your left. Repeat the exercise for the desired number of repetitions.

ex_CKRSL5.name: Dumbbell Seated Calf Raise
instructions: Sit on a bench with your forefeet on a weight plate with heels extended to the floor, feet hip-width apart. Place a dumbbell on each knee, holding them in place with your hands.
Lift your heels off the floor by extending your ankles, pushing through your forefeet to raise the dumbbells.
Pause at the top of the movement, squeezing your calf muscles.
Lower your heels back just before touching the floor with control, returning to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

ex_ZTQXBO.name: Dumbbell Seated One Leg Calf Raise Hammer Grip
instructions: Sit on a bench with your right forefoot on a weightplate. Hold a dumbbell in your right hand and place it on your right thigh near your knee.
Push through your right forefoot to raise your heel as high as possible, lifting the dumbbell. Briefly hold this position, squeezing your calf muscle.
Slowly lower your heel back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the left leg.

ex_ZTQXBO.description: Dumbbell Seated One Leg Calf Raise Hammer Grip is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category.

ex_B5T2UT.name: Dumbbell Side Lunge Alternating
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your arms at your sides.

Take a large step to your right with your right foot, bending your right knee and lowering your hips down and back as if you are sitting into a chair. Keeping your left leg straight and rotating it until your left foot points to the ceiling.

Lower yourself until your right thigh is parallel to the floor, ensuring your knee does not extend past your toes. The dumbbells should be hanging down towards the floor on either side of your right leg.
Push through your right heel to return to the starting position. Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.

Keep your feet facing forward and your weight distributed evenly.
Make sure your knee stays aligned with your toes during the lunge to prevent strain.
ex_B5T2UT.description: Dumbbell Side Lunge Alternating is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Adductors.

ex_HA7M6F.name: Dumbbell Side Lunge Left N Right

Take a large step to your right with your right foot, bending your right knee and lowering your hips down and back as if you are sitting into a chair. Keeping your left leg straight.

Lower yourself until your right thigh is parallel to the floor, ensuring your knee does not extend past your toes. The dumbbells should be hanging down towards the floor on either side of your right leg.
Push through your right heel to return to the starting position. Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.

Keep your feet facing forward and your weight distributed evenly.

ex_5HXQLA.name: Dumbbell Side Lunge Single Leg

Take a large step to your left with your left foot, bending your left knee and lowering your hips down and back as if you are sitting into a chair. Keep your right leg straight.
Lower yourself until your left thigh is parallel to the floor.
Push through your left heel to return to the starting position. Perform all repetitions on the left side before switching to the right side and repeating the exercise.

ex_5HXQLA.description: Dumbbell Side Lunge Single Leg is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Adductors.

ex_VHMAOI.name: Dumbbell Side Squat Side to Side
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell close to your chest.
Shift your weight to your right leg, bending your knee and pushing your hips back to lower into a side lunge. Keep your left leg straight and your chest up.
Push through your right heel to return to the starting position, straightening your leg.

ex_YL7XZ7.name: Dumbbell Single Arm Overhead Lunge
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in your right hand. Press the dumbbell overhead, fully extending your arm.

ex_VH45KT.name: Dumbbell Single Leg Calf Raise Wall Support

Press through your eight forefoot to raise your heel off the floor as high as possible.

ex_GE6MT7.name: Dumbbell Single Leg Deadlift
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand extended down in front of you. Shift your weight onto your left leg and lift your right foot slightly off the floor behind you.
Begin to hinge at your hips, extending your right leg straight behind you while lowering the dumbbells towards the floor. Keep a slight bend in your left knee.
Lower the dumbbells until your torso is parallel to the floor, or as far as your flexibility allows, maintaining a straight line from your head to your right heel.

Return to the starting position by driving through your left heel and bringing your right leg forward, keeping it off the floor. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the left hand and right leg.
tips: Ensure your back stays straight throughout the exercise to avoid injury.

ex_KSIPE5.name: Dumbbell Single Leg Hip Thrust

Press through your planted foot and extend your hips upward while keeping the opposite leg straight and elevated.
Lift until your torso and supporting thigh form a straight line, then pause briefly and squeeze your glutes.
Slowly lower your hips toward the floor while keeping the extended leg raised, then repeat before switching sides.
tips: Keep your upper back firmly supported against the bench throughout the movement.
Drive through the heel and middle of your planted foot rather than your toes.

ex_KSIPE5.description: Dumbbell Single Leg Hip Thrust is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Core, Obliques.

ex_XLXKZE.name: Dumbbell Single Leg Single Arm Deadlift

Lower the dumbbell toward the floor beside your supporting leg until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor, keeping your back straight and your hips level.

ex_MV6XD6.name: Dumbbell Single Leg Squat

Push through your right heel to return to standing position, keeping your left leg extended. Repeat for the desired repetitions, then switch to the left leg.

Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning forward.
Keep your balance by engaging your core and focusing on a fixed point in front of you.
ex_MV6XD6.description: Dumbbell Single Leg Squat is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

Lower yourself in a controlled manner to maintain balance and form.
ex_THTS2S.description: Dumbbell Squats is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

ex_5MA763.name: Dumbbell Squats to Shoulder Press
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height just in front of your shoulders, palms facing each other.
Lower into a squat by bending your knees and hips, keeping your back straight and chest up until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Push through your heels to stand up while simultaneously pressing the dumbbells overhead until your arms are fully extended.
Lower the dumbbells back to shoulder height as you prepare for the next squat. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your knees do not extend past your toes during the squat to avoid unnecessary strain.
Exhale as you press the dumbbells overhead and inhale as you lower into the squat.
Keep your back straight and avoid leaning forward during the squat.
ex_5MA763.description: Dumbbell Squats to Shoulder Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Hamstrings, Calves.

ex_BJMSI6.name: Dumbbell Staggered Deadlift
instructions: Stand with one foot fully planted and place the opposite foot a short step behind, resting on the ball of the foot with the heel raised. Hold a dumbbell in each hand using an overhand grip.
Shift most of your weight onto the front leg, slightly bend both knees, and push your hips backward as you hinge your torso forward.
Lower the dumbbells in front of your shins while keeping your back straight and the weights close to your legs.
Press through your front foot and drive your hips forward to return upright, then complete the repetitions before switching your stance.
tips: Keep most of your body weight on the front leg and use the rear foot mainly for balance.
Push your hips backward rather than lowering into a squat.
Stop lowering when you feel a controlled stretch without rounding your back.
Inhale as you hinge forward and exhale as you return to standing.
ex_BJMSI6.description: Dumbbell Staggered Deadlift is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Lower Back, Core.

ex_7IY5NA.name: Dumbbell Staggered Glute Bridge
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and hold a dumbbell securely across your hips. Plant one foot close to your hips and place the opposite heel slightly farther forward with the toes raised.
Press primarily through the foot closest to your hips while using the forward heel lightly for balance.
Lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from your shoulders to your knees, keeping your hips level.
Pause and squeeze your glutes, then lower your hips with control and complete the repetitions before switching to the other side.
tips: Keep the foot closest to your hips firmly planted throughout the movement.
Use the forward heel mainly for balance rather than pushing equally through both legs.
Drive through the heel and middle of your working foot rather than your toes.
Inhale as you lower your hips and exhale as you lift them.
ex_7IY5NA.description: Dumbbell Staggered Glute Bridge is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Core, Lower Back.

ex_WJ3YFR.name: Dumbbell Staggered Hip Thrust
instructions: Sit with your upper back against the edge of a flat bench and hold a dumbbell securely across your hips. Plant one foot close to your hips and place the opposite heel slightly farther forward with the toes raised.
Press primarily through the foot closest to your hips and lift your hips toward the ceiling while using the forward heel lightly for balance.
Continue lifting until your torso and working thigh form a straight line, keeping your hips level and squeezing your glutes at the top.
Lower your hips with control, then repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching to the other side.
tips: Place most of your weight through the foot closest to your hips.
Use the farther heel mainly for balance rather than driving equally through both legs.
Stop at full hip extension without arching your lower back.
Inhale as you lower your hips and exhale as you press them upward.
ex_WJ3YFR.description: Dumbbell Staggered Hip Thrust is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Core, Calves.

ex_TSZ4Z4.name: Dumbbell Standing Calf Raise on Step
instructions: Stand on a step platform with your heels hanging off the edge, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides. Position your feet hip-width apart.
Slowly raise your heels as high as possible by pushing through your forefeet, lifting your body upward.
Hold the top position for a brief moment, feeling the contraction in your calf muscles.
Lower your heels below the edge of the step, feeling a stretch in your calves. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure the step or platform is stable and secure before starting the exercise.
Keep your movements slow and controlled to maximize muscle engagement.
Avoid bouncing at the top or bottom of the movement.
ex_TSZ4Z4.description: Dumbbell Standing Calf Raise on Step is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category.

ex_FEI4YO.name: Dumbbell Standing Calf Raise
instructions: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides. Keep your posture straight and your core engaged.
Slowly raise your heels off the floor by pushing through your forefeet, lifting your body upward as high as possible.
Hold the top position for a brief moment, feeling the contraction in your calf muscles.
Lower your heels back down to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your movements slow and controlled to maximize muscle engagement.
Avoid bouncing at the top or bottom of the movement.
Maintain a straight posture throughout the exercise.
ex_FEI4YO.description: Dumbbell Standing Calf Raise is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shins.

ex_ZS6N5O.name: Dumbbell Standing Hip Abduction
instructions: Stand upright with your feet together and hold a dumbbell against the outside of one thigh with the same-side hand.
Shift your weight onto the opposite leg, engage your core, and keep your supporting knee slightly bent.
Keep your working leg straight and lift it out and upward to the side while maintaining an upright torso and keeping your toes facing forward.
Pause briefly at the top, then lower your leg with control and repeat before switching sides.
tips: Keep your supporting foot firmly planted and distribute your weight across the entire foot.
Keep your hips level and avoid leaning away from the working leg.
Avoid swinging your leg or using momentum to raise the dumbbell.
Exhale as you lift your leg and inhale as you lower it.
ex_ZS6N5O.description: Dumbbell Standing Hip Abduction is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Core, Obliques.

ex_AVMBLE.name: Dumbbell Standing Single Leg Calf Raise
instructions: Stand with your left foot on the floor, keeping your right foot a few inches off the floor, holding a dumbbell in both hands with your arms hanging by your sides.
Press through your left heel to raise your heel off the floor as high as possible by extending your ankle.
Hold the position briefly at the top, squeezing your calf muscle.
Lower your heel back down to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the right leg.
tips: Use a full range of motion, lifting your heel as high as possible.
Avoid bouncing; focus on a slow and controlled movement.
Maintain a steady pace and avoid using momentum.
ex_AVMBLE.description: Dumbbell Standing Single Leg Calf Raise is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category.

ex_C2U36R.name: Dumbbell Static Lunge
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides. Step your right foot forward and your left foot back.
Lower your body by bending both knees until your right thigh is parallel to the floor and your left knee nearly touches the floor.
Push through your right heel to return to the starting position, keeping your feet in the same place.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions before switching to the other leg.
tips: Maintain an upright posture throughout the exercise.
Keep your front knee aligned with your ankle to avoid strain.
Avoid letting your front knee extend past your toes.
ex_C2U36R.description: Dumbbell Static Lunge is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

ex_C3CK7L.name: Dumbbell Step Up on Bench
instructions: Begin by standing in front of a bench with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Place your right foot on the bench, ensuring your entire foot is firmly planted. Push through your right heel to lift your body onto the bench, bringing your left foot up to meet the right.
Step down with your left foot first, followed by your right foot, returning to the starting position.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other leg.
tips: Avoid pushing off with your back leg; focus on using your front leg to lift your body.
Ensure your entire foot is on the bench to avoid slipping.
Control your descent to prevent injury.
ex_C3CK7L.description: Dumbbell Step Up on Bench is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

ex_E7OFPW.name: Dumbbell Step-Up With Knee Raise
instructions: Begin by standing in front of a bench with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.

Place your right foot on the bench, ensuring your entire foot is firmly planted. Push through your right heel to lift your body onto the bench, simultaneously lifting your left knee up towards your chest.
Lower your left leg back down to the floor, followed by your right leg, returning to the starting position.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other leg.

Ensure your entire foot is on the bench to avoid slipping.
Control your ascend and descent to prevent injury.
ex_E7OFPW.description: Dumbbell Step-Up With Knee Raise is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

ex_FEZ72B.name: Dumbbell Stiff Leg Deadlift
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs with your palms facing your body.
Keeping a slight bend in your knees, hinge at your hips and lower the dumbbells towards the floor, maintaining a straight back and keeping the dumbbells close to your legs.
Lower the dumbbells until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings, ensuring your back remains straight.
Return to the starting position, extending your hips and standing tall. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

ex_FEZ72B.description: Dumbbell Stiff Leg Deadlift is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back.

ex_STSOYO.name: Dumbbell Straight Leg Deadlift
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing your thighs. Keep your legs straight but not locked.
Keep your back straight and hinge at your hips, lowering the dumbbells towards the floor. Push your hips back while keeping the dumbbells close to your legs.
Lower the dumbbells until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings, ensuring your back remains straight.
Return to the starting position by driving your hips forward and standing up straight, squeezing your glutes at the top. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Keep the dumbbells close to your legs as you lower and lift them.
Focus on hinging at the hips rather than bending at the waist.
ex_STSOYO.description: Dumbbell Straight Leg Deadlift is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back.

ex_X4S2XW.name: Dumbbell Suitcase Carry
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in one hand at your side, allowing your arm to hang. Ensure your shoulders are level and your posture is upright.
Begin walking forward in a straight line, keeping the dumbbell close to your body. Walk for the desired distance or time.
Maintain a neutral spine and avoid leaning to one side to balance the weight. Focus on keeping your torso stable and your strides even.
After completing the desired distance or time, switch the dumbbell to the other hand and repeat the exercise, ensuring equal work on both sides.

ex_X4S2XW.description: Dumbbell Suitcase Carry is an intermediate multi-joint compound loaded carry exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms, Hamstrings, Glutes.

ex_BYACUX.name: Dumbbell Sumo Squat Off Benches
instructions: Stand between two benches with a wide stance, toes pointed slightly outward. Hold a dumbbell with both hands, letting it hang between your legs.
Lower yourself into a wide squat by bending your knees and pushing your hips back. Lower until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Push through your heels to stand back up, squeezing your glutes at the top of the movement.

Keep your back straight and chest up to avoid leaning forward.

ex_BYACUX.description: Dumbbell Sumo Squat Off Benches is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Adductors.

ex_OEFT6C.name: Dumbbell Supported Sissy Squat
instructions: Position yourself on a sissy squat machine with your feet shoulder-width apart and your lower legs securely supported by the machine's pads. Hold a dumbbell close to your chest with both hands.
Slowly lower your body by bending your knees, keeping your back straight.
Lower until your thighs are almost parallel to the floor.
Push through your thighs to rise back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

ex_U646ET.name: Elevated Standing Calf Raise
instructions: Stand on the edge of a step with your heels hanging off, placing your forefeet securely on the edge. Hold onto a stable surface for balance if necessary.
Lower your heels below the level of the platform to feel a stretch in your calf muscles.
Press through your forefeet to raise your heels as high as possible, fully contracting your calf muscles.
Slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position, maintaining control throughout the movement. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

ex_TDAE4L.name: Exercise Ball Leg Curl
instructions: Lie on your back with your arms at your sides, palms facing down. Place your heels and calves on top of an exercise ball.
Engage your core and lift your hips off the floor, forming a straight line from your shoulders to your heels. This is your starting position.
Bend your knees and roll the ball towards your glutes by pulling your heels in. Keep your hips elevated and maintain the straight line from your shoulders to your knees.
Slowly extend your legs, rolling the ball back to the starting position while keeping your hips lifted. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Use a properly inflated exercise ball to provide stability and ease of movement.

Focus on steady breathing, exhaling as you curl the ball in and inhaling as you extend your legs.
ex_TDAE4L.description: Exercise Ball Leg Curl is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with a stability ball, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Calves.

ex_GHDNIW.name: Exercise Ball One Legged Diagonal Kick Hamstring Curl
instructions: Begin by lying on your back with your arms at your sides, palms facing down. Place your left heel and calf on top of an exercise ball, with your right leg extended straight and aligned with your hips.
Engage your core and lift your hips off the floor, forming a straight line from your shoulders to your left heel.
Bend your left knee and roll the ball diagonally towards the middle of your hips, pulling your heel in while simultaneously raising your right leg upwards along the line of your hips.
Extend your left leg, rolling the ball back to the starting position, while lowering your right leg back to the floor. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Switch legs and repeat the movement with your right heel and calf on the ball and your left leg extending upwards.
tips: Move slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Focus on steady breathing, exhaling as you curl the ball in and inhale as you extend your leg.
Use a properly inflated exercise ball to provide stability and ease of movement.
ex_GHDNIW.description: Exercise Ball One Legged Diagonal Kick Hamstring Curl is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with a stability ball, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Hip Flexors.

ex_YQ2UHH.name: Exercise Ball Wall Squat

Slowly lower your body into a squat position by bending your knees and hips, keeping your back straight and allowing the ball to roll along your back.
Lower yourself until your thighs are parallel to the floor, ensuring your knees do not extend past your toes.
Push through your heels to return to the starting position, straightening your legs. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

ex_6COKRW.name: Feet Together Barbell Squats

ex_HRVTXY.name: Fire Hydrant Bodyweight
instructions: Begin on the floor in an all-fours position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your knees under your hips. Keep your back straight and your core engaged.
Keeping your knee bent at a 90-degree angle, lift your right leg out to the side until your thigh is parallel to the floor. Keep your hips level and avoid rotating your torso.

Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to your left leg and repeat.

ex_AJEPJ7.name: Frog Jumps

Land softly in the same wide stance and immediately bend your knees.
Lower back into the squat, reach toward the floor, and continue repeating the movement.

Push through your heels to return to the starting position, extending your hips and knees. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

ex_YC75DT.name: Glute Bridge Bodyweight

ex_J7VDLF.name: Bodyweight In and Out Squat Jump
instructions: Stand tall with your back straight, feet shoulder-width apart, and clasp your hands in front of your chest.
Lower your hips, jump up and land into a squat position with your knees bent, thighs parallel to the floor, and feet placed wider than your shoulder width.

tips: Land softly on your forefeet to reduce impact on your joints.

ex_XUVB7Y.name: Jump Squats Bodyweight
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms at your sides.

ex_CAZXKN.name: Jumping Lunge
instructions: Stand in a split stance with one foot forward and clasp your hands in front of your chest.
Bend both knees and lower into a lunge until your back knee is just above the floor.
Jump straight upward, switch your legs in the air, and land with the opposite foot forward.

ex_322DKU.name: Jumping Pistol Squat
instructions: Stand on one leg with your hands on your hips and extend your opposite leg slightly forward.

Maintain an upright chest as you lower.

ex_FQO6KG.name: Kettlebell Bulgarian Split Squat Right
instructions: Stand facing away from a bench, holding a kettlebell in each hand with arms hanging by your sides. Place your right foot on the bench behind you.

ex_I76DB5.name: Kettlebell Split Squat

Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs and perform the same number of repetitions on the other side.

instructions: Hold the end of the landmine bar at your shoulder or chest, standing tall.
Rise onto the balls of your feet as high as possible.
Pause at the top.
Lower your heels slowly and repeat.
tips: Stand on a plate with your heels hanging off for a bigger range.
Keep your knees straight.
ex_KXQL7U.description: Landmine Calf Raise is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category.

ex_3ESSBS.name: Landmine Curtsy Lunge
instructions: Hold the end of the landmine bar at your chest with both hands.
Step one leg behind and across your body into a curtsy position.

ex_ENOJLL.name: Landmine Glute Kick Back

Brace your core.
Kick your leg back and up, lifting the bar with your heel.
Lower with control and repeat, then switch legs.

Squeeze your glute at the top.

ex_SVTVM3.name: Landmine Goblet Curtsy Lunge

Step one leg behind and across your body.

Drive back up to standing and repeat.

ex_FEPZAV.description: Landmine Hack Squat is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Hamstrings.

ex_INWMXV.name: Landmine Lunge to Overhead Press

Squat down until your thighs are about parallel to the floor.

ex_WETSQY.name: Lateral Band Walks
instructions: Place a resistance band around your legs, just above your knees or around your ankles.
Stand with your feet hip-width apart in a half squat.
Step sideways with one foot, then follow with the other, keeping tension on the band.

ex_WETSQY.description: Lateral Band Walks is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the abductors (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps.

ex_JUFH3L.name: Lateral Box Jump

ex_JUFH3L.description: Lateral Box Jump is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Abductors.

ex_XE676V.name: Leg Press Machine Close Stance
instructions: Sit on the leg press machine and position your feet close together in the center of the foot platform, keeping your feet flat and parallel. Adjust the seat so that your knees are bent at about a 90-degree angle.
Hold the handles on the sides of the seat for stability. Keep your back pressed against the backrest and your core engaged.
Press through your heels to extend your legs, pushing the platform away from you until your legs are fully extended but not locked at the knees.
Slowly return to the starting position by bending your knees with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back pressed against the backrest throughout the exercise.
Ensure both feet remain flat on the platform for better stability and muscle balance.
Exhale as you press the platform away and inhale as you return to the starting position.
ex_XE676V.description: Leg Press Machine Close Stance is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Hamstrings, Calves.

instructions: Sit on the lever leg extension machine. Position your feet under the padded lever, with the lever resting just above your ankles.
Grip the handles on the sides of the machine for support. Engage your core and keep your back pressed firmly against the backrest.
Extend your legs by pushing the padded lever upward, straightening your knees, then slowly lower the weight back to the starting position.

ex_7JGBLV.name: Lunge Front Kick
instructions: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart and your arms at your sides.
Lift your right leg to perform a front kick, extending your leg straight out in front of you.
As you bring your right leg back down, step it behind you into a lunge position, lowering your hips until your left thigh is parallel to the floor and your right knee nearly touches the floor.
Push through your left heel to stand back up, returning to the starting position. Repeat the movement on the same side or alternate legs for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your front knee is aligned with your ankle during the lunge to avoid strain.

ex_EL5INQ.name: Lunge Pulses Bodyweight
instructions: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart. Step your right foot forward into a lunge position, lowering your hips until your right thigh is parallel to the floor and your left knee nearly touches the floor.
From the lunge position, perform small pulses by slightly raising and lowering your hips in a controlled manner.
Continue pulsing for the desired number of repetitions or duration, keeping your core engaged and maintaining balance.
Return to the starting position by pushing through your right heel and repeat the exercise on the opposite leg.
tips: Ensure your front knee is aligned with your ankle and does not extend past your toes to avoid strain.
Use a controlled motion and avoid bouncing to maintain muscle tension and effectiveness.

ex_SVKT2H.name: Lunge Reverse With Resistance Band
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, placing the middle of the resistance band under your left foot. Hold the handles of the resistance band at shoulder height with your elbows bent and facing the floor.
Step your right leg back into a reverse lunge, bending both knees to lower your right knee towards the floor while keeping your left knee aligned with your ankle.
Push through your left heel to return to the starting position, bringing your right leg forward.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides to work the other leg.
tips: Exhale as you push back up to the starting position and inhale as you lower into the lunge.
Focus on engaging your glutes and quadriceps throughout the movement.
Ensure your front knee does not extend past your toes to avoid joint strain.
ex_SVKT2H.description: Lunge Reverse With Resistance Band is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves, Shoulders.

ex_KGGJTU.name: Lunge Rotation Left and Right Bodyweight
instructions: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart and your arms bent at your sides, hands close to your torso.
Step your right foot forward into a lunge position, lowering your hips until your right thigh is parallel to the floor and your left knee nearly touches the floor.
Rotate your torso to the right, bringing your arms to the right side, then rotate your torso to the left, bringing your arms to the left side.
Return your torso to the center and push through your right heel to return to the starting position. Repeat the movement on the opposite leg. Alternate sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your front knee is aligned with your ankle and does not extend past your toes to avoid strain.
Keep your back straight and your chest lifted to maintain proper posture.
Perform the rotations with control, avoiding any jerky movements to prevent injury.
ex_KGGJTU.description: Lunge Rotation Left and Right Bodyweight is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Hip Flexors.

ex_VN7U3D.name: Lunge to Knee Drive Left Bodyweight

Step your left foot back into a lunge position, lowering your hips until your right thigh is parallel to the floor and your left knee nearly touches the floor.

Return your left leg to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions. Switch sides and repeat the movement with your right leg stepping back.

Perform the knee drive with control, avoiding any jerky movements to prevent injury.
Focus on steady breathing, exhaling as you drive your knee up and inhaling as you lower into the lunge.
ex_VN7U3D.description: Lunge to Knee Drive Left Bodyweight is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings.

ex_R2UZEH.name: Seated Calf Raises Dumbbell on Knee
instructions: Sit on a bench with your forefeet on the edge of a plate, close together, allowing your heels to hang off. Place a dumbbell on both knees, holding them securely with your hands.
Raise your heels as high as possible, pushing through your forefeet and lifting the dumbbells.
Lower your heels back down to the starting position in a controlled manner. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the left leg and repeat.

Avoid bouncing or using momentum to lift the weight.
ex_R2UZEH.description: Seated Calf Raises Dumbbell on Knee is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category.

ex_SYUN5K.name: Seated Hip Abductor Machine
instructions: Sit down on the hip abduction machine and place your feet flat on the footrests while positioning your outer thighs against the padded levers.
Grip the side handles to stabilize your upper body and press your legs outward against the resistance, pushing the pads apart in a controlled motion.
Pause for a second at the peak of the movement, then slowly return to the starting position.

Focus on squeezing your glutes and outer thighs throughout the movement.

ex_7UAJQR.name: Seated Leg Curl Machine
instructions: Sit on the machine with your back against the backrest and your legs fully extended. Adjust the backrest and leg pads so the pad rests just above your heels.

ex_7UAJQR.description: Seated Leg Curl Machine is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes.

ex_GIFFDH.name: Seated Leg Extension Single Leg
instructions: Sit on the leg extension machine. Position both feet under the padded lever, with the lever resting just above your ankles.
Grip the handles on the sides of the machine for support. Engage your core and keep your back pressed firmly against the backrest.
Extend your right leg by pushing the padded lever upward, straightening your knee, then slowly lower the lever to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid locking your knees at the top of the movement to reduce strain on your joints.
Keep your back pressed firmly against the backrest to maintain proper form.
Exhale as you extend your legs and inhale as you lower them back down.
ex_GIFFDH.description: Seated Leg Extension Single Leg is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

ex_2H4JEK.name: Seated Leg Extension Alternate Legs
instructions: Sit on the leg extension machine. Position both feet under the padded lever, with the lever resting just above your ankles.
Grip the handles on the sides of the machine for support. Engage your core and keep your back pressed firmly against the backrest.
Extend your right leg by pushing the padded lever upward, straightening your knee, then slowly lower the lever to the starting position.

ex_GE5XEP.name: Seated Leg Extension Both Legs

ex_74BEI3.name: Seated Machine Hip Adductor
instructions: Sit on a hip abductor machine with your back straight, knees open wide and bent, and feet on the footrests.
Set the padded bars against the inner sides of your knees.
Close your knees to bring the bars together.
As the bars come together, return to the initial position and repeat.
ex_74BEI3.description: Seated Machine Hip Adductor is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the adductors (upper legs). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category.

instructions: Sit on a hip abductor machine with your back straight, knees open wide and bent, and feet on the footrests.

ex_FSTZ2N.description: Seated Hip Adductor Machine (Side View) is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the adductors (upper legs). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category.

ex_FEIFWX.name: Side Lunges Bodyweight
instructions: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart and your hands clasped in front of you for balance.
Take a big step to the right with your right foot, lowering your body into a lunge position. Your right knee should be bent and your left leg should remain straight.
Push through your right heel to return to the starting position.
Repeat on the other side by stepping out to the left with your left foot, lowering into a lunge, and then returning to the starting position.
tips: Ensure your knee does not extend past your toes in the lunge position to protect your knee joint.
Maintain a straight back and avoid leaning forward excessively during the lunge.

ex_FEIFWX.description: Side Lunges Bodyweight is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings.

ex_UUGJ3S.name: Side Lying Leg Lift Left
instructions: Lie on your right side with your legs extended straight and stacked on top of each other. Rest your head on your right arm and place your left hand on your hips.
Slowly lift your left leg straight up towards the ceiling, keeping it straight and in line with your body.
Hold the top position for a moment, feeling the contraction in your outer thigh and hip.
Slowly lower your leg back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to your left side and perform the exercise with your right leg.
tips: Breathe steadily, exhaling as you lift your leg and inhaling as you lower it.
Ensure your leg stays straight and in line with your body throughout the movement.
Avoid using momentum to lift your leg; focus on using your hip and thigh muscles.
ex_UUGJ3S.description: Side Lying Leg Lift Left is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abductors.

ex_NIUOI3.name: Side Lying Leg Lift Right
instructions: Lie on your left side with your legs extended straight and stacked on top of each other. Rest your head on your left arm and place your right hand on your hips.

Slowly lower your leg back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to your right side and perform the exercise with your left leg.

ex_JK6PSD.name: Single Leg Calf Raise Leg Press Machine
instructions: Lie on the leg press machine and straighten your left leg, placing your forefoot on the platform, while your heel hangs off the edge. Your right foot should be resting on the floor.
Press through your forefoot to lift the platform upward by extending your ankle and squeezing your calf at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower your heel back down to the starting position with control, ensuring you achieve a full range of motion.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the right leg.
tips: Keep your knee slightly bent to reduce strain on your joints.

Maintain a steady pace to ensure consistent tension on the muscles.
ex_JK6PSD.description: Single Leg Calf Raise Leg Press Machine is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Quadriceps.

ex_F5ELQU.name: Single Leg Incline 45 Degree Leg Press Machine
instructions: Lie on the leg press machine and place your left foot flat on the platform while your right foot rests on the floor.
Engage your core and keep your back pressed against the seat. Release the safety handles of the leg press machine.
Press through your left foot to extend your leg fully, pushing the platform upward.
Slowly lower the platform back down to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the right leg.
tips: Exhale as you press the platform upward and inhale as you lower it back down.
Ensure your knee stays aligned with your toes to avoid unnecessary strain.
