ex_PPQLO7.name: Single Leg Romanian Deadlift Dumbbell
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in your right hand. Shift your weight onto the right leg and keep it straight.
Hinge at your hips, extending your left leg straight back while lowering the dumbbell towards the floor.
Continue lowering until your upper body and extended leg are parallel to the floor and level from ankle to shoulders.
Return to the starting position by driving through your standing heel. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
tips: Exhale as you lower the dumbbell and inhale as you return to the start.
Maintain a slight bend in the standing knee to avoid joint strain.

ex_Y5TYVL.name: Single Leg Romanian Deadlifts Right Cable Resistance Band
instructions: Attach one end of the resistance band to a low anchor point and hold the other end in your right hand. Stand on your left leg with your right leg slightly bent and your left foot firmly on the floor.
Hinge at your hips and lower your torso until it's parallel to the floor while extending your right leg straight back, keeping your left knee slightly bent.
Return to the starting position by driving your hips forward and bringing your right leg back down.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the left leg.
tips: Exhale as you hinge forward and inhale as you return to the starting position.

ex_Y5TYVL.description: Single Leg Romanian Deadlifts Right Cable Resistance Band is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back.

ex_SASPLG.name: Sissy Squat Bodyweight
instructions: Stand tall holding a support for balance, feet hip-width apart.
Rise onto your toes and lean your torso back as you bend your knees forward.
Lower until you feel a strong stretch in your quadriceps, keeping hips and torso in a straight line.
Push through the balls of your feet to return to the start.

Keep your hips extended, not bent.
ex_SASPLG.description: Sissy Squat Bodyweight is an advanced multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors, Core.

ex_RROSGY.name: Smith Machine Bulgarian Split Squat
instructions: Position yourself under the bar of a smith machine, resting it across your shoulders, and hold it firmly with both hands. Place your right foot back on a bench or box behind you, ensuring your left foot is firmly planted on the floor in front.
Lower your body by bending your left knee, keeping your torso upright and your right knee pointing towards the floor.
Continue lowering until your left thigh is parallel to the floor and your right knee is close to, but not touching the floor.
Push through your left heel to return to the starting position, extending your left leg fully. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to your right leg.
tips: Ensure your front knee stays in line with your toes to avoid unnecessary strain on the knee joint.
Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning forward or backward excessively.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you push up and inhaling as you lower down.
ex_RROSGY.description: Smith Machine Bulgarian Split Squat is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a smith machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

ex_LAQLDZ.name: Smith Machine Calf Raise

Lift your heels off the floor by pushing through your forefeet, raising your body upwards.
Continue lifting until you are standing on your forefeet, then slowly lower your heels back to the starting position with control.

ex_SA7YFD.name: Smith Machine Narrow Stance Heels Elevated Squats

ex_SUUY2B.name: Standing Cable Hip Flexion
instructions: Attach an ankle strap to a low cable and fasten it to one ankle, facing away from the machine.

ex_XCZTGN.name: Standing Calf Raise Resistance Band

Continue lifting until you are standing on your forefeet, feeling a strong contraction in your calves.
Slowly lower your heels back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

ex_SKK43A.name: Standing Calf Raises Smith Machine

Slowly lower your heels back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

ex_YQFJS6.name: Standing Side Leg Raises

Hold the raised leg for a second, and slowly lower your right leg back to the starting position with control.

ex_ZYYXIS.name: Step Up on Chair Bodyweight
instructions: Stand facing a sturdy chair with your feet shoulder-width apart, keeping your posture upright.

Hold this position, keeping your back flat against the wall and your hands relaxed by your sides or on your thighs.
Maintain the position for the desired duration, then slowly stand back up.

ex_X4NWQ7.name: Dumbbell Face Down Lying Shoulder Press
instructions: Lie face down on a flat bench with your legs bent at 90 degrees and crossed together. Hold a dumbbell in each hand, with your arms bent and elbows pointing outwards at shoulder height.
Begin with the dumbbells at shoulder level, palms facing the floor. Press the dumbbells forward by extending your arms until your arms are fully extended but not locked out.
Slowly bring the dumbbells back to the starting position at shoulder level, maintaining control throughout the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your wrists remain straight and aligned with your forearms.
Keep your chest and abdomen firmly against the bench to avoid arching your back.
Use a weight that allows you to maintain proper form throughout the exercise.
ex_X4NWQ7.description: Dumbbell Face Down Lying Shoulder Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_HMRM5U.name: Dumbbell Front Raise (Front View)
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell vertical with both hands, arms fully extended down.
Raise the dumbbell in front of you to shoulder height, keeping your arms straight.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring your shoulders are not shrugging up towards your ears.
Slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position in a controlled manner. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid swinging the weights; use a controlled motion to lift and lower the dumbbell.
Maintain a slight bend in your elbows to reduce joint strain.
Keep your shoulders down and relaxed throughout the exercise.
ex_HMRM5U.description: Dumbbell Front Raise (Front View) is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_7ZSLEH.name: Dumbbell Front Raise
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your arms fully extended by your sides and palms facing your thighs.
Raise the dumbbells in front of you to shoulder height, keeping your arms straight and palms facing down.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring your shoulders are not shrugging up towards your ears.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position in a controlled manner. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid swinging the weights; use a controlled motion to lift and lower the dumbbells.
Maintain a slight bend in your elbows to reduce joint strain.
Keep your shoulders down and relaxed throughout the exercise.
ex_7ZSLEH.description: Dumbbell Front Raise is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_UVQV47.name: Dumbbell Half Kneeling Military Press
instructions: Begin in a half-kneeling position with your right knee on the floor and left foot flat on the floor in front of you. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder level with your palms facing forward.
Engage your core and press both dumbbells upward until your arms are fully extended overhead.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to shoulder level with control, maintaining a steady motion.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your gaze forward and your neck in a neutral position.
Exhale as you press the dumbbells up and inhale as you lower them.
Ensure your front knee remains aligned over your ankle to maintain balance.
ex_UVQV47.description: Dumbbell Half Kneeling Military Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps.

ex_AYCXL7.name: Dumbbell Incline Breeding
instructions: Sit on an incline bench set at a 45-degree angle, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your arms extended, elbows slightly bent, above your chest and palms facing forward.
Slowly lower the dumbbells to your sides in a wide arc, maintaining the slight bend in your elbows.
Bring the dumbbells back up in a controlled manner, following the same wide arc, until they meet above your chest.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, ensuring a controlled and steady motion throughout.
tips: Avoid locking your elbows; maintain a slight bend to protect your joints.
Ensure your wrists remain straight and aligned with your forearms.
Focus on a slow and controlled motion to maximize muscle engagement.
ex_AYCXL7.description: Dumbbell Incline Breeding is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

ex_OHJ5NW.name: Dumbbell Incline Front Raise
instructions: Lie on an incline bench set at a 45-degree angle with a dumbbell in each hand, arms straight, and palms facing down just over your thighs.
Raise both dumbbells in front of you, keeping your arms straight, until they reach opposite your chest.
Hold the position for a second, then slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining a steady and controlled motion.
tips: Avoid using momentum; focus on using your shoulder muscles to lift the weights.
Engage your core to stabilize your body and prevent arching of the back.
Exhale as you lift the dumbbells and inhale as you lower them.
ex_OHJ5NW.description: Dumbbell Incline Front Raise is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Chest.

ex_U53OIE.name: Dumbbell Incline Hammer Shoulder Press
instructions: Lie on an incline bench set at a 45-degree angle with your feet flat on the floor. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height with your palms facing each other (hammer grip) and elbows bent and set perpendicular to your torso.
Press the dumbbells forward in a controlled motion until your arms are fully extended opposite your chest, maintaining the hammer grip.
Return the dumbbells back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your wrists remain straight and aligned with your forearms.
Choose a weight that allows for proper form and control.
Focus on using your shoulder muscles to lift the weights, minimizing involvement from your chest.
ex_U53OIE.description: Dumbbell Incline Hammer Shoulder Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Chest, Triceps.

ex_C326ZK.name: Dumbbell Incline Lying Front Raise
instructions: Lie chest-first on an incline bench set at a 45-degree angle with your forefeet firm on the floor, allowing your arms to hang straight down with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing back.
Raise both dumbbells forward and upward until your arms are in level with your torso, maintaining a slight bend in your elbows.
Squeeze your shoulder muscles at the top of the movement, ensuring your arms are fully extended.
Lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control, allowing your arms to hang down. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you raise the dumbbells and inhale as you lower them.
Avoid swinging the dumbbells; use a slow and controlled motion.
Maintain a slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement.
ex_C326ZK.description: Dumbbell Incline Lying Front Raise is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_GQHIHX.name: Dumbbell Incline One Arm Lateral Raise
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 45-degree angle and lie on your side with your lower arm resting on the bench. Hold a dumbbell with your upper hand, arm extended at your side with your palm facing your body.
Raise the dumbbell up in an arc motion until your arm is straight at shoulder level.
Lower the dumbbell back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other side.
tips: Exhale as you lift the dumbbell and inhale as you lower it.
Hold the bench edge with your free hand to support your body during the exercise.
Maintain a slight bend in your elbow throughout the movement to reduce strain on the joint.
ex_GQHIHX.description: Dumbbell Incline One Arm Lateral Raise is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_EKWQCG.name: Dumbbell Incline Rear Lateral Raise
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 45-degree angle and lie chest-first against it, allowing your arms to hang down with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other.
Raise both arms out to the sides until they are at shoulder height, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Hold briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring your arms are parallel to the floor and in line with your shoulders.
Lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control, maintaining the slight bend in your elbows. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout the exercise to protect your joints.
Ensure your wrists remain straight and aligned with your forearms.
Select a weight that allows for proper form and control throughout the exercise.
ex_EKWQCG.description: Dumbbell Incline Rear Lateral Raise is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_UUVCXV.name: Dumbbell Incline Shrug
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 45-degree angle and sit back against it, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your arms extended at your sides, palms facing each other.
Shrug your shoulders upward, lifting the dumbbells towards your ears, without bending your elbows.
Slowly lower your shoulders back to the starting position, maintaining control throughout the movement. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you shrug your shoulders upward and inhale as you lower them.
Focus on lifting your shoulders straight up and down, avoiding any circular or forward motion.
Use a slow and controlled motion to maximize muscle engagement and avoid swinging.
ex_UUVCXV.description: Dumbbell Incline Shrug is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the traps (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

ex_6CEHXW.name: Dumbbell Kneeling Arnold Press
instructions: Begin by kneeling on the floor with your knees shoulder-width apart. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height with your palms facing your body and your elbows bent and facing down.
Rotate your palms forward as you press the dumbbells overhead until your arms are fully extended.
Reverse the motion, lowering the dumbbells back to shoulder height while rotating your palms back towards your body.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control throughout the movement.
tips: Avoid arching your back; keep your spine neutral.
Keep your movements smooth and controlled to avoid using momentum.
Focus on maintaining the alignment of your elbows and wrists throughout the exercise.
ex_6CEHXW.description: Dumbbell Kneeling Arnold Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Shoulders.

ex_DUTKOY.name: Dumbbell Lateral to Front Raise
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your arms at your sides and palms facing your body.
Lift the dumbbells laterally to shoulder height, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
From the lateral position, move the dumbbells forward until they are directly in front of you, keeping them at shoulder height.
Lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Maintain a slight bend in your elbows to protect your joints.
Keep your shoulders down and back to avoid straining your neck.
Use a weight that allows you to perform the exercise with proper form.
ex_DUTKOY.description: Dumbbell Lateral to Front Raise is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_CN626I.name: Dumbbell Laying 30 Degree Shrug
instructions: Lie on your right side on a 30 degree incline bench with your knees bent. Hold a dumbbell in your right hand using a neutral grip and let your arm hang straight toward the floor.
Keep your arm straight and raise your working shoulder toward your ear, lifting the dumbbell slightly upward.
Pause briefly at the top and squeeze your upper back while keeping your torso still.
Slowly lower your shoulder until your arm hangs fully extended, then repeat before switching sides.
tips: Keep the side of your torso firmly supported on the incline bench.
Keep your elbow straight and avoid curling the dumbbell.
Pause briefly at the top, then lower your shoulder slowly through the full range of motion.
Exhale as you raise your shoulder and inhale as you lower it.
ex_CN626I.description: Dumbbell Laying 30 Degree Shrug is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the traps (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms, Shoulders, Core.

ex_6NVMES.name: Dumbbell Laying Silverback Shrug
instructions: Lie face down on an incline bench with your chest supported, your legs extended, and your feet firmly on the floor. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip and let your arms hang straight below your shoulders.
Shrug your shoulders toward your ears and slightly backward while keeping your arms straight and your chest against the bench.
Pause briefly at the top and squeeze your upper back muscles.
Slowly lower your shoulders to the starting position, allowing them to fully relax before repeating.
tips: Keep your chest firmly supported on the bench throughout the exercise.
Move your shoulders upward and slightly backward without rolling them.
Avoid swinging the dumbbells or using momentum to lift them.
Exhale as you raise your shoulders and inhale as you lower them.
ex_6NVMES.description: Dumbbell Laying Silverback Shrug is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the traps (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Shoulders, Forearms.

ex_C5GTJO.name: Dumbbell Leaning Fly
instructions: Sit on a bench holding a dumbbell in each hand, with your arms hanging down by your sides and feet flat on the floor.
Lean your torso slightly forward, keeping your back straight. Raise both arms out to your sides at shoulder height, maintaining a slight bend in your elbows.
Lower the dumbbells down to your sides and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid using momentum; focus on a slow and controlled movement.
Maintain a slight bend in your elbows to protect your joints.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you bring the dumbbells across your body and inhaling as you extend them back out.
ex_C5GTJO.description: Dumbbell Leaning Fly is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_YYYVGE.name: Dumbbell Lying External Shoulder Rotation
instructions: Lie on your side on the floor with your knees slightly bent for stability. Support your head with your lower hand. Hold a dumbbell in your top hand, keeping your upper arm against your side and your elbow bent at 90 degrees.
Start with your forearm across your abdomen, perpendicular to the floor.
Rotate your shoulder to lift the dumbbell, bringing your forearm to a vertical position without moving your upper arm away from your side.
Slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position, maintaining control throughout the movement.
tips: Keep your upper arm stationary against your side to isolate the shoulder rotation.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to avoid momentum and ensure proper muscle activation.
Use a light weight to start with, as this exercise targets small stabilizing muscles.
ex_YYYVGE.description: Dumbbell Lying External Shoulder Rotation is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.

ex_UVEJWO.name: Dumbbell Lying One Arm Rear Lateral Raise
instructions: Lie face down on a flat bench with your legs bent and forefeet firm on the floor. Hold a dumbbell in one hand, letting it hang straight down from your shoulder and your free hand holding the bench for support.
Keeping your elbow slightly bent, raise the dumbbell out to the side and up to shoulder level, squeezing your shoulder blade at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position in a controlled manner. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.
tips: Avoid using momentum; focus on a slow and controlled movement.
Maintain a slight bend in your elbow throughout the exercise to reduce joint strain.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you lift the dumbbell and inhaling as you lower it.
ex_UVEJWO.description: Dumbbell Lying One Arm Rear Lateral Raise is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_VIDUJH.name: Dumbbell Lying Rear Delt Row
instructions: Lie face down on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging straight down, and palms facing forward.
Pull the dumbbells towards your ribcage by squeezing your shoulder blades together, keeping your elbows pointed backward.
Lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid using momentum to lift the weights; use controlled motions for effective muscle engagement.
Breathe out as you lift the dumbbells and breathe in as you lower them.
Ensure your body remains stable on the bench and avoid lifting your chest.
ex_VIDUJH.description: Dumbbell Lying Rear Delt Row is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_R35IHA.name: Dumbbell Lying Rear Lateral Raise
instructions: Lie face down on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging straight down, and palms facing each other.
Raise the dumbbells out to your sides until your arms are parallel to the floor, maintaining a slight bend in your elbows.
Lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your neck in a neutral position and avoid straining it during the exercise.
Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together to maximize the activation of your rear deltoids and upper back muscles.
Maintain a slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement to reduce joint strain.
ex_R35IHA.description: Dumbbell Lying Rear Lateral Raise is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_5TR3EB.name: Dumbbell One Arm Front Raise
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in one hand with your arm extended down by your side, palm facing your thigh.
Keeping your arm straight, lift the dumbbell directly in front of you to shoulder height, ensuring your palm is facing downwards.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.
tips: Keep your back straight and avoid swinging the dumbbell to use momentum.
Engage your core to maintain stability and control throughout the exercise.
Move the dumbbell in a slow and controlled manner to maximize muscle engagement.
ex_5TR3EB.description: Dumbbell One Arm Front Raise is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_ZKJZJU.name: Dumbbell One Arm Lateral Raise
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in one hand by your side with your palm facing your body. Keep your other hand on your hip or relaxed by your side.
Lift the dumbbell out to the side, maintaining a slight bend in your elbow. Raise your arm until it is parallel to the floor.
Lower the dumbbell back to the starting position, keeping the movement smooth and controlled.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
tips: Perform the movement slowly and deliberately for maximum control.
Avoid using momentum or swinging the dumbbell.
Keep your wrist straight and aligned with your forearm.
ex_ZKJZJU.description: Dumbbell One Arm Lateral Raise is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_NC4VN5.name: Dumbbell One Arm Low Fly
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in one hand. Extend your arm straight down in front of your body, palm facing forward.
Lift the dumbbell in front of you sideways in a wide arc, maintaining a slight bend in your elbow.
Raise your arm until the dumbbell is at your eye level, keeping your shoulder muscle engaged.
Lower the dumbbell back to the starting position in a controlled manner. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
tips: Maintain a slight bend in your elbow throughout the movement.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to avoid using momentum.
Focus on using your chest and shoulder muscles to lift the weight.
ex_NC4VN5.description: Dumbbell One Arm Low Fly is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_HGXHQ2.name: Dumbbell One Arm Shoulder Press (Version 2)
instructions: Begin standing with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in your right hand at shoulder height with your palm facing forward. Place your left hand on your hip for stability.
Engage your core and press the dumbbell overhead by extending your right arm fully overhead.
Lower the dumbbell back to shoulder height with control, maintaining a steady and smooth motion.
Repeat the exercise for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you press the dumbbell overhead and inhale as you lower it.
Avoid arching your back; maintain a neutral spine throughout the exercise.
Keep your movements controlled to prevent injury and ensure proper muscle engagement.
ex_HGXHQ2.description: Dumbbell One Arm Shoulder Press (Version 2) is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps.

ex_J3ZCFP.name: Dumbbell Plank Pullthrough
instructions: Begin in a high plank with your hands directly below your shoulders, your feet slightly apart, and a dumbbell positioned on the floor beside one hand.
Shift your weight onto one hand and reach your opposite hand underneath your torso to grasp the dumbbell.
Drag the dumbbell across the floor to the opposite side while keeping your shoulders and hips facing the floor.
Place your hand back on the floor, repeat the pull with the opposite arm, and continue alternating sides.
tips: Keep your hips level and avoid rotating your torso as you reach underneath.
Transfer your weight smoothly without collapsing into your supporting shoulder.
Drag the dumbbell across the floor instead of lifting it upward.
Exhale as you pull the dumbbell across and inhale as you return your hand to the floor.
ex_J3ZCFP.description: Dumbbell Plank Pullthrough is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Middle Back, Chest, Triceps.

ex_GW4YEO.name: Dumbbell Push Press
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height, palms facing each other. Keep your elbows close to your body.
Slightly bend your knees and lower your body into a quarter squat, then explosively extend your legs and perform a light jump to drive the dumbbells upward.
Press the dumbbells overhead by extending your arms fully, locking out your elbows at the top of the movement.
Lower the dumbbells back to shoulder height in a controlled manner and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Use the power generated from your legs and the light jump to help drive the dumbbells overhead.
Use a weight that allows you to perform the exercise with proper form.
Maintain a slight bend in your knees to absorb the impact of the weights.
ex_GW4YEO.description: Dumbbell Push Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Glutes.

ex_IGNUPH.name: Dumbbell Rear Delt Row
instructions: Kneel with your right knee on a bench and your left foot firmly planted on the floor for stability. Lean forward until your torso is parallel to the floor, and place your right hand on the bench for support. Hold a dumbbell in your left hand with an overhand grip, allowing it to hang straight down from your shoulder.
Row the dumbbell up towards your side, allowing your elbow to flare out to the side. Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
Hold the top position briefly, ensuring your upper arm is parallel to the floor and your elbow is pointing outward.
Slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position with control, allowing your arm to fully extend.
tips: Keep your elbow flared out to the side to target the rear delts effectively.
Exhale as you row the dumbbell up and inhale as you lower it back down.
Use a controlled and steady pace to maintain proper form and muscle engagement.
ex_IGNUPH.description: Dumbbell Rear Delt Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps.

ex_KTLFHR.name: Dumbbell Rear Full Shrugs
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand. Hold the dumbbells behind your back at shoulder width, with your palms facing each other.
Lift your shoulders as high as possible towards your ears, squeezing your shoulders at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower your shoulders back to the starting position with control, allowing your arms to fully extend.
tips: Avoid using momentum or jerking motions; focus on a slow and controlled movement.
Exhale as you lift your shoulders and inhale as you lower them back down.
Keep your neck relaxed and avoid tensing it during the exercise.
ex_KTLFHR.description: Dumbbell Rear Full Shrugs is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the traps (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

ex_HTREGR.name: Dumbbell Rear Lateral Raise
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your arms hanging straight down and palms facing each other.
Hinge at the hips to lean forward, keeping your back straight and knees slightly bent. Your torso should be almost parallel to the floor.
Lift the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc until your arms are in line with your shoulders. Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control and repeat.
tips: Focus on using your rear deltoids and upper back muscles to lift the weights.
Avoid swinging the weights or using momentum; aim for a controlled and smooth motion.
Exhale as you lift the dumbbells and inhale as you lower them.
ex_HTREGR.description: Dumbbell Rear Lateral Raise is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_WCTNRV.name: Dumbbell Reverse Fly
instructions: Begin by lying chest-first on an incline bench, with your feet planted firmly on the floor. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your arms hanging down, palms facing each other.
With a slight bend in your elbows, raise the dumbbells out to your sides until your arms are in line with your shoulders.
Lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control, maintaining the slight bend in your elbows.
Repeat the exercise for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your chest pressed against the bench to maintain stability.
Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
Exhale as you lift the dumbbells and inhale as you lower them.
ex_WCTNRV.description: Dumbbell Reverse Fly is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_PCUILA.name: Dumbbell Scott Press (360 Degree View)
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your face, arms bent at 90 degrees, upper arms parallel to the floor.
Move the dumbbells outward in an arc motion, keeping your elbows bent and slightly raised, until your arms are extended to your sides just higher than shoulder height.
Bring the dumbbells back to the starting position in front of your face, maintaining the 90-degree bend in your elbows.
Repeat the arc motion for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your wrists straight and aligned with your forearms.
Focus on using your shoulder muscles to move the weights.
Avoid using excessive weights that compromise your form.
ex_PCUILA.description: Dumbbell Scott Press (360 Degree View) is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_XZNPXP.name: Dumbbell Scott Press
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your face, arms bent at 90 degrees, upper arms parallel to the floor.
Move the dumbbells outward in an arc motion, keeping your elbows bent and slightly raised, until your arms are extended to your sides just higher than shoulder height.
Bring the dumbbells back to the starting position in front of your face, maintaining the 90-degree bend in your elbows.
Repeat the arc motion for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your wrists straight and aligned with your forearms.
Focus on using your shoulder muscles to move the weights.
Avoid using excessive weights that compromise your form.
ex_XZNPXP.description: Dumbbell Scott Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_3BSDQM.name: Dumbbell Seated Alternate Front Raise
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor and your back straight, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your arms hanging at your sides, palms facing your thighs.
Raise your right arm straight in front of you to shoulder height while rotating the dumbbell to face down, keeping a slight bend in your elbow.
Lower your right arm back to the starting position.
Repeat by alternating arms for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you raise each dumbbell and inhale as you lower it.
Avoid swinging your body or using momentum; focus on controlled movements.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows to reduce strain on your joints.
ex_3BSDQM.description: Dumbbell Seated Alternate Front Raise is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_KEH5XJ.name: Dumbbell Seated Alternate Press
instructions: Sit on a bench with your back straight on the backrest and feet flat on the floor, holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your face, arms bent at 90 degrees, upper arms parallel to the floor.
Press the right dumbbell overhead until your arm is fully extended, keeping your left dumbbell in place.
Lower the right dumbbell back to starting position and then press the left dumbbell overhead.
Continue to alternate arms for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your wrists remain straight and aligned with your forearms.
Use a weight that allows you to maintain proper form throughout the exercise.

Squeeze your shoulder muscles at the top of the movement and slowly return the handles to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back pressed against the backrest throughout the exercise.
Focus on engaging your shoulder muscles throughout the movement.
Exhale as you press the handles upward and inhale as you return them to the starting position.
ex_L5RIYY.description: Iso Lateral Shoulder Press Both Arms is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps.

ex_3D4S44.name: Iso Lateral Shoulder Press Single Arm
instructions: Sit on the Iso-Lateral Shoulder Press machine, back pressed against the backrest and feet flat on the floor. Grasp the handles with both hands, palms facing forward.
Press the right handle upward by extending your arm fully while keeping the other arm stationary.
Squeeze your shoulder muscles at the top of the movement and slowly return the handle to the starting position with control.
Repeat with the same arm for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back pressed against the backrest throughout the exercise.
Focus on engaging your shoulder muscles throughout the movement.
Exhale as you press the handle upward and inhale as you return it to the starting position.
ex_3D4S44.description: Iso Lateral Shoulder Press Single Arm is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps.

ex_XD2NTV.name: Jump Rope Face Pull
instructions: Loop the jump rope over a vertical bar or similar stable structure, ensuring the rope is at about hip height. Stand facing the bar with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handles of the jump rope with both hands.
Step back slightly to create tension in the rope, keeping your core engaged and your back straight.
Pull the rope towards your face by bending your elbows and bringing your hands towards your ears, engaging your upper back and shoulder muscles.
Extend your arms back out to the starting position with control. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together as you pull the rope towards your face to maximize muscle engagement.
Move slowly with control and avoid using momentum to prevent injury.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you pull the rope towards your face and inhaling as you extend your arms back out.
Ensure the vertical bar or structure is stable and can support the tension in the rope to prevent slipping or injury.
ex_XD2NTV.description: Jump Rope Face Pull is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a rope, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Biceps.

ex_E334VU.name: Kettlebell Front Raise
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and hold a kettlebell by the handle with both hands in front of you, keeping your arms extended.
Raise the kettlebell forward and upward, keeping your elbows straight as you are lifting the weight.
Continue lifting until your hands reach about chin height and your elbows are near shoulder height.
Lower the kettlebell along the same path until your arms are extended, then repeat.
tips: Maintain an upright torso throughout the exercise.
Avoid leaning backward to lift the kettlebell higher.
Raise and lower the weight smoothly without using momentum.
Exhale as you raise the kettlebell and inhale as you lower it.
ex_E334VU.description: Kettlebell Front Raise is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms, Core.

ex_7YNCC7.name: Kettlebell Half Kneeling Shoulder Press
instructions: Begin in a half-kneeling position with your right knee on the floor and your left foot flat on the floor in front of you. Hold a kettlebell in your right hand, racked at shoulder height with your elbow bent, facing the floor, and close to your body.
Press the kettlebell overhead by extending your right arm fully, keeping your wrist straight and in line with your shoulder.
Lower the kettlebell back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your knee and hip are aligned, maintaining a 90-degree angle in both legs.
Press the kettlebell straight up, avoiding any forward or backward motion.
Exhale as you press the kettlebell overhead and inhale as you lower it back down.
ex_7YNCC7.description: Kettlebell Half Kneeling Shoulder Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps.

ex_A4AOJU.name: Kettlebell Incline Shrug
instructions: Lie face down on an incline bench with your chest supported. Hold a kettlebell with both hands using an overhand grip, and let your arms hang straight toward the floor.
Keep your arms straight and shrug your shoulders upward toward your ears, allowing the kettlebell to rise slightly.
Pause briefly at the top and squeeze your upper back.
Lower your shoulders with control to the starting position, then repeat.
tips: Keep your chest supported on the bench throughout the movement.
Keep your arms straight and avoid bending your elbows.
Keep your neck neutral and your head aligned with your spine.
Exhale as you shrug upward and inhale as you lower.
ex_A4AOJU.description: Kettlebell Incline Shrug is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the traps (back). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

ex_ZSIDU3.name: Kettlebell Kneeling One Arm Shoulder Press
instructions: Begin in a kneeling position on both knees with your torso upright. Hold a kettlebell in your right hand at shoulder height, with your elbow bent, facing the floor, and close to your body.
Press the kettlebell overhead by extending your right arm fully, keeping your wrist straight and aligned with your shoulder.
Lower the kettlebell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Maintain a neutral spine throughout the movement.
Press the kettlebell straight up, avoiding any forward or backward motion.
Exhale as you press the kettlebell overhead and inhale as you lower it back down.
ex_ZSIDU3.description: Kettlebell Kneeling One Arm Shoulder Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps.

ex_VR3C7R.name: Kettlebell Long Lever Lateral Raise
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder width apart and hold a kettlebell in a neutral grip by your side with your arm straight.
Raise the kettlebell out to the side, keeping your arm extended.
Continue lifting diagonally upward until your elbow is above shoulder height.
Lower the kettlebell along the same path with control, then repeat before switching sides.
tips: Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning to the opposite side.
Avoid swinging the kettlebell or using momentum.
Lower the kettlebell slowly through the full range of motion.
Exhale as you raise the kettlebell and inhale as you lower it.
ex_VR3C7R.description: Kettlebell Long Lever Lateral Raise is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Rotator Cuff, Core.

ex_HXABWJ.name: Kettlebell Rear Delt Row
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart, bend your knees slightly, and hinge forward with a straight back. Hold a kettlebell with both hands, in an overhand grip, and let it hang between your legs.
Pull the kettlebell upward toward your upper chest while driving your elbows out to the sides.
Pause briefly at the top and squeeze the back of your shoulders and upper back.
Lower the kettlebell with control until your arms are extended, then repeat.
tips: Keep your elbows flared outward rather than tucked against your sides.
Keep your chest up and maintain a stable torso during each repetition.
Keep your shoulders down and avoid excessive shrugging.
Exhale as you pull and inhale as you lower.
ex_HXABWJ.description: Kettlebell Rear Delt Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Middle Back, Biceps, Forearms.

ex_ZHTIAF.name: Kettlebell Seesaw Press
instructions: Begin in a standing position with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in each hand at shoulder height. Your elbows should be bent, facing the floor and your palms facing inward.
Press the kettlebell in your right hand overhead by extending your right arm fully while slightly leaning your torso to your left side.
Lower the right kettlebell back to shoulder height and then press the kettlebell in your left hand overhead by extending your left arm fully and slightly leaning your torso to the right side.
Continue alternating the presses for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Press each kettlebell straight up, avoiding any forward or backward motion.
Exhale as you press each kettlebell overhead and inhale as you lower it back down.
Ensure your wrists stay straight and aligned with your forearms to prevent strain.
ex_ZHTIAF.description: Kettlebell Seesaw Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Core.

ex_OITXVO.name: Kettlebell Shoulder Extension
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart, bend your knees slightly, and hinge forward until your torso is parallel to the floor, with your back straight.
Brace your left hand on your left thigh and hold a kettlebell in the right hand using an overhand grip. Let your right arm hang below your shoulder with a slight bend in your elbow.
Keeping your torso still, raise the kettlebell straight behind you until your arm extends past your hip.
Lower the kettlebell with control until your arm returns toward the floor, then repeat before switching sides.
tips: Keep only a slight bend in your working elbow.
Move your arm from the shoulder instead of turning the movement into a row.
Raise the kettlebell straight backward rather than out to the side.
Exhale as you raise the kettlebell and inhale as you lower it.
ex_OITXVO.description: Kettlebell Shoulder Extension is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Forearms, Core.

ex_BGG5EN.name: Kettlebell Shrug
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and hold a kettlebell in each hand by your sides using a neutral grip.
Keep your arms straight and raise both shoulders directly toward your ears.
Pause briefly at the top and squeeze your upper back.
Lower your shoulders with control to the starting position, then repeat.
tips: Shrug your shoulders straight upward rather than rolling them.
Keep your neck relaxed and look straight ahead.
Lower your shoulders fully between repetitions.
Exhale as you shrug upward and inhale as you lower.
ex_BGG5EN.description: Kettlebell Shrug is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the traps (back). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

ex_OSJE23.name: Kettlebell Silverback Shrug
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart, bend your knees slightly, and hinge forward with your back straight. Hold a kettlebell in each hand using an overhand grip and let your arms hang straight down.
Keep your torso still and raise both shoulders upward toward your ears.
Pause briefly at the top and squeeze your upper back while keeping your arms straight.
Lower your shoulders with control until your arms hang fully again, then repeat.
tips: Keep your elbows straight and avoid rowing the kettlebells.
Keep your neck aligned with your spine.
Keep your chest up and your torso still during each repetition.
Exhale as you shrug upward and inhale as you lower.
ex_OSJE23.description: Kettlebell Silverback Shrug is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the traps (back). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms, Core, Lower Back.

ex_TMN5V3.name: Kettlebell Single Arm Lateral Raise
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and hold a kettlebell by your side using a neutral grip.
Keep your arm straight, with a slight bend in the elbow, and raise the kettlebell out to the side.
Continue lifting until your arm reaches approximately shoulder height.
Lower the kettlebell with control to your side, then repeat before switching arms.
tips: Keep a slight bend in your elbow throughout the movement.
Raise your arm directly out to the side.
Keep your chest up and your torso still during each repetition.
Exhale as you raise the kettlebell and inhale as you lower it.
ex_TMN5V3.description: Kettlebell Single Arm Lateral Raise is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Rotator Cuff, Core.

ex_VHBWRD.name: Kettlebell Single Arm Rear Delt Fly
instructions: Stand in a wide stance with your left foot forward and your right leg extended back. Bend your knees slightly, lean forward, rest your left hand on your left thigh, and hold the kettlebell in your right hand using a neutral grip.
Let your right arm hang toward the floor with a slight bend in your elbow.
Raise the kettlebell out and backward until your arm reaches about shoulder height, squeezing your posterior deltoid.
Lower the kettlebell with control, then repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching sides.
tips: Keep your chest up and your torso still during each repetition.
Raise your right arm directly out to the side without turning it into a row.
Avoid shrugging your right shoulder or swinging the kettlebell.
Exhale as you raise the kettlebell and inhale as you lower it.
ex_VHBWRD.description: Kettlebell Single Arm Rear Delt Fly is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Rotator Cuff, Core.

ex_R74GWS.name: Kettlebell Standing Bottoms-Up One Arm Shoulder Press
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in your right hand with the bell facing up (bottoms-up position). Place your left hand on your hip.
Press the kettlebell overhead by extending your elbow, keeping your wrist straight.
Once your arm is fully extended overhead, pause for a second to fully activate the shoulder muscles.
Slowly lower the kettlebell back to the starting position with control, keeping the bottoms-up orientation throughout the movement. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Maintain a strong grip on the kettlebell to keep it stable in the bottoms-up position.
Start with a lighter weight to master the balance and control required for the bottoms-up position.
Avoid locking your elbow completely at the top of the press to protect your joint.
ex_R74GWS.description: Kettlebell Standing Bottoms-Up One Arm Shoulder Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps.

ex_FFBOGF.name: Kettlebell Upright Row
instructions: Stand tall holding a kettlebell by the handle with both hands in front of your thighs.
Pull the kettlebell up along your body, leading with your elbows.
Stop when your elbows are at shoulder height.
Lower slowly and repeat.
tips: Don't raise your elbows above your shoulders.
Keep the bell close to your body.
ex_FFBOGF.description: Kettlebell Upright Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps.

ex_ZWUCYF.name: Landmine Alternating Single Arm Press
instructions: Stand facing the landmine with the end of the bar at one shoulder.
Brace your core and press the bar up and forward until your arm is straight.
Lower it to your shoulder.
Pass it to the other hand and press with that arm.
tips: Keep your ribs down.
Pass the bar under control.
ex_ZWUCYF.description: Landmine Alternating Single Arm Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Upper Chest, Core.

ex_D4XUFZ.name: Landmine Half Kneeling Single Arm Overhead Press
instructions: Kneel on one knee with the other foot in front, holding the end of the bar at your shoulder on the side of the down knee.
Squeeze the glute of the down leg and brace your core.
Press the bar up and forward until your arm is straight.
Lower it with control and repeat, then switch sides.
tips: Keep your torso upright.
Don't lean away from the bar.
ex_D4XUFZ.description: Landmine Half Kneeling Single Arm Overhead Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Core, Upper Chest.

ex_KRZ5GO.name: Landmine Kneeling Alternating Overhead Press
instructions: Kneel tall on both knees facing the landmine, holding the end of the bar at one shoulder.
Press it up and forward until your arm is straight.
Lower it to your shoulder.
Switch hands and press with the other arm.
tips: Squeeze your glutes to keep your hips forward.
Keep the movement smooth.
ex_KRZ5GO.description: Landmine Kneeling Alternating Overhead Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Core.

ex_OE7CLF.name: Landmine Kneeling Overhead Press
instructions: Kneel tall facing the landmine, holding the end of the bar at your chest with both hands.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes.
Press the bar up and forward until your arms are straight.
Lower it to your chest and repeat.
tips: Don't arch your lower back.
Keep your elbows slightly in front of your body.
ex_OE7CLF.description: Landmine Kneeling Overhead Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Upper Chest, Core.

ex_TK2DHH.name: Landmine Lateral Raise
instructions: Stand side-on to the landmine and hold the end of the bar with the hand furthest from it, down by your hip.
Keep your arm almost straight.
Raise the bar out to the side up to shoulder height.
Lower it with control and repeat, then switch sides.
tips: Lead with your elbow.
Don't lean to lift the bar.
ex_TK2DHH.description: Landmine Lateral Raise is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Traps.

ex_WXFPFY.name: Landmine Overhead Press
instructions: Stand facing the landmine with the end of the bar held at your chest in both hands.
Brace your core.
Press the bar up and forward until your arms are straight.
Lower it to your chest and repeat.
tips: Keep your ribs down and your back neutral.
Push your head slightly forward at the top.
ex_WXFPFY.description: Landmine Overhead Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Upper Chest.

ex_7PUNJR.name: Landmine Seated Alternating Overhead Press
instructions: Sit on a bench facing the landmine, holding the end of the bar at one shoulder.
Press the bar up and forward until your arm is straight.
Lower it to your shoulder.
Switch hands and press with the other arm.
tips: Sit tall with your feet planted.
Keep the bar path smooth.
ex_7PUNJR.description: Landmine Seated Alternating Overhead Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Core.

ex_CYENZE.name: Landmine Seated Overhead Press
instructions: Sit on a bench facing the landmine, holding the end of the bar at your chest with both hands.
Brace your core with your back tall.
Press the bar up and forward until your arms are straight.
Lower it and repeat.
tips: Don't lean back.
Keep your feet planted.
ex_CYENZE.description: Landmine Seated Overhead Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Upper Chest.

ex_UKMQAG.name: Landmine Seated Single Arm Overhead Press
instructions: Sit on a bench facing the landmine, holding the end of the bar at one shoulder.
Brace your core.
Press the bar up and forward with one arm until it is straight.
Lower it and repeat, then switch arms.
tips: Keep your torso square.
Control the lowering phase.
ex_UKMQAG.description: Landmine Seated Single Arm Overhead Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Core.

ex_H4X2DK.name: Landmine Single Arm Push Press
instructions: Stand facing the landmine, holding the end of the bar at one shoulder.
Dip slightly by bending your knees.
Drive up through your legs and press the bar up and forward until your arm is straight.
Lower it to your shoulder and repeat, then switch arms.
tips: Use the leg drive to move heavier weight.
Keep the dip short and upright.
ex_H4X2DK.description: Landmine Single Arm Push Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Quadriceps, Core.

ex_QSCPL6.name: Landmine Single Arm Staggered Overhead Press
instructions: Stand in a staggered stance holding the end of the bar at the shoulder on the side of your back leg.
Brace your core.
Press the bar up and forward until your arm is straight.
Lower it and repeat, then switch sides.
tips: Keep your hips square.
Squeeze the glute of your back leg.
ex_QSCPL6.description: Landmine Single Arm Staggered Overhead Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Core, Upper Chest.

ex_LAF3UQ.name: Lateral Raise Bodyweight
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms at your sides.
Raise your arms out to the sides until they are parallel to the floor, keeping your elbows slightly bent and your palms facing down.
Hold the position for a second, then slowly lower your arms back to your sides with control.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining a steady and controlled pace.
tips: Avoid lifting your shoulders; focus on using your deltoids to raise your arms.
Move slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you raise your arms and inhaling as you lower them.
Ensure your elbows remain slightly bent to reduce strain on your joints.
ex_LAF3UQ.description: Lateral Raise Bodyweight is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_YJNKSH.name: Lateral Raise to Shoulder Press Resistance Band Cable
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, placing the resistance band under both feet. Hold the handles of the resistance band with your palms facing inward and your arms at your sides.
Perform a lateral raise by lifting the handles out to the sides until your arms are parallel to the floor, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Once your arms are parallel to the floor, rotate your wrists so your palms face forward, bend your arms at 90 degrees up and press the handles overhead until your arms are fully extended.
Lower the handles back to shoulder height, rotate your wrists back to the starting position, and then lower your arms back to your sides. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back straight and avoid using momentum.
Use a lighter resistance band if needed to ensure proper form and gradually increase the resistance as you get stronger.
Exhale as you lift the handles and press them overhead, and inhale as you lower them back down.
ex_YJNKSH.description: Lateral Raise to Shoulder Press Resistance Band Cable is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Chest, Triceps, Rotator Cuff.

ex_LFID7R.name: Lateral Raises Dumbbell Seated With Swing
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your arms hanging by your sides and palms facing your body. Keep your torso leaning towards the floor.
Begin raising your torso while swinging both arms out to the sides until they reach shoulder height, using a controlled momentum and bending your elbows at 90 degrees as you raise up.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring your arms are parallel and your torso vertical to the floor.
Lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Do not raise the dumbbells higher than shoulder height to prevent shoulder strain.
Use a controlled swing to lift the weights; avoid excessive momentum.
Exhale as you lift the dumbbells and inhale as you lower them.
ex_LFID7R.description: Lateral Raises Dumbbell Seated With Swing is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Lower Back.

ex_KJPKO4.name: Lateral Raises Dumbbell
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with your palms facing your body.
Raise both arms out to the sides until they reach shoulder height, maintaining a slight bend in your elbows.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring your arms are parallel to the floor.
Lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Do not raise the dumbbells higher than shoulder height to prevent shoulder strain.
Maintain a slight bend in your elbows throughout the exercise.
Keep your wrists straight and aligned with your forearms.
ex_KJPKO4.description: Lateral Raises Dumbbell is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_6RUSTH.name: Lateral Raises on Cable Machine
instructions: Stand with your right side facing the cable machine, feet shoulder-width apart. Attach a handle to the low pulley and grasp the handle with your left hand, palm facing inward.
Raise the handle out to your side until your left arm is parallel to the floor, keeping a slight bend in your elbow.
Slowly lower the handle back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides to work the opposite arm.
tips: Keep your back straight and avoid using momentum.
Focus on engaging your shoulder muscles throughout the movement.
Exhale as you raise the handle and inhale as you lower it back down.
ex_6RUSTH.description: Lateral Raises on Cable Machine is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_5OZ56U.name: Laying Lateral Raise
instructions: Lie on your side on a bench or the floor, holding a light weight in your top hand.
Start with your arm in front of your body.
Raise your arm up and out until it points toward the ceiling.
Lower it slowly and repeat, then switch sides.
tips: Use a light weight.
Keep a slight bend in your elbow.
ex_5OZ56U.description: Laying Lateral Raise is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Rear Shoulders.

ex_UDDGLG.name: Leaning Dumbbell Lateral Raise
instructions: Stand next to a lifting cage, holding a dumbbell in your right hand. Grasp the lifting cage bar for support with your left hand and lean your body to the opposite side by extending your arm.
With your right arm hanging down, raise the dumbbell out to your side until your arm is parallel to the floor, keeping a slight bend in your elbow and your palm facing down.
Lower the dumbbell back to the starting position with control. Complete the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid using momentum; lift the dumbbell with control.
Exhale as you lift the dumbbell and inhale as you lower it.
Maintain a slight bend in your elbow throughout the exercise.
ex_UDDGLG.description: Leaning Dumbbell Lateral Raise is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_62MNGJ.name: Low Cable Overhead Flyes
instructions: Stand in the center of a cable machine with the pulleys set at the lowest position. Grasp the handles with each hand, palms facing up, and take a step forward to create tension in the cables.
Lean lightly forward and position your feet shoulder-width apart, keeping your back straight and your arms extended slightly behind you.
Raise the handles up and together in a wide arc, bringing them to meet above your head, while keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Slowly lower your arms back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back straight and avoid using momentum.
Focus on squeezing your shoulder muscles at the top of the movement.
Exhale as you raise the handles and inhale as you lower them back down.
ex_62MNGJ.description: Low Cable Overhead Flyes is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Biceps.

ex_AICYR3.name: Lying Bench External Shoulder Rotation
instructions: Lie on your back on a bench with your arms extended out to the sides, your elbows bent at 90 degrees, and your forearms hanging off the sides of the bench, perpendicular to the floor in line with your head.
Rotate your shoulders to lift your forearms upward until they are vertical to the floor, maintaining the 90-degree angle at your elbows throughout the movement.
Slowly lower your forearms back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your core engaged and your back flat against the bench to maintain stability.
Move slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Keep your elbows fixed at a 90-degree angle throughout the movement to isolate the shoulder rotation.
ex_AICYR3.description: Lying Bench External Shoulder Rotation is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

ex_XNJEQZ.name: Lying Bench Internal Rotation Stretch
instructions: Lie on your back on a bench with your arms extended out to the sides, your elbows bent at 90 degrees, and your forearms hanging off the sides of the bench, perpendicular to the floor in line with your torso.
Rotate your shoulders to lift your forearms upward until they are vertical to the floor, maintaining the 90-degree angle at your elbows throughout the movement.
Slowly lower your forearms back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your core engaged and your back flat against the bench to maintain stability.
