tips: Exhale as you lift your arms and inhale as you lower them back down.
Use a resistance band that provides enough tension to challenge your muscles without compromising form.
Avoid swinging your body or using momentum to lift the band.
ex_A5VB2U.description: Side Lateral Raise Resistance Band is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_SZFB65.name: Smith Machine Shoulder Press
instructions: Position an adjustable bench under the Smith machine and set it to a vertical position. Adjust the barbell to your shoulder height.
Sit on the bench with your back straight and feet flat on the floor. Grip the barbell with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the barbell and press it upward until your arms are fully extended above your head.
Lower the barbell back to shoulder height with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your back remains flat against the bench throughout the movement.
Focus on using your shoulder muscles to press the weight, avoiding excessive strain on your neck.
Keep your elbows slightly bent at the top to avoid straining your elbow joints.
ex_SZFB65.description: Smith Machine Shoulder Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a smith machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Upper Chest, Upper Back.

ex_FFMPFI.name: Standing Arnold Press Dumbbell
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height. Your palms should be facing backward, and your elbows should be bent.
Begin to press the dumbbells overhead. As you press, rotate your palms so they face forward at the top of the movement.
Fully extend your arms at the top, ensuring your biceps are near your ears.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position by rotating your palms back towards your shoulders. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Rotate your wrists smoothly during the pressing and lowering phases to avoid strain.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you press the weights up and inhaling as you lower them back down.
Focus on the full range of motion to engage all parts of the shoulder muscles effectively.
ex_FFMPFI.description: Standing Arnold Press Dumbbell is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Chest, Triceps.

ex_YZW4JO.name: Standing Dumbbell Alternate Shoulder Press
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height with your palms facing forward and elbows pointing to the floor.
Press the right dumbbell overhead until your arm is fully extended, keeping the left dumbbell at shoulder height.
Lower the right dumbbell back to shoulder height with control and then press the left dumbbell overhead until your arm is fully extended.
Continue alternating arms for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on your breathing: exhale while pressing the dumbbell up and inhale while lowering it.
Avoid shrugging your shoulders to minimize neck strain.
Incorporate shoulder warm-up exercises to prepare the muscles for the workout.
ex_YZW4JO.description: Standing Dumbbell Alternate Shoulder Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Upper Back.

ex_CT3NXX.name: Standing Front Raise Dumbbell
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your arms fully extended in front of your hips and palms facing your thighs.
Raise both arms straight in front of you until they are parallel to the floor, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Lower your arms back to the starting position with control.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Warm up your shoulders with light exercises before starting to prevent injury.
Keep your head and neck in a neutral position to avoid unnecessary strain.
Focus on your breathing: exhale as you lift the dumbbell and inhale as you lower it.
ex_CT3NXX.description: Standing Front Raise Dumbbell is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Lower Back.

ex_H3ZGT5.name: Standing Overhand Shoulder Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, arms extended straight out in front of you at shoulder level, palms facing down.
Swiftly raise your right arm overhead while simultaneously lowering your left arm down towards your thigh to your side. Keeping both arms straight.
Swiftly return to the starting position and repeat the stretch by raising your left arm overhead and lowering your right arm.
Perform the stretch for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily throughout the stretch, exhaling as you raise and lower your arms and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
Focus on keeping both arms straight and avoiding any twisting or turning of your torso.
Use a gentle motion to avoid over-stretching and potential muscle strain.
ex_H3ZGT5.description: Standing Overhand Shoulder Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Chest.

ex_PD557M.name: Standing Reverse Shoulder Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, keeping your posture upright. Clasp your hands behind your back, interlocking your fingers.
Straighten your arms and slowly lift your hands upwards, feeling a stretch in your shoulders.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, and return to the starting position by lowering your hands and releasing the clasp.
Repeat the stretch for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on keeping your arms straight and avoiding any bending at the elbows.
Ensure your shoulders remain relaxed and avoid tensing them up towards your ears.
Use a gentle motion to avoid over-stretching and potential muscle strain.
ex_PD557M.description: Standing Reverse Shoulder Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Chest.

ex_32NW2D.name: Standing Shoulder Press Dumbbell
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height with your palms facing forward and elbows pointing to the floor.
Press both dumbbells overhead until your arms are fully extended, keeping your elbows slightly bent at the top.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to shoulder height with control, maintaining tension in your shoulders.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily: exhale as you press the dumbbells up and inhale as you lower them down.
Focus on using your shoulder muscles to lift the weight, avoiding excessive strain on your neck.
Keep your back straight and avoid arching your lower back during the press.
ex_32NW2D.description: Standing Shoulder Press Dumbbell is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Upper Back.

ex_SSJLIJ.name: Standing Swimmer
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, your left arm extended up, your right arm extended down, and your palms facing forward.
Simultaneously move your right arm up while moving your left arm down and lightly rotating your core, mimicking a swimming motion. Keep your arms straight throughout the movement.
Continue alternating arms in a smooth, controlled motion for the desired repetitions.
tips: Keep your core tight to maintain balance and stability.
Focus on keeping your movements smooth and fluid, avoiding any jerky motions.
Breathe steadily: exhale as you move your arms back and inhale as you return to the starting position.
ex_SSJLIJ.description: Standing Swimmer is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Core.

ex_IRMYVN.name: Standing Y Raise
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, with your arms extended forward, parallel to each other.
With slightly bent elbows, raise both arms diagonally overhead to form a "Y" shape.
Slowly lower your arms back to the starting position.
Repeat the movement for the desired repetitions
tips: Move slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and avoid injury.
Breathe steadily: exhale as you raise your arms and inhale as you lower them.
Focus on keeping your arms in a diagonal line to form a "Y" shape and avoid any excessive swinging.
ex_IRMYVN.description: Standing Y Raise is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_M2IAHG.name: Suspension Trainer With Grips Face Pull
instructions: Adjust the suspension trainer handles to about chest height. Stand facing the handles with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handles with your arms extended straight in front of you and palms facing each other.
Engage your core and lean back slightly, keeping your body straight from head to heels.
Pull the handles towards your face, bending your elbows and flaring them out to the sides until your hands are at face level.
Slowly extend your arms back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily: exhale as you pull the handles towards your face and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Focus on using your upper back and shoulder muscles to perform the pull, avoiding excessive use of your arms.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid shrugging them towards your ears.
ex_M2IAHG.description: Suspension Trainer With Grips Face Pull is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a suspension trainer, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Forearms.

ex_F3NLX6.name: Suspension Trainer With Grips Front Raise
instructions: Adjust the suspension trainer handles to about chest height. Stand facing the handles with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handles with your arms extended straight in front of you and palms facing down.
Engage your core and lean back slightly, keeping your body straight from head to heels.
Keeping your arms straight, raise the handles upward until your arms are fully extended above your head, forming a straight line with your body.
Slowly lower the handles back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep tension in the suspension trainer straps throughout the exercise.
Avoid letting your hips sag to maintain proper body alignment.
If you feel strain in your lower back, readjust your position and ensure your core is engaged.
ex_F3NLX6.description: Suspension Trainer With Grips Front Raise is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a suspension trainer, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Core.

ex_RMKFRW.name: Suspension Trainer With Grips Rear Delt Row
instructions: Adjust the suspension trainer handles to about chest height. Stand facing the anchor point with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handles with a neutral grip (palms facing each other), and lean back slightly with your arms extended.
Engage your upper back and pull your chest towards the handles by bending your elbows and driving them out to the sides, focusing on squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Continue pulling until your upper arms are parallel to the floor and your elbows are bent at a 90-degree angle.
Slowly extend your arms back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily: exhale as you pull your chest towards the handles and inhale as you extend your arms back.
Keep your core tight to maintain stability and prevent your hips from sagging.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid shrugging them towards your ears.
ex_RMKFRW.description: Suspension Trainer With Grips Rear Delt Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a suspension trainer, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Forearms.

ex_IP4AK3.name: Suspension Trainer With Grips Single Arm Rear Delt Row
instructions: Adjust the suspension trainer handle to about chest height. Stand facing the handle, holding one handle with an overhand grip (palm facing down), and lean back slightly with your arm extended and feet shoulder-width apart.
Engage your arm and pull your chest towards the handle by bending your elbow and driving it out to the side, focusing on squeezing your shoulder blade towards your spine.
Continue pulling until your upper arm is parallel to the floor and your elbow is bent at a 90-degree angle.
Slowly extend your arm back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
tips: Focus on using your rear deltoid and upper back muscles to perform the row, avoiding excessive use of your arm.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid shrugging them towards your ears.
Breathe steadily: exhale as you pull your chest towards the handle and inhale as you extend your arm back.
ex_IP4AK3.description: Suspension Trainer With Grips Single Arm Rear Delt Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a suspension trainer, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Forearms.

ex_EHFUB7.name: Suspension Trainer With Grips Split Fly
instructions: Adjust the suspension trainer handles to about chest height. Stand facing the handles with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a handle in each hand with an overhand grip (palm facing down) with the left hand and an underhand with the right (palm facing up).
Engage your core and lean back slightly with your arm extended, keeping your body straight from head to heels and your arms extended in front of you at shoulder height.
Spread your arms in front of you, bringing your left arm overhead and the right arm by your hip, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Slowly bring your arms back together to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Start with a smaller range of motion and gradually increase as your strength and flexibility improve.
Ensure your wrists are straight and not bending during the movement.
Breathe steadily: exhale as you open your arms and inhale as you bring them back together.
ex_EHFUB7.description: Suspension Trainer With Grips Split Fly is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a suspension trainer, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_3ZZLFQ.name: Trap Bar Shrug
instructions: Stand in the center of a trap bar with your feet shoulder-width apart. Bend your knees and hips to lower your body, and grasp the handles of the trap bar with a neutral grip (palms facing in).
Stand up straight with the trap bar at arm's length by your sides, keeping your core engaged and back straight.
Lift your shoulders towards your ears, squeezing your traps at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower your shoulders back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily: exhale as you shrug your shoulders and inhale as you lower them.
Keep your neck relaxed and avoid straining it during the movement.
Ensure your back remains straight and avoid leaning forward or backward.
ex_3ZZLFQ.description: Trap Bar Shrug is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the traps (back). Performed with a trap bar, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Forearms.

ex_QPCW7B.name: Barbell Upright Row (Front View)
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an overhand grip (palms facing down), hands placed shoulder-width apart. Allow the barbell to rest against your thighs with your arms fully extended.
Pull the barbell upward along the front of your body by bending your elbows and lifting your upper arms.
Continue lifting the barbell until it reaches chest height, keeping your elbows higher than your wrists throughout the movement.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position by extending your arms fully. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Lead with your elbows to ensure proper muscle engagement and avoid wrist strain.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you lift the barbell and inhaling as you lower it back down.
Avoid using momentum or swinging your body to lift the barbell.
ex_QPCW7B.description: Barbell Upright Row (Front View) is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Biceps.

ex_BGBGCM.name: Upright Row Cable Resistance Band
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart in the middle of a resistance band, holding a handle in each hand with an overhand grip (palms facing back). Ensure the band is taut when your arms are extended downwards.
Lift the handles straight up towards your chin, leading with your elbows and keeping the band close to your body.
Raise the handles until your elbows are slightly higher than your shoulders and pointing to your sides.
Slowly lower the handles back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily: exhale as you lift the handles and inhale as you lower them.
Use a resistance band that allows you to maintain control and proper form throughout the exercise.
Avoid lifting the handles too high, which can put unnecessary strain on your shoulder joints.
ex_BGBGCM.description: Upright Row Cable Resistance Band is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Biceps.

ex_6X3YP2.name: Upright Row Dumbbell

Lift the dumbbells straight up towards your chin, leading with your elbows and keeping the weights close to your body.
Raise the dumbbells until your elbows are level with your shoulders, ensuring your upper arms are parallel to the floor.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Focus on using your shoulders and upper back to lift the dumbbells, avoiding excessive use of your biceps.
Avoid lifting the dumbbells too high, which can put unnecessary strain on your shoulder joints.
ex_6X3YP2.description: Upright Row Dumbbell is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Biceps.

ex_JIYSJO.name: Upright Row EZ Bar

Pull the EZ Bar upward along the front of your body by bending your elbows and lifting your upper arms.
Continue lifting the EZ Bar until it reaches chest height, keeping your elbows higher than your wrists throughout the movement.
Slowly lower the EZ Bar back to the starting position by extending your arms fully. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Breathe steadily, exhaling as you lift the barbell and inhaling as you lower it back down.

ex_JIYSJO.description: Upright Row EZ Bar is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with an ez barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Biceps.

ex_GJHGW2.name: Upward Rotation Bent Arms
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, arms bent at 90 degrees with your upper arms parallel to the floor, and your forearms pointing down to the floor.
Rotate your forearms upwards until your fingers point towards the ceiling, keeping your upper arms stationary.
Slowly rotate them back to the starting position.

Lift your arms as high as comfortable, to avoid unnecessary strain on your shoulder joints.
ex_GJHGW2.description: Upward Rotation Bent Arms is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Rotator Cuff.

ex_PMXW2P.name: Weighted Standing Shoulder Press With Plate
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a weight plate with both hands at chest level, elbows bent and pointing down.
Press the plate upward by extending your arms fully above your head, keeping your core tight and your back straight.
Lower the plate back down to chest level in a controlled manner.

ex_PMXW2P.description: Weighted Standing Shoulder Press With Plate is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps.

ex_MUGG3U.name: Abdominal Stretch
instructions: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and drawn towards your chest.
Wrap your arms around your knees, hugging them tightly.
Hold the stretch in this position, allowing your back to round slightly and your head to relax forward.
After holding the stretch for the desired amount of time, release your arms and return to a neutral sitting position.

ex_Z6SWRH.name: Above Head Chest Stretch

Hold the stretch in this position, keeping your back straight and core engaged.
After holding the stretch for the desired amount of time, return to the starting position.

Breathe deeply and steadily throughout the stretch to help relax your muscles.
Maintain a straight back and engaged core to ensure proper form and maximize the stretch.

ex_EV3R2X.name: Across Chest Shoulder Stretch

ex_ZISSOU.name: Adductor Stretch Side Standing

ex_6VOB4D.name: Adductor Stretch

Open your legs wide apart, stretching your inner thighs.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, or as needed.

ex_6VOB4D.description: Adductor Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the adductors (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors, Quadriceps.

ex_U5QDGM.name: All Fours Quad Stretch
instructions: Start in an all-fours position on a mat, with your hands directly under your shoulders and your knees under your hips.

ex_UNPA3K.name: Arms Behind Back Chest Stretch
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder width apart and clasp your hands behind your lower back.

ex_54M7RW.name: Arms Wide Chest Stretch

ex_USBTEH.name: Back Stretch Standing With Bench

ex_USBTEH.description: Back Stretch Standing With Bench is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Lower Back.

ex_PL5SQO.name: Back and Shoulder Stretch

ex_PL5SQO.description: Back and Shoulder Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Lats.

ex_RKXAKX.name: Backward Abdominal Stretch
instructions: Get down on your knees with your back straight, thighs extended, and legs resting on the floor.
Lean backward and hold your feet by extending your arms to stretch your abdominal muscles.
Maintain this stretch for 30-60 seconds.
tips: Keep your hips stable to ensure a deep and effective stretch.
Avoid overextending your back; only lean as far back as is comfortable and safe for your flexibility.
Breathe deeply and steadily to help relax your muscles and enhance the stretch.
ex_RKXAKX.description: Backward Abdominal Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Hip Flexors.

ex_6LWMN5.name: Backward Forward Turn to Side Neck Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your head in a neutral position.
Tilt your head backward, stretching the front of your neck.
Return to the neutral position, then tilt your head forward to stretch the back of your neck.
Turn your head to one side, holding briefly, and then return to the neutral position. Repeat on the other side.
tips: Perform the movements slowly and gently to avoid straining your neck muscles.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and down to prevent tension in your upper back and shoulders.
Breathe deeply and steadily to help relax your muscles and enhance the stretch.
ex_6LWMN5.description: Backward Forward Turn to Side Neck Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the levator scapulae (neck). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_2N6Z5E.name: Bent Arm Chest Stretch
instructions: Stand beside a wall and place your bent arm (elbow at a 90-degree angle) against the wall, with your forearm and hand flat against the wall.
Gently rotate your torso away from the wall to feel a stretch in your chest.
Hold this position for 15-30 seconds, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep your shoulder down and away from your ear to avoid strain and ensure proper alignment.
Rotate your torso slowly to control the intensity of the stretch and prevent overstretching.
Breathe deeply and steadily to help relax your muscles and enhance the stretch.
ex_2N6Z5E.description: Bent Arm Chest Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.

ex_4J6RUE.name: Biceps Stretch Behind the Back
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and clasp your hands together behind your back.
Straighten your arms and pull your shoulders back to feel a stretch in your biceps.
Keep your arms straight and maintain the stretch.
Hold this position for 15-30 seconds, then return to the starting position.
tips: Keep your back straight and avoid arching to maintain proper form.
Ensure your hands are firmly clasped together to maximize the effectiveness of the stretch.
Breathe deeply and steadily to help relax your muscles and enhance the stretch.
ex_4J6RUE.description: Biceps Stretch Behind the Back is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.

ex_X4TMXT.name: Boat Stretch
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended straight in front of you.
Bend your knees slightly and lift your legs off the floor, balancing on your buttocks.
Extend your arms forward, parallel to the floor, to grab your legs and lean back slightly while keeping your back straight.
Hold this position, maintaining balance.
tips: Engage your core to maintain balance and prevent your lower back from rounding.
Keep your chest lifted and shoulders relaxed to ensure proper form.
Breathe deeply and steadily to help maintain the stretch and balance.
ex_X4TMXT.description: Boat Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps.

ex_KQXKDT.name: Bodyweight Standing Back Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and bring both arms straight behind your back, holding your hands together.
Gently arch your back, pushing your hips forward and looking towards the ceiling.
Hold the stretched position for a few seconds, maintaining a gentle and controlled stretch.
Return to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep the movement gentle to avoid straining your lower back.
Engage your core to support your lower back during the stretch.
Breathe deeply and steadily to enhance the stretch and relaxation.
ex_KQXKDT.description: Bodyweight Standing Back Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Abdominals, Chest.

ex_6B7JWV.name: Both Arms Behind on Wall Biceps Stretch
instructions: Stand upright facing away from a wall and place both palms facing upward against it behind your body with your arms fully extended.
Bend your knees slowly while keeping your hands against the wall until you feel a gentle stretch in your upper arms and shoulders.
Keep your elbows fully extended, your chest up, and hold the stretch for the desired duration.
Return to starting position to release tension.
tips: Keep both elbows fully extended throughout the stretch.
Stand tall and avoid leaning your torso forward.
Bend your knees gradually, reaching a comfortable stretch without feeling pain.
Breathe slowly and evenly while holding the stretch.
ex_6B7JWV.description: Both Arms Behind on Wall Biceps Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Forearms.

ex_RO6QFD.name: Bulgarian Split Squat Stretch
instructions: Place your front foot flat on the floor and keep your torso upright.
Kneel in a split stance with your rear knee on the floor and the top of your rear foot resting against a wall behind you.
Gently shift your hips backward until you feel a comfortable stretch through the front of your rear thigh and hip.
Hold the stretch for the desired duration, then return to the starting position and repeat on the opposite side.
tips: Keep your torso upright throughout the stretch.
Keep your hips facing forward and avoid twisting your pelvis.
Shift your hips backward gradually until you feel a gentle stretch without pain.
Breathe slowly and evenly while holding the stretch.
ex_RO6QFD.description: Bulgarian Split Squat Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Hamstrings, Core.

ex_XLYK6H.name: Butterfly Yoga Flaps
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs bent and the soles of your feet pressed together, allowing your knees to fall out to the sides.
Hold your feet with both hands and sit up tall, lengthening your spine.
Gently flap your knees up and down like the wings of a butterfly, keeping your movements smooth and controlled.
Continue the flapping motion for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back straight and avoid slouching to maintain proper posture.
Breathe deeply and evenly throughout the exercise to relax your muscles and enhance the stretch.
Perform the flapping motion gently to avoid straining your hip joints and inner thighs.
ex_XLYK6H.description: Butterfly Yoga Flaps is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the adductors (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

ex_ZCWXCU.name: Calf Push Stretch With Hands Against Wall (Variation 2)
instructions: Stand facing a wall with your feet shoulder-width apart. Place your hands on the wall at shoulder height and shoulder-width apart.
Step your right foot back and keep on your toes, keeping your leg straight and bring your left leg close to the wall, touching it with your forefoot.
Press your back heel flat to the floor, pushing with your left forefoot against the wall to deepen the stretch in your calf.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, then switch legs and repeat.
tips: Maintain a straight back and avoid arching or rounding your spine.
Use a lighter push against the wall if you are new to stretching, gradually increasing the pressure as you become more flexible.
Breathe deeply and steadily throughout the stretch to help relax your muscles.
ex_ZCWXCU.description: Calf Push Stretch With Hands Against Wall (Variation 2) is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category.

ex_G64VUQ.name: Calf Stretch With Hands Against Wall
instructions: Stand facing a wall with your feet shoulder-width apart. Place your hands on the wall at shoulder height and shoulder-width apart.
Step one foot back, keeping your back leg straight and your front leg slightly bent. Press your back heel into the floor.
Lean forward slightly, pushing against the wall to deepen the stretch in your calf.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, then switch legs and repeat.
tips: Keep your back leg straight and your heel pressed into the floor to maximize the stretch.
Stretch both legs equally to maintain balanced flexibility.
Breathe deeply and steadily throughout the stretch to help relax your muscles.
ex_G64VUQ.description: Calf Stretch With Hands Against Wall is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category.

ex_747VFO.name: Calf Stretch With Rope
instructions: Lie on the floor with your legs extended straight on the floor. Pass a rope with handles under your right forefoot, holding the handles with both hands.
Keep your back flat against the floor and gently pull the rope towards you, flexing your foot and bringing your toes towards your shin.
Straighten your leg fully to deepen the stretch in your calf muscle.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, then release the rope and switch to the other foot, repeating the stretch.
tips: Breathe deeply and steadily throughout the stretch to help relax your muscles.
Use a moderate amount of tension on the rope to ensure a good stretch without causing discomfort or pain.
Focus on feeling the stretch in your calf muscle, not your lower back or hamstrings.
ex_747VFO.description: Calf Stretch With Rope is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with a rope, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings.

ex_REWGH2.name: Calve Stretch Foot on Wall
instructions: Stand facing a wall and place both hands against it for support. Position the ball of one foot against the wall with your heel off the wall, while your opposite foot remains behind you for balance.
Keep your stretching leg straight and slowly lean your body toward the wall until you feel a stretch in your calf.
Hold the stretch while keeping your heel firmly in contact with the floor.
Return to the starting position with control and repeat before switching legs.
tips: Lean forward gradually until you feel a comfortable stretch without pain.
Keep both hips facing the wall to maintain proper alignment.
Inhale as you prepare and exhale as you lean into the stretch.
ex_REWGH2.description: Calve Stretch Foot on Wall is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings.

ex_TJP77S.name: Calve Stretch From Wall to Floor
instructions: Stand facing a wall and place both hands against it for support. Step one foot forward near the wall and extend your opposite leg straight behind you.
Slowly lean your body toward the wall, bending your front leg at the knee joint , while straightening your back leg.
Hold the stretch when you feel it in the calf of your back leg, keeping your heel as on the floor.
Return to the starting position with control and repeat before switching legs.
tips: Keep your back leg straight throughout the stretch.
Lean forward gradually until you feel a comfortable stretch.
Inhale before leaning forward and exhale as you deepen the stretch.
ex_TJP77S.description: Calve Stretch From Wall to Floor is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings.

ex_Q4XT2K.name: Calves Stretch on Stairs
instructions: Stand on a step or stair with one foot on a higher step and the other foot on a lower step, ensuring the lower foot's heel is hanging off the edge.
Hold onto the railing or wall for support to maintain balance.
Slowly lower the heel of the lower foot below the level of the step until you feel a stretch in your calf muscle.
Hold the stretch for the desired duration, then slowly raise your heel back to the starting position. Repeat as needed for both legs.
tips: Maintain an upright posture and engage your core to ensure balance and stability.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to avoid straining your calf muscles.
Use the railing or wall for support but ensure your legs are performing the stretch.
Perform this stretch after a workout or when your muscles are warm to maximize flexibility and prevent injury.
ex_Q4XT2K.description: Calves Stretch on Stairs is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps.

ex_DFNCM3.name: Calves Stretch on Step
instructions: Stand on the edge of a step with the balls of both feet on the platform and your heels hanging off the edge. Place both hands against a wall for support.
Keep your legs straight and slowly lower your heels below the level of the step until you feel a stretch in your calves.
Hold the stretch while keeping your movements relaxed and controlled.
Raise your heels back to the starting position with control and repeat for the desired number of repetitions or hold time.
tips: Lower your heels slowly to deepen the stretch without bouncing.
Keep the balls of your feet firmly on the edge of the step.
Stretch only until you feel a comfortable pull in your calves, not pain.
Inhale before lowering your heels and exhale as you deepen the stretch.
ex_DFNCM3.description: Calves Stretch on Step is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings.

ex_4C3BOC.name: Ceiling Look Stretch
instructions: Begin in a tabletop position on all fours, with your wrists aligned under your shoulders and your knees aligned under your hips.
Slowly lift your torso upwards, arching your back gently and leaning backward.
Allow your hands to slide down to your legs, supporting your upper body as you look up towards the ceiling.
Hold this position for the desired duration and slowly return to the starting tabletop position. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe deeply and evenly, inhaling as you lift your torso and exhaling as you return to the starting position.
Avoid forcing the stretch; only lean back as far as is comfortable without causing pain.
Use a mat or cushion under your knees for added comfort and support.
Perform this stretch to enhance flexibility in your spine and relieve tension in your chest and neck.
ex_4C3BOC.description: Ceiling Look Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Neck.

ex_EUO7UJ.name: Chest Out Hands Behind (Hold)
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart, keeping your back straight and shoulders relaxed.
Interlace your fingers behind your back, extending your arms straight.
Lift your arms slightly while pushing your chest out and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Hold this position for the desired duration, maintaining a steady and controlled breath throughout the stretch.
tips: Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together to deepen the stretch in your chest and shoulders.
Keep your neck relaxed and in a neutral position to avoid tension.
Use a mirror to check your form and ensure you are maintaining proper alignment.
ex_EUO7UJ.description: Chest Out Hands Behind (Hold) is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_VRZ6VV.name: Chest Stretch With Exercise Ball
instructions: Begin on all fours, with your knees directly under your hips and your hands directly under your shoulders.
Place your right forearm on an exercise ball positioned to your side, with your elbow bent at a 90-degree angle.
Slowly lower your chest towards the floor to deepen the stretch in your chest.
Hold this position for the desired duration, then return to the starting position and switch arms to repeat the stretch on the other side.
tips: Allow your chest to lower gently towards the floor, but do not force it. Only go as far as is comfortable to avoid straining your shoulder.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize the effectiveness of the stretch.
Focus on relaxing your chest and shoulder to deepen the stretch.
Ensure your hips remain aligned with your knees to maintain a stable base.
Use a mirror or partner to check your form and ensure you are maintaining proper alignment.
ex_VRZ6VV.description: Chest Stretch With Exercise Ball is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a stability ball, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.

ex_D2KRYI.name: Child Pose Lower Back Stretch
instructions: Kneel on the floor with your big toes together and knees apart.
Sit your hips back toward your heels.
Reach your arms forward and lower your chest toward the floor.
Rest your forehead down and breathe deeply into your lower back.
tips: Keep your knees closer together for a deeper back stretch.
Relax your shoulders.
ex_D2KRYI.description: Child Pose Lower Back Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Lats, Glutes.

ex_DV4NCP.name: Circles Knee Stretch
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet together and knees slightly bent. Place your hands on your hips for support.
Keeping your knees together, bend them together and slowly rotate them in a circular motion to the right, making small controlled circles.
Continue circling your knees for the desired number of repetitions, then reverse the direction of the circles and rotate to the left.
Maintain a steady pace and keep your upper body relaxed throughout the exercise.
tips: Focus on making smooth and controlled movements to avoid straining your knees and joints.
Perform the movement slowly to maintain control and improve knee mobility.
Ensure your knees remain close together to maximize the effectiveness of the stretch.
ex_DV4NCP.description: Circles Knee Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Hip Flexors.

ex_6LEZTK.name: Cobra Stretch
instructions: Lie face down with your legs extended and the tops of your feet resting on the floor. Place your hands beneath your shoulders with your elbows close to your body.
Press through your hands to slowly lift your chest while extending your arms and keeping your hips in contact with the floor.
Raise your chest until you feel a comfortable stretch through your lower back and abdomen while keeping your shoulders relaxed.
Hold the stretch briefly, then slowly lower your chest back to the starting position with control.
tips: Keep your hips and legs in contact with the floor throughout the stretch.
Press up gradually and avoid forcing your lower back into excessive extension.
Keep your elbows close to your body as you lift your chest.
Exhale as you lift your chest and inhale as you lower back down.
ex_6LEZTK.description: Cobra Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Shoulders, Lower Back.

ex_56NWED.name: Cocoons
instructions: Begin by lying flat on your back with your legs extended straight and your arms extended overhead on the floor.
Engage your core and simultaneously lift your legs off the floor while bringing your arms forward to meet your knees, curling your body into a "cocoon" position.
Hold the cocoon position for a moment, squeezing your core muscles.
Slowly lower your legs and arms back to the starting position, maintaining control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on using your abdominal muscles to lift your legs and upper body, avoiding momentum.
Use a mat or soft surface to support your back and prevent discomfort during the exercise.
Ensure your lower back remains in contact with the floor as you lift and lower your legs to avoid unnecessary strain.
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you curl into the cocoon position and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
ex_56NWED.description: Cocoons is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors, Obliques.

ex_SB4JYU.name: Corner Wall Chest Stretch
instructions: Begin by standing in front of a corner of a wall with your feet shoulder-width apart. Place your palms flat against the walls at your sides, with your elbows slightly below shoulder height.
Lean forward into the corner, keeping your legs in place, to lean into the stretch.
Push your chest forward towards the corner, feeling the stretch across your chest and shoulders. Hold this position for the desired duration.
Slowly step back to return to the starting position and repeat the stretch as needed.
tips: Perform the stretch with control, gradually increasing the intensity as your muscles loosen.
Breathe deeply and steadily throughout the stretch, inhaling as you prepare and exhaling as you lean into the stretch.
Ensure your palms remain flat against the wall to maximize the stretch across your chest and shoulders.
Use a mat or soft surface for your feet if needed to prevent slipping during the stretch.
ex_SB4JYU.description: Corner Wall Chest Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back, Biceps.

ex_XWMIGV.name: Crescent Moon Pose Quad Stretch With Block
instructions: Begin by standing beside a yoga block and move into a lunge position with one foot forward and your back knee resting on the floor.
Keeping your torso upright, grasp your back leg by the ankle and place your hand nearest to the block on top of it for support.
Gently shift your hips forward until you feel a stretch along the front of your back thigh. Hold the stretch while keeping your hips facing forward
Return to the starting position with control and repeat on the opposite side.
tips: Keep your front knee directly above your ankle.
Stretch only until you feel a comfortable pull in the front of your back thigh.
Maintain an upright torso throughout the stretch, using the yoga block as support for stability.
Inhale before moving forward and exhale as you deepen the stretch.
ex_XWMIGV.description: Crescent Moon Pose Quad Stretch With Block is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors, Glutes, Core.

ex_UK4QO4.name: Crescent Moon Pose Quad Stretch
instructions: Begin in a lunge position with one foot forward and your back knee resting on the floor. Bend your back knee and reach behind you to grasp your back foot with both hands.
Gently draw your back heel toward your glutes while keeping your chest lifted and your hips facing forward.
Hold the stretch until you feel a comfortable stretch along the front of your back thigh and hip.
Release your foot with control, return to the starting position, and repeat on the opposite side.
tips: Keep your front knee directly above your ankle.
Engage your core to help maintain balance and alignment.
Keep your chest lifted and avoid leaning excessively forward.
Inhale before deepening the stretch and exhale as you gently pull your foot closer.
ex_UK4QO4.description: Crescent Moon Pose Quad Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors, Glutes, Core.

ex_ZB47BP.name: Cross Body Elbow Pull Shoulder Stretch
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder width apart and your arms relaxed by your sides. Bend one arm behind your lower back with your elbow pointing outward.
Reach across your body with your opposite hand and grasp the elbow of your bent arm.
Gently pull the elbow across your body until you feel a comfortable stretch in the your shoulder.
Hold the stretch, then slowly release and repeat on the opposite side.
tips: Pull your elbow gently without forcing it beyond a comfortable range.
Maintain a slow, steady pull rather than using quick movements.
Keep your neck relaxed and your shoulders away from your ears.
Inhale before applying the stretch and exhale as you gently deepen it.
ex_ZB47BP.description: Cross Body Elbow Pull Shoulder Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Rotator Cuff, Upper Back, Chest.

ex_HJN5ZH.name: Cross Body Shoulder Stretch
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder width apart and your arms relaxed by your sides.
Raise one arm straight across the front of your chest at shoulder height.
Grasp your upper arm just above the elbow with your opposite hand and gently pull it closer to your chest while keeping your shoulders relaxed.
Hold the stretch, then slowly release and repeat on the opposite side.
tips: Pull from your upper arm rather than your forearm or wrist.
Keep your shoulders level and avoid shrugging them toward your ears.
Stretch only until you feel a comfortable pull in the back of your shoulder.
Inhale before applying the stretch and exhale as you gently pull your arm closer.
ex_HJN5ZH.description: Cross Body Shoulder Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Rotator Cuff.

ex_22Z6O2.name: Crossover Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch
instructions: Begin in a lunge position with your right foot on the floor and your left knee on the floor, ensuring both legs are bent at 90 degrees.
Engage your core and rotate your torso towards your right leg, placing both arms straight and pulling on the outside of your right thigh.
Gently push your hips forward while keeping your back straight to stretch.
Hold this position for the desired duration, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Ensure your front knee is aligned over your ankle to avoid unnecessary strain on your knee joint.
Perform the stretch with control to avoid overextending your hip flexors.
Breathe deeply and steadily throughout the stretch, inhaling through your nose and exhaling through your mouth.
ex_22Z6O2.description: Crossover Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Hamstrings.

ex_2VRKUJ.name: Crouching Heel Back Calf Stretch
instructions: Begin standing with your legs wide in a semi-lunge position, turned to the right side, with your left leg extended back and your right knee bent.
Bend forward at the hips and place your hands on the floor in front of you for balance, keeping your back as straight as possible.
Push your left heel down towards the floor, feeling a stretch in your left calf muscle.
Hold the stretch for the desired duration, then switch sides and repeat the stretch on the right side.
tips: Focus on keeping your back straight and your shoulders down and away from your ears.
Perform the stretch with control to avoid overextending your calf muscles.
Breathe deeply and steadily throughout the stretch, inhaling through your nose and exhaling through your mouth.
Ensure your supporting leg (the one in front) remains bent to maintain balance.
ex_2VRKUJ.description: Crouching Heel Back Calf Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Hamstrings, Glutes.

ex_5DSLQ2.name: Dead Hang Stretch
instructions: Begin by standing under a pull-up bar or a similar overhead bar.
Reach up and grasp the bar with both hands, palms facing forward (overhand grip), and your hands shoulder-width apart.
Allow your body to hang freely with your feet off the floor, keeping your arms fully extended and your shoulders relaxed.
Hold this position for the desired duration, focusing on deep breathing and maintaining a relaxed grip.
tips: Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid shrugging them towards your ears.
Focus on deep, steady breaths to enhance the stretch and promote relaxation.
Use a bar that is high enough to allow your body to hang freely without touching the floor.
If you find it challenging to maintain the grip, use chalk to prevent slipping.
Ensure the bar and your grip are secure to avoid any accidents during the stretch.
ex_5DSLQ2.description: Dead Hang Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Forearms, Chest.

ex_BQYIDW.name: Dumbbell RDL Stretch Isometric
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in your left hand, arm fully extended by your side, and your palm facing your thigh.
Hinge at your hips, lowering the dumbbell towards the floor while raising your left leg straight behind you, keeping it in line with your body. Your left leg should move in unison with your torso.
Continue lowering the dumbbell until your torso is parallel to the floor and you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
Hold this stretched position for the desired duration, then return to the starting position.
tips: Focus on hinging at your hips rather than bending your back.
Keep your shoulders retracted and your chest lifted throughout the movement.
Ensure your standing foot remains flat on the floor, with your weight distributed evenly.
ex_BQYIDW.description: Dumbbell RDL Stretch Isometric is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back.

ex_B3M5PJ.name: Dynamic Back Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms straight down by your sides.
Explosively swing your arms upwards in a wide arc until they are overhead, stretching your back muscles dynamically.
Immediately swing your arms back down to your sides in a controlled manner, allowing your back to relax.
Repeat the movement continuously for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your movements fluid and controlled to maximize the stretch and avoid any sudden jerks that could cause injury.
Engage your core muscles to support your lower back throughout the movement.
Ensure your knees are slightly bent to maintain balance and reduce strain on your lower back.
ex_B3M5PJ.description: Dynamic Back Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_QCPIR4.name: Elbow Back Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms at your sides.
Bring both hands behind you and place them on your lower back, fingers pointing downward.
Gently push your hips forward and lean your upper body backward, feeling a stretch in your chest and shoulders.
Hold the stretch for a few seconds, then return to the starting position. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Engage your core muscles to support your lower back as you lean backward.
Avoid overextending your lower back; only lean back as far as comfortable without causing pain.
Breathe deeply throughout the exercise, inhaling as you prepare to stretch and exhaling as you lean back.
ex_QCPIR4.description: Elbow Back Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_Z4KSXI.name: Elbow Extension and Supination Pronation Forearm Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms extended in front of you at hip level, palms open and over each other, with one hand crossing over the other.
Keep your palms crossed over each other and perform a wrist curl by bending your wrists upward.
Extend your wrists back down to the starting position.
Repeat the wrist curl and extension movements for the desired number of repetitions, then switch the position of your hands and repeat.
tips: Ensure your wrists and forearms do the majority of the movement, minimizing shoulder involvement.
Maintain straight arms and avoid bending your elbows during the stretch.
Perform the stretch with both hand positions to maintain muscle balance and flexibility.
ex_Z4KSXI.description: Elbow Extension and Supination Pronation Forearm Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Biceps.

ex_HARI3K.name: Elbow Flexor Stretch
instructions: Stand next to a wall with your feet shoulder-width apart, and extend your right arm out fully against the wall at shoulder height, palm facing the wall.
Rotate your torso away from the wall to increase the stretch in your arm.
Ensure your right arm is straight and press your palm firmly against the wall.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, feeling the stretch in your forearm and elbow flexors, then switch to the other arm.
tips: Ensure the stretch is felt in the forearm, elbow flexors, and chest muscles without causing pain.
Breathe deeply and steadily throughout the stretch, focusing on relaxing the muscles.
Perform the stretch on both arms to maintain muscle balance and flexibility.
ex_HARI3K.description: Elbow Flexor Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Biceps.

ex_RQSOKR.name: Elbows Back Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms at your sides.
Bring both hands behind you and place them on your lower back, fingers pointing downward.
Gently push your hips forward and lean your upper body backward, feeling a stretch in your chest and shoulders.
Hold the stretch for a few seconds, then return to the starting position. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Engage your core muscles to support your lower back as you lean backward.
Avoid overextending your lower back; only lean back as far as comfortable without causing pain.
Breathe deeply throughout the exercise, inhaling as you prepare to stretch and exhaling as you lean back.
ex_RQSOKR.description: Elbows Back Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_JM7JDZ.name: Exercise Ball Back Stretch
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart, and your hands resting on your thighs.
Slowly walk your feet forward and roll your body down the ball, allowing your back to drape over the ball until your lower back is supported.
Extend your arms at your sides, allowing them to hang naturally to the floor, and relax into the stretch, letting your spine gently curve over the ball.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, breathing deeply and allowing your back muscles to relax.
tips: Ensure your feet are firmly planted on the floor to maintain stability and balance.
Use a properly inflated exercise ball to ensure it supports your weight and provides a comfortable stretch.
Focus on relaxing your back and letting your spine naturally curve over the ball.
Breathe deeply and steadily, inhaling through your nose and exhaling through your mouth to enhance relaxation.
ex_JM7JDZ.description: Exercise Ball Back Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with a stability ball, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

ex_H2GKFX.name: Exercise Ball Hip Flexor Stretch
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball in a lunge position with your left foot flat on the floor in front of you and your right leg extended behind you, the ball supporting your hips.
Lower your hips downwards towards the floor, allowing the ball to support your weight and feeling a stretch in your right hip flexor.
Keep your torso upright and your core engaged as you hold the stretch.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, then switch legs and repeat on the other side.
tips: Move slowly into the stretch to prevent overextending or causing discomfort.
Breathe deeply and steadily, focusing on relaxing the hip flexor muscles.
Use a properly inflated exercise ball to provide adequate support for your hips.
ex_H2GKFX.description: Exercise Ball Hip Flexor Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a stability ball, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps.

ex_Z2LOPY.name: Exercise Ball Lat Stretch
instructions: Begin on the floor in a tabletop position with your hands and knees on the floor.
Have an exercise ball on your right side and position your right hand on the ball, keeping your arm bent at 90 degrees.
Slowly roll the ball forward with your right hand, extending your right arm overhead and lowering your chest lightly towards the floor, feeling the stretch along your back.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, then slowly roll the ball back towards you to return to the starting position. Repeat on the left side.
tips: Ensure your hips remain above your knees to maintain proper form and support.
Move slowly into the stretch to prevent overextending or causing discomfort.
Use a properly inflated exercise ball to provide adequate support for your arm.
ex_Z2LOPY.description: Exercise Ball Lat Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a stability ball, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.

ex_MAUHBD.name: Exercise Ball Lower Back Dynamic Stretch
instructions: Begin on your hands and feet with your arms and legs straight, positioning an exercise ball under your hips.
Slowly lower your body onto the ball, allowing it to support your hips and torso, while keeping your arms and legs straight and your hips bent.
Relax into the stretch for a second, letting your back gently arch over the ball and feeling a stretch in your lower back.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on deep, steady breathing, inhaling as you lower onto the ball and exhaling as you return to the starting position.
Ensure the exercise ball is properly inflated to provide adequate support and facilitate smooth movement.
Avoid overextending your back; only lower onto the ball as far as is comfortable without causing strain.
ex_MAUHBD.description: Exercise Ball Lower Back Dynamic Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with a stability ball, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Shoulders.

ex_RDRNSW.name: Exercise Ball Lower Back Prone Stretch
instructions: Begin on your hands and feet with your arms and legs straight, positioning an exercise ball under your hips.
Slowly lower your body onto the ball, allowing it to support your hips and torso, while keeping your arms and legs straight and your hips bent.
Relax into the stretch, letting your back gently arch over the ball and feeling a stretch in your lower back.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on deep, steady breathing, inhaling as you lower onto the ball and exhaling as you return to the starting position.
Ensure the exercise ball is properly inflated to provide adequate support and facilitate smooth movement.
Avoid overextending your back; only lower onto the ball as far as is comfortable without causing strain.
ex_RDRNSW.description: Exercise Ball Lower Back Prone Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with a stability ball, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Shoulders.

ex_GPKQRV.name: Exercise Ball Lying Side Lat Stretch (Variation 2)
instructions: Begin by lying on your side with an exercise ball positioned under your armpit and lower ribs. Extend your top leg straight and bend your lower leg, placing the foot flat on the floor for stability.
Allow your bottom arm to hang in a comfortable position for support over the ball and extend your left arm overhead, reaching it along the line of your body.
Allow your body to relax over the ball, feeling a stretch along the side of your torso and through your latissimus dorsi (lats).
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, breathing deeply and steadily. Slowly roll back to the starting position and repeat on the other side.
tips: Focus on deep, steady breathing, inhaling as you extend into the stretch and exhaling as you hold the stretch.
Avoid overextending your back; only stretch as far as is comfortable without causing strain.
Make sure your top leg is firmly planted on the floor to provide stability and support.
ex_GPKQRV.description: Exercise Ball Lying Side Lat Stretch (Variation 2) is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a stability ball, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Obliques, Shoulders.

ex_GZP5RI.name: Exercise Ball Lying Side Lat Stretch
instructions: Begin by lying on your side with an exercise ball positioned under your armpit and lower ribs. Extend your top leg straight and bend your lower leg, placing the foot flat on the floor for stability.
Extend your top arm on your side, keeping it along the line of your body, and allow your bottom arm to hang in a comfortable position for support over the ball.
Allow your body to relax over the ball, feeling a stretch along the side of your torso and through your latissimus dorsi (lats).
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, breathing deeply and steadily. Slowly roll back to the starting position and repeat on the other side.
tips: Focus on deep, steady breathing, inhaling as you extend into the stretch and exhaling as you hold the stretch.
Avoid overextending your back; only stretch as far as is comfortable without causing strain.
Make sure your top leg is firmly planted on the floor to provide stability and support.
ex_GZP5RI.description: Exercise Ball Lying Side Lat Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a stability ball, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Obliques, Shoulders.

ex_SRE4UK.name: Exercise Ball Seated Hamstring Stretch
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart, and your back straight.
Extend your right leg straight out in front of you, keeping your heel on the floor and your toes pointing up.
Slowly hinge at your hips, leaning forward while keeping your back straight, and reach towards your right toes with your right hand. Feel the stretch along the back of your right leg (hamstring).
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, breathing deeply and steadily. Return to the starting position and repeat with your left leg.
tips: Focus on deep, steady breathing, inhaling as you prepare to stretch and exhaling as you lean forward.
Only stretch as far as is comfortable without causing pain or discomfort.
Ensure the exercise ball is properly inflated to provide adequate support and stability.
ex_SRE4UK.description: Exercise Ball Seated Hamstring Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with a stability ball, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Calves.

ex_C66SQ6.name: Exercise Ball Seated Quad Stretch
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
Slowly roll forward until your back is supported on the ball, keeping your shoulders and head relaxed on the ball, and place your arms at your sides for balance.
Bend your left leg with your foot flat on the floor for support. Bend your right leg, placing the forefoot on the floor and the heel on the ball to feel the stretch in your right quadriceps.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, breathing deeply and steadily. Slowly return to the starting position and repeat with the opposite leg.
tips: Focus on deep, steady breathing, inhaling as you prepare to stretch and exhaling as you hold the stretch.
Only stretch as far as is comfortable without causing pain or discomfort.
Ensure the exercise ball is properly inflated to provide adequate support and stability.
ex_C66SQ6.description: Exercise Ball Seated Quad Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a stability ball, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

ex_JTJES3.name: Extension and Inclination Neck Stretch
instructions: Stand with your back straight and shoulders relaxed.
Slowly rotate your head to the left side while diagonally lowering your head, bringing your chin towards your left shoulder to feel a stretch in your neck.
Hold the stretch for a few seconds, breathing deeply and steadily.

Return to the neutral position and repeat on the other side by rotating your head to the right and diagonally lowering your head towards your right shoulder. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Maintain good posture with your back straight and shoulders relaxed throughout the exercise.
Perform the stretches in a smooth, fluid motion to enhance flexibility and reduce muscle tension.
Avoid overextending your neck; only stretch as far as is comfortable without causing pain or discomfort.
ex_JTJES3.description: Extension and Inclination Neck Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the levator scapulae (neck). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Neck.

ex_DPKQYV.name: Extension of Arms in Vertical Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, your back straight, and your core engaged.
Raise your arms overhead, interlocking your fingers and turning your palms upward.
Stretch upwards as much as possible, lengthening your spine and reaching towards the ceiling. Hold the position for 15-30 seconds.
Slowly release the stretch and bring your arms back down to your sides. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Move slowly and with control to maximize the stretch and avoid any sudden movements.
Focus on deep, steady breathing, inhaling as you reach upwards and exhaling as you hold the stretch.
Avoid arching your back; instead, focus on lengthening your spine.
ex_DPKQYV.description: Extension of Arms in Vertical Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Arms, Forearms.

ex_5P2L5F.name: Fixed Bar Stretch
instructions: Stand facing a fixed vertical bar. Position your feet shoulder-width apart and grasp the bar with both hands, palms facing each other.
Step back slightly and lean your hips backward, allowing your arms to extend fully and your upper body to lean forward. Keep your back straight and your knees bent.
Lean backwards and down to the floor while pulling back with your hips to feel a deep stretch in your shoulders, upper back, and lats.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, breathing deeply and steadily. Slowly return to the starting position by stepping forward and releasing the bar.
tips: Move slowly and with control to maximize the stretch and avoid any sudden movements.
Only stretch as far as is comfortable without causing pain or discomfort.
Ensure the bar is securely fixed and can support your weight.
ex_5P2L5F.description: Fixed Bar Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Arms.

ex_Y7RWC4.name: Foam Roller Back
instructions: Sit on the floor with a foam roller behind you and lie back so it is under your upper back.
Support your head with your hands and lift your hips slightly.
Roll slowly up and down from the bottom of your shoulder blades to the top of your back.
Pause on tight spots and breathe.
tips: Don't roll your lower back directly.
Move slowly.
ex_Y7RWC4.description: Foam Roller Back is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a roller, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Middle Back.

ex_ZSLFPT.name: Foam Roller Calves
instructions: Sit with your legs straight and a foam roller under your calves.
Lift your hips with your hands on the floor.
Roll slowly from your ankles to just below your knees.
Turn your legs in and out to reach the sides of your calves.
tips: Cross one leg over the other for more pressure.
Pause on tight spots.
ex_ZSLFPT.description: Foam Roller Calves is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with a roller, it falls under the flexibility category.

ex_O3GCCN.name: Foam Roller Lateral Quads
instructions: Lie on your side with a foam roller under the outside of your thigh.
Support yourself on your forearm and your top foot.
Roll slowly between your hip and your knee.
Pause on tender areas and breathe, then switch sides.
tips: Take weight through your top foot if it is too intense.
Don't roll over your knee.
ex_O3GCCN.description: Foam Roller Lateral Quads is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a roller, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Abductors.

ex_XTLFSK.name: Foam Roller Quads
instructions: Lie face down with a foam roller under the front of your thighs.
Support yourself on your forearms.
Roll slowly from your hips to just above your knees.
Pause on tight spots and breathe.
tips: Roll one leg at a time for more pressure.
Keep your core tight.
ex_XTLFSK.description: Foam Roller Quads is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a roller, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

ex_LSI65W.name: Forearms Pull With Opposite Hand Stretch
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder width apart and extend your right arm straight in front of your chest with your palm facing down.
Place your left hand over your right hand while keeping the working elbow straight and your shoulder relaxed.
Gently pull your right hand downward and toward your body until you feel a comfortable stretch along the top of your forearm.
Hold the stretch briefly, release your hand with control, and repeat for the desired duration before switching arms.
tips: Keep the elbow of your stretching arm fully extended throughout the movement.
Pull through the fingers rather than pressing directly against the wrist joint.
Stop if you feel sharp pain, tingling, or numbness in your wrist or hand.
Inhale before applying the stretch and exhale as you gently pull your fingers downward.
ex_LSI65W.description: Forearms Pull With Opposite Hand Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Shoulders.

ex_3JIO2N.name: Forearms Stretch on Wall Fingers Facing Down
instructions: Stand facing a wall and place the fingers of your right hand against it at shoulder height, pointing them downward. Keep your palm slightly away from the wall and maintain a small bend in your elbow.
Keep your fingers in contact with the wall as you slowly shift your body weight forward.
Gently press your right palm into the wall until you feel a comfortable stretch in your forearm.
Shift your weight backward and lift your palm away from the wall while keeping your fingers in contact, then repeat before switching to your left hand.
tips: Keep your fingers in contact with the wall throughout every repetition.
Maintain a small bend in your elbow instead of locking your arm.
Use a comfortable range of motion and stop if you feel pain, tingling, or numbness.
Inhale as you move your palm away and exhale as you press it into the wall.
ex_3JIO2N.description: Forearms Stretch on Wall Fingers Facing Down is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Forearms, Biceps.

ex_5FTQEE.name: Forearms Stretch on Wall
instructions: Stand with your right side beside a wall and place your right palm flat against it at shoulder height.
Keep your right hand against the wall, with a bend in your elbow and your shoulder relaxed.
Slowly shift your weight forward until you feel a stretch along your right forearm.
Hold the stretch, then release and repeat with your left arm.
tips: Keep your palm and fingers flat against the wall.
Keep your stretching arm straight throughout the stretch.
Stop if you feel pain, tingling, or numbness.
Inhale before turning and exhale as you deepen the stretch.
ex_5FTQEE.description: Forearms Stretch on Wall is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Chest, Shoulders.

ex_RSG6AC.name: Front Shoulder Stretch With Bar
