instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a bar with both hands, palms facing down, and hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Extend your arms straight down in front of you at shoulder height, keeping your back straight and core engaged.
Gently raise the bar overhead and bend them both at 90 degrees to lower them until you feel a stretch in your shoulders.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds. Repeat as needed.
tips: Keep your back straight and avoid arching or rounding your spine.
Use a lighter bar to ensure proper form and gradually increase the stretch as you become more flexible.
Breathe deeply and steadily throughout the stretch to help relax your muscles.
ex_RSG6AC.description: Front Shoulder Stretch With Bar is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Chest.

ex_CSG4MH.name: Half Neck Rolls
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder width apart and cross your arms over your chest.
Lower your chin toward your chest and slowly roll your head from the left side toward the right side.
Reverse the movement and roll your head back toward the left, keeping your chin moving across the front of your chest.
Continue moving slowly from side to side for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your shoulders relaxed and away from your ears.
Do not roll your head backward or drop it behind your shoulders.
Stop if you feel pain, dizziness, or tingling.
Inhale as you reach one side and exhale as your chin moves across your chest.
ex_CSG4MH.description: Half Neck Rolls is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the levator scapulae (neck). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_JG2GWT.name: Hamstring Lying Curl Up Stretch
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs extended and your arms at your sides.
Bend your right knee and bring it towards your chest until thigh is vertical to the floor, interlacing your fingers behind your thigh.
Slowly straighten your right leg, extending your heel towards the ceiling and feeling the stretch in your hamstring. Keep your left leg extended and flat on the floor.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, then slowly bend your right knee and lower your leg back to the starting position. Repeat on the left side.
tips: Keep your lower back pressed into the floor to maintain proper alignment and support.
Engage your core to stabilize your body and prevent your back from arching.
Move slowly and with control to maximize the stretch and avoid any sudden movements.
ex_JG2GWT.description: Hamstring Lying Curl Up Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Calves.

ex_3SMLRS.name: Hamstring Lying Straight Leg Stretch
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs extended and your arms at your sides.
Lift your right leg towards the ceiling, keeping it straight. Use both hands to gently hold the back of your right leg, just below the knee or higher if possible.
Pull your right leg gently towards your torso, feeling the stretch in your hamstring. Keep your left leg extended and flat on the floor.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, then slowly lower your right leg back to the starting position. Repeat on the left side.
tips: Move slowly and with control to maximize the stretch and avoid any sudden movements.
Perform the stretch on a comfortable surface, such as a yoga mat, to prevent discomfort or injury.
Only stretch as far as is comfortable without causing pain or discomfort.
ex_3SMLRS.description: Hamstring Lying Straight Leg Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Calves.

ex_ZCPWTN.name: Hands Clapped Forearms Stretch
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder width apart and press your palms together in front of your chest with your fingers pointing upward.
Keep your palms together and your elbows lifted as you rotate your hands until your fingers point downward.
Gently lower your joined hands toward your abdomen until you feel a stretch through your wrists and forearms.
Reverse the movement, return your fingers upward, then lower your arms to the starting position.
tips: Rotate your hands slowly without separating them.
Lower your hands only as far as your wrists remain comfortable.
Stop if you feel pain, tingling, or numbness.
Inhale as your fingers point upward and exhale as you lower your hands.
ex_ZCPWTN.description: Hands Clapped Forearms Stretch is an advanced single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Shoulders.

ex_OVWIYB.name: Intermediate Hip Flexor and Quad Stretch
instructions: Lie on your stomach with your legs extended and your arms at your sides. Position an elastic cable around your right ankle.
Bend your right knee to bring your foot towards your glutes, holding the elastic cable in your both hands.
Gently pull on the cable to bring your foot closer to your glutes, feeling the stretch in your quadriceps. Hold this position for a moment.

Extend your right leg lightly backwards, allowing the cable to provide resistance and deepen the stretch in your hip flexor and quadriceps. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the left leg.
tips: Focus on deep, steady breathing, inhaling as you extend your leg and exhaling as you pull your foot towards your glutes.
If you find it difficult to reach the cable, use a longer strap or adjust the tension to ensure a comfortable stretch.
Ensure your head and neck remain in a neutral position, looking down towards the floor to avoid strain.
Perform the stretch on a comfortable surface, such as a yoga mat, to prevent discomfort or injury.
ex_OVWIYB.description: Intermediate Hip Flexor and Quad Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Glutes.

ex_S426V3.name: Iron Cross Stretch
instructions: Lie on your back with your arms extended out to your sides, forming a T-shape, and your legs extended straight.
Lift your right leg towards the ceiling, keeping it straight, and then lower it across your body towards your left hand while keeping your shoulders flat on the floor.
Allow your right leg to lower as far as comfortably possible, feeling a stretch in your lower back, glutes, and hamstrings.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, then slowly return your right leg to the starting position. Repeat on the other side with your left leg.
tips: Only stretch as far as is comfortable without causing pain or discomfort.
Perform the stretch on a comfortable surface, such as a yoga mat, to prevent discomfort or injury.
If you have limited flexibility, bend your knee slightly to reduce strain and gradually work towards straightening your leg.
ex_S426V3.description: Iron Cross Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

ex_XZ75L5.name: Knee to Chest Stretch
instructions: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart and your arms at your sides.
Lift your right knee towards your chest, wrapping your hands around your knee to gently pull your knee closer to your chest.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, feeling the stretch. Keep your left leg straight and maintain your balance.
Release your right knee and lower your leg back to the starting position. Repeat the stretch with your left knee. Alternate sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Use a gentle but firm grip to avoid pulling too hard and causing strain.
Engage your core to maintain balance and stability throughout the stretch.
Move slowly and with control to maximize the effectiveness of the stretch and avoid any sudden movements.
ex_XZ75L5.description: Knee to Chest Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

ex_RMP3H5.name: Kneeling Forearm Flexor Stretch
instructions: Kneel on the floor and place your palms on the floor with your fingers pointing back toward your knees.
Keep your arms straight.
Gently sit back until you feel a stretch along the inside of your forearms.
Hold, breathing steadily, then release.
tips: Go gently; wrists are sensitive.
Keep your palms flat.
ex_RMP3H5.description: Kneeling Forearm Flexor Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category.

ex_6CQAL6.name: Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch
instructions: Begin in a kneeling position with your right knee on the floor and your left foot in front of you, forming a 90-degree angle with your left knee.
Place your hands on your hips or on your left thigh for support. Engage your core and keep your back straight.
Gently push your hips forward, feeling the stretch in your right hip flexor. Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds.
Return to the starting position and switch legs, performing the stretch with your left knee on the floor and your right foot in front. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your front knee is directly above your ankle to avoid putting unnecessary strain on your knee joint.
Maintain an upright posture with your shoulders relaxed and your chest open.
Move slowly and with control to maximize the effectiveness of the stretch and avoid any sudden movements.
ex_6CQAL6.description: Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps.

ex_54REMM.name: Kneeling Lat Floor Stretch
instructions: Begin in a tabletop position on the floor with your hands directly under your shoulders and your knees under your hips.
Extend your right arm forward on the floor, palm facing up, while keeping your left hand in place.
Bend your left elbow to lower your chest towards the floor, feeling the stretch in your lat muscles and upper back. Keep your head relaxed and look down at the floor.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, breathing deeply and steadily. Slowly return to the starting position and repeat on the other side by extending your left arm forward and bending your right elbow.
tips: Ensure your extended arm is fully extended to get the most effective stretch in your lats and upper back.
Perform the stretch on a comfortable surface, such as a yoga mat, to prevent discomfort or injury.
Relax your shoulders and neck to avoid tension in these areas.
ex_54REMM.description: Kneeling Lat Floor Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_2ZY3J3.name: Kneeling Wrist Flexor Stretch
instructions: Begin in a tabletop position on the floor with your hands directly under your shoulders and your knees under your hips.
Rotate your hands so that your fingers are pointing towards your knees, palms flat on the floor.
Slowly shift your weight back towards your heels to increase the stretch in your wrists and forearms, keeping your palms flat on the floor.

Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, breathing deeply and steadily. Release the stretch by shifting your weight forward and gently lifting your hands off the floor. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your palms flat on the floor and your fingers pointing towards your knees to maximize the stretch in your wrist flexors.
Move slowly and with control to avoid any sudden movements that could cause strain.
If the stretch is too intense, reduce the angle by bringing your hands closer to your knees.
ex_2ZY3J3.description: Kneeling Wrist Flexor Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

ex_6EOE6M.name: Lats Stretch Elbow on Wall
instructions: Stand facing a wall and place one elbow on it above your head.
Step back slightly and lower your chest toward the floor.
Push your hips back until you feel a stretch along the side of your back.
Hold, then switch sides.
tips: Keep your back flat.
Breathe into the stretch.
ex_6EOE6M.description: Lats Stretch Elbow on Wall is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Shoulders.

ex_GBRKYT.name: Lats Stretch on Wall
instructions: Stand facing a wall and place both hands on it at shoulder height or higher.
Walk your feet back and hinge at your hips.
Lower your chest toward the floor until you feel a stretch under your arms.
Hold and breathe.
tips: Keep your arms straight.
Push your hips back.
ex_GBRKYT.description: Lats Stretch on Wall is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Chest.

ex_D24JSC.name: Leg Extended Stretch on Bench
instructions: Begin by sitting on the edge of a bench with both legs bent and your feet flat on the floor. Keep your back straight and your core engaged.
Extend your right leg forward until it is parallel to the floor, keeping your leg straight.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, feeling the stretch in your hamstring and lower back.
Slowly bring your right leg back to the starting position with both feet flat on the floor. Repeat the stretch with your left leg extended. Alternate sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your extended leg is straight and parallel to the floor to get the most effective stretch.
Perform the stretch on a stable, non-slip surface to prevent discomfort or injury.
If you find it difficult to hold your leg up, you can use your hands to support your thigh.
ex_D24JSC.description: Leg Extended Stretch on Bench is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Glutes.

ex_3TJNVQ.name: Legs Hand Reach Spine Stretch
instructions: Begin by sitting on the floor with your legs extended straight together in front of you. Keep your back straight and your core engaged.
Slowly bend forward at the hips, reaching your hands towards your feet. Keep your legs straight and your toes pointing up.
Continue to reach forward, aiming to touch your toes or go as far as your flexibility allows. Allow your head and neck to relax as you stretch.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, breathing deeply and steadily.
tips: Allow your head and neck to relax completely to maximize the stretch in your spine.
Perform the stretch on a comfortable, non-slip surface to prevent slipping or discomfort.
If you find it difficult to reach your toes, use a yoga strap or towel around your feet to assist.
ex_3TJNVQ.description: Legs Hand Reach Spine Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Calves.

ex_RLIMHM.name: Lunging Straight Leg Calf Stretch
instructions: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart and your arms at your sides.
Step your right foot back into a lunge position, keeping your right leg straight and your heel on the floor. Bend your left knee slightly, keeping your left foot flat on the floor.
Lean forward slightly, pressing your hips downward and feeling the stretch in your right calf. Hold this position for 15-30 seconds.
Return to the starting position and switch legs, stepping your left foot back and repeating the stretch.
tips: Ensure your back leg remains straight and your heel stays on the floor to maximize the stretch in your calf.
Keep your front knee aligned with your ankle to avoid unnecessary strain on your joints.
Perform the stretch on a stable, non-slip surface to prevent slipping or discomfort.
ex_RLIMHM.description: Lunging Straight Leg Calf Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings.

ex_A2P7WW.name: Lying (Prone) Abdominal Stretch
instructions: Begin by lying face down on the floor with your legs extended straight behind you and your hands placed under your shoulders, palms flat on the floor.
Slowly press your hands into the floor to lift your chest upward, extending your spine. Keep your hips and legs relaxed on the floor.
Continue to lift your chest until you feel a comfortable stretch in your abdomen and lower back. Hold this position for 15-30 seconds, keeping your elbows slightly bent.
Slowly lower your chest back down to the floor and return to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid locking your elbows; keep them slightly bent to prevent strain on your joints.
Breathe deeply and steadily, inhaling as you lift your chest and exhaling as you hold the stretch.
Perform the stretch on a comfortable surface, such as a yoga mat, to prevent discomfort or injury.
ex_A2P7WW.description: Lying (Prone) Abdominal Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Hip Flexors.

ex_AKCZJG.name: Lying Bent Knee Cross Glutes Stretch
instructions: Lie on your back with both knees bent and feet flat.
Cross one ankle over the opposite knee.
Pull the lower leg toward your chest until you feel a stretch in the glute of the crossed leg.
Hold, then switch sides.
tips: Keep your head and shoulders relaxed on the floor.
Push the crossed knee away gently for more stretch.
ex_AKCZJG.description: Lying Bent Knee Cross Glutes Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

ex_RB7U7K.name: Lying Crossover Stretch
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs extended straight and your arms out to the sides to form a T shape.
Bend and lift your right leg and cross it over your body, aiming to touch the floor on the left side, and extend your left arm to hold your right knee down.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, feeling the stretch in your lower back and hips.
Slowly return your right leg to the starting position. Repeat the stretch with your left leg, crossing it over your body to the right side. Alternate sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Move slowly and with control to avoid any sudden movements that could cause strain.
Focus on deep, steady breathing, inhaling as you lift your leg and exhaling as you hold the stretch.
Avoid forcing your leg to touch the floor if you feel any pain; go as far as your flexibility allows.
ex_RB7U7K.description: Lying Crossover Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors, Obliques.

ex_IEACLM.name: Lying Face Down Quadriceps Stretch
instructions: Lie face down on the floor.
Bend one knee and reach back to hold your ankle or foot.
Gently pull your heel toward your glute until you feel a stretch in the front of your thigh.
Hold, then switch sides.
tips: Keep your hips pressed into the floor.
Use a strap if you can't reach your foot.
ex_IEACLM.description: Lying Face Down Quadriceps Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

ex_QNGQYV.name: Lying Glute Stretch
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Cross your right ankle over your left knee, forming a figure-four position.
Grasp the back of your left thigh with both hands and gently pull your left leg towards your chest. Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, feeling the stretch in your right glute and hip.
Slowly release your left leg and return to the starting position. Repeat the stretch with your left ankle crossed over your right knee. Alternate sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your head and shoulders relaxed on the floor to avoid tension in your neck and upper back.
Avoid pulling too hard; go as far as your flexibility allows without causing pain.
Use a towel or strap if needed to assist in pulling your leg towards your chest.
ex_QNGQYV.description: Lying Glute Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

ex_X2QYRI.name: Lying Hip Flexor Stretch
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs straight on the floor.
Lift your right knee towards your chest, holding it with both hands to keep it close while extending your left leg straight off floor, keeping it in line with your right foot.

Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, then slowly release your right knee and return to the starting position. Repeat the stretch with your left knee lifted towards your chest and your right leg extended. Alternate sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your lower back pressed into the floor to avoid strain and to deepen the stretch.
Start with a smaller range of motion if you feel any discomfort, gradually increasing as flexibility improves.
Focus on deep, steady breathing, inhaling as you prepare for the stretch and exhaling as you hold the stretch.
ex_X2QYRI.description: Lying Hip Flexor Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps.

ex_SEMPGM.name: Lying Knee Hugs Lower Back Stretch
instructions: Lie on your back.
Pull both knees toward your chest.
Wrap your arms around your shins and hug them in.
Hold, breathing slowly, and relax your lower back into the floor.
tips: Rock gently side to side for a light massage.
Keep your head on the floor.
ex_SEMPGM.description: Lying Knee Hugs Lower Back Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Glutes.

ex_4DKCA3.name: Lying Knee Pull Glutes Stretch
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs straight.
Bend one knee and pull it toward the opposite shoulder.
Hold until you feel a stretch in your glute.
Release and switch sides.
tips: Keep the other leg relaxed on the floor.
Breathe deeply.
ex_4DKCA3.description: Lying Knee Pull Glutes Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back.

ex_GDAD47.name: Lying Knees to Floor Lower Back Stretch
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and arms out to the sides.
Keeping your shoulders on the floor, lower both knees to one side.
Hold, feeling a stretch in your lower back and side.
Bring your knees back to the centre and lower them to the other side.
tips: Turn your head away from your knees for a deeper stretch.
Move slowly.
ex_GDAD47.description: Lying Knees to Floor Lower Back Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Glutes.

ex_GBQY4F.name: Lying Quadriceps Stretch
instructions: Lie face down on the floor with your legs extended straight and your arms resting by your sides.
Bend your right knee and reach back with your right hand to grasp your right ankle or foot.
Gently pull your right foot towards your glutes, feeling the stretch in your right quadriceps. Keep your hips pressed into the floor.

Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, then slowly release your right foot and return to the starting position. Repeat the stretch on your left leg. Alternate sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your hips pressed into the floor to maximize the stretch in your quadriceps and avoid straining your lower back.
Move slowly and with control to avoid any sudden movements that could cause strain.
If you cannot reach your foot comfortably, use a towel or strap around your ankle to assist with the stretch.
ex_GBQY4F.description: Lying Quadriceps Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

ex_5YNU2P.name: Lying Side Quadriceps Stretch
instructions: Lie on your side with your legs extended straight and your head resting on your lower hand. Extend your top arm and reach back to grasp your top ankle or foot.
Bend your top knee and gently pull your foot towards your glutes with your hand, feeling the stretch in your quadriceps. Keep your hips stacked and your body in a straight line.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, breathing deeply and steadily.
Slowly release your foot and return to the starting position. Repeat the stretch on the other side. Alternate sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your hips stacked and your body in a straight line to maintain proper alignment and maximize the stretch.
If you cannot reach your foot comfortably, use a towel or strap around your ankle to assist with the stretch.
Focus on deep, steady breathing, inhaling as you prepare for the stretch and exhaling as you hold the stretch.
ex_5YNU2P.description: Lying Side Quadriceps Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

ex_WVL7S5.name: Lying Single Leg Extended on Wall Hamstrings Stretch
instructions: Lie on your back in a doorway or next to a wall.
Place one leg straight up against the wall, the other flat on the floor.
Move closer to the wall until you feel a stretch in the back of the raised leg.
Hold, then switch legs.
tips: Keep both legs straight.
Relax your shoulders and neck.
ex_WVL7S5.description: Lying Single Leg Extended on Wall Hamstrings Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Calves.

ex_7SMUB5.name: Middle Back Rotation Stretch
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart and your hands placed on your hips.
Slowly rotate your torso to the right, keeping your hips facing forward. Twist as far as is comfortable, feeling the stretch in your middle back.
Return to the center and repeat the rotation to the right once more.
Rotate your torso to the left side twice in the same manner, alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your hips facing forward to ensure the stretch targets your middle back effectively.
Perform the stretch on a stable, non-slip surface to prevent slipping or discomfort.
Avoid forcing the twist; go as far as your flexibility allows without causing pain.
ex_7SMUB5.description: Middle Back Rotation Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back.

ex_XABQ2C.name: Overhead Triceps Stretch (45 Degree View)
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Raise your right arm overhead and bend your elbow, reaching your right hand down towards your upper back.
Bring your left arm overhead and hold your right elbow with your left hand, gently pulling your right elbow to the left side to deepen the stretch. Hold this position for 15-30 seconds.

Release the stretch and return to the starting position. Repeat on the left side by raising your left arm overhead and bending your elbow, using your right hand to assist with the stretch. Alternate sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid arching your back; keep your spine neutral to maximize the stretch and prevent injury.
Keep your core engaged to maintain balance and support your lower back.
Use gentle pressure when pulling on your elbow to avoid overstretching and potential discomfort.
ex_XABQ2C.description: Overhead Triceps Stretch (45 Degree View) is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

ex_WAVM2S.name: Plyo Side Lunge Stretch
instructions: Stand upright with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart and both arms extended straight out to your sides.
Bend your right knee and lower into a side lunge while simultaneously rotating your torso to the right and bringing your left hand to touch your right leg. Keeping your left leg straight.
Push off your right foot to return to the starting wide stance position, straightening your right leg and rotating your torso back to the center.

Repeat the movement on the left side, bending your left knee into a side lunge and rotating your torso to bring your right hand to touch your left leg. Alternate sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your bent knee stays aligned with your toes to avoid strain on your knee joint.
Move with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Focus on steady breathing, exhaling as you lower into the lunge and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
ex_WAVM2S.description: Plyo Side Lunge Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

ex_ZAMCZY.name: Pretzel Stretch
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended straight in front of you.
Bend your right knee, placing your right foot flat on the floor inside your left thigh.
Rotate your torso to the right and place your left elbow on the outside of your right knee, using your right hand on the floor behind you for support.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, then slowly release and return to the starting position. Repeat on the other side by switching the positions of your legs and rotating your torso to the left.
tips: Use your supporting hand on the floor behind you to maintain balance and assist with the rotation.
Move into the stretch slowly and with control to prevent overstretching and injury.
Breathe deeply and steadily, using your breath to help deepen the stretch and relax your muscles.
ex_ZAMCZY.description: Pretzel Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Hip Flexors.

ex_4OBTPU.name: Rear Deltoid Stretch
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Extend your right arm, slightly bent, across your body at shoulder height.
Use your left hand to gently pull your right arm towards your chest, feeling the stretch in the rear deltoid.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, then slowly release and return to the starting position. Repeat on the other side by extending your left arm and using your right hand to assist with the stretch.
tips: Keep your shoulders relaxed and away from your ears to maximize the stretch.
Avoid twisting your torso; keep your upper body facing forward.
Move slowly and with control to avoid any sudden movements that could cause strain.
ex_4OBTPU.description: Rear Deltoid Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_LOAXAH.name: Resistance Band Assisted Front Rack Stretch
instructions: Stand in the middle of a weight cage with a horizontal bar at chest level. Place the resistance band under your left foot and hold the other end of the band with your left hand.
Bring your left elbow up and rest it on the horizontal bar, allowing your forearm to lean backward. The band should extend down by your shoulder, creating tension.
Slowly allow your forearm to lean back to increase the stretch in your shoulder, keeping your hand close to your shoulder.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, then slowly release the tension and switch to the other arm.
tips: Keep your elbow securely on the bar to ensure proper stretch.
Allow your forearm to naturally lean back without forcing the movement.
Keep a relaxed grip on the band to avoid unnecessary tension.
ex_LOAXAH.description: Resistance Band Assisted Front Rack Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Biceps.

ex_LEQ5XN.name: Revolved Head to Knee
instructions: Sit with one leg extended to the side and the other bent, foot against the inside of the extended thigh.
Turn your torso toward the bent knee.
Side-bend over the extended leg and reach your top arm overhead toward the foot.
Hold, breathing into the side of your body, then switch sides.
tips: Keep your chest open toward the ceiling.
Bend the extended knee slightly if your hamstrings are tight.
ex_LEQ5XN.description: Revolved Head to Knee is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Lats, Adductors.

ex_ZBK5LU.name: Runner Stretch
instructions: Begin in a standing position with your feet hip-width apart.
Step your right foot slightly forward, keeping it straight. Lightly bend your left knee.
Lower your torso and arms towards your right foot, reaching down with your hands while keeping your back straight.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, feeling the stretch in your right hamstring. Slowly return to the starting position and repeat on the other side.
tips: Ensure your front knee remains straight but not locked to maximize the hamstring stretch.
Keep your back leg slightly bent and your heel on the floor to deepen the calf stretch.
Perform the stretch on a stable, non-slip surface to ensure safety and prevent slipping.
ex_ZBK5LU.description: Runner Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Calves.

ex_VNKK5Z.name: Seated Calf Stretch
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended straight in front of you. Keep your back straight and your core engaged.
Extend your right foot while lightly bending the left knee, reaching forward to grasp your toes with both hands.
Gently pull your toes towards you, feeling the stretch in your calf muscle.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, then slowly release. Repeat on the left leg.
tips: Focus on maintaining a straight back to enhance the effectiveness of the stretch.
Ensure your movements are slow and controlled to prevent overstretching or injury.
If you find it difficult to reach your toes, use a towel or strap for assistance without forcing the stretch.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and away from your ears to prevent unnecessary tension.
ex_VNKK5Z.description: Seated Calf Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings.

ex_JGNHSW.name: Seated Figure Four With Twist Glute Stretch
instructions: Sit tall with your legs extended.
Cross one ankle over the opposite knee and draw that foot in.
Twist your torso toward the bent knee, placing your opposite elbow against it.
Hold, then switch sides.
tips: Sit tall; don't round your back.
Breathe and deepen the twist slowly.
ex_JGNHSW.description: Seated Figure Four With Twist Glute Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Obliques, Lower Back.

ex_ZNDHOI.name: Seated Forward Bend
instructions: Sit with your legs extended straight in front of you.
Sit tall and inhale, reaching your arms up.
Exhale and hinge forward from your hips, reaching toward your feet.
Hold, breathing slowly.
tips: Lead with your chest, not your head.
Bend your knees if your hamstrings are tight.
ex_ZNDHOI.description: Seated Forward Bend is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Calves.

ex_ELNB2T.name: Seated Side Bend Pose
instructions: Sit cross-legged with a tall spine.
Place one hand on the floor beside you.
Reach the other arm overhead and lean toward the hand on the floor.
Hold, then switch sides.
tips: Keep both hips on the floor.
Breathe into the side of your ribs.
ex_ELNB2T.description: Seated Side Bend Pose is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

ex_JFGPYC.name: Seated Single Leg Hamstring Stretch
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended straight in front of you.
Bend your left knee and place the sole of your left foot against your right inner thigh. Keep your right leg extended and straight.
Reach forward with both hands towards your right foot, keeping your back straight. Aim to grasp your toes or reach as far as comfortable.

Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, feeling the stretch in your right hamstring. Slowly release and return to the starting position. Repeat on the other side by extending your left leg and bending your right knee.
tips: Keep your extended leg straight and avoid locking your knee to protect the joint.
Ensure your bent knee is relaxed and the sole of your foot is comfortably placed against your inner thigh.
Move into the stretch gradually and with control to prevent muscle strain or injury.
ex_JFGPYC.description: Seated Single Leg Hamstring Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Calves.

ex_RU3HAJ.name: Seated Single Leg Toe Touch Hamstring Stretch
instructions: Sit with one leg extended and the other bent, foot against the inner thigh.
Sit tall and face the extended leg.
Hinge forward from your hips and reach toward your toes.
Hold, then switch sides.
tips: Keep your back long.
Don't bounce.
ex_RU3HAJ.description: Seated Single Leg Toe Touch Hamstring Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Lower Back.

ex_3ZIA3S.name: Seated Straight Leg Calf Stretch
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended straight in front of you.
Lightly bend both knees and extend your right foot, reaching forward to grasp your toes with your right hand.
Gently pull your toes towards you, feeling the stretch in your calf muscle.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, then slowly release. Repeat on the left leg.
tips: Maintain a straight back as you reach forward to enhance the effectiveness of the stretch.
Engage your core muscles to support your lower back and avoid rounding your shoulders.
Move slowly and with control to prevent overstretching or injury.
ex_3ZIA3S.description: Seated Straight Leg Calf Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings.

ex_H5M7S5.name: Seated Toe Touch Hamstrings Stretch
instructions: Sit with both legs extended in front of you.
Sit tall and reach your arms forward.
Hinge from your hips and reach toward your toes.
Hold, breathing slowly.
tips: Bend your knees slightly if needed.
Relax your neck.
ex_H5M7S5.description: Seated Toe Touch Hamstrings Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Lower Back.

ex_DZQTJD.name: Seated Twist
instructions: Sit tall with your legs extended.
Bend one knee and place that foot outside the opposite knee.
Twist toward the bent knee, using your opposite arm against the knee to deepen the twist.
Hold, then switch sides.
tips: Lengthen your spine on each inhale.
Twist a little further on each exhale.
ex_DZQTJD.description: Seated Twist is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Glutes.

ex_XXJI4B.name: Side Bend Standing Lats Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart.
Reach one arm overhead.
Lean to the opposite side until you feel a stretch along your side.
Hold, then switch sides.
tips: Keep your hips centred.
Don't lean forward or back.
ex_XXJI4B.description: Side Bend Standing Lats Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

ex_XUSWKG.name: Side Chest Stretch on Wall
instructions: Stand beside a wall and place your forearm and palm against it at shoulder height.
Step forward with the leg nearest the wall.
Gently turn your body away from the wall until you feel a stretch across your chest.
Hold, then switch sides.
tips: Change the height of your arm to stretch different parts of the chest.
Don't force the stretch.
ex_XUSWKG.description: Side Chest Stretch on Wall is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Front Shoulders, Biceps.

ex_HOFNDM.name: Side Lying Floor Stretch
instructions: Lie on your left side with your legs stacked on top of each other and your body in a straight line. Rest your head on your left arm.
Extend your right arm straight over your head.
Slowly lower your right hand towards your left hand to stretch your back.

Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, feeling the stretch in your back and shoulders. Slowly return to the starting position and repeat on the other side by lying on your right side and following the same steps.
tips: Ensure your extended arm stays straight to maximize the stretch in your back and shoulders.
Keep your core engaged to support your lower back during the stretch.
Perform the stretch on a comfortable, non-slip surface to ensure safety and reduce discomfort.
ex_HOFNDM.description: Side Lying Floor Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.

ex_NZGRGY.name: Side Wrist Pull Stretch
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Extend your right arm across your torso at chest height, keeping it bent and your forearm parallel to the floor.
Bend your left arm and use your left hand to grasp your right hand, gently pulling your right wrist backward to feel a stretch in your right wrist and forearm.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, then slowly release. Repeat on the other side.
tips: Move your wrist slowly and with control to avoid any sudden movements that could cause strain.
Breathe deeply and steadily as you hold the stretch.
Focus on relaxing into the stretch to allow your muscles to lengthen fully.
ex_NZGRGY.description: Side Wrist Pull Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

ex_MC4IDS.name: Single Arm Extended Pull Downwards Biceps Stretch
instructions: Extend one arm in front of you, palm facing up.
With your other hand, gently pull your fingers down toward the floor.
Keep your arm straight until you feel a stretch in your biceps and forearm.
Hold, then switch arms.
tips: Keep your elbow straight.
Pull gently.
ex_MC4IDS.description: Single Arm Extended Pull Downwards Biceps Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

ex_3N6YH5.name: Single Arm Palm Down on Wall Biceps Stretch
instructions: Stand side-on to a wall and place your palm flat on it behind you at shoulder height, fingers pointing back.
Keep your arm straight.
Slowly turn your body away from the wall until you feel a stretch in your biceps.
Hold, then switch arms.
tips: Move slowly into the stretch.
Keep your shoulder down.
ex_3N6YH5.description: Single Arm Palm Down on Wall Biceps Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Front Shoulders.

ex_I3KHBF.name: Single Arm on Wall Side Biceps Stretch
instructions: Stand beside a wall and place your hand on it at shoulder height with your arm straight.
Rotate your thumb downward.
Turn your body gently away from the wall until you feel a stretch in your biceps.
Hold, then switch arms.
tips: Keep your arm straight.
Breathe steadily.
ex_I3KHBF.description: Single Arm on Wall Side Biceps Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Front Shoulders, Chest.

ex_3KBM7V.name: Standing Adductor Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly outward. Keep your hands to your hips.
Shift your weight to your right leg, bending your right knee while keeping your left leg straight. Lean your torso slightly forward.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, feeling a stretch along the inner thigh of your left leg.
Return to the starting position and repeat the stretch on the other side by shifting your weight to your left leg and bending your left knee.
tips: Ensure your bent knee does not extend past your toes to avoid unnecessary strain on the knee joint.
Perform the stretch slowly and with control to maximize muscle flexibility and reduce injury risk.
Gradually increase the depth of the stretch as your flexibility improves.
ex_3KBM7V.description: Standing Adductor Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the adductors (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Hamstrings, Glutes.

ex_THZAKF.name: Standing Bow Hamstring Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet together and your arms by your sides. Engage your core and maintain an upright posture.
Hinge at your hips and lower your torso towards your legs, reaching your hands towards the back of your feet. Keep your back straight and avoid rounding your shoulders.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, feeling a stretch along the back of your legs.
Return to the starting position and repeat the stretch as needed.
tips: Perform the stretch slowly and with control to maximize muscle flexibility and reduce injury risk.
Ensure your weight is distributed evenly on both feet to maintain balance.
Focus on keeping your back straight and avoiding excessive rounding of your spine.
ex_THZAKF.description: Standing Bow Hamstring Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Lower Back, Glutes.

ex_7EYL3S.name: Standing Gastrocnemius Stretch
instructions: Stand facing a bench with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Place your right foot on the bench, keeping your heel on the bench and your toes pointing up. Your left foot should remain flat on the floor.
Lean forward slightly, grab your right heel with your right hand, and straighten your leg while lightly pulling your forefoot.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, then switch legs and repeat. Perform the stretch for the desired number of repetitions on each side.
tips: Keep your knees slightly bent to avoid strain or injury of your joints.
Gradually increase the depth of the stretch as your flexibility improves.
Use a bench at a comfortable height to ensure an effective stretch.
ex_7EYL3S.description: Standing Gastrocnemius Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Calves, Hamstrings.

ex_EOR26K.name: Standing Hamstring Calf Stretch With Resistance Band
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a resistance band in both hands. Place the center of the band under your right forefoot.
Extend your right leg straight out in front of you, keeping your heel on the floor and your toes pointing upward. Hold the ends of the resistance band to create tension.
Gently pull on the resistance band, leaning your torso forward to increase the stretch in your right hamstring. Keep your back straight and avoid rounding your shoulders.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, then switch to your left leg and repeat. Perform the stretch for the desired number of repetitions on each side.
tips: Focus on keeping your extended leg straight and your toes pointing upward.
Ensure your standing leg remains slightly bent to maintain balance.
Use a resistance band with appropriate tension to provide an effective stretch.
ex_EOR26K.description: Standing Hamstring Calf Stretch With Resistance Band is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Lower Back, Glutes.

ex_TVBEUM.name: Standing Lateral Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, arms relaxed by your sides. Engage your core and maintain an upright posture.
Place your right hand behind your head. Keep your left hand extended down the side of your leg.
Gently bend your torso to the left as far as possible and hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, feeling a stretch along the right side of your torso.
Return to the starting position and repeat the stretch on the other side.
tips: Perform the stretch slowly and with control to maximize muscle flexibility and reduce injury risk.
Gradually increase the depth of the stretch as your flexibility improves.
Focus on keeping your back straight and avoiding excessive rounding of your spine.
ex_TVBEUM.description: Standing Lateral Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Core.

ex_ZEKTXZ.name: Standing Leg Elevated Hamstring Stretch
instructions: Stand facing an incline bench with your feet shoulder-width apart. Place your right heel on the edge of the bench headrest, keeping your leg straight and toes pointing upward.
Engage your core and hinge at your hips, leaning your torso towards your right leg.
Reach towards your right foot with both hands, feeling a stretch along the back of your right leg (hamstring). Hold this position for 20-30 seconds.
Return to the starting position and switch legs. Perform the stretch for the desired number of repetitions on each side.
tips: Focus on keeping your extended leg straight and your toes pointing upward.
Ensure your standing leg remains slightly bent to maintain balance.
Set the bench at an elevated surface at a comfortable height to ensure an effective stretch.
ex_ZEKTXZ.description: Standing Leg Elevated Hamstring Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Lower Back, Glutes.

ex_O27UP3.name: Standing One Arm Chest Stretch
instructions: Stand with your right side facing near a wall with your feet shoulder-width apart. Extend your right arm to the side at shoulder height and place your palm flat against the wall.
Slowly turn your body away from the wall, keeping your arm extended and feeling a stretch in your chest and shoulder.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, maintaining a gentle pressure.
Return to the starting position and repeat the stretch on the left side. Perform the stretch for the desired number of repetitions on each side.
tips: Focus on keeping your extended arm straight and your palm flat against the wall.
Ensure your shoulders remain relaxed and avoid tensing them up towards your ears.
Use a gentle motion to avoid over-stretching and potential muscle strain.
ex_O27UP3.description: Standing One Arm Chest Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.

ex_Y5MVVV.name: Standing Quadriceps Stretch (Side View)
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and find a stable surface to hold onto for balance if needed.
Bend your right knee and bring your heel towards your glutes. Grasp your right ankle with your right hand.
Keep your knees close together and lightly pull your right ankle upward, feeling a stretch along the front of your right thigh.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, then release your right ankle and return to the starting position. Repeat the stretch on the left leg.
tips: Perform the stretch slowly and with control to maximize muscle flexibility and reduce injury risk.
Ensure your supporting leg remains slightly bent to maintain balance.
Focus on keeping your torso upright and avoid leaning forward or backward.
ex_Y5MVVV.description: Standing Quadriceps Stretch (Side View) is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

ex_AX2DSV.name: Standing Quadriceps Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and find a stable surface to hold onto for balance if needed.
Bend your right knee and bring your heel towards your glutes. Grasp your right ankle with your right hand.
Keep your knees close together and lightly pull your right ankle upward, feeling a stretch along the front of your right thigh.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, then release your right ankle and return to the starting position. Repeat the stretch on the left leg.
tips: Perform the stretch slowly and with control to maximize muscle flexibility and reduce injury risk.
Ensure your supporting leg remains slightly bent to maintain balance.
Focus on keeping your torso upright and avoid leaning forward or backward.
ex_AX2DSV.description: Standing Quadriceps Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

ex_FKIDKV.name: Standing Side Slope Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, keeping your posture upright. Raise your right arm overhead and allow your left hand to hang by your side.
Gently lean your torso to the left, reaching your right arm over your head and feeling a stretch along the right side of your torso.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, and slowly return to the starting position.
Perform the stretch for the desired number of repetitions on each side.
tips: Ensure your shoulders remain relaxed and avoid tensing them up towards your ears.
Use a gentle motion to avoid over-stretching and potential muscle strain.
Gradually increase the depth of the stretch as your flexibility improves.
ex_FKIDKV.description: Standing Side Slope Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Core.

ex_IKBRND.name: Standing Straight-Leg Hamstring Stretch
instructions: Stand tall and place the heel of one foot on a low step or out in front of you with the leg straight.
Keep your back flat.
Hinge forward from your hips until you feel a stretch in the back of that leg.
Hold, then switch legs.
tips: Keep the standing knee soft.
Lead with your chest.
ex_IKBRND.description: Standing Straight-Leg Hamstring Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Calves.

ex_7FQJDM.name: Triceps Light Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and raise your right arm at chest height across your chest, bending your elbow.
Use your left hand to gently grab your right elbow, pulling it across your chest to deepen the stretch in your triceps.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle stretch in your triceps.
Release the stretch and repeat with your left arm. Perform the stretch for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid twisting your torso; keep it stable and facing forward.
Breathe deeply and steadily, relaxing into the stretch.
Do not pull too hard; the stretch should be gentle and not cause pain.
ex_7FQJDM.description: Triceps Light Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

ex_W3GBKL.name: Upper Back Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and extend your arms straight out in front of you at shoulder height, rounding your upper back and pushing your hands forward.
Lower both arms backward, bringing them to your sides just past behind your hips.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle squeeze in your upper back and shoulder blades.
Release and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe deeply and steadily, relaxing into the stretch.
Avoid shrugging your shoulders up towards your ears; keep them relaxed.
Do not overextend your arms; the stretch should be gentle and not cause pain.
ex_W3GBKL.description: Upper Back Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Middle Back.

ex_OKZEVS.name: Band Skullcrusher
instructions: Attach one end of a loop resistance band to a sturdy anchor point at head height. Stand facing away from the anchor point. Hold the other end of the band with your hands in a neutral grip.
Lean forward slightly, allowing the band to extend. While hinging at the elbow joint, squeeze your triceps to straightening your arms. Hold for 1-2 seconds.
Slowly release the tension in the band, returning to the starting position.
Repeat the movement for the desired repetitions.
tips: Keep your upper arms close to your head throughout the movement. Avoid letting your elbows flare outward during the extension.
Extend only at the elbows and keep your shoulders as still as possible.
Control the lowering phase to keep constant tension on the triceps.
Exhale as you straighten your arms and inhale as you return.
ex_OKZEVS.description: Band Skullcrusher is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Forearms, Serratus Anterior.

ex_6HUPTU.name: Band Triceps Pushdown Single Arm
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and a slight bend in the knees, facing the anchored resistance band.
Using an overhand grip, grasp the other end of the band, keeping your elbow bent and tucked close to your side.
Press downward by squeezing your triceps, extending your arm at the elbow joint. Pause briefly at the bottom of the exercise.
Slowly return to the starting position. Repeat for the desired amount of repetitions and switch arms.
tips: Keep your elbow close to your torso throughout the movement and upper arm stationary, moving only at the elbow joint.
Fully extend your arm without forcefully locking your elbow. Control the return phase to maintain constant tension on the band.
Stand tall with your chest up and core engaged to prevent body sway.
Exhale as you press downward and inhale as you return.
ex_6HUPTU.description: Band Triceps Pushdown Single Arm is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms, Shoulders, Core.

ex_GKXGTD.name: Barbell Close Grip Press
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor, holding a barbell with your hands placed closer than shoulder-width apart, arms straight over your chest.
Lower the barbell slowly and with control to your lower chest, keeping your elbows tucked close to your body.
Press the barbell back up to the starting position by extending your arms fully, focusing on using your triceps muscles.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your elbows tucked in close to your body to engage your triceps effectively.
Maintain a controlled pace to ensure that you're using muscle strength rather than momentum.
Keep your feet flat on the floor to maintain stability and support your lower back.
ex_GKXGTD.description: Barbell Close Grip Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Shoulders.

ex_SPNI2O.name: Barbell Lying Triceps Extension
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor, holding a barbell with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart. Your arms should be fully extended above your chest.
Slowly lower the barbell by bending your elbows, bringing the barbell towards over your forehead.
When the barbell is behind your head, reverse the movement by extending your elbows to return the barbell to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then carefully rack the barbell back onto the bench press rack.
tips: Keep your upper arms stationary and only move your forearms to isolate the triceps.
Lower the barbell slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Ensure a firm grip on the barbell to maintain control and proper alignment throughout the movement.
ex_SPNI2O.description: Barbell Lying Triceps Extension is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

ex_MWBUIJ.name: Barbell Lying Triceps Skull Crusher
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor, holding a barbell with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart. Your arms should be fully extended above your chest.
Slowly lower the barbell by bending your elbows, bringing the barbell towards your forehead.
When the barbell is just above your forehead, reverse the movement by extending your elbows to return the barbell to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then carefully rack the barbell back onto the bench press rack.
tips: Keep your upper arms stationary and only move your forearms to isolate the triceps.
Lower the barbell slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Ensure a firm grip on the barbell to maintain control and proper alignment throughout the movement.
ex_MWBUIJ.description: Barbell Lying Triceps Skull Crusher is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

ex_WZMFPT.name: Barbell Seated Overhead Triceps Press
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor, maintaining an upright posture. Hold a barbell with a close grip (palms facing up), hands positioned slightly narrower than shoulder-width apart.
Position the barbell behind your head with your elbows bent and pointing upwards. Press the barbell overhead by extending your elbows until your arms are fully extended.
Lower the barbell back down to the starting position with control, bending your elbows.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Maintain an upright posture to ensure proper form and avoid leaning forward.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Ensure your elbows stay pointed upwards to maintain proper alignment and effectively target the triceps.
ex_WZMFPT.description: Barbell Seated Overhead Triceps Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

ex_6XZ43G.name: Barbell Standing Overhead Triceps Extension
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an overhand grip (palms facing forward), hands placed closer than shoulder-width apart. Lift the barbell overhead, fully extending your arms. Your elbows should be close to your head.
Slowly lower the barbell behind your head by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary.
Lower the barbell until your forearms are parallel to the floor, feeling the stretch in your triceps.
Press the barbell back up to the starting position by extending your arms fully. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your upper arms stationary and close to your head throughout the movement to isolate your triceps.
Focus on smooth, controlled movements to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Use a weight that allows for proper form and control throughout the exercise to prevent strain or injury.
ex_6XZ43G.description: Barbell Standing Overhead Triceps Extension is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

ex_QBHLZ6.name: Bench Dip (Knees Bent)
instructions: Sit on the edge of a bench with your hands placed on the bench beside your hips.
Slide your hips off the bench, supporting your body with your hands, and bend your knees at a 90-degree angle with your feet flat on the floor.
Lower your body by bending your elbows until your upper arms are parallel to the floor.
Push through your palms to raise your body back to the starting position.
tips: Keep your elbows pointed backward and close to your body to engage your triceps effectively.
Avoid locking your elbows at the top of the movement to maintain tension in your triceps.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
ex_QBHLZ6.description: Bench Dip (Knees Bent) is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Shoulders.

ex_VHZQ27.name: Bench Dip on Floor
instructions: Sit on a bench and place your hands on its edge near your hips.
Walk your feet out, extend your legs, shift your weight on heels, and take your hips off the bench while holding the bench with straight arms.
Lower your hips down by folding your arms and legs.
As your arms form a 90-degree angle, raise your hips and repeat.
tips: Keep your elbows pointed backward and close to your body to engage your triceps effectively.
Engage your core and glutes to keep your body stable.
Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears to avoid strain and ensure proper alignment.
ex_VHZQ27.description: Bench Dip on Floor is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Shoulders.

ex_GWVVDS.name: Bench Triceps Dip Leg Curls
instructions: Sit down on a bench and place your hands on its edge near your hips.
Walk your feet out, extend your legs, and lift your hips off the bench while holding the bench.
Lower your hips down by folding your arms and bending your knees.
As your arms form a 90-degree angle, raise your hips while extending your legs, and repeat.
tips: Keep your elbows pointed backward and close to your body to engage your triceps effectively.
Maintain a controlled movement for both the dip and the leg curl to maximize muscle activation.
Engage your core to maintain stability and proper form throughout the exercise.
ex_GWVVDS.description: Bench Triceps Dip Leg Curls is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Shoulders.

ex_WZWGAH.name: Bench Triceps Dip Straight Legs
instructions: Sit down on a bench and place your hands on the edge near your hips.
Walk your feet out, straighten your legs, and lift your hips off the bench while holding the bench.
Lower your hips down by folding your arms.
As your arms form a 90-degree angle, raise your hips, and repeat.
tips: Keep your elbows pointed backward and close to your body to engage your triceps effectively.
Maintain a straight line from your hips to your heels to ensure proper form.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
ex_WZWGAH.description: Bench Triceps Dip Straight Legs is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Shoulders.

ex_XRN66Z.name: Body-Up
instructions: Start in a plank position with your hands placed directly under your shoulders and your body forming a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your body towards the floor by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your torso.
Push through your palms to lift your body back up to the starting plank position.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Triceps (Triceps Brachii), Chest (Pectoralis Major)
ex_XRN66Z.description: Body-Up is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Glutes.

ex_EZY56J.name: Bodyweight Kneeling Triceps Extension
instructions: Start in a kneeling position with your knees on the floor. Place your hands on the floor in front of you opposite your head, close together, and lean forward.
Bend your elbows to lower your forearms and head towards the floor, engaging your triceps.
Push through your hands to extend your arms back to the starting position, straightening your elbows.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your body stable by engaging your core throughout the movement.
Keep your elbows close to your body to target the triceps more effectively.
Control the movement, avoiding any jerking motions, to enhance muscle engagement and prevent injury.
ex_EZY56J.description: Bodyweight Kneeling Triceps Extension is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Chest.

ex_J4PTLO.name: Bodyweight Overhead Triceps Extension
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms extended overhead with hands holding together, elbows slightly bent.
Bend your elbows to lower your hands behind your head, engaging your triceps.
Extend your arms back to the starting overhead position.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your upper arms stationary and close to your ears throughout the exercise to effectively target the triceps.
Engage your core to maintain stability and avoid arching your back.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
ex_J4PTLO.description: Bodyweight Overhead Triceps Extension is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

ex_MU6W75.name: Bodyweight Triceps Extension
instructions: Begin in a plank position on your toes and elbows, with your hands positioned at shoulder-width apart, palms on the floor.
Push through your palms to extend your arms straight, keeping your palms in place.
Lower your forearms to the floor back to the starting plank position.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels to maintain proper form.
Engage your core to stabilize your body and prevent your hips from sagging.
Focus on your breathing; inhale as you lower your forearms and exhale as you extend your arms back to the plank position.
ex_MU6W75.description: Bodyweight Triceps Extension is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Chest.

ex_IZG3F7.name: Cable Alternate Triceps Extension
instructions: Stand with your back facing the low pulley, holding the handle behind your head with your arm bent, elbow pointing up and palm facing the ceiling. Use your other hand to support the active arm by holding it just above the elbow.
Extend your active arm up overhead, straightening your elbow to push the handle upward.
Slowly return your arm to the starting position behind your head. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
tips: Keep your upper arm stationary throughout the exercise to isolate the triceps.
Avoid using momentum; perform the movement slowly and with control.
Exhale as you extend your arm and inhale as you return to the starting position.
ex_IZG3F7.description: Cable Alternate Triceps Extension is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category.

ex_ZFZYTN.name: Cable Cross Pushdown
instructions: Stand upright between two high cable pulleys and hold each handle in the opposite hand.Bend your elbows so that the handles are crossing in front of your chest.
Extend your elbows to press the handles down and outward until your arms are fully extended.
Pause briefly while squeezing your triceps at the bottom of the movement.
Slowly bend your elbows to return the handles to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your elbows close to your sides throughout the exercise.
Move only at your elbows and avoid swinging your shoulders.
Keep your torso upright and your core engaged throughout the movement.
Inhale as you return to the starting position and exhale as you press the handles downward.
ex_ZFZYTN.description: Cable Cross Pushdown is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Forearms, Core.

ex_FKWWLF.name: Cable Lying Triceps Extension (Low)
instructions: Attach a straight bar to the low pulley of a cable machine. Lie on a flat bench with your head positioned near the pulley. Grasp the bar or rope with an overhand grip, your arms extended straight up above your chest.
Lower the bar towards your forehead by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary.
Just before touching your forehead, extend your arms back to the starting position, focusing on contracting your triceps.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your upper arms stationary and only move your forearms to isolate the triceps.
Focus on the contraction of your triceps as you extend your arms.
Exhale as you extend your arms and inhale as you lower the bar.
ex_FKWWLF.description: Cable Lying Triceps Extension (Low) is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

ex_VRSO7C.name: Cable Lying Triceps Extension
instructions: Attach a straight bar to the middle pulley of a cable machine. Lie on a flat bench with your head positioned near the pulley. Grasp the bar or rope with an overhand grip, your arms extended straight up above your chest.
Lower the bar towards your forehead by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary.
Just before touching your forehead, extend your arms back to the starting position, focusing on contracting your triceps.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your upper arms stationary and only move your forearms to isolate the triceps.
Focus on the contraction of your triceps as you extend your arms.
Exhale as you extend your arms and inhale as you lower the bar.
ex_VRSO7C.description: Cable Lying Triceps Extension is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

ex_GUSHJI.name: Cable Neutral Grip Kickback
instructions: Attach a handle to a middle pulley on a cable machine. Stand facing the machine and grasp the handle with your left hand, using a neutral grip (palm facing your body). Step back to create tension in the cable.

Position your feet shoulder-width apart and bend slightly at the hips, keeping your back straight and core engaged. Your upper arm should be parallel to the floor and close to your body with your elbow bent at a 90-degree angle.
Extend your left arm straight back by straightening your elbow, keeping your upper arm stationary and focusing on contracting your triceps.
Slowly return your arm to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to your right hand.
tips: Keep your upper arm stationary and only move your forearm to isolate the triceps.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and reduce the risk of injury.
Exhale as you extend your arm and inhale as you return to the starting position.
ex_GUSHJI.description: Cable Neutral Grip Kickback is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.
