ex_22VNUO.name: Cable Overhead Extension Rope
instructions: Attach a rope handle to the high pulley on a cable machine. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, back to the machine, and grasp the rope handle with both hands, palms facing each other.
Step forward to create tension in the cable. Extend your arms straight in level with your torso, keeping your elbows close to your head.
Lower the rope behind your head by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary.
Extend your arms back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back straight and avoid using momentum.
Focus on squeezing your triceps at the top of the movement.
Exhale as you extend your arms and inhale as you lower the rope.
ex_22VNUO.description: Cable Overhead Extension Rope is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Forearms.

ex_LLJJAG.name: Cable Pushdown
instructions: Stand facing the cable machine with a straight bar attached to the high pulley. Grasp the bar with both hands, palms facing down, and place your hands shoulder-width apart.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and lean slightly forward, keeping your back straight and elbows close to your body. Your forearms should be parallel to the floor.
Push the bar down towards your thighs by straightening your elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary.
Slowly return to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you push the bar down and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Stand with a slight bend in your knees for better stability.
Focus on squeezing your triceps at the bottom of the movement.
ex_LLJJAG.description: Cable Pushdown is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Forearms.

ex_D5EKZB.name: Cable Rear Drive
instructions: Stand straight with your feet shoulder-width apart, facing the cable machine. Set the pulley at shoulder height and grasp the handle of the cable with your right hand, palm facing down. Set your arm parallel to the floor in front of you and bent at 90 degrees.
Drive your elbow sideways while slowly straightening your arm, pulling the cable across your chest.
Slowly bring your arm back to the starting position with control.

instructions: Sit on the edge of a chair with your hands placed next to your hips, gripping the edge of the chair.

ex_VCQVI6.name: Decline Chair Push Up Diamond
instructions: Begin by placing your feet on a chair and positioning your hands on the floor close together, forming a diamond shape with your thumbs and index fingers.

instructions: Begin in a plank position with your hands close together under your chest, fingers forming a diamond shape (thumbs and index fingers touching).

Push back up to the starting plank position, maintaining a straight line from your head to your heels throughout the movement.

ex_QYFPIV.name: Dip Leg Raise on Couch
instructions: Sit on the edge of a couch with your hands placed next to your hips, gripping the edge for support.
Lift your hips off the couch by pressing down into your hands and straightening your arms, while keeping your feet flat on the floor and both knees bent.
As you bend your elbows to lower your body into a dip, simultaneously lift one leg, bent at the knee, towards your chest.
Push through your hands to raise your body back up, straightening your arms and simultaneously lowering your lifted leg back to the starting position.
tips: Ensure your grip on the couch is secure to maintain balance and control throughout the exercise.
Focus on a controlled, smooth motion both when lowering into the dip and lifting your body up to maximize muscle engagement.

ex_WYNUWS.name: Dip on Floor With Chair
instructions: Sit on the floor with your back facing a chair and place your hands on the edge of the chair seat, fingers pointing towards your body.

Press down into the chair with your hands to lift your hips off the floor, straightening your arms.
Bend your elbows to lower your body towards the floor until your elbows form about a 90-degree angle and push through your hands to lift your body back up to the starting position.

instructions: Position two chairs parallel to each other, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, with the seats facing away from you.

tips: Check that the chairs are stable and strong enough to support your weight without tipping or moving.

ex_QYTMLO.name: Dumbbell Kickback

Start with your right arm bent at a 90-degree angle, with the upper arm parallel to the floor and the dumbbell close to your torso.
Extend your arm backward by straightening your elbow, keeping your upper arm stationary and focusing on squeezing your triceps at the top of the movement.

Slowly bend your elbow to return to the starting position, maintaining control and keeping your upper arm parallel to the floor. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching to the other arm.
tips: Keep your upper arm stationary throughout the movement to isolate the triceps effectively.
Engage your core to maintain stability and prevent excessive movement of your torso.

Keeping your upper arm stationary, extend your elbow to lift the dumbbell towards the ceiling.

Lower the dumbbell back to the starting position with control, ensuring your forearm returns to being parallel to the floor. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.

Focus on a slow and controlled motion to maximize muscle engagement.

Maintain a neutral wrist position to prevent strain and injuries.

ex_LJSJT6.name: Dumbbell One Arm Triceps Extension (On Bench)
instructions: Begin by sitting on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor. Hold a dumbbell in your right hand, extending your arm straight above your shoulder. Place your left hand on your hip for support.

ex_HLV7TD.name: Dumbbell Overhead Extension Seated
instructions: Sit on a bench, holding a dumbbell with both hands and extending your arms fully overhead. Hold a dumbbell with your fingers wrapped around the dumbbell handle.
Slowly bend your elbows, lowering the dumbbell behind your head until your forearms are parallel to the floor.
Press the dumbbell back up by straightening your elbows, returning to the starting position with arms fully extended overhead.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, keeping your core engaged and back pressed against the bench.

ex_36FOHW.name: Dumbbell Overhead Extension Standing
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell with both hands. Hold a dumbbell with your fingers wrapped around the dumbbell handle.
Slowly bend your elbows, lowering the dumbbell behind your head until your forearms are parallel to the floor.
Press the dumbbell back up by straightening your elbows, returning to the starting position with arms fully extended overhead.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, keeping your core engaged and back straight.

Use a controlled motion, avoiding any jerking or swinging of the weight.

ex_36FOHW.description: Dumbbell Overhead Extension Standing is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

ex_CNQMUL.name: Dumbbell Pronate-Grip Triceps Extension
instructions: Lie flat on a bench with your feet firmly planted on the floor, holding a dumbbell in each hand. Extend your arms bent behind your head, keeping your arms at 45 degrees, holding the dumbbell with an overhand grip at shoulder width.
Keeping your elbows stationary, bend your arms to lower the dumbbell behind your head.
Extend your elbows to raise the dumbbell back to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on moving only your forearms; your upper arms should remain stationary.
Avoid locking your elbows at the top of the movement.
Use a controlled motion and avoid swinging the weight.
ex_CNQMUL.description: Dumbbell Pronate-Grip Triceps Extension is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

ex_47GODM.name: Dumbbell Seated Bench Extension
instructions: Sit on a bench with your back straight and feet flat on the floor, holding a dumbbell with both hands, positioning it behind your head.
Begin with your elbows bent and pointed upwards, keeping your upper arms close to your head.
Extend your elbows to lift the dumbbell upwards until your arms are fully extended, keeping your upper arms stationary.
Lower the dumbbell back to the starting position with control, bending your elbows.
tips: Avoid flaring your elbows out; keep them close to your head.
Exhale as you extend your elbows and inhale as you lower the dumbbell.
Ensure a slow and controlled movement to maintain proper form.
ex_47GODM.description: Dumbbell Seated Bench Extension is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

ex_X3SR2J.name: Dumbbell Seated Kickback
instructions: Sit on the edge of a bench with your feet flat on the floor. Hold a dumbbell in each hand, leaning slightly forward from your hips while keeping your back straight.
Lift both upper arms so that they are parallel to the floor, keeping your elbows bent at a 90-degree angle. Your forearms should be hanging down, and your palms facing your body.
Extend your arms straight back by straightening your elbows, keeping your upper arm stationary. Squeeze your triceps at the top of the movement.
Slowly bend your elbows to return to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back straight and avoid rounding your shoulders.
Exhale as you extend your arm and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Use a controlled motion, focusing on squeezing your triceps at the top.
ex_X3SR2J.description: Dumbbell Seated Kickback is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

ex_T2DV5A.name: Dumbbell Skullcrusher
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with your feet firmly planted and hold a dumbbell in each hand above your chest using a neutral grip.
Keep your upper arms fixed, then bend your elbows to lower the dumbbells beside your head.
Extend your elbows to raise the dumbbells along the same path until your arms are straight.
Repeat for the required amount of repetitions.
tips: Keep your elbows pointing upward instead of allowing them to flare outward.
Maintain contact between your head, upper back, hips, and the bench.
Hold your upper arms steady and move only through your elbows.
Inhale as you lower the dumbbells and exhale as you extend your elbows.
ex_T2DV5A.description: Dumbbell Skullcrusher is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Forearms, Chest.

ex_X3WR7V.name: Dumbbell Standing Both Arms Kickback
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand. Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and your torso almost parallel to the floor.
Begin with your arms bent at 90 degrees, elbows close to your sides, and dumbbells hanging down.
Extend both arms straight back by straightening your elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary and close to your body. Focus on squeezing your triceps at the top of the movement.
Slowly bend your elbows to return the dumbbells to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back flat and avoid rounding your shoulders.
Keep your head in a neutral position, looking slightly forward.
Exhale as you extend your arms back and inhale as you return to the starting position.
ex_X3WR7V.description: Dumbbell Standing Both Arms Kickback is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

ex_B4QW6O.name: Dumbbell Standing One Arm Extension
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in your right hand and place your left hand to your hip for support. Raise your right arm overhead, extending it fully with your palm facing forward.
Keep your upper arm stationary and your elbow close to your head. Lower the dumbbell behind your head by bending your elbow.
Extend your arm back to the starting position by straightening your elbow. Ensure your upper arm remains stationary throughout the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the left arm.
tips: Focus on isolating the triceps, minimizing movement in your shoulder and upper arm.
Maintain a slight bend in your elbow to avoid locking out the joint.
Breathe out as you extend the dumbbell and inhale as you lower it.
ex_B4QW6O.description: Dumbbell Standing One Arm Extension is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

ex_JUXILH.name: Dumbbell Standing Triceps Extension
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell with both hands behind your head. Your elbows should be bent, and your upper arms should be close to your ears.
Extend your arms fully by pressing the dumbbell overhead until your arms are straight. Keep your elbows close to your head.
Lower the dumbbell back down behind your head by bending your elbows, returning to the starting position.
Repeat the extension and flexion of your arms for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid flaring your elbows out; keep them close to your ears.
Use a controlled motion, avoiding swinging the dumbbell.
Exhale as you extend your arms and inhale as you lower the dumbbell.
ex_JUXILH.description: Dumbbell Standing Triceps Extension is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

ex_BM6IKU.name: Dumbbell Tate Press
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand. Position the dumbbells above your chest, with your arms fully extended and your palms facing forward.
Bend your elbows and lower the dumbbells inward and towards your chest, keeping the dumbbells facing forward.
Bring the dumbbells together just before touching your chest, elbows pointing out to the sides.
Extend your arms back to the starting position, extending the dumbbells upward. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your wrists straight and aligned with your forearms.
Focus on controlled movements and avoid using momentum.
Choose a weight that allows for proper form and full range of motion.
ex_BM6IKU.description: Dumbbell Tate Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Shoulders.

ex_RECIKP.name: Dumbbell Triceps Kick Back Single Arm
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in your right hand. Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at your hips, keeping your back straight. Place your left hand on your left knee for support.
Lift your right elbow backward to bring the dumbbell close to your torso, with your upper arm parallel to the floor and your forearm perpendicular to the floor.
Extend your right arm fully behind you by straightening your elbow, keeping your upper arm stationary. Squeeze your triceps at the top of the movement.
Slowly return the dumbbell to the starting position by bending your elbow. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the left arm and repeat.
tips: Keep your upper arm close to your body and stationary throughout the exercise.
Focus on a slow and controlled movement to maximize triceps engagement.
Avoid swinging the weight; use only your triceps to perform the movement.
ex_RECIKP.description: Dumbbell Triceps Kick Back Single Arm is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

ex_G2B2Z2.name: Dumbbells Triceps Kick Back Both Arms
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand. Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at your hips and lower your upper body to almost parallel to the floor.
Bend your elbows to bring the dumbbells close to your torso, with your upper arms parallel to the floor and your forearms perpendicular to the floor.
Extend your arms fully behind you by straightening your elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary. Squeeze your triceps at the top of the movement.
Slowly return the dumbbells to the starting position by bending your elbows. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid swinging the weights; use only your triceps to perform the movement.
Focus on a slow and controlled movement to maximize triceps engagement.
Exhale as you extend your arms and inhale as you return to the starting position.
ex_G2B2Z2.description: Dumbbells Triceps Kick Back Both Arms is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

ex_TJ5UHR.name: EZ Bar Overhead Extensions Standing
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding an EZ bar with an overhand grip. Raise the bar overhead until your arms are fully extended, with your hands positioned closer together on the bar.
Keep your elbows close to your head and slowly lower the bar behind your head by bending your elbows.
Lower the bar until your arms are fully bent.
Extend your elbows to raise the bar back to the starting position, fully extending your arms overhead.
tips: Ensure your elbows remain close to your head throughout the movement to effectively target the triceps.
Use a controlled motion and avoid swinging the bar or using momentum.
Avoid locking your elbows at the top of the movement to maintain tension on the triceps.
ex_TJ5UHR.description: EZ Bar Overhead Extensions Standing is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with an ez barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Core.

ex_GJR67P.name: Floor Tricep Dip
instructions: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and your heels planted in front of you with your toes pointing upward. Place both hands behind your hips with your palms flat, your fingers pointing toward your feet, and your elbows slightly bent.
Press through your palms and heels to lift your hips slightly above the floor, keeping your chest raised and your shoulders pulled back.
Press firmly through your palms and extend your elbows to lift your hips. Pause at the top, while squeezing your triceps.
Bend your elbows and lower your hips, returning to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Point your elbows backward instead of allowing them to flare outward.
Move through your elbows rather than dropping and raising your hips alone.
Keep your shoulders down and avoid shrugging them toward your ears.
Inhale as you lower your hips and exhale as you press upward.
ex_GJR67P.description: Floor Tricep Dip is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Chest, Forearms.

ex_5QLYVJ.name: Incline Diamond Push Up on Bench
instructions: Position yourself facing a bench. Place your hands on the edge of the bench close together so that your thumbs and index fingers form a diamond shape.
Step your feet back to extend your legs fully, keeping your body in a straight line from head to heels. Engage your core to maintain stability.
Lower your chest towards the bench by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your body.
Push through your hands to extend your arms and return to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Move slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Focus on steady breathing, exhaling as you push up and inhaling as you lower down.
Avoid flaring your elbows out to the sides; keep them close to your body to engage your triceps more effectively.
Use a stable, non-slip bench to prevent any movement or slipping during the exercise.
ex_5QLYVJ.description: Incline Diamond Push Up on Bench is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

ex_WHSBPD.name: Incline Push Ups on Chair
instructions: Stand facing a chair and place your hands on top, close to the edge, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Step your feet back to extend your legs behind you, forming a straight line from your head to your heels.
Engage your core and keep your body straight. Lower your chest towards the chair by bending your elbows, keeping them at a 45-degree angle to your body.
Lower yourself until your chest is close to the chair, then push through your hands to extend your arms and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you push up and inhale as you lower yourself down.
Use a chair that can support your weight without moving.
Keep your core engaged to maintain a straight body line and avoid sagging your hips.
ex_WHSBPD.description: Incline Push Ups on Chair is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Shoulders, Core.

ex_K5JYHE.name: Kettlebell Decline Skull Crusher
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor. Lift your hips and hold a kettlebell above your chest with both hands using a neutral grip.
Keep your hips raised as you bend your elbows and lower the kettlebell toward your forehead, stopping just above it with control.
Extend your elbows and raise the kettlebell back above your chest.
Repeat the movement while maintaining the bridge position, for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Maintain your hips in a raised and level position.
Keep your elbows close together as you lower the weight.
Avoid arching your lower back as you hold the bridge.
Inhale as you lower the kettlebell and exhale as you extend your elbows.

ex_XQMMX7.name: Kettlebell Skull Crusher
instructions: Lie on a bench holding a kettlebell by the horns above your chest with straight arms.

Bend your elbows to lower the kettlebell toward your forehead.
Extend your elbows to return and repeat.

Lower slowly.
ex_XQMMX7.description: Kettlebell Skull Crusher is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category.

ex_OBKNSE.name: Kettlebell Standing Tricep Extension
instructions: Stand tall holding a kettlebell by the horns overhead with both hands.
Keep your upper arms close to your head.
Lower the kettlebell behind your head by bending your elbows.

ex_434AHO.name: Landmine Lying Tricep Extension

Bend your elbows to lower the bar toward your forehead.
Extend your arms to press it back up and repeat.

Control the lowering.

ex_W2KCKO.name: Overhead Triceps Stretch (Front View)
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Raise your right arm overhead and bend your elbow, reaching your right hand down towards your upper back.
Bring your left arm overhead and hold your right elbow with your left hand, gently pulling your right elbow to the left side to deepen the stretch. Hold this position for 15-30 seconds.

tips: Avoid arching your back; keep your spine neutral to maximize the stretch and prevent injury.

ex_ZML5HD.name: Overhead Extension Resistance Band Both Arms

Lower the handles behind your head by bending your elbows until your forearms are about parallel to the floor, keeping your upper arms stationary.
Extend your arms back to the starting position by straightening your elbows.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

ex_ZML5HD.description: Overhead Extension Resistance Band Both Arms is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Core.

ex_QV7N32.name: Pike Push Up
instructions: Begin in a plank position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your feet hip-width apart. Your body should form a straight line from head to heels.
Walk your feet towards your hands, lifting your hips up towards the ceiling to form an inverted V-shape. Keep your arms and legs straight, and your head between your arms.
Lower your head towards the floor by bending your elbows, keeping them pointed outwards.
Push through your hands to return to the starting inverted V position, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your head aligned with your arms to avoid straining your neck.
Ensure your elbows point outwards to target your shoulders effectively.
Perform the exercise on a stable, non-slip surface to prevent slipping and ensure safety.
ex_QV7N32.description: Pike Push Up is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Triceps.

ex_ZDPLPR.name: Plate Curl to Overhead Press to Tricep Extension

ex_JVD2X2.name: Plate Overhead Tricep Extension

ex_Y4TEDA.name: Single Arm Overhead Extension Resistance Band

ex_TCOT7Y.name: Suspension Trainer With Grips Triceps Extension

Keep your arms bent at 90 degrees. Engage your core and keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Extend your arms by pressing through your hands until your elbows are fully straight.
Slowly bend your elbows to return to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily: exhale as you extend your arms and inhale as you bend your elbows.
Focus on using your triceps to perform the extension, avoiding excessive use of your chest, shoulders or back.
Keep your upper arms close to your head and avoid flaring them out to the sides.
ex_TCOT7Y.description: Suspension Trainer With Grips Triceps Extension is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a suspension trainer, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.

ex_64OLGF.name: Tricep Cable Kickback on Crossover Machine

ex_AT52FQ.name: Tricep Extension Machine

Grasp the handles with a neutral grip, ensuring your elbows are below the pivot point.
Push the handles forward by straightening your elbows and fully extending your arms while keeping your upper arms stationary.
Slowly return to the starting position by bending your elbows. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Focus on using your triceps to push the handles, avoiding excessive use of your shoulders or back.

ex_IE5GEE.name: Tricep Rope Extension on Crossover Machine
instructions: Attach a rope to a high cable and hold the ends with your palms facing each other.

Push the rope down until your arms are straight, separating the ends at the bottom.

ex_SOXYQC.name: Triceps Dip Machine

ex_XLYIXY.name: Ab Wheel Plank
instructions: Start by kneeling on a mat with the ab wheel placed on the floor in front of you, holding it with both hands. Ensure your arms are extended and your back is straight.
Roll the ab wheel forward until your body is in a plank position, with your arms extended and your body forming a straight line from head to knees.
Hold the plank position, keeping your core engaged and your body stable, as long as required.
Roll the ab wheel back to the starting position.

Focus on engaging your entire core, including your abdominals, obliques, and lower back, to maintain stability.
Roll out and back in with controlled movements to maximize muscle engagement and minimize the risk of injury.
ex_XLYIXY.description: Ab Wheel Plank is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a wheel roller, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Obliques, Hip Flexors.

ex_SG5OQI.name: Alternate Sprinter Lunge
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart.
Lunge back with your right leg, bending both knees to lower your body into a lunge position while reaching your hands towards your left foot.
Push off your right foot to return to the starting position.
Lunge back with your left leg, reaching your hands towards your right foot. Continue alternating sides.
tips: Keep your core engaged to maintain balance and stability throughout the exercise.
Ensure your front knee does not extend past your toes to avoid strain on your knee joint.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
ex_SG5OQI.description: Alternate Sprinter Lunge is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors, Calves.

ex_P7RCWY.name: Alternating Leg Downward Dog
instructions: Start in a downward dog position with your hands and feet on the mat, hips lifted towards the ceiling, and body forming an inverted V shape.
Bend your right knee towards your chest, keeping your foot on the floor and maintaining balance on your left foot and both hands.
Straighten your right leg back to the starting position.
Bend your left knee towards your chest while maintaining balance. Continue alternating sides.
tips: Keep your core engaged to maintain stability and balance throughout the exercise.

ex_U2RWA7.name: Alternating Lunge With Rotation
instructions: Start in a plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your body forming a straight line from head to heels.
Step your right foot forward, placing it outside your right hand, and rotate your torso to the right, extending your right arm towards the ceiling.
Return your right hand and foot to the plank position.

Step your left foot forward, placing it outside your left hand, and rotate your torso to the left, extending your left arm towards the ceiling. Return to the plank position. Continue alternating sides.
tips: Keep your core engaged to maintain stability and proper alignment throughout the movement.

Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
ex_U2RWA7.description: Alternating Lunge With Rotation is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Obliques, Hip Flexors, Triceps.

ex_RZ5KW5.name: Archer Step Back
instructions: Stand tall with your back straight and feet shoulder-width apart.
Extend your arms forward while keeping your palms inward.
Take a step backward by extending your left leg behind you while taking your elbow past your back like an archer.
Hold for a while, return to the initial position, and repeat by taking your right leg backward.
tips: Engage your core to maintain balance and stability throughout the exercise.
Ensure your front knee is aligned with your ankle and does not extend past your toes to avoid strain on your knee joint.
Perform the movement with controlled motions to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
ex_RZ5KW5.description: Archer Step Back is an advanced multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Obliques, Hip Flexors.

ex_O6AIAV.name: Basic Toe Touch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Bend at the hips and reach down towards your toes, keeping your legs as straight as possible.
Hold the stretch for a few seconds, feeling the stretch in your hamstrings and lower back.
Return to the standing position and repeat the movement.
tips: Keep your back straight as you bend to avoid straining your lower back.

ex_O6AIAV.description: Basic Toe Touch is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Glutes.

ex_JSR73Q.name: Bench Reverse Plank Hold
instructions: Place your feet on a bench with your legs extended and your hands on the floor directly under your shoulders, arms straight.
Lift your hips straight until torso comes parallel to the floor.

tips: Engage your core and glutes to maintain a straight and stable torso throughout the hold.
Keep your elbows slightly bent to avoid locking your joints and ensure muscle engagement.
Breathe steadily and avoid holding your breath to maintain control and endurance during the hold.
ex_JSR73Q.description: Bench Reverse Plank Hold is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Chest.

ex_II7GIW.name: Bicycle Air Legs
instructions: Lie on your back and lift your hips off the floor, supporting them with your hands while keeping your elbows on the floor.
Perform a bicycle motion with your legs by extending your right leg straight forward while bending your left knee towards the floor.
Switch legs by extending your left leg straight forward and bending your right knee towards the floor, continuing the bicycle motion.

tips: Ensure your hands are firmly supporting your lower back to maintain proper alignment and stability.

Ensure your movements are smooth and controlled to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
ex_II7GIW.description: Bicycle Air Legs is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Hamstrings.

ex_KOAOSP.name: Bird Dog (Version 2)
instructions: Start in a tabletop position on your hands and knees, with your wrists aligned under your shoulders and your knees under your hips.
Extend your left leg backward, and right arm forward simultaneously, keeping your extending arm straight, until both are slightly higher than torso level.
Hold this position briefly, maintaining balance and stability.
Return to the starting position and repeat the movement with your left arm and right leg.
tips: Engage your core to maintain stability and prevent your back from sagging.
Keep your movements slow and controlled to maximize muscle activation and improve balance.

instructions: Start in a tabletop position on your hands and knees, with your wrists aligned under your shoulders and your knees under your hips.
Extend your left leg backward, toes extended back, and right arm forward simultaneously, keeping your extending arm straight, until both are parallel to the floor.
Hold this position briefly, maintaining balance and stability.
Return to the starting position and repeat the movement with your left arm and right leg.

Keep your movements slow and controlled to maximize muscle activation and improve balance.

instructions: Start in a tabletop position on your hands and knees, with your wrists aligned under your shoulders and your knees under your hips.

ex_XIVRJE.name: Body Saw Plank
instructions: Start in a forearm plank position, with your elbows directly under your shoulders and your body forming a straight line from head to heels.
Rock your body back by pushing through your forearms, moving your shoulders behind your elbows level.
Rock your body forward by pulling with your forearms, moving your shoulders in front of your elbows level.

tips: Focus on keeping your body in a straight line from head to heels to maintain proper form.
Ensure your movements are slow and deliberate to enhance control and muscle engagement.

ex_Q3BV3J.name: Bodyweight Kneeling Push-Up Row
instructions: Start in a kneeling push-up position with your hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your body on the floor.
Push up by extending both arms, keeping your knees on the floor. Lift your right hand off the floor, performing a rowing motion by bringing your elbow up towards the ceiling.
Return your right hand to the floor and lower your body to the starting position.
Repeat alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Engage your core to maintain stability and prevent your hips from sagging during the push-up and row.

ex_Q3BV3J.description: Bodyweight Kneeling Push-Up Row is a beginner multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Core.

ex_QCBTW5.name: Bow Pose
instructions: Lie face down with your legs stretched back and your arms extended in front of you, palms facing down.
Bend your knees and reach back to grasp your ankles with your hands.
Lift your chest and thighs off the floor by pressing your legs into your hands until you feel a comfortable stretch.
Hold the position for the desired duration, then slowly lower your body and release your ankles.
tips: Engage your core to help stabilize your spine.
Avoid forcing the stretch beyond a comfortable range of motion.
Lift your chest by pressing your legs into your hands rather than pulling with your arms.
Breathe slowly and evenly while holding the stretch.
ex_QCBTW5.description: Bow Pose is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Chest, Hip Flexors.

ex_SGGF44.name: Bridge Hip Abduction
instructions: Begin by lying on your back with your knees bent, feet flat on the floor at shoulder width, and arms extended by your sides.
Lift your hips off the floor to form a straight line from your shoulders to your knees, engaging your glutes and core.
While keeping your hips elevated, move your knees outwards in a controlled manner and back.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.

Ensure your hips remain elevated and level throughout the exercise to maximize glute activation.
Perform the leg abductions slowly and with control to avoid any jerky movements and enhance muscle engagement.
ex_SGGF44.description: Bridge Hip Abduction is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Abductors, Hamstrings.

ex_A5RK6Q.name: Bridge Pose Setu Bandhasana
instructions: Lie down on your back with your knees bent, feet together on the floor, and arms resting at your sides.
Raise your hips and straighten your thighs with your back while your knees are closed.
Maintain this position, raise your arms and then land them overhead with your palms facing upward.
Return to the initial position and repeat.
tips: Keep your feet hip-width apart and ensure your knees stay aligned with your ankles to maintain proper form.
Engage your core and glutes to support your lower back and maintain stability.
Breathe deeply and evenly throughout the pose, relaxing your shoulders and neck.

ex_AOHJML.name: Bridge With Alternating Leg Raise
instructions: Begin by lying on your back with your knees bent, feet flat on the floor, and arms resting by your sides.
Lift your hips off the floor to form a straight line from your shoulders to your knees, engaging your glutes and core.
While keeping your hips elevated, extend your right leg straight keeping it in level with torso, then lower it back to the starting position.

Repeat the movement with your left leg, extending it straight keeping it in level with torso, then lowering it back to the starting position. Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your core engaged to maintain stability and support your lower back.
Ensure your hips remain elevated and level throughout the exercise to maximize glute activation.
Perform the leg raises slowly and with control to avoid any jerky movements and to enhance muscle engagement.
ex_AOHJML.description: Bridge With Alternating Leg Raise is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Quadriceps.

ex_RJLPIL.name: Butterfly Yoga Pose
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs bent and the soles of your feet pressed together, allowing your knees to fall out to the sides.
Hold your feet with both hands and sit up tall, then lean forward slightly towards the floor, creating a gentle arch in your back.
Press your knees gently towards the floor to deepen the stretch in your hips.
Hold the position for the desired duration, breathing deeply and evenly throughout.
tips: Maintain a gentle arch in your back while leaning forward to ensure a proper stretch and avoid straining.
Inhale deeply and exhale slowly throughout the pose to help relax your muscles and enhance the stretch.
Apply gentle pressure to your knees without forcing them down to prevent overstraining your hip joints.
ex_RJLPIL.description: Butterfly Yoga Pose is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the adductors (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

ex_KYE74I.name: Cat Pose
instructions: Begin on all fours with your hands directly under your shoulders and your knees under your hips. Keep your arms straight and your gaze toward the floor.
Slowly round your back toward the ceiling by tucking your chin toward your chest and drawing your tailbone underneath you.
Hold the stretched position briefly while keeping your shoulders relaxed and your core gently engaged.
Return to the starting position with control and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your hands directly beneath your shoulders and your knees beneath your hips.
Draw your belly button inward to help deepen the spinal movement.
Round your spine evenly from your neck to your lower back.
Inhale in the starting position and exhale as you round your back.
ex_KYE74I.description: Cat Pose is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Core, Upper Back, Shoulders.

ex_VSJH67.name: Cat Stretch
instructions: Begin on your hands and knees in a tabletop position, with your wrists aligned under your shoulders and your knees aligned under your hips.
Inhale deeply, then slowly arch your back upwards towards the ceiling, tucking your chin towards your chest and drawing your navel in towards your spine.
Hold the arched position for a few seconds, feeling the stretch along your spine and back muscles.
Exhale and slowly return to the starting tabletop position. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on your breath, inhaling deeply as you arch your back and exhaling as you return to the starting position.
Ensure your wrists and knees remain aligned throughout the exercise to maintain proper form and avoid strain.
Relax your neck and avoid straining it as you tuck your chin towards your chest.
Perform this stretch as part of a cool-down routine or whenever you need to relieve tension in your back.
ex_VSJH67.description: Cat Stretch is a beginner multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Traps, Lats.

ex_KHNBSY.name: Chair Pose
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder width apart and raise both arms overhead with your palms facing each other.
Push your hips back and bend your knees to lower into a squat while keeping your chest lifted and your arms extended overhead.
Hold the position while keeping your heels on the floor, and your weight evenly distributed across both feet.
Press through your heels to return to the starting position with control and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Sit your hips back as if lowering onto a chair.
Keep your knees aligned with your toes without allowing them to collapse inward.
Engage your core to improve balance and stability.
Inhale as you lower into the pose and exhale as you return to standing.
ex_KHNBSY.description: Chair Pose is a beginner multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves, Core.

ex_7VDOLJ.name: Child Pose Arms Extended Left Right
instructions: Begin in a kneeling position with your hips resting on your heels, face forward with your hands to your sides.
Lower your torso toward the floor and slowly extend both hands to one side while keeping your hips resting on your heels, resting your forehead on your hands.
Hold the stretch when you feel it along the side of your upper back and torso.
Return your to your starting position, repeat the stretch to the opposite side, and continue alternating sides.
tips: Keep your hips resting on your heels throughout the stretch.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid shrugging them toward your ears
Stretch only until you feel a comfortable pull along your side.
Inhale in the center and exhale as you reach to each side.

ex_2JBPQC.name: Child Pose Arms on Side
instructions: Begin in a tall kneeling position with your knees slightly apart and your hands resting by your sides.
Sit your hips back onto your heels as you lower your chest toward your thighs, allowing your forehead to rest on the floor.
Extend your arms alongside your body with your palms facing upward and relax your shoulders.

ex_BC56FG.name: Child Pose Elbows on Block
instructions: Begin in a tall kneeling position with two yoga blocks placed in front of you. Rest both elbows on each block and bring your hands together behind your head.
Sit your hips back toward your heels as you lower your chest toward the floor.
Allow your elbows to remain on the block while gently sinking your chest to deepen the stretch through your shoulders and upper back.
Hold the stretch, then slowly return to the starting position with control.
tips: Keep your elbows supported on the block throughout the stretch.
Keep your hips moving toward your heels as you lower your chest.
Avoid rounding your lower back excessively.

ex_BC56FG.description: Child Pose Elbows on Block is a beginner multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Upper Back, Lower Back.

ex_IAEYF7.name: Child Pose Up
instructions: Begin on all fours with your hands directly under your shoulders and your knees under your hips. Keep your elbows bent close to your body with chest close to the floor.
Push through your hands to lift your upper body slightly while simultaneously pushing your hips backwards towards your heels. Straighten your arms as you move your hips back.
Continue to push your hips back until they are close to your heels, extending your arms fully in front of you on the floor.
Hold this position for the desired duration, breathing deeply and allowing your body to relax into the stretch.

Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize the effectiveness of the stretch.

ex_IAEYF7.description: Child Pose Up is a beginner multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Chest.

ex_D2VAZK.name: Child Pose
instructions: Begin by kneeling on the floor with your knees together or slightly apart, and your big toes touching.
Sit back on your heels, extending your arms forward on the floor, lowering your torso down between your thighs.
Rest your forehead on the floor, keeping your arms extended out in front of you with palms facing down.
Hold this position for the desired duration, breathing deeply and allowing your body to relax into the stretch.

Allow your hips to sink back towards your heels to deepen the stretch in your lower back and hips.
If needed, you can place a cushion or folded blanket between your thighs and calves for added comfort.

ex_3LUDBD.name: Cobra Full Push Up
instructions: Begin in a plank position with your hands placed under your shoulders, your body forming a straight line from head to heels.
Perform a push-up by lowering your body towards the floor by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your sides.
As your chest reaches the floor, leave your hips on the floor and press through your palms to lift your chest up, straightening your arms and arching your back into the cobra position.
Bend your arms to lower your chest back to the floor, then press through your palms to lift your body back to the starting plank position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on using your chest, shoulders, and triceps to push your body up while keeping your elbows close to your sides.

. Slowly lower your chest back to the floor by bending your elbows, returning to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

From the cobra position, slowly rotate your torso to the right, looking over your right shoulder, and hold the stretch for a moment, feeling the stretch along the left side of your abdomen. Return to the center cobra position.

Slowly rotate your torso to the left, looking over your left shoulder, and hold the stretch, feeling the stretch along the right side of your abdomen. Return to the center cobra position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

ex_AWQY3J.description: Cobra Side Ab Stretch is a beginner multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Lower Back.

ex_ZIB7GC.name: Cobra Yoga Pose Hold
instructions: Begin by lying face down on the floor with your legs extended straight behind you and your hands placed at shoulder level, palms flat on the floor.

ex_KSYTGZ.name: Crab Pose

Engage your core and press through your palms and feet to lift your hips off the floor, creating a tabletop position with your body.

ex_7DGCLF.name: Crescent Moon Pose
instructions: Begin in a lunge position with one foot forward and your back knee resting on the floor. Bend your back knee and reach behind you to grasp your back foot with both hands.
Gently draw your back heel toward your glutes while keeping your chest lifted and your hips facing forward.
Hold the stretch until you feel a comfortable stretch along the front of your back thigh and hip.
Release your foot with control, return to the starting position, and repeat on the opposite side.

ex_JTPKSE.name: Criss Cross Bow Tie Pose

Walk your hands out in opposite directions as far as possible, dipping your head and chest toward the floor.
Relax your shoulders and hold the position until you feel a comfortable stretch across the back of your shoulder and upper back.
Release the stretch slowly and repeat with the opposite arm crossed underneath.

ex_OZ4XNA.name: Crow Pose

Lean your body forward and position the insides of your knees against the outsides of your elbows.
Shift your weight onto your hands and lift both feet off the floor, balancing with your knees supported slightly above your elbows.
Hold the position briefly, then slowly lower your feet back to the floor and return to the starting position.
tips: Spread your fingers wide to create a stable base of support.
Keep your gaze slightly forward rather than directly at the floor to help maintain balance.

ex_BUMU7K.name: Dead Bug (Multiple Reps)

Engage your core and slowly lower your right arm and left leg towards the floor, keeping your back flat on the floor and not allowing it to arch.

ex_QHW5IH.name: Double Pigeon Pose
