ex_BGQCHT.description: Lat Pull Down Normal Grip is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Shoulders, Upper Back.

ex_RQD3OQ.name: Lat Pull Down Wide Grip
instructions: Sit at the lat pulldown machine with your feet flat on the floor and knees secured under the pads. Grasp the bar with both hands, wider than shoulder-width apart, and your arms fully extended above you.
Pull the bar down towards your upper chest by bending your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together, keeping your back straight.
Hold the contraction for a second, then slowly return the bar to the starting position with control, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back straight and avoid leaning backward excessively.
Focus on engaging your back muscles throughout the movement.
Exhale as you pull the bar down and inhale as you return to the starting position.
ex_RQD3OQ.description: Lat Pull Down Wide Grip is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Shoulders, Upper Back.

ex_UR7YFP.name: Lawnmower Row
instructions: Stand in a split stance with one hand on your front thigh or a bench, holding a dumbbell in the other hand.
Hinge forward with a flat back and let the dumbbell hang below your shoulder.
Pull the weight up and back toward your hip, rotating your torso slightly as you would starting a lawnmower.
Lower the weight with control and repeat, then switch sides.
tips: Lead with your elbow and keep it close to your body.
Keep the rotation small and controlled.
ex_UR7YFP.description: Lawnmower Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Rear Shoulders, Obliques.

ex_YJIHKW.name: Lying Back Extension
instructions: Begin by lying face down on the floor with your legs extended straight behind you and your hands placed behind your head, elbows out to the sides.
Engage your core and glutes, then lift your upper torso off the floor, keeping your neck in a neutral position and your lower body relaxed on the floor.
Hold the top position for a moment, squeezing your lower back muscles.
Slowly lower your upper torso back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your neck in a neutral position to avoid straining it.
Perform the exercise on a comfortable, non-slip surface to prevent discomfort or injury.
If you find it challenging to lift your upper torso, you can start with smaller movements and gradually increase the range of motion as you build strength.
ex_YJIHKW.description: Lying Back Extension is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Hamstrings.

ex_RXGLPJ.name: Plate Alternating Deadstop Row
instructions: Place two weight plates on the floor and hinge over them with a flat back, knees slightly bent.
Grip one plate and row it up toward your hip.
Lower it back to the floor and let it come to a full stop.
Row the other plate and keep alternating.
tips: Each rep starts from a dead stop, so don't bounce the plate.
Keep your torso still as you pull.
ex_RXGLPJ.description: Plate Alternating Deadstop Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Rear Shoulders, Forearms.

ex_ZBPONQ.name: Plate Glute Bridge to Pullover
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, holding a weight plate above your chest with both hands.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips into a glute bridge.
Holding the bridge, lower the plate behind your head with slightly bent arms until you feel a stretch in your lats.
Pull the plate back over your chest, then lower your hips and repeat.
tips: Keep your ribs down while the plate moves overhead.
Squeeze your glutes throughout the bridge.
ex_ZBPONQ.description: Plate Glute Bridge to Pullover is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Chest, Triceps.

ex_QATXGR.name: Plate Good Morning
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and hold a weight plate against your chest.
With a slight bend in your knees, hinge forward from your hips with a flat back.
Lower your torso until it is close to parallel with the floor, or until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
Drive your hips forward to return to standing.
tips: Keep your back flat; don't round it to go lower.
Push your hips back rather than bending your knees more.
ex_QATXGR.description: Plate Good Morning is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes.

ex_QNEHEG.name: Plate Pinch Grip Deadlift
instructions: Stand over two weight plates and pinch one in each hand by its rim, fingers on one face and thumb on the other.
Hinge at your hips and bend your knees with a flat back.
Drive through your feet to stand up tall, holding the plates at your sides.
Lower them back down with control by hinging at your hips.
tips: The pinch grip limits the weight, so this is mainly a grip and posture drill.
Keep your shoulders back and chest up.
ex_QNEHEG.description: Plate Pinch Grip Deadlift is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Quadriceps, Traps.

ex_3K3PXU.name: Plate Pinch Grip Row
instructions: Pinch a weight plate in one hand and hinge forward with a flat back, supporting yourself on a bench or your thigh with the other hand.
Let the plate hang below your shoulder.
Row the plate up toward your hip by driving your elbow back.
Lower it with control and repeat, then switch sides.
tips: Keep the plate from swinging.
Squeeze your shoulder blade at the top.
ex_3K3PXU.description: Plate Pinch Grip Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Forearms, Rear Shoulders.

ex_AEYXHQ.name: Prone Bench Row Barbell Pronated Grip
instructions: Lie chest-first on an incline bench, holding a barbell with a pronate grip (palms facing down) and your hands placed shoulder-width apart. Extend your arms straight down towards the floor.
Pull the barbell towards your upper abdomen by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement, ensuring the barbell reaches close to the bench.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position with control, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on pulling with your back muscles rather than your arms.
Exhale as you pull the barbell up and inhale as you lower it.
Use a weight that allows you to maintain proper form throughout the exercise.
ex_AEYXHQ.description: Prone Bench Row Barbell Pronated Grip is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Shoulders.

ex_DRNHYA.name: Prone Bench Row Barbell Reverse Grip
instructions: Lie chest-first on an incline bench, holding a barbell with a reverse grip (palms facing up) and your hands placed shoulder-width apart. Extend your arms straight down towards the floor.
Pull the barbell towards your abdomen by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement, ensuring the barbell reaches close to the bench.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position with control, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on pulling with your back muscles rather than your arms.
Exhale as you pull the barbell up and inhale as you lower it.
Keep your elbows close to your body to maximize back muscle engagement.
ex_DRNHYA.description: Prone Bench Row Barbell Reverse Grip is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Shoulders.

ex_CFSE6N.name: Pull Up Normal Grip
instructions: Stand beneath a pull-up bar and grasp it with an overhand grip (palms facing away from you), hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Engage your back muscles and pull yourself up towards the bar by bending your elbows.
Continue pulling until your chin is above the bar, focusing on contracting your back muscles.
Lower yourself back to the starting position in a controlled manner, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Use a full range of motion, fully extending your arms at the bottom and pulling up until your chin is above the bar.
Focus on engaging your back muscles, particularly the latissimus dorsi, to perform the pull-up effectively.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you pull up and inhaling as you lower yourself down.
Avoid using momentum to swing your body; maintain a controlled movement throughout the exercise.
Perform the exercise on a stable, secure pull-up bar to ensure safety.
ex_CFSE6N.description: Pull Up Normal Grip is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.

ex_VSKGCQ.name: Pull Up Wide Grip (Front View)
instructions: Stand beneath a pull-up bar and grasp it with an overhand grip (palms facing away from you), hands wider than shoulder-width apart.
Engage your back muscles to pull yourself up towards the bar by bending your elbows.
Continue pulling until your chin is above the bar, focusing on contracting your back muscles.
Lower yourself back to the starting position in a controlled manner, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Use a full range of motion, fully extending your arms at the bottom and pulling up until your chin is above the bar.
Focus on engaging your back muscles, particularly the latissimus dorsi, to perform the pull-up effectively.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you pull up and inhaling as you lower yourself down.
Avoid using momentum to swing your body; maintain a controlled movement throughout the exercise.
Perform the exercise on a stable, secure pull-up bar to ensure safety.
ex_VSKGCQ.description: Pull Up Wide Grip (Front View) is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.

ex_OYFEYI.name: Push Pull Chair Over Head Pull
instructions: Sit tall on the machine chair, or a cable seat, and take the overhead handles with your arms extended.
Brace your core and keep your chest up.
Pull the handles down toward your shoulders by driving your elbows down and back.
Return the handles overhead with control and repeat.
tips: Lead with your elbows, not your hands.
Avoid leaning back to finish the rep.
ex_OYFEYI.description: Push Pull Chair Over Head Pull is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Upper Back, Rear Shoulders.

ex_LGRDJS.name: Resistance Band - Cable Row
instructions: Attach a resistance band to a sturdy anchor point at chest height. Kneel on one knee with the opposite leg forward, foot flat on the ground.
Hold the band handles with both hands, arms extended forward, and palms facing down.
Pull the band handles towards your chest by bending your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together at the end of the movement.
Return to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired repetitions.
tips: Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together at the peak of the row to maximize back activation.
Adjust the resistance band tension or your kneeling position for an appropriate challenge.
Avoid shrugging your shoulders; keep them down and relaxed.
ex_LGRDJS.description: Resistance Band - Cable Row is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Biceps.

ex_3POZ6H.name: Resistance Band Cross Body Single Straight Arm Supinated Pulldown
instructions: Attach the resistance band to a high anchor point in front of you, on your left side. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handle with your right hand, palm facing up.
Extend your right arm straight opposite the left side of your head, keeping your arm straight.
Pull the handle down across your body towards your right hip until fully extended by your side and slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other side.
tips: Exhale as you pull the band down and inhale as you release it back up.
Focus on pulling with your back muscles rather than your arm for better engagement.
Ensure your hips stay square and stable, avoiding any twisting motion.
ex_3POZ6H.description: Resistance Band Cross Body Single Straight Arm Supinated Pulldown is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.

ex_6YE3EG.name: Resistance Band Floor Hyperextension
instructions: Lie face down on the floor with a loop resistance band over your ankles and another loop resistance band over your forearms. Extend your arms forward and keep your legs straight.
Engage your core and glutes, and lift your chest and legs off the floor simultaneously, spreading your legs apart against the resistance of the band.
Squeeze your lower back muscles at the top of the movement, keeping your arms and legs straight.
Slowly lower your chest and legs back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your neck in a neutral position to avoid straining it.
Focus on engaging your lower back and glute muscles throughout the movement.
Exhale as you lift your chest and legs and inhale as you lower them back down.
ex_6YE3EG.description: Resistance Band Floor Hyperextension is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Shoulders.

ex_A3ROPV.name: Resistance Band Kneeling Cross Body Single Straight Arm Supinated Pulldown
instructions: Attach the resistance band to a high anchor point in front of you, on your left side. Kneel on the floor on your right knee and your left foot flat on the floor, holding the handle with your right hand, palm facing up.
Extend your right arm straight opposite the left side of your head, keeping your arm straight.
Pull the handle down across your body towards your right hip until fully extended by your side and slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other side.
tips: Exhale as you pull the band down and inhale as you release it back up.
Focus on pulling with your back muscles rather than your arm for better engagement.
Ensure your hips stay square and stable, avoiding any twisting motion.
ex_A3ROPV.description: Resistance Band Kneeling Cross Body Single Straight Arm Supinated Pulldown is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.

ex_YT5DS5.name: Resistance Band Lying Hyperextension Abduction
instructions: Lie face down on the floor with your arms crossed under your head, resting your forehead on your arms. Place a loop resistance band around your thighs, just above your knees. Keep your legs extended and feet together.
Engage your core and glutes to lift your legs straight off the floor while keeping your head resting on your arms.
While lifting your legs, open them wide apart against the band's resistance, keeping your legs straight.
Slowly bring your legs back together while lowering your legs back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on engaging your glutes and hip abductors throughout the movement.
Exhale as you lift and open your legs, and inhale as you bring them back together and lower them.
Keep your core engaged throughout the exercise to maintain stability and protect your lower back.
ex_YT5DS5.description: Resistance Band Lying Hyperextension Abduction is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Core.

ex_K376HJ.name: Reverse Grip Lat Pull Down
instructions: Sit at a lat pulldown machine with your feet flat on the floor and knees secured under the pads. Grasp the bar with an underhand grip (palms facing you) at shoulder-width apart, arms fully extended above you.
Engage your core and keep your back straight. Lean back slightly to create a natural arch in your lower back.
Pull the bar towards your upper chest, bringing your elbows down to your sides while squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Slowly return the bar to the starting position with control, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you pull the bar down and inhale as you return it to the starting position.
Avoid using momentum or swinging your body to lift the weight.
Keep your wrists straight and avoid letting them bend backward.
ex_K376HJ.description: Reverse Grip Lat Pull Down is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Forearms.

ex_4TJLQ3.name: Seated Cable Row v Bar Machine
instructions: Sit on the cable row machine with your feet secure on the foot platform. Grasp the V bar with both hands.
Sit upright with your back straight, extending your arms fully in front of you.
Pull the V bar towards your abdomen by bringing your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Slowly extend your arms back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired repetitions.
tips: Keep your back straight throughout the exercise to avoid strain.
Engage your core to maintain stability and proper posture.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and reduce the risk of injury.
ex_4TJLQ3.description: Seated Cable Row v Bar Machine is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Shoulders, Biceps.

ex_LL6ID3.name: Seated Normal Grip Row Machine
instructions: Sit on a bench facing a row machine with a straight back and your feet placed on the footrests.
Hold the rod above your knees with an overhand grip of your hands while keeping your arms straight.
Pull the cable towards your chest by bending your arms and taking your elbows past your back.
Return to the initial position and repeat.
ex_LL6ID3.description: Seated Normal Grip Row Machine is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Rear Shoulders.

ex_VVUR2U.name: Seated Resistance Band - Cable Rows
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs fully extended and feet together, anchoring the resistance band around the soles of your feet. Hold the handles with both hands, arms extended forward, palms facing each other.
Keep your back straight, chest up, and core engaged to stabilize your body.
Pull the handles towards your torso by bending your elbows, keeping your arms close to your body. Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together at the peak of the movement.
Slowly extend your arms back to the starting position, maintaining control over the resistance band. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back straight and avoid slouching to maintain proper form.
Engage your core to prevent any rocking or unnecessary movement during the exercise.
Use a controlled motion to pull and release the resistance band, avoiding jerking movements.
ex_VVUR2U.description: Seated Resistance Band - Cable Rows is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Biceps, Core.

ex_N6UVX4.name: Seated Row Machine Rows
instructions: Sit on the machine with your chest against the pad, or your feet on the platform, and grab the handles.
Sit tall with your shoulders down and arms extended.
Pull the handles toward your torso, driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Return the handles with control until your arms are straight and repeat.
tips: Don't rock your torso to move the weight.
Pause briefly with your shoulder blades squeezed.
ex_N6UVX4.description: Seated Row Machine Rows is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Rear Shoulders.

ex_NOECF7.name: Single Arm Cable Row Left
instructions: Set the cable pulley to a mid position and attach a single handle. Stand facing the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart. Grasp the handle with your left hand, arm extended towards the machine.
Slightly bend your knees, push your hips backward, and lean forward slightly for balance.
Pull the handle towards your torso, bending your elbow and squeezing your shoulder blade back. Keeping your elbow close to your body.
Slowly extend your arm back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired repetitions, then switch to the right arm.
tips: Exhale as you pull the handle towards your torso and inhale as you extend your arm back.
Use a weight that provides enough resistance to challenge your muscles without compromising form.
Avoid using your body to generate momentum; keep the movement isolated to your arm and back.
ex_NOECF7.description: Single Arm Cable Row Left is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Shoulders, Core.

ex_QMX42V.name: Single Arm Cable Row Right
instructions: Set the cable pulley to a mid position and attach a single handle. Stand facing the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart. Grasp the handle with your right hand, arm extended towards the machine.
Slightly bend your knees, push your hips backward, and lean forward slightly for balance.
Pull the handle towards your torso, bending your elbow and squeezing your shoulder blade back. Keeping your elbow close to your body.
Slowly extend your arm back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired repetitions, then switch to the right arm.
tips: Exhale as you pull the handle towards your torso and inhale as you extend your arm back.
Use a weight that provides enough resistance to challenge your muscles without compromising form.
Avoid using your body to generate momentum; keep the movement isolated to your arm and back.
ex_QMX42V.description: Single Arm Cable Row Right is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Shoulders, Core.

ex_7AD5EH.name: Single Arm Standing Low Cable Row
instructions: Set the cable pulley to a low position and attach a single handle. Stand facing the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart. Grasp the handle with your left hand, arm extended towards the machine.
Slightly bend your knees, push your hips backward, and lean forward slightly for balance.
Pull the handle towards your torso, bending your elbow and squeezing your shoulder blade back. Keeping your elbow close to your body.
Slowly extend your arm back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired repetitions, then switch to the right arm.
tips: Exhale as you pull the handle towards your torso and inhale as you extend your arm back.
Use a weight that provides enough resistance to challenge your muscles without compromising form.
Avoid using your body to generate momentum; keep the movement isolated to your arm and back.
ex_7AD5EH.description: Single Arm Standing Low Cable Row is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Shoulders, Core.

ex_PESVZP.name: Straight Arm Cable Lat Pull Down
instructions: Stand facing a high cable pulley holding a straight bar or rope, arms extended and slightly bent.
Hinge slightly forward at the hips and brace your core.
Keeping your arms straight, pull the bar down in an arc to your thighs.
Let the bar rise back to shoulder height with control and repeat.
tips: Your elbows stay fixed; the movement comes from your shoulders.
Squeeze your lats at the bottom.
ex_PESVZP.description: Straight Arm Cable Lat Pull Down is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Rear Shoulders, Core.

ex_72KSGA.name: Straight Bar Cable Pull Down
instructions: Stand facing a cable machine with a straight bar attached to the high pulley. Grip the bar with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, palms facing down.

Slightly bend your knees, push your hips back, and lean your torso forward slightly. Pull the bar down towards your thighs in a straight line, keeping your arms straight and your elbows slightly bent.
Pull the bar down until it reaches your thighs, feeling a strong contraction in your lats.
Slowly return the bar to the starting position with control, maintaining tension in your lats. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily: exhale as you pull the bar down and inhale as you return it to the starting position.
Adjust the weight on the cable machine to provide enough challenge without compromising form.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid shrugging them towards your ears.
ex_72KSGA.description: Straight Bar Cable Pull Down is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Middle Back, Upper Back, Core.

ex_CT7BW5.name: Straight Bar Cable Row Close Grip
instructions: Sit at a cable row machine with your feet placed on the footrests and knees slightly bent. Grasp the straight bar with a close grip, palms facing down.
Engage your core and maintain a straight back. Pull the bar towards your abdomen, squeezing your shoulder blades together and keeping your elbows close to your body.
Hold the contraction for a moment, feeling the muscles in your back activating.
Slowly extend your arms to return the bar to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily: exhale as you pull the bar towards you and inhale as you extend your arms.
Adjust the weight on the cable machine to provide enough challenge without compromising form.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid shrugging them towards your ears.
ex_CT7BW5.description: Straight Bar Cable Row Close Grip is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Forearms, Shoulders.

ex_IIWUYJ.name: Straight Bar Cable Row Normal Grip
instructions: Sit at a cable row machine with your feet placed on the footrests and knees slightly bent. Grasp the straight bar with hands just wider than shoulder-width, palms facing down.
Engage your core and maintain a straight back. Pull the bar towards your abdomen, squeezing your shoulder blades together and keeping your elbows close to your body.
Hold the contraction for a moment, feeling the muscles in your back activating.
Slowly extend your arms to return the bar to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily: exhale as you pull the bar towards you and inhale as you extend your arms.
Adjust the weight on the cable machine to provide enough challenge without compromising form.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid shrugging them towards your ears.
ex_IIWUYJ.description: Straight Bar Cable Row Normal Grip is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Forearms, Shoulders.

ex_WDW5WC.name: Superman Pulls Resistance Bands
instructions: Lie face down on the floor with your arms extended straight out in front of you and your legs extended straight behind you.
Simultaneously lift your arms and chest off the floor as high as you comfortably can, engaging your lower back and glutes.
While holding the lifted position, bend your elbows and pull your arms back towards your shoulders, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Extend your arms back out in front of you and slowly lower your chest back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily: exhale as you lift and pull the resistance band, and inhale as you extend your arms and lower your body.
Gradually increase the duration of the hold and the number of repetitions as your strength improves.
Keep your neck in a neutral position to avoid straining it.
ex_WDW5WC.description: Superman Pulls Resistance Bands is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Shoulders, Core.

ex_USVWIV.name: Superman Pulls
instructions: Lie face down on the floor with a resistance band secured to a low anchor point in front of you. Hold one end of the resistance band in each hand with your arms extended straight out in front of you and your legs extended straight behind you.
Simultaneously lift your arms, chest, and legs off the floor as high as you comfortably can, engaging your lower back and glutes.
While holding the lifted position, bend your elbows and pull the resistance band towards your shoulders, squeezing your shoulder blades together.

Extend your arms back out in front of you, keeping tension on the resistance band, and then slowly lower your arms, chest, and legs back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on using your lower back and glute muscles to lift your body off the floor.
Keep your neck in a neutral position to avoid straining it.
Use a mat to provide cushioning and support for your body.
ex_USVWIV.description: Superman Pulls is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Shoulders, Core.

ex_ZLYB4S.name: Superman
instructions: Lie face down on the floor with your arms extended straight out in front of you and your legs extended straight behind you.
Simultaneously lift your arms, chest, and legs off the floor as high as you comfortably can, engaging your lower back and glutes.
Hold the lifted position for a second, feeling the contraction in your lower back and glutes.
Slowly lower your arms, chest, and legs back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on using your lower back and glute muscles to lift your body off the floor.
Keep your neck in a neutral position to avoid straining it.
Use a mat to provide cushioning and support for your body.
ex_ZLYB4S.description: Superman is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Shoulders, Core.

ex_BLRWSE.name: Supine Push Up
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Position your elbows to your sides with your forearms perpendicular to the floor and hands kept closed.
Engage your core and press your elbows into the floor, lifting your upper back and shoulders off the floor.
Hold the lifted position for a second, feeling the contraction in your upper back.
Slowly lower your upper back and shoulders back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily: exhale as you lift your upper back and shoulders, and inhale as you lower them back down.
Focus on using your shoulders and upper back muscles to lift your upper body off the floor.
Use a mat to provide cushioning and support for your back.
ex_BLRWSE.description: Supine Push Up is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Core.

ex_QQ7YV7.name: Suspension Trainer With Grips Bent Knee Inverted Row
instructions: Adjust the suspension trainer handles to about waist height. Sit on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, holding the handles with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Lean back, extend your arms, and lift your hips off the floor, keeping your body in a straight line from head to knees parallel to the floor.
Pull your chest towards the handles by bending your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Slowly lower your body back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Curl the EZ bar towards your shoulders by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms pressed against the pad.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement, ensuring the bar reaches shoulder height.
Slowly lower the bar back to the starting position with control, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your upper arms stationary against the pad to isolate the biceps.
Use a weight that allows you to maintain proper form throughout the exercise.
Exhale as you curl the barbell up and inhale as you lower it.
ex_FGKHQ5.description: Preacher Curl EZ Bar is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with an ez barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

ex_ZIHX2B.name: Reverse Grip Resistance Band Simultaneous
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and place the middle of a resistance band under both feet. Hold one handle in each hand with an overhand grip (palms facing down), arms fully extended by your sides.
Simultaneously curl both handles upward towards your shoulders by bending your elbows and squeezing your biceps at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the handles back to the starting position with control, fully extending your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you curl the handles upward and inhale as you lower them back down.
Use a resistance band that provides enough tension to challenge your muscles without compromising form.
Maintain a steady pace to ensure consistent tension on the muscles.
ex_ZIHX2B.description: Reverse Grip Resistance Band Simultaneous is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

ex_5ZRK4K.name: Spider Curl Barbell
instructions: Set an incline bench at a 45-degree angle and lie face down, ensuring your chest is supported and your feet are firm on the floor. Hold a barbell with an underhand grip and hands shoulder-width apart.
Let your arms hang straight down towards the floor, keeping your elbows slightly bent.
Curl the barbell towards your shoulders by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary, and focusing on contracting your biceps.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position with control, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Use a full range of motion to fully engage the biceps.
Ensure your elbows remain stationary and do not flare out during the movement.
Adjust the weight of the barbell to provide enough challenge without compromising form.
ex_5ZRK4K.description: Spider Curl Barbell is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

Curl the dumbbells towards your shoulders by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary, and focusing on contracting your biceps.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Ensure your elbows remain stationary and do not flare out during the movement.
Adjust the weight of the dumbbells to provide enough challenge without compromising form.
ex_G4EFHL.description: Spider Curl Dumbbells Simultaneous is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

Let your arms hang straight down towards the floor, keeping your elbows slightly bent.
Curl the EZ bar towards your shoulders by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary, and focusing on contracting your biceps.

ex_N6JICV.name: Zottman Curl Dumbbell Simultaneous
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with an underhand grip (palms facing forward) and arms hanging by your sides.
Curl the dumbbells towards your shoulders by bending your elbows and keeping your upper arms stationary.
At the top of the curl, rotate your wrists so that your palms face forward (overhand grip), and then lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position with control.
Rotate your wrists back to the underhand grip once you reach the bottom of the movement. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid using momentum; focus on using your biceps and forearms to lift and lower the dumbbells.
Keep your core engaged to maintain balance and stability.
Ensure a smooth and controlled rotation of the wrists at the top of the movement.
ex_N6JICV.description: Zottman Curl Dumbbell Simultaneous is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms, Shoulders.

ex_BEMRHG.name: Zottman Curls Resistance Band Simultaneous
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, in the middle of a resistance band, holding the handles with an underhand grip (palms facing forward), arms hanging by your sides.
Curl the handles towards your shoulders by bending your elbows and keeping your upper arms stationary.
At the top of the curl, rotate your wrists so that your palms face forward (overhand grip), and then lower the handles back down to the starting position with control.
Rotate your wrists back to the underhand grip once you reach the bottom of the movement. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid using momentum; focus on using your biceps and forearms to lift and lower the handles.
Keep your core engaged to maintain balance and stability.
Ensure a smooth and controlled rotation of the wrists at the top of the movement.
ex_BEMRHG.description: Zottman Curls Resistance Band Simultaneous is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms, Shoulders.

ex_XLXPGD.name: 180 Jump Turns
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and lower into a shallow squat with your chest up.
Drive through your feet to jump vertically while rotating your body 180 degrees in the air.
Land softly with your knees slightly bent, facing the opposite direction.
Repeat the movement, alternating the direction of rotation.
tips: Keep your knees aligned with your toes during takeoff and landing.
Exhale during the jump and inhale as you land and reset.
Maintain a controlled rhythm and prioritize landing quality over speed.
Land softly on the balls of your feet by bending your knees.
ex_XLXPGD.description: 180 Jump Turns is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Core, Obliques.

ex_A4YQOQ.name: 4 Corners Curtsy
instructions: Start with feet shoulder-width apart, hands close to your chest.
Step your right foot back and to the left, crossing behind your left leg and bending both knees into a curtsy lunge while extending both arms straight to the opposite side in front of your torso.
Return to the starting position by stepping your right foot forward to meet your left foot.
Repeat the curtsy lunge the opposite side while straightening both arms on the opposite side.
tips: Maintain Balance: Keep your core engaged to help maintain balance throughout the movement.
Controlled Movements: Perform each step and curtsy with control to maximize muscle activation and reduce the risk of injury.
Keep Knees Aligned: Ensure your front knee stays aligned with your front foot to avoid unnecessary strain on your knee joint.
ex_A4YQOQ.description: 4 Corners Curtsy is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Adductors.

ex_RKDEW3.name: 4 Corners Side Step
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent.
Keep your hands close in front of your chest with your fists forming a punch and facing forward.
Lift your right foot to the back, straightening it sideways and lightly touching the floor when fully extended. While extending both fists frontwards.
Bring your right foot back to starting position and both fists close to your chest at starting position and repeat with alternating legs
tips: Keep your knees slightly bent. This helps absorb the impact and engages your leg muscles more effectively.
Maintain a tight core. Engaging your core muscles will help with balance and stability throughout the movement.
Use controlled movements. Avoid rushing; perform each step deliberately to maximize muscle activation and reduce the risk of injury.
ex_RKDEW3.description: 4 Corners Side Step is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Hip Flexors, Abductors.

ex_2PSGLY.name: 4 Punches Side Squat
instructions: Start with feet shoulder-width apart, hands in fists at chest level.
Perform four punches in front of you, alternating between left and right hands.
Step your right foot out to the side and lower into a squat position, keeping your back straight and knees aligned with your toes.
Return to the standing position by stepping your left foot back in, and repeat the exercise.
tips: Engage Your Core: Keep your core muscles engaged to help with balance and stability during punches and squats.
Controlled Movements: Perform punches and squats in a controlled manner to maximize muscle activation and reduce injury risk.
Keep Knees Aligned: Ensure your knees stay in line with your toes during the squat to avoid unnecessary strain on your knee joints.
ex_2PSGLY.description: 4 Punches Side Squat is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Shoulders.

ex_YSKWTA.name: 45 Degrees Step Out
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart keeping them bent to a half squat position.
Step your right foot out at a 45-degree angle to the side until your leg is completely straight.
Bring your right foot back to the starting position.
Repeat the movement with your left foot, continuing to alternate sides.
tips: Keep your core engaged to maintain balance and stability throughout the movement.
Ensure your knees are aligned with your toes when you step out to protect your joints.
Perform the exercise with controlled movements to maximize muscle engagement and reduce the risk of injury.
ex_YSKWTA.description: 45 Degrees Step Out is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Abductors.

ex_BFH2IO.name: Agility Ladder Advanced Hop Position
instructions: Stand at the end of an agility ladder on the balls of your feet with your knees slightly bent.
Hop forward into the first square, landing softly on both feet.
Keep hopping through each square in a quick, steady rhythm.
Pump your arms and stay light on your feet to the end of the ladder.
tips: Stay on the balls of your feet; avoid landing on your heels.
Speed comes after clean footwork.
ex_BFH2IO.description: Agility Ladder Advanced Hop Position is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Hamstrings, Core.

ex_JLI56N.name: Agility Ladder Advanced Single-Leg
instructions: Stand on one leg at the end of an agility ladder.
Hop forward into each square on the same leg, landing softly.
Keep your balance and a quick rhythm through the ladder.
Repeat the drill on the other leg.
tips: Land with a slightly bent knee that tracks over your toes.
Use your arms for balance.
ex_JLI56N.description: Agility Ladder Advanced Single-Leg is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Hamstrings, Core.

ex_UCSWKJ.name: Agility Ladder Advancing Laterally Switching Base
instructions: Stand side-on at the end of the agility ladder in an athletic stance.
Move sideways along the ladder, stepping in and out of each square while switching your lead foot.
Keep your hips low and your feet quick.
Continue to the end of the ladder, then repeat leading with the other side.
tips: Stay low and keep your chest up.
Keep the rhythm before trying to go faster.
ex_UCSWKJ.description: Agility Ladder Advancing Laterally Switching Base is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Adductors, Abductors.

ex_CKY462.name: Agility Ladder Lateral Movement With Double Hop
instructions: Stand side-on at the end of the agility ladder on the balls of your feet.
Hop sideways into the first square, then hop again in the same square.
Continue moving sideways with two quick hops in each square.

instructions: Stand side-on to the agility ladder, facing along it.

Step back out with the first foot as you move sideways to the next square.

Stay on the balls of your feet.
ex_GBXPYH.description: Agility Ladder Lateral Movement in in Out is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Adductors, Abductors.

instructions: Stand at the end of the agility ladder.
Skip forward, touching one foot down in each square.
Drive your opposite knee up and swing your arms with each skip.

Step into the square with one foot, then the other, lifting each knee high.

ex_5U4VE5.description: Agility Ladder in in Out Out With Knee Lift is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Glutes, Core.

ex_6KTT7Z.description: Agility Ladder in in Out Out is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Adductors, Abductors.

Perform the movement at a pace that allows you to maintain proper technique.

instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and arms bent by your sides.
Jump lightly and lift your right leg and extend it forward in a kicking motion while simultaneously swing your left arm forward.
Lower your right leg and left arm back to the starting position.

instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your hands held up in a guard position near your chest.
Punch forward with your right arm, rotating your upper torso slightly.
Return your right hand to the guard position and punch forward with your left arm, again rotating your upper torso slightly.

tips: Keep your core engaged to maintain balance and stability throughout the exercise.

Maintain a slight bend in your knees to absorb the impact and enhance stability.

ex_I6TPK7.name: Alternating Hamstring Curl With Punch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms bent at a 90-degree angle with fists close to your chest.
Curl your right leg back, bringing your heel towards your glutes while simultaneously punching forward with your left arm.
Lower your right leg and return your left arm to the starting position.
Curl your left leg back, bringing your heel towards your glutes while punching forward with your right arm. Continue alternating sides.
tips: Focus on squeezing your hamstrings and glutes as you curl your leg to enhance muscle activation.
Keep a steady rhythm to ensure both sides of your body are working evenly.
Maintain a strong and upright posture to avoid unnecessary strain on your back.

instructions: Stand tall with your back straight and feet shoulder-width apart.
Bring your forearms forward with your palms facing the floor and make a 90-degree angle with your upper arms.
Tighten your upper arms and move your hands towards each other.
As your one hand comes over the other one, return to the initial position and repeat.
tips: Engage your core to maintain stability and support your back throughout the exercise.
Keep your movements small and controlled to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Focus on maintaining an even rhythm and alternating the crossover to ensure balanced muscle engagement.
ex_D7HFT2.description: Arm Pulses Cross is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid tensing your neck and upper back.
Focus on maintaining a consistent pace and range of motion to ensure proper form.

instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder width apart, arms at your sides, and a slight bend in your elbows.
Raise your arms laterally until they reach shoulder height while rotating your shoulders so your palms face upward (supinated).
Rotate your arms at the shoulder joint so that your palms face down.

Pull yourself up until your head is facing the floor and your legs are overhead.

ex_GVM6C7.name: Ball Slams

instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a balloon in front of you.
Toss the balloon into the air and tap it lightly to keep it afloat.
As the balloon is in the air, perform a squat by bending your knees and lowering your hips until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Stand back up and tap the balloon again as it comes down, repeating the process.
tips: Start with a shallow squat if you are new to the exercise and gradually increase the depth as you become more comfortable.
Focus on keeping your back straight and your knees aligned with your toes during the squat.
Perform the movement smoothly and with control to maximize muscle activation and coordination.
ex_7PL2BH.description: Balloon Drill is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Arms.

ex_MQUJV4.name: Band Squat Row
instructions: Securely loop a resistance band around a sturdy anchor point, at the hip level. Standing with legs at shoulder width, grip the other end of the resistance band palms facing down.
Begin the exercise in a squat position, keeping your chest up and your arms fully extended in front of you.
Stand up explosively, while pulling the band with your arms toward your torso, bringing your elbows to your sides.
Lower your body to a squat position, extending your arms forward. Repeat the movement for the desired amount of repetitions.
tips: Keep your torso upright and avoid rounding your lower back or leaning forward during the movement.
Drive through the heels of your feet, focusing on your quads and glutes.
Keep your elbows tucked in when pulling the band near your torso, avoid flaring your elbows.
Exhale during the explosive part of the movement, inhale while slowly returning to the starting position.
ex_MQUJV4.description: Band Squat Row is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Shoulders, Hamstrings.

ex_XK334Z.name: Barbell Jump Shrug
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, bend at your hips and knees to grip the barbell with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Hold the barbell against your thighs.
Begin the exercise by hinging at the hips, lowering the barbell to knee level, then explosively extend your hips and knees and lightly jump off the floor, while shrugging your shoulders.
Allow the barbell to rise naturally from the momentum without pulling it with your arms.
Land softly with your knees slightly bent, absorb the impact, and reset before performing the next repetition.
tips: Keep your arms straight throughout the entire movement.
Generate power from your hips and legs rather than your shoulders.
Maintain a neutral spine, keep your chest up and brace your core before each repetition.
Exhale during the explosive jump and inhale as you reset.
ex_XK334Z.description: Barbell Jump Shrug is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the traps (back). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Forearms, Core.

ex_RTQIKS.name: Battle Rope Alternating Arm Waves
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and hold the ends of the battle ropes with a neutral grip. Lean your torso forward, bend your knees slightly and brace your core.
Raise one arm while lowering the other to create alternating waves in the ropes.
Continue alternating your arms in a smooth, controlled rhythm while keeping your torso stable.
Maintain the movement for the desired duration, then lower the ropes with control.
tips: Generate the waves with your arms while maintaining a stable body position.
Keep your shoulders down and avoid shrugging during each repetition.
Avoid rounding your back by keeping your chest up throughout the exercise.
Maintain an even rhythm to produce consistent alternating waves.
ex_RTQIKS.description: Battle Rope Alternating Arm Waves is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a rope, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Triceps, Forearms.

ex_QQLLHL.name: Battle Rope Double Arm Slams
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and hold the ends of the battle ropes with a neutral grip. Bend your knees slightly and engage your core.
Raise both arms together to bring the ropes upward, moving through the shoulder joint, while keeping your torso stable.
Forcefully slam both ropes toward the floor by driving your arms downward and slightly hinging at your hips.
Continue repeating the movement with control for the desired duration.
tips: Generate power by driving your arms down forcefully during each slam.
Allow a slight hip hinge to help produce powerful slams.
Keep a consistent rhythm while maintaining good technique.
Inhale as you raise the ropes and exhale as you slam them to the floor.
ex_QQLLHL.description: Battle Rope Double Arm Slams is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a rope, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Triceps, Biceps.

ex_ISX6US.name: Bear Crawls
instructions: Start on all fours with your hands under your shoulders, your knees under your hips, and your knees slightly off the floor.
Move one hand and the opposite foot forward at the same time while keeping your hips level.
Continue crawling forward with alternating hand and foot movements while maintaining a steady pace, until you complete the desired distance or duration.
tips: Keep your knees just above the floor throughout the exercise.
Keep your hips level and minimize side-to-side movement.
Keep your movements slow and controlled rather than rushing forward.
Maintain a neutral spine and avoid arching or rounding your back.
ex_ISX6US.description: Bear Crawls is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Triceps, Glutes.

ex_XXZHCL.name: Box Sled Push
instructions: Load the sled and grip the handles or upright posts with your arms extended.
Lean forward at about 45 degrees with your body in a straight line.
Drive the sled forward with short, powerful steps, pushing through the balls of your feet.
Keep pushing for the set distance or time.
tips: Keep your back flat and your core braced.
Short steps keep the sled moving smoothly.
ex_XXZHCL.description: Box Sled Push is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a sled machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Hamstrings, Shoulders.

ex_U64BPS.name: Burpee To Pull-Up
instructions: Stand under a pull-up bar.
Squat down, place your hands on the floor and jump your feet back into a plank, then jump them back in.
Jump up to grab the bar and pull your chin over it.
Lower yourself, drop down and go straight into the next burpee.
tips: Land softly from the jump before the pull-up.
Use a band on the bar if the pull-up is too hard.
ex_U64BPS.description: Burpee To Pull-Up is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Quadriceps, Biceps.

ex_ZVMKBG.name: Burpees
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Squat down and place your hands on the floor in front of your feet.
Jump your feet back into a plank, then jump them back in toward your hands.
Explode up into a jump, reaching your arms overhead, and land softly into the next rep.
tips: Keep your core tight in the plank so your hips don't sag.
Step back instead of jumping to make it easier.
ex_ZVMKBG.description: Burpees is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Chest, Shoulders.

ex_NXKCDS.name: Butt Kick (Slow)
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms relaxed by your sides.
Begin by jogging in place, lifting your heels towards your buttocks with each step.

Alternate lifting your right and left heels in a quick, continuous motion, keeping your knees pointing down. Swing your arms naturally with each step, allowing them to move opposite to your legs for balance.
Maintain a steady pace for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your upper body upright and avoid leaning forward to maintain proper form.
Engage your core to support balance and stability throughout the exercise.
Focus on a quick, light motion with each heel lift to effectively engage your hamstrings.
ex_NXKCDS.description: Butt Kick (Slow) is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Glutes.

ex_VITZDN.name: Butt Kick
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms relaxed by your sides.
Begin by jogging in place, lifting your heels towards your buttocks with each step.

Alternate lifting your right and left heels in a quick, continuous motion, keeping your knees pointing down. Swing your arms naturally with each step, allowing them to move opposite to your legs for balance.
Maintain a steady pace for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your upper body upright and avoid leaning forward to maintain proper form.
Engage your core to support balance and stability throughout the exercise.
Focus on a quick, light motion with each heel lift to effectively engage your hamstrings.
ex_VITZDN.description: Butt Kick is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Glutes.

ex_AY6YHV.name: Crawl With Sled Drag
instructions: Attach a light sled to a harness or belt around your waist.
Get on your hands and feet in a bear-crawl position with your knees just off the floor.
Crawl forward, moving opposite hand and foot together, dragging the sled behind you.
Continue for the set distance with your back flat.
tips: Keep your hips level and low.
Take small, controlled steps.
ex_AY6YHV.description: Crawl With Sled Drag is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a sled machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Glutes, Triceps.

ex_ELSSGN.name: Double Kettlebell Sled Push
instructions: Place two kettlebells on the sled and grip the sled handles.
Lean into the sled at about 45 degrees with your arms extended.
Drive forward with powerful steps through the balls of your feet.
Keep pushing for the set distance.
tips: Brace your core and keep your back flat.
Drive your knees forward.
ex_ELSSGN.description: Double Kettlebell Sled Push is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a sled machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Hamstrings, Shoulders.

ex_Y3TSOS.name: Dumbbell Swing
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and hold a dumbbell vertically with both hands between your legs, keeping your arms extended.
Push your hips backward and bend your knees as you swing the dumbbell between your legs while maintaining a straight back.
Drive your hips forward and straighten your legs to swing the dumbbell upward until your arms reach approximately shoulder height.
Allow the dumbbell to descend with control, hinge your hips backward as it passes between your legs, and continue for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Generate the upward movement by driving your hips forward rather than lifting primarily with your arms.
Keep your spine neutral and avoid rounding your back during the downward swing.
Control the dumbbell as it travels between your legs instead of allowing it to pull you forward.
Inhale as the dumbbell swings downward and exhale as you drive your hips forward.
ex_Y3TSOS.description: Dumbbell Swing is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Lower Back, Core.

ex_TWJGAV.name: Front Lever Raise to Hold
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, your arms straight, and your legs together.
Engage your core and raise your legs and torso together until your body is parallel to the floor.
Keep your arms and legs straight as you hold the horizontal position.
Slowly lower your body back to the hanging position, then repeat.
tips: Keep your body straight from your shoulders to your feet.
Keep your elbows fully extended throughout the movement.
Avoid swinging or using momentum.
Exhale as you raise your body and inhale as you lower it.
ex_TWJGAV.description: Front Lever Raise to Hold is an advanced single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back, Hip Flexors.

ex_W4IEHR.name: Front Lever Raise
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, your arms straight, and your legs together.
Engage your core and raise your legs and torso together while keeping your body straight.
Continue lifting past horizontal until your feet rise above the bar.
Lower your body with control until you return to the hanging position, then repeat.
tips: Keep your arms straight throughout the movement.
Keep your core engaged during the lowering phase.
Avoid swinging or using momentum.
Exhale as you raise your body and inhale as you lower it.
ex_W4IEHR.description: Front Lever Raise is an advanced single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back, Hip Flexors.

ex_DSX45O.name: Gorilla Walk
instructions: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width and squat down until you can place your hands on the floor in front of you.
Place your hands on the floor and shift your weight onto them.
Hop or step your feet forward to land outside your hands.
Repeat, moving forward in a low, gorilla-like stance.
tips: Keep your hips low and your back flat.
Land softly.
ex_DSX45O.description: Gorilla Walk is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Core, Hamstrings.

ex_DBSHJE.name: Gym Elliptical Machine Fast Speed
instructions: Step on the elliptical machine and place your feet securely on the pedals. Grip the handles with both hands for stability.
Begin moving your legs in a smooth, elliptical motion, coordinating with the handles as they move back and forth. Start at a moderate pace to get comfortable with the movement.
Gradually increase your speed to a fast pace, maintaining a smooth and controlled motion with both your legs and arms.
Continue pedaling and moving the handles at a fast pace for the desired duration.
tips: Breathe steadily and deeply to maintain oxygen flow during the exercise.
Focus on using both your legs and arms to distribute the effort evenly and prevent early fatigue.
Adjust the resistance level if needed to provide a challenging but manageable workout.
ex_DBSHJE.description: Gym Elliptical Machine Fast Speed is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with an elliptical machine, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Shoulders, Upper Back.

ex_UBCISX.name: Gym Elliptical Machine Normal Speed
instructions: Step on the elliptical machine and place your feet securely on the pedals. Grip the handles with both hands for stability.
Begin moving your legs in a smooth, elliptical motion, coordinating with the handles as they move back and forth. Start at a moderate pace to get comfortable with the movement.
Maintain a consistent, moderate speed, ensuring smooth and controlled movements with both your legs and arms.
Continue pedaling and moving the handles at a steady pace for the desired duration.
tips: Breathe steadily and deeply to maintain oxygen flow during the exercise.
Focus on using both your legs and arms to distribute the effort evenly and prevent early fatigue.
