ex_NVLF3H.name: Gym Elliptical Machine Sprint Speed
instructions: Step on the elliptical machine and place your feet securely on the pedals. Grip the handles with both hands for stability.
Begin moving your legs in a smooth, elliptical motion, coordinating with the handles as they move back and forth. Start at a moderate pace to get comfortable with the movement.
Gradually increase your speed to a sprint pace, maintaining a fast, explosive rhythm with smooth, controlled movements.
Continue pedaling and moving the handles at a sprint pace for the desired duration.
tips: Breathe steadily and deeply to maintain oxygen flow during the exercise.
Focus on using both your legs and arms to distribute the effort evenly and prevent early fatigue.
Adjust the resistance level if needed to provide a challenging but manageable workout.
ex_NVLF3H.description: Gym Elliptical Machine Sprint Speed is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with an elliptical machine, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Shoulders, Upper Back.

ex_VXJXUE.name: Gym Rowing Machine Fast Speed
instructions: Sit on the rowing machine with your feet securely strapped into the footrests, knees bent, and hands grasping the handle with an overhand grip.
Push through your legs to extend your knees and drive your body backward, keeping your arms straight until your legs are almost fully extended.
Just before your legs are fully extended, pull the handle towards your lower chest by bending your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Reverse the motion by extending your arms forward first, then bending your knees to return to the starting position. Repeat the motion at a fast pace for the desired duration.
tips: Keep your back straight and avoid rounding your spine throughout the exercise.
Use a moderate resistance level to ensure proper form and gradually increase the resistance as you get stronger.
Exhale as you pull, and inhale as you return to the starting position.
ex_VXJXUE.description: Gym Rowing Machine Fast Speed is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a rowing machine, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Shoulders, Arms.

ex_B4JBIJ.name: Gym Rowing Machine Normal Speed
instructions: Sit on the rowing machine with your feet securely strapped into the footrests, knees bent, and hands grasping the handle with an overhand grip.
Push through your legs to extend your knees and drive your body backward, keeping your arms straight until your legs are almost fully extended.
Just before your legs are fully extended, pull the handle towards your lower chest by bending your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Reverse the motion by extending your arms forward first, then bending your knees to return to starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions or time.
tips: Keep your back straight and avoid rounding your spine throughout the exercise.
Use a moderate resistance level to ensure proper form and gradually increase the resistance as you get stronger.
Exhale as you pull, and inhale as you return to the starting position.
ex_B4JBIJ.description: Gym Rowing Machine Normal Speed is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a rowing machine, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Shoulders, Arms.

ex_RFA5BE.name: Gym Rowing Machine Sprint Speed
instructions: Sit on the rowing machine with your feet securely strapped into the footrests, knees bent, and hands grasping the handle with an overhand grip.
Push through your legs to extend your knees and drive your body backward, keeping your arms straight until your legs are almost fully extended.
Just before your legs are fully extended, pull the handle towards your lower chest by bending your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Reverse the motion by extending your arms forward first, then bending your knees to return to the starting position. Repeat the motion at a sprint pace for the desired duration.
tips: Keep your back straight and avoid rounding your spine throughout the exercise.
Use a moderate resistance level to ensure proper form and gradually increase the resistance as you get stronger.
Exhale as you pull, and inhale as you return to the starting position.
ex_RFA5BE.description: Gym Rowing Machine Sprint Speed is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a rowing machine, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Shoulders, Arms.

ex_USBGNA.name: Half Burpees
instructions: Begin in a high plank position with your hands placed directly under your shoulders and your body forming a straight line from head to heels.
Quickly jump your feet forward towards your hands, landing with your heels on the floor in a squat position.
Immediately jump your feet back to return to the high plank position, keeping your body straight and your core engaged.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining a quick and controlled pace.
tips: Focus on steady breathing, exhaling as you jump your feet forward and back, and inhaling as you hold the plank position.
Ensure your hands are placed directly under your shoulders in the plank position to maintain proper form and prevent strain.
Use a non-slip surface to prevent your feet or hands from slipping during the exercise.
ex_USBGNA.description: Half Burpees is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

ex_CBWCJD.name: Hand Stand Hold
instructions: Begin in a handstand with your hands shoulder width apart, your arms straight, and your legs extended overhead.
Press firmly through your palms and shoulders to keep your body lifted.
Engage your core and glutes while keeping your body as straight as possible.
Hold the position for the desired duration.
tips: Spread your fingers wide and press through your entire palms.
Keep your elbows straight without allowing your arms to bend.
Look toward the floor between your hands without lifting your head excessively.
Inhale and exhale steadily throughout the hold.
ex_CBWCJD.description: Hand Stand Hold is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Core, Forearms.

ex_RGC4KI.name: Headstand
instructions: Place your forearms on the floor and clasp your hands behind your head, resting the crown of your head on the floor. Lift your hips and extend your legs together behind you.
Bend both knees and draw them toward your chest as you stack your hips above your shoulders.
Straighten both legs upward until your body forms a vertical line, then pause briefly.
Bend your knees, lower them toward your chest, and extend your legs behind you to return to the starting position.
tips: Press firmly through your forearms to reduce pressure on your head and neck.
Engage your core to control the raising and lowering phases.
Practise near a wall until you can maintain balance safely.
Exhale as you raise your legs and inhale as you lower them.
ex_RGC4KI.description: Headstand is an advanced multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Forearms, Hip Flexors.

ex_GMXFZS.name: Heavy Bag Sled Drag
instructions: Attach the sled to a rope or strap and hold it in both hands, or attach it to a harness.
Face away from the sled and lean slightly forward.
Walk or run forward with powerful strides, dragging the sled behind you.
Continue for the set distance.
tips: Keep your chest up and drive through your legs.
Keep tension on the rope; don't jerk it.
ex_GMXFZS.description: Heavy Bag Sled Drag is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a sled machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves, Forearms.

ex_N2W7VG.name: High Knees
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your arms at your sides.
Begin by lifting your right knee towards your chest as high as possible while simultaneously swinging your left arm forward.
Quickly switch to lift your left knee towards your chest while swinging your right arm forward, mimicking a running motion.
Continue to alternate knees rapidly, maintaining a steady rhythm and engaging your core. Repeat for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
tips: Lift your knees as high as possible while maintaining proper form and balance.
Move quickly but with control to maximize cardiovascular benefits and prevent injury.
Ensure your movements are balanced and coordinated to avoid straining your muscles.
ex_N2W7VG.description: High Knees is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

ex_BXKCRC.name: Indoor Cycling Spinbike Sprint
instructions: Set the saddle so your knee is slightly bent at the bottom of the pedal stroke.
Warm up at an easy pace.
Add moderate resistance and pedal as fast as you can for the sprint interval.
Recover at an easy cadence, then repeat the sprints.
tips: Stay seated with a stable upper body.
Keep enough resistance that you don't bounce in the saddle.
ex_BXKCRC.description: Indoor Cycling Spinbike Sprint is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a stationary bike, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Glutes, Calves.

ex_5SFXBF.name: Indoor Cycling Spinbike
instructions: Set the saddle so your knee is slightly bent at the bottom of the pedal stroke.
Hold the handlebars lightly and keep your back neutral.
Pedal at a steady cadence, adjusting the resistance to your target effort.
Keep a smooth, circular pedal stroke for the set time.
tips: Push down and pull up through the whole stroke.
Don't grip the handlebars too tightly.
ex_5SFXBF.description: Indoor Cycling Spinbike is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a stationary bike, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Glutes, Calves.

ex_FQLCRF.name: Jogging
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your arms relaxed by your sides. Engage your core and maintain an upright posture.
Begin jogging by taking short, quick steps, lifting your knees slightly higher than walking pace.
Swing your arms naturally with each step, keeping them bent at a 90-degree angle.
Maintain a steady, comfortable pace and continue jogging for the desired duration or distance.
tips: Gradually increase your jogging duration and intensity to build endurance and strength.
Breathe steadily and rhythmically to maintain oxygen flow during the jog.
Stay hydrated and take breaks if needed, especially during longer jogging sessions.
ex_FQLCRF.description: Jogging is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Hip Flexors, Core.

ex_J4PU65.name: Jump Rope Alternating Foot
instructions: Stand with your feet together, holding a jump rope with the handles in each hand. Position the rope behind you, ready to swing it over your head.
Swing the rope over your head and, as it passes under your feet, lift one foot off the floor, quickly followed by the other foot, allowing the rope to pass beneath both feet in succession.
Continue to alternate feet with each jump, lifting one foot after the other, maintaining a steady rhythm and keeping your jumps low and controlled.
Repeat the movement for the desired duration or number of repetitions, ensuring a smooth and continuous motion.
tips: Focus on quick, controlled movements, keeping your jumps low to minimize impact on your joints.
Use your wrists to swing the rope, rather than your arms, to maintain a smooth and efficient motion.
Wear supportive footwear to protect your feet and ankles during the exercise.
ex_J4PU65.description: Jump Rope Alternating Foot is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with a rope, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings.

ex_DPS7SJ.name: Jump Rope Basic Jump
instructions: Stand with your feet together, holding a jump rope with the handles in each hand. Position the rope behind you, ready to swing it over your head.
Swing the rope over your head and, as it passes under your feet, jump with both feet simultaneously, keeping your jumps low to the floor.
Land softly on your forefeet and immediately swing the rope over your head again for the next jump.
Continue jumping at a steady rhythm, maintaining a smooth and continuous motion for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on quick, controlled movements, keeping your jumps low to minimize impact on your joints.
Use your wrists to swing the rope, rather than your arms, to maintain a smooth and efficient motion.
Wear supportive footwear to protect your feet and ankles during the exercise.
ex_DPS7SJ.description: Jump Rope Basic Jump is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with a rope, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings.

ex_6Y2CJL.name: Jump Rope Double Bounce
instructions: Stand with your feet together, holding a jump rope with the handles in each hand. Position the rope behind you, ready to swing it over your head.
Swing the rope over your head and, as it passes under your feet, perform a small jump, landing on your forefeet.
Immediately perform a second smaller bounce while keeping the rope in motion and preparing for the next swing.
Continue with the double bounce rhythm, maintaining a smooth and controlled motion for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on quick, controlled movements, keeping your jumps low to minimize impact on your joints.
Use your wrists to swing the rope, rather than your arms, to maintain a smooth and efficient motion.
Wear supportive footwear to protect your feet and ankles during the exercise.
ex_6Y2CJL.description: Jump Rope Double Bounce is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with a rope, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings.

ex_QKZR5Z.name: Kettlebell Sled Drag
instructions: Place a kettlebell on the sled and attach a rope or strap to it.
Face the sled and walk backward, or face away and walk forward, holding the strap.
Drag the sled with steady, powerful steps.
Continue for the set distance with your core braced.
tips: Keep your chest up.
Walking backward targets the quadriceps more.
ex_QKZR5Z.description: Kettlebell Sled Drag is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a sled machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves, Forearms.

ex_OR2R3N.name: Kettlebell Snatch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and a kettlebell between your feet.
Hinge at your hips and grab the handle with one hand.
Swing the kettlebell back between your legs, then drive your hips forward and pull it straight up close to your body.
Punch your hand through as the bell flips onto your forearm, locking out overhead; lower it back into the next swing.
tips: Keep the bell close to avoid it slamming your forearm.
Power comes from your hips, not your arm.
ex_OR2R3N.description: Kettlebell Snatch is an advanced multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Traps, Core.

ex_EPBKIC.name: Kettlebell Turkish Get Up
instructions: Lie on your back holding a kettlebell straight above your shoulder, with the knee on the same side bent.
Roll onto your opposite forearm, then hand, keeping the bell locked out overhead.
Lift your hips, sweep your straight leg under you into a kneeling position, and stand up.
Reverse every step with control back to lying down.
tips: Keep your eyes on the kettlebell.
Learn the movement with a light weight or no weight first.
ex_EPBKIC.description: Kettlebell Turkish Get Up is an advanced multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Quadriceps, Triceps.

ex_DN4T3E.name: Kettlebell Walkover Pushup
instructions: Start in a push-up position with one hand on a kettlebell handle and the other on the floor.
Do a push-up.
Move your hands so the other hand goes onto the kettlebell, walking over it.
Do another push-up and keep alternating.
tips: Keep your body in a straight line.
Make sure the kettlebell is stable before putting weight on it.
ex_DN4T3E.description: Kettlebell Walkover Pushup is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Shoulders, Core.

ex_A36SFT.name: Kettlebell Windmill
instructions: Press a kettlebell overhead with one arm and turn your feet about 45 degrees away from that side.
Keeping your eyes on the bell, push your hips out to the side of the raised arm.
Hinge and slide your free hand down the inside of your front leg toward the floor.
Return to standing by driving your hips back under you, keeping the bell locked out.
tips: Keep your top arm vertical throughout.
Only go as low as your hamstrings allow.
ex_A36SFT.description: Kettlebell Windmill is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Glutes, Core.

ex_QXN55M.name: Landmine Alternating Lunge and Twist
instructions: Stand facing the landmine and hold the end of the bar at chest height with both hands.
Step back into a reverse lunge.
In the lunge, rotate your torso to bring the bar toward the side of your front leg.
Rotate back, stand up and repeat on the other leg.
tips: Keep your front knee over your foot.
Rotate from your torso, not your hips.
ex_QXN55M.description: Landmine Alternating Lunge and Twist is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Shoulders, Core.

ex_HRS2KT.name: Landmine Alternating Lunge to Chest Press
instructions: Stand facing the landmine and hold the end of the bar at your chest with both hands.
Step back into a reverse lunge.
As you lower, press the bar forward and up until your arms are straight.
Bring the bar back to your chest, stand up and repeat with the other leg.
tips: Keep your torso upright in the lunge.
Brace your core during the press.
ex_HRS2KT.description: Landmine Alternating Lunge to Chest Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps, Hamstrings.

ex_OUGLHJ.name: Landmine Rotational Lift to Press
instructions: Stand side-on to the landmine and hold the end of the bar beside your hip with both hands.
Squat slightly and rotate toward the bar.
Drive from your legs and rotate your torso to lift the bar across your body.
Press it overhead on the opposite side, then reverse with control.
tips: Pivot your back foot as you rotate.
Power comes from your legs and hips.
ex_OUGLHJ.description: Landmine Rotational Lift to Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Quadriceps, Triceps.

ex_RM6CHV.name: Lateral Sled Drag
instructions: Attach a rope or strap to the sled and stand side-on to it, holding the strap.
Bend your knees into a quarter squat.
Step sideways away from the sled, dragging it with each step.
Continue for the set distance, then switch to lead with the other side.
tips: Stay low and don't cross your feet.
Keep your torso upright.
ex_RM6CHV.description: Lateral Sled Drag is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a sled machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Adductors, Core.

ex_426A4N.name: Low Box Lateral Runner
instructions: Stand beside a low box or step.
Step one foot onto the box.
Quickly run sideways over the box, switching feet with each step.
Continue moving side to side for the set time.
tips: Stay on the balls of your feet.
Keep your steps quick and light.
ex_426A4N.description: Low Box Lateral Runner is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Abductors, Adductors.

ex_EDBVHK.name: Low Box Quick Feet
instructions: Stand facing a low box or step.
Tap one foot onto the box, then the other, in quick succession.
Keep alternating taps as fast as you can with control.
Continue for the set time.
tips: Stay on the balls of your feet.
Pump your arms to keep the rhythm.
ex_EDBVHK.description: Low Box Quick Feet is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Glutes.

ex_SOKBOJ.name: Low Rotational Med Ball Chops (Quarter Squat, Rotating Med Ball Left and Right Across Core)
instructions: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width in a quarter squat, holding a medicine ball at chest height.
Rotate your torso to bring the ball down to the outside of one hip.
Rotate back across your body, keeping the ball low as it rides across your core to the other hip.
Continue alternating sides in a smooth, controlled rhythm.
tips: Stay in the quarter squat throughout.
Pivot your feet slightly to protect your knees.
ex_SOKBOJ.description: Low Rotational Med Ball Chops (Quarter Squat, Rotating Med Ball Left and Right Across Core) is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a medicine ball, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abdominals, Quadriceps, Glutes.

ex_CRADXM.name: Low Sled Push
instructions: Grip the sled at the low handles, arms extended.
Lean forward so your torso is nearly parallel to the floor with a flat back.
Drive the sled forward with short, fast steps through the balls of your feet.
Keep pushing for the set distance.
tips: Keep your hips low and your back flat.
Drive your knees forward.
ex_CRADXM.description: Low Sled Push is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a sled machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Hamstrings, Shoulders.

ex_6HF4PM.name: Lying Neck Curls
instructions: Lie on your back on a bench with your head and neck past the end.
Let your head lower gently back until it is in line with the bench.
Tuck your chin and slowly curl your head up toward your chest.
Lower it back with control and repeat.
tips: Move slowly with no jerking.
Start with bodyweight only; add a towel-wrapped plate only when this is easy.
ex_6HF4PM.description: Lying Neck Curls is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the levator scapulae (neck). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category.

ex_ZCTAAK.name: Lying Neck Extension
instructions: Lie face down on a bench with your head and neck past the end.
Let your head lower gently toward the floor.
Slowly lift your head back until it is in line with your spine.
Lower it with control and repeat.
tips: Don't lift your head beyond a neutral line.
Move slowly and without weight at first.
ex_ZCTAAK.description: Lying Neck Extension is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the levator scapulae (neck). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Traps.

ex_UBH37I.name: Lying on Side Arm Circle Warm Up
instructions: Lie on your side with your knees bent and both arms extended in front of you at chest height.
Lift your top arm and draw a large circle over your head and behind you.
Let your chest open and your eyes follow your hand as the arm goes behind you.
Bring the arm back to the start and repeat, then switch sides.
tips: Keep your knees together and on the floor.
Move slowly through the full range.
ex_UBH37I.description: Lying on Side Arm Circle Warm Up is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Upper Back.

ex_7GIVZY.name: Med Ball Jumping Jacks
instructions: Stand with your feet together, holding a medicine ball at your chest.
Jump your feet out wide while pressing the ball overhead.
Jump your feet back together as you bring the ball back to your chest.
Repeat at a steady pace.
tips: Land softly on the balls of your feet.
Use a light ball.
ex_7GIVZY.description: Med Ball Jumping Jacks is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a medicine ball, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Calves, Quadriceps.

ex_PG2EHA.name: Med Ball Side Wall Slams
instructions: Stand side-on to a wall about an arm's length away, holding a medicine ball at your hip.
Rotate away from the wall to load.
Rotate explosively and throw the ball into the wall at hip to chest height.
Catch the rebound and repeat, then switch sides.
tips: Pivot your back foot so your hips drive the throw.
Use a ball made for wall throws.
ex_PG2EHA.description: Med Ball Side Wall Slams is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a medicine ball, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abdominals, Shoulders, Glutes.

ex_34TNJM.name: Med Ball Slam Burpees
instructions: Stand holding a medicine ball overhead.
Slam the ball to the floor in front of you.
Place your hands on the ball or the floor, jump your feet back into a plank, then jump them back in.
Pick up the ball, stand and lift it overhead into the next rep.
tips: Use a slam ball that doesn't bounce.
Keep your back flat when you pick up the ball.
ex_34TNJM.description: Med Ball Slam Burpees is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a medicine ball, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Abdominals, Quadriceps.

ex_RLG6PB.name: Monkey Bar Swings
instructions: Hang from the first bar of a monkey bar set with both hands.
Swing your body slightly and reach one hand forward to the next bar.
Shift your weight and swing the other hand forward to the following bar.
Continue across the bars, keeping your shoulders engaged.
tips: Use your hips to create a gentle swing.
Keep a firm grip and active shoulders.
ex_RLG6PB.description: Monkey Bar Swings is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Shoulders, Core.

ex_Z2FEQJ.name: Mountain Climber Jumps
instructions: Start in a high plank with your hands under your shoulders.
Jump one foot forward toward your hands, with the other leg extended behind.
Switch legs in mid-air so the opposite foot lands forward.
Keep switching quickly while holding your hips level.
tips: Keep your shoulders over your hands.
Don't let your hips bounce up.
ex_Z2FEQJ.description: Mountain Climber Jumps is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Quadriceps, Chest.

ex_D67YLC.name: Overhead Med Ball Throw
instructions: Stand facing a wall or open space, holding a medicine ball overhead.
Bend slightly at the knees and hips and take the ball back behind your head.
Throw the ball forward explosively with your arms and core.
Catch the rebound or retrieve the ball and repeat.
tips: Brace your core so your lower back doesn't overextend.
Release the ball at head height.
ex_D67YLC.description: Overhead Med Ball Throw is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a medicine ball, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Lats, Chest.

ex_W3NZTD.name: Pike Alternating Opposite Hip Taps
instructions: Start in a pike position, hips high, with your hands and feet on the floor.
Shift your weight onto one hand.
Reach the other hand back to tap the opposite hip or ankle.
Return the hand to the floor and alternate sides.
tips: Keep your hips high and still.
Move slowly to stay balanced.
ex_W3NZTD.description: Pike Alternating Opposite Hip Taps is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Triceps.

ex_UNHBTT.name: Pike Individual Alternating Arm Reaches
instructions: Start in a pike position, hips high, with your hands and feet on the floor.
Shift your weight onto one hand.
Reach the other arm forward in line with your head.
Return it to the floor and alternate arms.
tips: Keep your hips high and level.
Press the floor away with the supporting hand.
ex_UNHBTT.description: Pike Individual Alternating Arm Reaches is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Hamstrings.

ex_YACQOA.name: Pike Jacks Feet Kicking in and Out
instructions: Start in a pike position, hips high, with your hands and feet on the floor.
Jump your feet out wide.
Jump them back together.
Keep repeating while your hands stay planted.
tips: Keep your hips high and your arms straight.
Land softly on the balls of your feet.
ex_YACQOA.description: Pike Jacks Feet Kicking in and Out is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Core, Hamstrings, Abductors.

ex_LDGMJ3.name: Pike Shoulder Taps
instructions: Start in a pike position, hips high, with your hands and feet on the floor.
Lift one hand and tap the opposite shoulder.
Place the hand back down and tap with the other hand.
Keep alternating with your hips still.
tips: Widen your feet for more stability.
Move slowly and with control.
ex_LDGMJ3.description: Pike Shoulder Taps is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Hamstrings.

ex_HTCE5I.name: Plank Individual Arm Reach
instructions: Start in a high plank with your hands under your shoulders and feet hip-width apart.
Brace your core and lift one arm straight forward.
Hold briefly without letting your hips rotate.
Place the hand back down and switch arms.
tips: Widen your feet if you lose balance.
Keep your hips level.
ex_HTCE5I.description: Plank Individual Arm Reach is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abdominals, Obliques.

ex_UXOERA.name: Plank IYTW
instructions: Start in a high plank with your feet slightly wider than hip-width.
Lift one arm straight overhead in line with your body (I), then return it.
Lift it diagonally (Y), then out to the side (T), returning to the floor each time.
Bend the elbow and pull it back (W), then repeat the sequence with the other arm.
tips: Keep your hips steady throughout.
Squeeze your shoulder blade with each position.
ex_UXOERA.description: Plank IYTW is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Core, Shoulders.

ex_X7VZLZ.name: Plank Lunges
instructions: Begin in a plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your body forming a straight line from head to heels.
Bring your right knee forward and place your right foot outside your right hand, keeping your left leg extended straight back.
Return your right foot to the plank position.
Repeat the movement with your left knee, bringing your left foot forward to place it outside your left hand. Alternate sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Move your leg slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you bring your foot forward and inhaling as you return to the plank position.
Ensure your body stays in a straight line, avoiding sagging hips or raised buttocks.
ex_X7VZLZ.description: Plank Lunges is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Glutes.

ex_YO4PUB.name: Plank Pushup
instructions: Start in a forearm plank.
Place one hand on the floor and press up, then the other, until you are in a high plank.
Lower back to one forearm, then the other.
Alternate the leading arm each rep.
tips: Keep your hips from rocking.
Widen your feet for more stability.
ex_YO4PUB.description: Plank Pushup is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Chest.

ex_JKUBD3.name: Plate Overhead Carry
instructions: Hold a weight plate overhead with both hands, arms locked out.
Brace your core and stand tall.
Walk forward with steady, controlled steps.
Continue for the set distance or time, then lower the plate with control.
tips: Keep your ribs down; don't arch your lower back.
Keep the plate directly over your head.
ex_JKUBD3.description: Plate Overhead Carry is an intermediate multi-joint compound loaded carry exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Traps, Upper Back.

ex_XKRAK6.name: Pull Sled or Dog Sled Push
instructions: Grip the sled handles with your arms extended.
Lean forward with a flat back.
Drive the sled forward with powerful steps.
Continue for the set distance.
tips: Brace your core.
Keep your steps short and fast.
ex_XKRAK6.description: Pull Sled or Dog Sled Push is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a sled machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Hamstrings, Shoulders.

ex_2BL3WL.name: Pushup to Renegade Row
instructions: Start in a high plank holding a dumbbell in each hand on the floor.
Do a push-up.
At the top, row one dumbbell to your hip, then lower it.
Row the other dumbbell, then go into the next push-up.
tips: Widen your feet to stop your hips from rotating.
Use hex dumbbells so they don't roll.
ex_2BL3WL.description: Pushup to Renegade Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Lats, Core.

ex_WXFUR6.name: Rebounder High Knee Runs
instructions: Stand in the middle of a rebounder trampoline.
Run on the spot, driving your knees up toward hip height.
Pump your arms in rhythm with your legs.
Keep going for the set time.
tips: Stay in the centre of the mat.
Stand tall.
ex_WXFUR6.description: Rebounder High Knee Runs is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Core.

ex_K7WH6A.name: Rebounder Knee Jumps
instructions: Stand in the middle of a rebounder trampoline.
Bounce, then jump and bring both knees up toward your chest.
Land softly with bent knees.
Repeat in a steady rhythm.
tips: Use your arms to help the jump.
Land in the centre of the mat.
ex_K7WH6A.description: Rebounder Knee Jumps is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Abdominals, Glutes.

ex_AROP4W.name: Rebounder Knee Pushes
instructions: Kneel beside a rebounder and place your hands on the mat in a kneeling push-up position.
Lower your chest toward the mat.
Press up quickly using the rebound of the mat.
Repeat in a steady rhythm.
tips: Keep a straight line from head to knees.
Keep your elbows at about 45 degrees.
ex_AROP4W.description: Rebounder Knee Pushes is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Shoulders, Core.

ex_2PUO4P.name: Rebounder Light Jumps
instructions: Stand in the middle of a rebounder trampoline with your feet hip-width apart.
Bounce gently, keeping your feet close to the mat.
Keep your knees soft and your core engaged.
Continue for the set time.
tips: A good warm-up; keep it easy.
Stay in the centre of the mat.
ex_2PUO4P.description: Rebounder Light Jumps is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Core.

ex_CMENGE.name: Rebounder in & Out From Ground
instructions: Stand next to a rebounder.
Step or jump onto the mat, bounce once, and step or jump back to the ground.
Alternate the lead foot.
Continue for the set time.
tips: Make sure the rebounder is stable.
Land softly each time.
ex_CMENGE.description: Rebounder in & Out From Ground is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Core.

ex_57HOVM.name: Rebounder in & Out Jacks
instructions: Stand in the middle of a rebounder with your feet together.
Bounce your feet out wide.
Bounce them back together.
Repeat in a steady rhythm, adding arm swings if you like.
tips: Keep your knees soft.
Stay in the centre of the mat.
ex_57HOVM.description: Rebounder in & Out Jacks is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Adductors, Shoulders.

ex_5YMYN7.name: Resistance Band Pull Apart
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a loop resistance band with both hands. Your arms should be extended straight in front of you at shoulder height, and your palms should be facing down.
Pull the resistance band apart by moving your arms out to your sides, squeezing your shoulder blades together, and keeping your arms straight.
Slowly return your arms to the starting position with control, maintaining tension in the band.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your arms straight throughout the exercise, maintaining a slight bend in your elbows.
Maintain a neutral wrist position to prevent strain.
Focus on engaging your upper back and shoulder muscles throughout the movement.
ex_5YMYN7.description: Resistance Band Pull Apart is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Rotator Cuff.

ex_QYBZJL.name: Resistance Band Shoulder Adduction
instructions: Attach one end of a resistance band to a sturdy anchor point at a high height. Stand with your left side facing the anchor point, holding the other end of the band with your right hand.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart. Extend your right arm straight out to the side parallel to the floor, palm facing down.
Pull the band towards your body, bringing your right hand close to your hip, keeping your arm straight.
Slowly return your right arm to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the left side.
tips: Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and reduce injury risk.
Exhale as you pull the band across your body and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Use a resistance band that provides enough tension to challenge your muscles without compromising form.
ex_QYBZJL.description: Resistance Band Shoulder Adduction is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_P3VCKC.name: Resistance Band Standing External Rotation
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and place a loop resistance band around your wrists. Keep your elbows bent at 90 degrees and close to your sides, with your forearms parallel to the floor and pointing forward.
Rotate your shoulders outwards by pulling the resistance band apart while keeping your elbows fixed at your sides.
Slowly return your forearms to the starting position with control, maintaining tension in the band.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and reduce shoulder injury risk.
Exhale as you rotate your forearms outward and inhale as you return them to the starting position.
Keep your elbows fixed at your sides to ensure proper form.
ex_P3VCKC.description: Resistance Band Standing External Rotation is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.

ex_JZASUQ.name: Resistance Band Standing Single Arm Shoulder Extension
instructions: Attach one end of a resistance band to a sturdy anchor point at hips height. Stand facing the anchor point and hold the other end of the band in your right hand.
Extend your right arm up, pointing to the anchor point, with your palm facing down.
Pull the band backward, keeping your arm straight, and until it reaches parallel to your side.
Slowly return your arm to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the left arm.
tips: Focus on engaging your shoulder and upper back muscles throughout the movement.
Keep your elbow slightly bent to reduce strain on your joints.
Ensure the resistance band stays taut throughout the exercise.
ex_JZASUQ.description: Resistance Band Standing Single Arm Shoulder Extension is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps.

ex_U4BBXC.name: Resistance Band Standing Single Arm Shoulder Flexion
instructions: Attach one end of a resistance band to a sturdy anchor point at hips height. Stand with your back facing the anchor point and hold the other end of the band in your right hand.
Extend your right arm back, pointing to the anchor point, with your palm facing forward.
Pull the band forward, keeping your arm straight, and until it reaches your lower chest height.
Slowly return your arm to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the left arm.
tips: Focus on engaging your shoulder and upper back muscles throughout the movement.
Keep your elbow slightly bent to reduce strain on your joints.
Ensure the resistance band stays taut throughout the exercise.
ex_U4BBXC.description: Resistance Band Standing Single Arm Shoulder Flexion is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps.

ex_OSK25K.name: Ring Dips
instructions: Grip a pair of gymnastic rings and jump into a support position with your arms straight and rings turned out.
Lower your body by bending your elbows until your shoulders are slightly below your elbows.
Keep the rings close to your body.
Press back up to full extension and repeat.
tips: Rings are unstable; master bar dips first.
Keep your shoulders down and back.
ex_OSK25K.description: Ring Dips is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Core.

ex_UZALN2.name: Running
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, your arms relaxed by your sides, and your core engaged. Maintain an upright posture.
Begin running by taking quick, powerful strides, lifting your knees higher than jogging.
Swing your arms naturally with each step, keeping them bent at a 90-degree angle.
Maintain a steady, comfortable pace and continue running for the desired duration or distance.
tips: Stay hydrated and take breaks, especially during longer runs.
Breathe steadily and rhythmically to maintain oxygen flow during the run.
Focus on maintaining a relaxed posture and avoid tensing your shoulders.
ex_UZALN2.description: Running is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Hip Flexors, Core.

ex_JP255T.name: Shadow Boxing
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, one foot slightly in front of the other, and your knees slightly bent. Position your hands in front of your face in a guard position, with your elbows close to your body. Begin throwing punches in the air, alternating between jabs, crosses, hooks, and uppercuts. Use a full range of motion and rotate your hips and shoulders to generate power. Move around as you throw your punches, incorporating footwork to simulate a real boxing match. Step forward, backward, and side to side, keeping light on your feet. Continue shadow boxing for the desired duration, maintaining a steady pace and controlled movements.
tips: Focus on proper form and technique with each punch to maximize effectiveness and prevent injury.
Breathe steadily, exhaling with each punch and inhaling between movements.
Keep your hands up in the guard position to protect your face, even while moving and throwing punches.
Use your lower body to generate power, rotating your hips and pivoting on your feet with each punch.
Maintain a light and agile stance, allowing you to move quickly and fluidly.
ex_JP255T.description: Shadow Boxing is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Core.

ex_FSKLWZ.name: Shoulder Tap
instructions: Start in a high plank with your hands under your shoulders.
Lift one hand and tap the opposite shoulder.
Place it back down and tap with the other hand.
Keep alternating while your hips stay still.
tips: Widen your feet for more stability.
Squeeze your glutes.
ex_FSKLWZ.description: Shoulder Tap is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Chest.

ex_OKPG24.name: Side to Side Punch
instructions: Stand upright with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart and your knees slightly bent. Hold your fists up in front of your face in a guard position.
Rotate your torso to the left as you punch across your body with your right hand, extending your arm fully. Keep your legs and hips stationary.
Quickly return to the starting position, then rotate your torso to the right as you punch across your body with your left hand.
Continue alternating punches from side to side for the desired duration or number of repetitions, maintaining a steady rhythm and controlled movements.
tips: Focus on rotating your torso to generate power in your punches while keeping your legs and hips stationary.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you punch and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
Keep your fists up in a guard position when not punching to simulate a defensive stance.
ex_OKPG24.description: Side to Side Punch is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Core.

ex_KIBUHQ.name: Single Kettlebell Sled Push
instructions: Place a kettlebell on the sled and grip the handles.
Lean forward at about 45 degrees with your arms extended.
Drive the sled forward with short, powerful steps.
Continue for the set distance.
tips: Keep your back flat.
Push through the balls of your feet.
ex_KIBUHQ.description: Single Kettlebell Sled Push is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a sled machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Hamstrings, Shoulders.

ex_AOMLX7.name: Skater Hops
instructions: Stand on one leg with a slight bend in the knee.
Leap sideways and land softly on the other leg.
Swing the free leg behind you and touch the floor lightly, or keep it lifted.
Leap back to the other side and keep alternating.
tips: Land softly and stick each landing.
Swing your arms across your body for momentum.
ex_AOMLX7.description: Skater Hops is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Abductors, Calves, Core.

ex_73TFIL.name: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Alternating Arm Pull
instructions: Stand in front of the ski ergometer machine with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handles above you with both hands.
Begin by pulling one handle down towards your hip by extending your elbow downward.
Alternate the movement by pulling the opposite handle down towards your hip while bending the other arm upward, mimicking a skiing motion.
Continue alternating the arm pull movements at a steady pace. Repeat for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily and rhythmically to maintain oxygen flow during the exercise.
Adjust the resistance level if needed to provide a challenging but manageable workout.
Use a full range of motion with the handles to engage your upper body muscles effectively.
ex_73TFIL.description: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Alternating Arm Pull is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a skierg machine, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Middle Back, Arms, Core.

ex_7ZUDQV.name: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Basic Pull
instructions: Stand in front of the ski ergometer machine with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handles with both hands.
Begin by pulling both handles down towards your thighs simultaneously, extending your elbows while pushing your hips back, bending your knees, and leaning your torso forward.
Bring your arms back up to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Continue pulling the handles down at a consistent pace for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily and rhythmically to maintain oxygen flow during the exercise.
Focus on using both your arms and legs to distribute the effort evenly and delay fatigue.
Adjust the resistance level if needed to provide a challenging but manageable workout.
ex_7ZUDQV.description: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Basic Pull is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a skierg machine, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Middle Back, Arms, Core.

ex_UOGUF2.name: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Face Biceps Curl Pull
instructions: Stand in front of the ski ergometer machine with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handles with both hands, palms facing each other. Engage your core and maintain an upright posture.
Begin by pulling both handles towards your face in a curl motion, bending your elbows, and keeping your upper arms stationary.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement, ensuring the handles reach close to your face.
Extend your arms back to the starting position with control, maintaining a steady rhythm. Repeat the movement for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
tips: Maintain a steady pace to ensure consistent tension on the muscles.
Use a weight or resistance level that provides enough challenge without compromising form.
Keep your upper arms stationary and avoid using your shoulders to lift the handles.
ex_UOGUF2.description: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Face Biceps Curl Pull is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a skierg machine, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.

ex_AQITF7.name: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Flyes
instructions: Stand with your back facing the ski ergometer machine, feet shoulder-width apart. Hold the handles with both hands. Arms extended out to the sides at shoulder height.
Begin by pulling both handles inward towards each other in a fly motion, keeping a slight bend in your elbows and squeezing your chest muscles as your hands come together.
Pause briefly when the handles are close together in front of your chest, ensuring a strong contraction.
Slowly extend your arms back to the starting position with control, maintaining a steady rhythm. Repeat the movement for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
tips: Keep a slight bend in your elbows to reduce strain on your joints.
Maintain a steady pace to ensure consistent tension in the muscles.
Focus on engaging your chest muscles throughout the movement.
ex_AQITF7.description: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Flyes is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a skierg machine, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Core.

ex_A7WQJK.name: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Jump Squat Pull
instructions: Stand in front of the ski ergometer machine with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handles with both hands. Engage your core and maintain an upright posture.
Begin by pulling both handles down towards your hips while simultaneously lowering into a squat position, bending your knees, and pushing your hips back.
Explosively jump up from the squat position, extending your legs fully while pulling the handles back up in a controlled manner.
Land softly back into the squat position with control, immediately transitioning into the next repetition. Repeat for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
tips: Perform the movement with control, focusing on a smooth transition between the squat and jump to maximize efficiency and reduce injury risk.
Breathe steadily and rhythmically to maintain oxygen flow during the exercise.
Focus on using both your arms and legs to distribute the effort evenly and prevent fatigue.
ex_A7WQJK.description: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Jump Squat Pull is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a skierg machine, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves, Upper Back.

ex_GUCQ2A.name: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Kneeling Reverse Fly Pull
instructions: Kneel on the floor facing the ski ergometer machine, holding opposite handles with cables crossing, arms extended forward at head height. Engage your core and keep your back straight.
Begin by pulling both handles outward in a reverse fly motion, keeping a slight bend in your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together as your arms move out to your sides.
Pause for a second when your arms are fully extended to the sides and slowly return your arms to the starting position with control, maintaining a steady rhythm.
Repeat the movement for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you pull the handles outward and inhale as you return them to the starting position.
Use a resistance level that provides enough challenge without compromising form.
Focus on engaging your upper back and shoulder muscles throughout the movement.
ex_GUCQ2A.description: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Kneeling Reverse Fly Pull is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a skierg machine, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Core, Arms.

ex_VNDOHA.name: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Pullover Pull
instructions: Stand in front of the ski ergometer machine with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handles with both hands and arms straight. Slightly bend your knees, push your hips back, and lean slightly forward.
Begin by pulling both handles down and back in a pullover motion, keeping your arms straight.
Pull the handles down until they are at hip level, then slowly return your arms to the starting position with control, maintaining a steady rhythm.
Repeat the movement for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you pull the handles down and inhale as you return them to the starting position.
Use a resistance level that provides enough challenge without compromising form.
Keep your arms straight but avoid locking your elbows.
ex_VNDOHA.description: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Pullover Pull is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a skierg machine, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Core, Arms.

ex_NLNTRV.name: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Reverse Fly Pull
instructions: Stand in front of the ski ergometer machine with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding opposite handles with cables crossing. Extend your arms forward at head height.
Begin by pulling both handles outward in a reverse fly motion, keeping a slight bend in your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together as your arms move out to your sides.
Pause for a second when your arms are fully extended to the sides and slowly return your arms to the starting position with control, maintaining a steady rhythm.
Repeat the movement for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you pull the handles outward and inhale as you return them to the starting position.
Use a resistance level that provides enough challenge without compromising form.
Focus on engaging your upper back and shoulder muscles throughout the movement.
ex_NLNTRV.description: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Reverse Fly Pull is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a skierg machine, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Core, Arms.

ex_3X53PY.name: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Reverse Lunge Pull
instructions: Stand in front of the ski ergometer machine with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handles with both hands. Engage your core and maintain an upright posture.

Begin by stepping your right foot back into a reverse lunge position, lowering your body until your right knee is close to the floor and your left thigh is parallel to the floor. Simultaneously, pull both handles down towards your hips.

Pause briefly at the bottom of the lunge, then push through your left heel to return to the starting position, extending your left leg and bringing your right foot forward. Extend your arms back up in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the left leg.
tips: Keep your front knee in line with your toes to avoid unnecessary strain.
Maintain a steady pace to ensure consistent tension in the muscles.
Exhale as you pull the handles down and step back into the lunge; inhale as you return to the starting position.
ex_3X53PY.description: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Reverse Lunge Pull is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a skierg machine, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Hamstrings, Core.

ex_E63KBG.name: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Reverse Triceps Extension Pull
instructions: Stand with your back facing the ski ergometer machine, with the right foot a step forward and the other a step back for support. Hold the handles with both hands, palms facing each other, and upper arms parallel to the floor.
Begin by pulling both handles forward, extending your elbows, and engaging your triceps.
Continue pulling until your arms are fully extended in front of you, then slowly return your arms to the starting position with control, maintaining a steady rhythm.
Repeat the movement for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your upper arms stationary and elbows pointing forward to isolate the triceps.
Maintain a steady pace to ensure consistent tension in the muscles.
Exhale as you extend your arms and inhale as you return them to the starting position.
ex_E63KBG.description: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Reverse Triceps Extension Pull is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a skierg machine, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

ex_3ZWYWY.name: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Squat Pull Half Circles
instructions: Stand in front of the ski ergometer machine with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handles with both hands.

Bring the handles back in a half-circle motion in a controlled manner as you stand back up from the squat.
Repeat the movement for the desired duration or number of repetitions.

ex_3ZWYWY.description: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Squat Pull Half Circles is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a skierg machine, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves, Upper Back.

ex_FDSBVP.name: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Squat Wide Lat Pull
instructions: Stand in front of the ski ergometer machine with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handles with both hands. Engage your core and maintain an upright posture.
Begin by pulling both handles down in a wide arc motion while simultaneously lowering into a squat position, bending your knees, and pushing your hips back.

ex_FDSBVP.description: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Squat Wide Lat Pull is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a skierg machine, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves, Upper Back.

ex_37ZDI5.name: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Triceps Extension Pull
instructions: Stand in front of the ski ergometer machine with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handles with both hands, palms facing each other. Arms bent at 90 degrees with elbows pointing down.

Continue pulling until your arms are fully extended down, then slowly return your arms to the starting position with control, maintaining a steady rhythm.

ex_37ZDI5.description: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Triceps Extension Pull is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a skierg machine, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

ex_43RDG3.name: Skipping
instructions: Stand with your feet together and arms by your sides as if holding the handles of a skipping rope, one in each hand. Engage your core and maintain an upright posture.
Swing your hands in a circular motion as if turning a skipping rope, and jump lightly off the floor, keeping your knees slightly bent and landing softly on your forefeet.
Keep your jumps low and quick, simulating skipping with a rope. Repeat for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily and rhythmically to maintain oxygen flow during the exercise.
Focus on keeping your jumps low to the floor to minimize impact on your joints.
Stay relaxed and avoid tensing your shoulders and arms.
ex_43RDG3.description: Skipping is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Hip Flexors, Shoulders.

ex_R3HYT3.name: Sled Battle Rope Pull
instructions: Attach a long rope to a loaded sled and walk away to the end of the rope.
Stand in an athletic stance, or sit, facing the sled.
Pull the rope hand over hand to bring the sled toward you.
Keep pulling until the sled reaches you.

Pull with your back, not just your arms.
ex_R3HYT3.description: Sled Battle Rope Pull is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a sled machine, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Forearms, Core.

ex_244GXJ.name: Sled Drag and Row
instructions: Attach a rope or straps to the sled and face it, holding the handles.
Walk backward a few steps, dragging the sled.
Stop, hinge slightly and row the sled toward you.
Alternate between walking backward and rowing.

ex_244GXJ.description: Sled Drag and Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a sled machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Glutes, Lats.

ex_IAM3A6.name: Standing Toe Touch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, keeping your posture upright and your arms relaxed by your sides.
Simultaneously lift your right leg straight up to hip height while raising your left arm to touch your right toes.
Return your right leg and left arm to the starting position with control.
Repeat the movement on the opposite side. Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on keeping both your leg and arm straight throughout the movement.
Ensure your supporting leg remains slightly bent to maintain balance.
Keep your core tight to maintain balance and stability.
ex_IAM3A6.description: Standing Toe Touch is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Shoulders, Quadriceps.

ex_HT3VCO.name: Star Jump
instructions: Stand with your feet together and your arms by your sides, maintaining an upright posture.
Bend your knees slightly and lower into a half-squat position to prepare for the jump.
Explosively jump upwards, spreading your legs out to the sides and extending your arms overhead to form a star shape in mid-air.
Land softly with your feet together and your arms by your sides, immediately bending your knees to absorb the impact. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on using your leg muscles to generate the jump, avoiding excessive strain on your knees.
Ensure your knees are slightly bent as you land to absorb the impact and prevent injury.

ex_KAWGAP.name: Stepmill Machine Steps
instructions: Step onto the stepmill and hold the rails lightly.
Start the machine at a comfortable speed.

Increase the speed gradually.

ex_NR3PHK.name: Suspension Trainer With Grips Mountain Climber
instructions: Adjust the suspension trainer handles to about knee height. Place your feet in the handles and assume a plank position with your hands placed directly under your shoulders, arms fully extended.
Engage your core and maintain a straight line from your head to your heels.
Drive your right knee towards your chest, keeping your left leg extended. Quickly switch legs, driving your left knee towards your chest while extending your right leg back.
Continue alternating legs in a running motion for the desired number of repetitions or duration.
tips: Perform the movement with a steady and controlled tempo to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Keep your shoulders directly over your hands to maintain proper alignment.
Start with a slower pace and gradually increase your speed as your strength and coordination improve.
ex_NR3PHK.description: Suspension Trainer With Grips Mountain Climber is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a suspension trainer, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Triceps.

ex_3S6YW6.name: Suspension Trainer With Grips Pike

Keeping your legs straight, lift your hips towards the ceiling, forming an inverted V-shape with your body.
Slowly lower your hips back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Turn your shoulders and take your hitting arm back.
Step toward the ball and rotate your hips and torso to swing forward.
Follow through across your body and return to the ready position.

instructions: Stand facing a wall about an arm's length away, holding a medicine ball at your chest.
Squat down with your chest up.
Drive up explosively and throw the ball to a target high on the wall.
Catch the ball and go straight into the next squat.

Push off with your right foot, quickly bringing your left foot forward to step, swinging your right arm forward and left arm back. Increase your pace while maintaining control.
Continue this alternating pattern, maintaining a brisk and consistent stride. Repeat for the desired distance or time.

ex_L4EMF6.name: Walking

ex_FGOGOD.name: Archer Push Up
instructions: Start in a push-up position with your hands placed wider than shoulder-width apart and your body forming a straight line from head to heels.
Bend your right elbow to lower your chest towards your right hand while keeping your left arm extended straight to the side.
Push back up to the starting position.
