Push through your palms to extend your elbows and lift your body back to the starting position. Maintain the forward lean throughout the movement to keep the focus on your chest muscles.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your body remains slightly forward to maximize chest activation and minimize strain on your shoulders.
Use a weight that allows you to perform the exercise with proper form and control.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you push up and inhaling as you lower yourself.
Avoid locking your elbows at the top of the movement; maintain a slight bend to keep tension on your muscles.
ex_TKBLQ5.description: Chest Dip Weighted is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

ex_PDPHLK.name: Chest Dip With Pause Bodyweight
instructions: Begin by grasping the parallel bars with your palms facing inward and your arms fully extended to lift your body off the floor and lean slightly forward, crossing your ankles behind you for balance.
Lower your body by bending your elbows until your upper arms are parallel to the floor, keeping your chest leaning forward to engage your chest muscles.

Push through your palms to extend your elbows and lift your body back to the starting position. Pause in the upper position for a few seconds, allowing for a couple seconds of rest. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on leaning forward slightly to emphasize the chest muscles rather than the triceps.
Avoid locking your elbows at the top of the movement to maintain tension on your muscles.
Ensure your shoulders remain down and away from your ears to prevent unnecessary strain.
ex_PDPHLK.description: Chest Dip With Pause Bodyweight is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Shoulders.

ex_KZFCZJ.name: Chest Fly High to Low Resistance Band
instructions: Attach the resistance band to a low anchor point behind you. Stand facing away from the anchor point, holding a handle in each hand with your palms facing up.
Position one leg forward and the other back, with both knees slightly bent, keeping your back straight and your arms extended down and slightly behind you.
Raise the handles up and together in a wide arc, bringing them to meet at head level while keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Slowly lower your arms back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you raise the handles and inhale as you lower them back down.
Use a lighter resistance band if needed to ensure proper form and gradually increase the resistance as you get stronger.
Focus on squeezing your upper chest muscles at the top of the movement.
ex_KZFCZJ.description: Chest Fly High to Low Resistance Band is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Biceps.

ex_44IM6Q.name: Chest Fly Low to High Resistance Band
instructions: Attach the resistance band to a high anchor point behind you. Stand facing away from the anchor point, holding a handle in each hand with your palms facing forward.
Position one leg forward and the other back, with both knees slightly bent. Keep your back straight and your arms extended out to the sides at head height.
Bring the handles down and together in a wide arc, meeting in front of your lower abdomen while keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Slowly raise your arms back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you raise the handles and inhale as you lower them back down.
Use a lighter resistance band if needed to ensure proper form and gradually increase the resistance as you get stronger.
Focus on squeezing your upper chest muscles at the top of the movement.
ex_44IM6Q.description: Chest Fly Low to High Resistance Band is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Biceps.

ex_UAICXF.name: Chest Press Front Resistance Band
instructions: Attach the resistance band to a sturdy anchor point behind you at chest height. Stand facing away from the anchor point, holding a handle in each hand with your palms facing down.
Position one leg forward and the other back, with both knees slightly bent. Start with your elbows bent at 90 degrees, your hands at chest level, and your arms parallel to the floor.
Push the handles forward until your arms are fully extended, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Slowly return to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you push the handles forward and inhale as you return them to the starting position.
Maintain a neutral wrist position to prevent strain.
Focus on engaging your chest muscles throughout the movement.
ex_UAICXF.description: Chest Press Front Resistance Band is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

ex_WBLJ2H.name: Chest Press Low to High Resistance Band
instructions: Attach the resistance band to a low anchor point behind you. Stand facing away from the anchor point, holding a handle in each hand with your palms facing down.
Position one leg forward and the other back, with both knees slightly bent. Start with your elbows bent and your hands close to your chest sides.
Push the handles forward and up in a diagonal motion until your arms are fully extended.
Slowly return to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you push the handles forward and down, and inhale as you return them to the starting position.
Keep your back straight and avoid using momentum.
Focus on engaging your upper chest muscles throughout the movement.
ex_WBLJ2H.description: Chest Press Low to High Resistance Band is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

ex_NFGVTJ.name: Chest Press Machine
instructions: Sit down on the chest press machine with your feet flat on the floor and your back pressed firmly against the backrest. Grasp the handles with both hands, palms facing forward, and position your elbows at a 90-degree angle.
Push the handles forward and extend your arms fully, keeping a slight bend in your elbows to avoid locking them.
Slowly return to the starting position by bending your elbows and bringing the handles back towards your chest.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back and head flat against the backrest to maintain proper form.
Focus on engaging your chest muscles throughout the movement.
Exhale as you push the handles forward and inhale as you return to the starting position.
ex_NFGVTJ.description: Chest Press Machine is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps.

ex_WLETNN.name: Dumbbell Chest Press Decline
instructions: Lie on a decline bench with your feet securely placed under the footpads. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your arms fully extended above your chest, palms facing forward.
Lower the dumbbells slowly towards your chest by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms at a 45-degree angle to your body.
Push the dumbbells back to the starting position by straightening your arms, squeezing your chest at the top of the movement.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control throughout the exercise.
tips: Ensure your feet are securely positioned under the footpads to prevent slipping during the movement.
Maintain a steady and controlled motion, avoiding any jerking or sudden movements.
Breathe in as you lower the dumbbells and exhale as you press them back up.
ex_WLETNN.description: Dumbbell Chest Press Decline is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps.

ex_AZO3ER.name: Dumbbell Chest Pull Over
instructions: Lie crosswise on a bench, with your upper back and shoulders supported, feet firmly planted on the floor and hips slightly lowered. Hold a dumbbell with both hands above your chest, arms slightly bent.
Slowly lower the dumbbell in an arc over your head and down towards the floor, maintaining a slight bend in your elbows.
Bring the dumbbell back up to the starting position by reversing the arc motion, focusing on engaging your chest and lats.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control throughout the exercise.
tips: Keep a firm grip on the dumbbell to maintain control and prevent it from slipping.
Avoid lowering the dumbbell too far to prevent shoulder strain.
Engage your core to stabilize your body and support your lower back.
ex_AZO3ER.description: Dumbbell Chest Pull Over is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

ex_RYG26J.name: Dumbbell Decline Close Neutral Grip Press
instructions: Lie back on a decline bench with your feet firmly planted. Hold a dumbbell in each hand close together above your chest using a neutral grip.
Bend your elbows and lower the dumbbells toward your chest while keeping your palms facing each other and your elbows close to your torso.
Press both dumbbells upward together until your arms are extended directly above your chest without locking your elbows.
Slowly lower the dumbbells along the same path until they return close to your chest, then repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your elbows tucked close to your torso as you lower the weights.
Press the dumbbells directly above your chest without letting them drift toward your head.
Maintain contact between your head, back, hips, and the bench throughout the exercise.
Inhale as you lower the dumbbells and exhale as you press them upward.
ex_RYG26J.description: Dumbbell Decline Close Neutral Grip Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Forearms.

ex_MD3JHX.name: Dumbbell Fly Flat Bench Slow
instructions: Begin by lying on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor for stability. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your arms extended straight above your chest, palms facing each other.
Slowly lower the dumbbells out to your sides in a wide arc, maintaining a slight bend in your elbows. Lower until your upper arms are parallel to the floor or slightly below chest level.
Slowly bring the dumbbells back up to the starting position by squeezing your chest muscles, keeping the slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement.
tips: Avoid allowing the dumbbells to touch at the top to maintain tension in the chest muscles.
Keep your feet flat on the floor to provide stability and support.
Ensure your wrists remain straight and aligned with your forearms.
ex_MD3JHX.description: Dumbbell Fly Flat Bench Slow is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

ex_VUZKJW.name: Dumbbell Fly Flat Bench
instructions: Begin by lying on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor for stability. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your arms extended straight above your chest, palms facing each other.
Lower the dumbbells out to your sides in a wide arc, maintaining a slight bend in your elbows. Lower until your upper arms are parallel to the floor or slightly below chest level.
Bring the dumbbells back up to the starting position by squeezing your chest muscles, keeping the slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement.
tips: Avoid allowing the dumbbells to touch at the top to maintain tension in the chest muscles.
Keep your feet flat on the floor to provide stability and support.
Ensure your wrists remain straight and aligned with your forearms.
ex_VUZKJW.description: Dumbbell Fly Flat Bench is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

ex_PQEXWQ.name: Dumbbell Fly Incline Bench
instructions: Lie down on an incline bench with your feet flat on the floor. Hold a dumbbell in each hand and lie back on the bench with your arms extended straight above your chest, palms facing each other.
Slowly lower the dumbbells out to your sides in a wide arc, maintaining a slight bend in your elbows. Lower until your upper arms are parallel to the floor or slightly below chest level.
Bring the dumbbells back up to the starting position by squeezing your chest muscles, keeping the slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control and proper form throughout the exercise.
tips: Avoid allowing the dumbbells to touch at the top to maintain tension in the chest muscles.
Keep your feet flat on the floor to provide stability and support.
Ensure your wrists remain straight and aligned with your forearms.
ex_PQEXWQ.description: Dumbbell Fly Incline Bench is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

ex_Y7K3JR.name: Dumbbell Hex Press
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with your feet firmly on the floor. Hold two dumbbells together above the center of your chest with your palms facing each other and your elbows bent.
Press the dumbbells upward while squeezing them firmly together until your arms are extended.
Pause briefly at the top while keeping the dumbbells pressed together and your chest engaged.
Bend your elbows and lower the dumbbells toward your chest with control, then repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your elbows close to your torso as you lower the dumbbells.
Focus on squeezing your chest as you press the dumbbells upward.
Lower the dumbbells slowly without bouncing them against your chest.
Inhale as you lower the dumbbells and exhale as you press them upward.
ex_Y7K3JR.description: Dumbbell Hex Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Forearms.

ex_SKQLRH.name: Flat Bench Cable Fly
instructions: Position a flat bench between two cable machines with the pulleys set at the lowest position. Attach handles to the pulleys and lie down on the bench with your feet flat on the floor.
Grasp the handles with both hands, palms facing up, and extend your arms out to your sides at chest level.
Raise the handles over your chest in a wide arc, keeping a slight bend in your elbows, squeezing your chest at the top.
Slowly bring the handles back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement to avoid straining your joints.
Focus on engaging your chest muscles throughout the movement.
Inhale as you lower the handles back down and exhale as you raise them up.
ex_SKQLRH.description: Flat Bench Cable Fly is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Biceps.

ex_6CWZ4J.name: Floor Cable Resistance Band Press
instructions: Lie on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Position a resistance band under your upper back, holding a handle in each hand with your palms facing forward.
Position your elbows on the floor bent at a 90-degree angle.
Press the handles straight up towards the ceiling until your arms are fully extended, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Slowly return to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you press the handles up and inhale as you return them to the starting position.
Use a lighter resistance band if needed to ensure proper form and gradually increase the resistance as you get stronger.
Focus on engaging your chest muscles throughout the movement.
ex_6CWZ4J.description: Floor Cable Resistance Band Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps.

ex_M2R56S.name: Hammer Strength MTS Iso-Lateral Decline Press Alternating Arms

instructions: Sit on the Hammer Strength Plate-Loaded Iso-Lateral Chest Press machine, back pressed against the backrest and feet flat on the floor. Grasp the handles with both hands, palms facing down.

ex_XBHHYO.name: Medicine Ball Hold the World Chest Press
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with your feet firmly on the floor. Hold a medicine ball above the center of your chest with both hands and your elbows bent.
Press the medicine ball straight upward until your arms are extended above your chest.
Pause briefly at the top while keeping the ball steady.
Bend your elbows and lower the ball toward your chest with control, then repeat.
tips: Keep your wrists straight and aligned with your forearms.
Press the ball straight upward without moving it toward your head.
Avoid bouncing the ball against your chest.
Inhale as you lower the ball and exhale as you press it upward.
ex_XBHHYO.description: Medicine Ball Hold the World Chest Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a medicine ball, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Shoulders, Forearms.

ex_PYY7RL.name: Incline Bench Cable Fly
instructions: Set an incline bench between two cable machines with the pulleys positioned at the middle setting. Lie back on the bench with your feet flat on the floor. Grasp a handle in each hand, with your palms facing up and your arms extended to your sides.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows and your back pressed firmly against the bench.
Raise the handles opposite your chest in a wide arc, until your arms are level with your chest, squeezing your chest muscles at the top of the movement.
Lower the handles back the starting position in a controlled manner. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout the exercise to avoid straining your joints.
Keep your back and head pressed firmly against the bench.
Exhale as you bring the handles up and inhale as you lower them down.
ex_PYY7RL.description: Incline Bench Cable Fly is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Biceps.

ex_DEXBRQ.name: Kettlebell Single Arm Chest Fly
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with your feet firmly on the floor and hold a kettlebell above your chest using a neutral grip.
Keep a slight bend in your elbow and slowly lower the kettlebell out to the side in a wide arc.
Lower until you feel a comfortable stretch across your chest while keeping your shoulders supported on the bench.
Bring the kettlebell back above your chest along the same path, then repeat before switching sides.
tips: Keep your shoulders and upper back firmly against the bench.
Lower only as far as your shoulder remains comfortable.
Keep your chest up and your torso still during each repetition.
Inhale as you lower the kettlebell and exhale as you raise it.
ex_DEXBRQ.description: Kettlebell Single Arm Chest Fly is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Biceps, Forearms.

ex_AIDFR5.name: Kneeling Push-Up
instructions: Kneel on the floor and place your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Walk your hands forward until your body forms a straight line from head to knees.
Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows.
Press back up and repeat.
tips: Keep your hips in line with your body.
A good step toward full push-ups.
ex_AIDFR5.description: Kneeling Push-Up is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Front Shoulders, Core.

ex_KDXOYZ.name: Landmine Chest Press
instructions: Begin by standing with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the end of a barbell with the right hand at chest level. The other end of the barbell should be anchored securely in a landmine attachment or corner.
Press the barbell forward and slightly upward until your arm is fully extended.
Squeeze your chest muscles at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position at chest level. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back straight and avoid arching it during the press.
Exhale as you press the barbell forward and inhale as you lower it back.
Focus on using your chest muscles to press the barbell.
ex_KDXOYZ.description: Landmine Chest Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Core.

ex_R6NVNC.name: Lying Pull Over With Resistance Band Cable
instructions: Attach the middle of the resistance band to a low anchor point behind you. Lie on your back on the floor, knees bent and feet flat on the floor, holding a handle in each hand with your arms extended straight above your head, palms facing forward.
Keeping your arms straight, pull the handles over your head and towards the floor until your arms are in line with your body.
Slowly return the handles to the starting position with control, keeping your arms straight.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you pull the handles over your head and inhale as you return them to the starting position.
Maintain a slight bend in your elbows to reduce strain on your joints.
Focus on engaging your lats and chest muscles throughout the movement.
ex_R6NVNC.description: Lying Pull Over With Resistance Band Cable is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

ex_4SGUVF.name: Machine Fly

Keep a slight bend in your elbows and your arms extended out to your sides.
Bring the handles together in front of your chest by squeezing your chest muscles, keeping your elbows slightly bent.
Slowly return the handles to the starting position with control, bringing them back to your sides. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Focus on engaging your chest muscles throughout the movement.
Exhale as you bring the handles together and inhale as you return them to the starting position.
ex_4SGUVF.description: Machine Fly is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps.

ex_NTS5BI.name: One Arm Push Up

Place your other hand behind your back.
Lower your chest toward the floor, keeping your body straight.

ex_UN4AB3.name: Pec Deck Fly Machine Flies
instructions: Adjust the seat so the handles are at chest height and sit with your back flat against the pad.
Grip the handles or place your forearms on the pads, arms open to the sides.
Bring the handles together in front of your chest.
Return slowly to the open position and repeat.

Don't let the weight stack slam between reps.
ex_UN4AB3.description: Pec Deck Fly Machine Flies is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Front Shoulders.

ex_WALP43.name: Plate Deficit Pushup
instructions: Place two weight plates on the floor shoulder-width apart and put a hand on each.
Get into a push-up position.
Lower your chest below the level of your hands.
Press back up and repeat.
tips: Only go as deep as your shoulders allow.
Keep your body in a straight line.
ex_WALP43.description: Plate Deficit Pushup is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Front Shoulders, Core.

ex_AJ4CVD.name: Plate Glute Bridge to Chest Press
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent, holding a weight plate at your chest.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips into a bridge.
Holding the bridge, press the plate straight up over your chest.
Lower the plate, then lower your hips and repeat.
tips: Squeeze your glutes at the top.
Keep your ribs down while pressing.
ex_AJ4CVD.description: Plate Glute Bridge to Chest Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Triceps.

ex_FU42IN.name: Plate Press
instructions: Stand or lie down holding a weight plate at your chest, squeezing it between your palms.
Press the plate straight out in front of you while squeezing your hands together.
Pause with your arms extended.
Bring the plate back to your chest and repeat.
tips: Squeeze the plate hard the whole time.
Keep your shoulders down.
ex_FU42IN.description: Plate Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Front Shoulders, Triceps.

ex_6LWHTT.name: Push Pull Front Handle Push
instructions: Sit tall on the machine and take the front handles at chest height.
Brace your core with your back against the pad.
Press the handles forward until your arms are straight.

tips: Don't lock your elbows hard at the end.
Keep your shoulders down.
ex_6LWHTT.description: Push Pull Front Handle Push is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Front Shoulders.

ex_RSH3GT.name: Push Up and Rotation
instructions: Begin in a plank position with your hands placed shoulder-width apart and your feet together. Your body should form a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your body towards the floor by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your body. Perform a push-up.
As you push back up, shift your weight onto your left hand and rotate your torso to the right, raising your right arm towards the ceiling. Your body should form a T-shape.

Return your right hand to the floor and lower your body into another push-up. Repeat the movement, this time rotating to the left and raising your left arm towards the ceiling. Alternate sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily, exhaling as you push up and rotate, and inhaling as you lower your body.
Ensure your body forms a straight line during the push-up and rotation, avoiding any sagging or arching of the back.
Keep your feet hip-width apart to provide a stable base for the rotation.
ex_RSH3GT.description: Push Up and Rotation is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Core, Upper Back, Triceps.

ex_KK4RJV.name: Push Ups Bodyweight
instructions: Begin in a plank position with your hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your feet together. Your body should form a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your body towards the floor by bending your elbows, keeping them at a 45-degree angle to your body.
Lower your chest until it is just above the floor, maintaining a straight body line and keeping your neck neutral.
Push through your hands to raise your body back to the starting position, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your core engaged throughout the exercise to maintain a straight body line and avoid sagging your hips.
Lower yourself with control, ensuring your chest almost touches the floor while maintaining proper form.
Keep your elbows at a 45-degree angle to your body to maximize chest and triceps engagement and reduce shoulder strain.
ex_KK4RJV.description: Push Ups Bodyweight is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

ex_NTL55J.name: Resistance Band Assisted Push-Up
instructions: Secure two loop elastic bands on a straight bar, ensuring they are securely anchored. Position each band over your shoulders.
Set yourself in a plank position with your hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and your feet together. The resistance bands should provide support as you perform the push-ups.
Engage your core and lower your body towards the floor by bending your elbows, keeping them at a 45-degree angle to your body. Allow the resistance bands to assist you as you descend.
Push through your hands to raise your body back to the starting position, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure the resistance bands are securely positioned over your shoulders and anchored to the straight bar to provide consistent assistance.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you push up and inhaling as you lower yourself.
Lower yourself with control, ensuring your chest almost touches the floor while maintaining proper form.
Keep your elbows at a 45-degree angle to your body to maximize chest and triceps engagement and reduce shoulder strain.
ex_NTL55J.description: Resistance Band Assisted Push-Up is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

ex_STYEUG.name: Suspension Trainer With Grips Chest Fly
instructions: Adjust the suspension trainer handles to about waist height. Stand facing away from the anchor point with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handles with your palms facing each other.
Engage your core and lean forward, extending your arms straight to the sides to form a T-shape. Your body should be in a straight line from head to heels.
Slowly bring your hands together in front of your chest by squeezing your chest muscles, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Return to the starting position by allowing your arms to extend back to the sides with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily: exhale as you bring your hands together and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Focus on using your chest muscles to bring your hands together, avoiding excessive use of your arms.
Keep your core tight to maintain a straight body line and avoid sagging your hips.
ex_STYEUG.description: Suspension Trainer With Grips Chest Fly is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a suspension trainer, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back, Core.

ex_G67ZVN.name: Suspension Trainer With Grips Push-Up to Side Plank
instructions: Adjust the suspension trainer handles to about knee height. Place your feet in the handles and assume a push-up position with your hands placed directly under your shoulders, arms fully extended, and body in a straight line from head to heels.
Perform a push-up by bending your elbows and lowering your chest towards the floor while keeping your body straight.
Push back up to the starting position and rotate your body to the right as you reach the top, extending your right arm towards the ceiling to enter a side plank position.
Return to the push-up position and repeat the movement, rotating to the left for the side plank. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Perform the exercise on a non-slip surface to avoid slipping.
Focus on smooth transitions between the push-up and side plank for fluid motion.
Maintain even breathing to help keep your movements controlled and steady.
ex_G67ZVN.description: Suspension Trainer With Grips Push-Up to Side Plank is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a suspension trainer, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps, Upper Back.

ex_ZUBCE5.name: Suspension Trainer With Grips Reverse Push-Up
instructions: Adjust the suspension trainer handles close to the floor. Grasp the handles with an underhand grip (palms facing forward) and position your body in a straight line, feet together and arms fully extended.
Engage your core and maintain a straight line from your head to your heels.
Lower your chest towards the handles by bending your elbows, keeping your body straight and elbows close to your sides.
Press through your hands to extend your arms and return to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Perform the movement with a steady and controlled tempo to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Breathe steadily: exhale as you push up and inhale as you lower your body.
Ensure your wrists are under your shoulders to maintain proper alignment.
ex_ZUBCE5.description: Suspension Trainer With Grips Reverse Push-Up is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a suspension trainer, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Abdominals, Upper Back.

ex_GZHF7G.name: Svend Press Decline Bench
instructions: Lie on a decline bench with your feet secured under the foot pads and your back firmly against the bench. Hold a weight plate with both hands, pressing your palms against the flat sides of the plate at chest level with your fingers pointing up.
Engage your chest and press the weight plate straight out in front of you by extending your arms.
Squeeze your chest muscles as you press the plate outward until your arms are fully extended.
Slowly bring the plate back to your chest with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on pressing through your chest, not your shoulders, to emphasize chest muscle activation.
Choose a weight that challenges you but allows you to maintain proper form.
Avoid locking your elbows completely at the top of the movement to keep tension on the chest muscles.
ex_GZHF7G.description: Svend Press Decline Bench is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

ex_R5SSNI.name: Svend Press Flat Bench
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor and your back firmly against the bench. Hold a weight plate with both hands, pressing your palms against the flat sides of the plate at chest level with your fingers pointing up.
Engage your chest and press the weight plate straight out in front of you by extending your arms.
Squeeze your chest muscles as you press the plate outward until your arms are fully extended.
Slowly bring the plate back to your chest with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on pressing through your chest, not your shoulders, to emphasize chest muscle activation.
Choose a weight that challenges you but allows you to maintain proper form.
Avoid locking your elbows completely at the top of the movement to keep tension on the chest muscles.
ex_R5SSNI.description: Svend Press Flat Bench is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

ex_BL2T5F.name: Svend Press Incline Bench
instructions: Lie on an incline bench with your feet flat on the floor and your back firmly against the bench. Hold a weight plate with both hands, pressing your palms against the flat sides of the plate at chest level with your fingers pointing up.
Engage your chest and press the weight plate straight out in front of you by extending your arms.
Squeeze your chest muscles as you press the plate outward until your arms are fully extended.
Slowly bring the plate back to your chest with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on pressing through your chest, not your shoulders, to emphasize chest muscle activation.
Choose a weight that challenges you but allows you to maintain proper form.
Avoid locking your elbows completely at the top of the movement to keep tension on the chest muscles.
ex_BL2T5F.description: Svend Press Incline Bench is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

ex_ECHTKK.name: Band Wrist Curl
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor, holding the end of a resistance band, with your right hand, anchored under your right foot. Rest your forearm on your thigh with your palm facing up.
Start with your wrist extended down towards the floor, keeping your forearm stationary.
Curl your wrist upward, bringing your knuckles towards your forearm, squeezing your forearm muscles at the top of the movement.
Slowly return to the starting position, extending your wrist downwards. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your forearm stationary on your thighs to isolate the wrist movement.
Focus on squeezing your forearm muscles at the top of the movement to enhance muscle activation.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you curl your wrists and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
ex_ECHTKK.description: Band Wrist Curl is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps.

ex_MM6BWR.name: Barbell Palm Down Wrist Curl Over a Bench
instructions: Kneel in front of a flat bench, holding a barbell with both hands, palms facing down (overhand grip). Rest your forearms on the bench with your wrists hanging over the edge and allow them to hang down.
Curl your wrists upward, lifting the barbell as high as possible while keeping your forearms flat on the bench.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid using your forearms or upper arms to lift the weight; the movement should come from your wrists.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid tensing them during the exercise.
Maintain a steady pace to ensure consistent tension in the muscles.
ex_MM6BWR.description: Barbell Palm Down Wrist Curl Over a Bench is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms, Forearms.

ex_C2VCLX.name: Cable Wrist Extension
instructions: Stand sideways, facing away from a low cable pulley and hold the handle with one hand using an underhand grip. Bend your elbow to approximately 90 degrees and keep it tucked against your side with your forearm stationary.
Extend your hand at the wrist joint, moving your hand downward while keeping the rest of your arm still. Pause for 1 - 2 seconds.
Curl the weight by flexing at the wrist joint, bringing your hand upward. Pause for 1 - 2 seconds.
Slowly lower your hand back to the starting position with control and repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching sides.
tips: Keep your elbow tucked against your side throughout the exercise.
Move only at your wrist while keeping your forearm still.
Use a controlled range of motion without forcing your wrist beyond a comfortable position.
Inhale as you lower your hand and exhale as you raise it.
ex_C2VCLX.description: Cable Wrist Extension is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Core.

ex_DEOHNF.name: Kettlebell Wrist Curl
instructions: Sit with your forearm resting on your thigh or a bench, palm up, holding a kettlebell by the handle.
Let your wrist bend back and lower the bell.
Curl your wrist up as far as possible.
Lower slowly and repeat, then switch hands.
tips: Only your wrist moves.
Use a light kettlebell.
ex_DEOHNF.description: Kettlebell Wrist Curl is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category.

ex_7KK7H4.name: Kettlebell Wrist Extension
instructions: Sit with your forearm resting on your thigh or a bench, palm down, holding a kettlebell.
Let your wrist lower.
Raise the back of your hand as far as possible.
Lower slowly and repeat, then switch hands.
tips: Use a light weight.
Move only at the wrist.
ex_7KK7H4.description: Kettlebell Wrist Extension is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category.

ex_YTTI57.name: 4 Reverse Lunge and 4 Side Taps
instructions: Start with feet shoulder-width apart, arms straight in front of your torso.
Step your right foot back into a reverse lunge, bending both knees to 90 degrees. Return to the starting position by stepping your right foot forward and repeat 1 time.
Return to standing position and perform four side taps by stepping your right foot out to the side and tapping the floor, then bringing it back to the center. Repeat on the other side.
Return to starting position and repeat.
tips: Keep your core muscles engaged to maintain balance and stability during lunges and taps.
Perform each lunge and tap with control to maximize muscle activation and minimize injury risk.
Ensure your front knee stays aligned with your front foot during lunges to avoid unnecessary strain on your knee joint.
ex_YTTI57.description: 4 Reverse Lunge and 4 Side Taps is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Hip Flexors.

ex_K5D4U7.name: Alternate Single Leg Raise Plank
instructions: Start in a plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your body forming a straight line from head to heels.
Lift your right leg off the floor, extending it straight back while maintaining the plank position. Hold briefly.
Lower your right leg back to the starting position.
Lift your left leg off the floor, extending it straight back. Hold briefly before lowering it back to the starting position. Continue alternating sides.
tips: Keep your core engaged throughout the exercise to maintain stability and prevent your hips from sagging.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Maintain a straight line from head to heels, avoiding any arching or rounding of your back.
ex_K5D4U7.description: Alternate Single Leg Raise Plank is an intermediate single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Hip Flexors.

ex_CYSEZ2.name: Alternating Step Out
instructions: Stand tall with your back straight and your feet shoulder-width apart.
Bend your knees slightly and clasp your hands in front of your chest.
Lift one of your feet off the floor and step to your side.
Return to the initial position and do the same with your other foot. Repeat.
tips: Focus on keeping your upper body upright and avoid leaning too far forward or backward.
Use a steady pace to maintain a rhythm, which will help with coordination and balance.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you step out and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
ex_CYSEZ2.description: Alternating Step Out is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abductors, Adductors.

ex_RCHRXP.name: Ankle Dorsal Flexion
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your hands resting on your hips or at your sides for balance.
Flex both feet simultaneously, bringing your toes towards your shins, and then return to the starting position.
Repeat the movement, flexing and relaxing both feet simultaneously.
tips: Keep your core engaged to maintain balance and stability throughout the exercise.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Focus on the movement of your ankles and avoid using your leg muscles to assist.
ex_RCHRXP.description: Ankle Dorsal Flexion is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Calves.

ex_TSSSN4.name: Ankle Plantar Flexion
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your hands resting on your hips or at your sides for balance..
Rise onto your toes, lifting your heels off the floor.
Lower your heels back to the starting position. Repeat the movement.
tips: Keep your knees slightly bent to reduce strain on your joints and enhance stability.
Use a mirror to check your form and ensure that your ankles are aligned properly.
Focus on maintaining a steady breathing pattern, exhaling as you rise and inhaling as you lower.
ex_TSSSN4.description: Ankle Plantar Flexion is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shins.

ex_SYK7F6.name: Ankle Circles
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, hands at your hips.
Lift your right foot off the floor slightly and rotate your ankle in a circular motion, making small controlled circles.
After a set number of rotations, switch direction and rotate your ankle in the opposite direction.
Repeat the movement with your left ankle, rotating in both directions.
tips: Keep your core engaged to maintain balance and stability throughout the exercise.
Ensure your leg remains still and only your ankle is moving to focus on the targeted muscles.
Perform the exercise for an equal amount of time or repetitions in both directions to ensure balanced muscle development.
ex_SYK7F6.description: Ankle Circles is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shins.

ex_G5TMVP.name: Ankle Pumps
instructions: Sit or lie with your legs straight.
Point your toes away from you as far as you comfortably can.
Pull your toes back toward your shins.
Keep alternating in a slow, steady rhythm.
tips: Useful for circulation and ankle mobility.
Move through the full range.
ex_G5TMVP.description: Ankle Pumps is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category.

ex_2IBJIL.name: Assisted Bulgarian Split Squat
instructions: Stand facing away from an elevated box and place your right foot on it. Hold onto a stable bar or support in front of you with your right hand. Keep your chest upright and your front foot flat on the floor.
Lower your body by bending your front knee and hip until your back knee is close to the floor.
Pause for a second at the bottom and push through the heel of your front foot to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired repetitions, then switch legs and repeat.
tips: Use the support only for balance, not to pull yourself up.
Do not let your front knee travel excessively past your toes to reduce joint stress.
Maintain an upright torso to keep the tension on your quads and glutes.
ex_2IBJIL.description: Assisted Bulgarian Split Squat is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

ex_4AIO24.name: Assisted Pistol Squats
instructions: Stand upright while holding onto a sturdy equipment with both hands for balance. Extend one leg straight forward and keep it off the floor while the other leg remains on the floor.
Lower yourself slowly by bending the standing leg at the hip and knee, keeping your chest up and your extended leg straight in front of you.
Descend until your glutes are close to your heel and then push through the heel of your planted foot to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired repetitions, then switch legs and repeat.
tips: Lower yourself slowly and avoid collapsing at the bottom of the squat to avoid injury.
Extend your non-working leg fully in front of you and keep it parallel to the floor.
Use your arms only for assistance, not to pull yourself up or down.
ex_4AIO24.description: Assisted Pistol Squats is an advanced multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

ex_6H2SBR.name: Back Forward Leg Swings
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and use a nearby support (such as a squat cage, wall or a chair) for balance.
Swing your right leg forward and backward in a controlled, rhythmic manner.
After completing the desired number of swings with your right leg, switch to your left leg and repeat the movement.
Focus on smooth and controlled swings, avoiding excessive momentum.
tips: Focus on maintaining a steady rhythm to ensure controlled movements.
Ensure your upper body remains upright and avoid leaning forward or backward.
Keep your supporting leg slightly bent to enhance balance and reduce strain on your joints.
ex_6H2SBR.description: Back Forward Leg Swings is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Quadriceps.

ex_CEHKSG.name: Balance Board (Version 2)
instructions: Stand on the balance board with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Shift your weight side to side by straightening one leg while lightly bending the other.
Shift your weight to the opposite side by bending the extended leg lightly and straightening the other leg.
Continue the movement in a controlled, rhythmic manner to improve balance.
tips: Focus on a point in front of you to help maintain your balance.
Start with slow movements and gradually increase the speed as you become more comfortable.
Keep your movements controlled to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
ex_CEHKSG.description: Balance Board (Version 2) is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the balance category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Glutes.

ex_A4AXO5.name: Ball Headlock Squat
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold an exercise ball to your side with one arm wrapped around it as if in a headlock. Extend the opposite arm in front of you for balance.
Begin lowering into a squat by bending your hips and knees, keeping your chest upright and back straight.
Descend until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor and then push through your heels to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired repetitions, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep the ball securely pressed to your side to maintain upper body control and tension.
Use your extended arm for balance and avoid shifting your torso.
Do not let your knees cave inward and keep them in line with your toes.
ex_A4AXO5.description: Ball Headlock Squat is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a stability ball, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves, Abdominals.

ex_TQVMA7.name: Band Bent-Over Hip Extension
instructions: Attach one end of the resistance band low on a sturdy piece of equipment and secure the other end around your right ankle. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and lean slightly forward, holding the equipment for support with both hands.
Lift your right leg straight back until parallel to the floor, squeezing your glutes at the top of the movement.
Slowly return your leg to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the left leg.
tips: Ensure the resistance band is securely attached to the equipment and your ankle to avoid slipping.
Exhale as you lift your leg back and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Maintain a slight bend in your supporting knee to protect your knee joint and lower back.
ex_TQVMA7.description: Band Bent-Over Hip Extension is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Lower Back.

ex_MRTBWQ.name: Band Cross Abduction
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and place the resistance band under both feet, crossing the band in front of you. Hold the handles of the band in opposite hands with arms hanging in front of your hips.
Keeping your right leg straight, lift it sideways away from your body until your leg is fully extended to the side.
Slowly lower your leg back to the starting position with control, keeping tension in the band.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the left leg.
tips: Ensure the resistance band is securely placed under your feet and properly crossed to avoid slipping.
Keep your upper body stationary and avoid leaning to the side.
Perform the exercise slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement.
ex_MRTBWQ.description: Band Cross Abduction is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abductors (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Abductors, Core.

ex_CHBGKV.name: Band Deadlift
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and place the resistance band under both feet, holding one handle of the band in each hand with your arms extended straight down, palms facing your hips.
Hinge at your hips, keeping your back straight and your knees bent, lowering your torso until it is almost parallel to the floor.
Press through your heels and extend your hips and knees to stand back up straight, bringing the handles up along your legs until you are fully upright.
Repeat the exercise for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure the resistance band is securely placed under your feet to avoid slipping.
Exhale as you stand up and inhale as you lower back down.
Use a resistance band with appropriate tension to ensure you can perform the exercise with good form.
ex_CHBGKV.description: Band Deadlift is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps.

ex_NYWALV.name: Band Hip Adduction
instructions: Secure one end of the resistance band to a stable anchor and attach the other end around the ankle closest to the anchor.
Stand sideways to the anchor with your supporting leg slightly bent and your core engaged. Place your hands on hips for stability.
Sweep the banded leg inward across the front of your body while keeping your torso upright and your movement controlled.
Slowly return your leg to the starting position without letting the band pull it back, then repeat before switching sides.
tips: Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning to either side.
Maintain a slight bend in your supporting knee for better stability. Keep the working leg straight or slightly bent throughout the movement.
Control the return phase and resist the band's pull. Use a resistance level that allows a full, controlled range of motion.
Exhale as you bring your leg inward and inhale as you return.
ex_NYWALV.description: Band Hip Adduction is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the adductors (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors, Glutes, Core.

ex_ZSG5QW.name: Band Kneeling Rear Kick
instructions: Kneel on all fours, on your knees and elbows, with your hands holding the handles of the band and the band looped around your right foot.
Extend your right leg straight back, keeping your foot flexed and your leg in level with your body.
Squeeze your glutes at the top of the movement, ensuring a full contraction.
Slowly return your right leg to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you extend your leg back and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Maintain a neutral spine to avoid strain on your lower back.
Avoid rotating your hips outward; maintain square hips to the floor.
ex_ZSG5QW.description: Band Kneeling Rear Kick is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Lower Back.

ex_EQJUKN.name: Band Leg Press
instructions: Attach a resistance band at a low-mid point on sturdy equipment. Lie on your back facing the extended cable passing over your torso, and attach your right ankle to the band using a cuff.
Bend your right knee and pull it toward your chest, while the other leg stays extended and relaxed on the floor.
Press your foot forward against the resistance, straightening your leg fully without locking the knee.
Return slowly to the starting position. Repeat for the desired repetitions, switch legs, and repeat.
tips: Engage your core to stabilize your body during the motion.
Adjust your body’s distance from the anchor to maintain consistent tension.
Ensure the band or cable has tension at the start of the movement.
ex_EQJUKN.description: Band Leg Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Hamstrings, Calves.

ex_V4AVBL.name: Band Pullthrough
instructions: Stand facing away from the anchor point with your feet shoulder-width apart and the resistance band passing between your legs, held securely with both hands in front of you. Keep your knees slightly bent and your spine neutral.
Push your hips back while hinging at the hips, allowing your hands to move between your legs as the band stretches. Maintain a flat back and keep your arms extended.
Drive your hips forward by squeezing your glutes and return to a fully upright position while keeping your arms straight and the band under tension.
Pause briefly at the top with your glutes fully contracted, then repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your spine neutral and avoid rounding your back throughout the movement.
Focus on hinging at the hips rather than squatting down.
Maintain a slight bend in your knees throughout the exercise.
ex_V4AVBL.description: Band Pullthrough is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Core.

ex_XQPDK6.name: Band Single Leg Split Squat
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the ends of a resistance band anchored under your front foot. Place your back foot on a bench behind you.
Lower your body by bending your front knee until your front thigh is parallel to the floor.
Push through the heel of your front foot to return to the starting position, straightening your front leg.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs to work the other side.
tips: Maintain an upright torso throughout the exercise to avoid leaning forward.
Ensure your front knee stays in line with your toes to avoid putting stress on the knee joint.
Keep your weight evenly distributed on your front leg during the exercise.
ex_XQPDK6.description: Band Single Leg Split Squat is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves, Abdominals.

ex_KJ4LMW.name: Band Spanish Split Squat
instructions: Stand in a split stance with your left leg forward and the other leg behind you, facing sturdy equipment. Loop a resistance band around your left leg, just under the knee, and anchor it in front of you at knee level.
Hold your hands together in front of your chest and keep your torso upright.
Lower your body straight down by bending both knees until your left thigh is parallel to the floor.
Push through the heel of your left foot to return to the starting position. Repeat for the desired repetitions, switch legs, and repeat.
tips: Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning forward during the movement.
Drive through the heel of your front foot for better glute and quad engagement.
Adjust the band tension before starting to ensure proper resistance.
Inhale as you lower and exhale as you stand.
ex_KJ4LMW.description: Band Spanish Split Squat is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves, Abdominals.

ex_CZRMYZ.name: Band Standing Leg Curl
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding to a weight cage for balance. Attach a resistance band to a low anchor point and loop the other end around your right ankle. Shift your weight onto your left leg.
Curl your right leg by bending your knee, bringing your heel towards your glutes while keeping your upper leg stationary.
Slowly return to the starting position, straightening your leg and controlling the resistance band.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
tips: Focus on squeezing your hamstrings at the top of the movement to enhance muscle activation.
Maintain an upright posture throughout the exercise; avoid leaning forward or backward.
Keep your supporting knee slightly bent to maintain balance.
ex_CZRMYZ.description: Band Standing Leg Curl is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Calves.

ex_3KTKHD.name: Band Two Legs Calf Raise - (Band Under Both Legs) Version 2
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart on the resistance band, holding the ends in each hand with the band securely anchored under both feet.
Rise up onto your forefeet, lifting your heels as high as possible while keeping the tension in the band.
Slowly lower your heels back to the floor, maintaining control throughout the movement.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily, exhaling as you rise up and inhaling as you lower down.
Keep your knees slightly bent to avoid locking them out during the movement.
Focus on squeezing your calves at the top of the movement to enhance muscle activation.
ex_3KTKHD.description: Band Two Legs Calf Raise - (Band Under Both Legs) Version 2 is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shins.

ex_O3V4DQ.name: Banded Feet Elevated Hip Thrusters
instructions: Lie on your back with your arms by your sides and your heels placed on an elevated surface such as a bench or box. Wrap a resistance band just above your knees to add extra glute activation.
Bend your knees at approximately 90 degrees and keep your feet hip-width apart. Brace your core and maintain a neutral spine.
Drive through your heels and lift your hips off the ground by contracting your glutes, forming a straight line from your shoulders to your knees at the top.
Pause at the top while pushing your knees slightly outward against the band, then lower your hips back to the ground in a controlled motion. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure the resistance band stays under consistent tension throughout the movement.
Drive through your heels to maximize glute activation.
Do not let your legs cave inward; push them outward against the band.
Exhale as you lift your hips, and inhale as you lower your hips.
ex_O3V4DQ.description: Banded Feet Elevated Hip Thrusters is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Core, Quadriceps, Abductors.

ex_3DOUWM.name: Barbell Bench Lateral Step-Up
instructions: Stand beside a bench with a barbell across your upper back. Your hands should grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step laterally onto the bench with your closest foot, pushing through your heel to lift your body up onto the bench.
Bring your trailing leg up to meet the stepping leg by the bench, maintaining balance and control.
Step down off the bench with your trailing leg first, then the stepping leg. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
tips: Ensure your entire foot is placed on the bench to provide a stable base for the step-up.
Move slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you step up and inhaling as you step down.
ex_3DOUWM.description: Barbell Bench Lateral Step-Up is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

ex_MOBOCF.name: Barbell Bench Squat
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, back facing a bench, holding a barbell across your upper back. Your hands should grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Keep your chest up. Begin the squat by pushing your hips back and bending your knees, lowering your body until you sit down on the bench.
Push through your heels to stand back up to the starting position, extending your hips and knees fully. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your knees track over your toes to prevent knee injuries and ensure proper form.
Keep your chest up and back straight throughout the movement to maintain proper alignment.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you push up and inhaling as you lower down.
ex_MOBOCF.description: Barbell Bench Squat is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Lower Back.

ex_R35D4D.name: Barbell Box Squat
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, back facing a sturdy box. Position a barbell across your upper back, gripping it with both hands, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Slowly lower your body into a squat position by bending your knees and pushing your hips back, keeping your back straight.
Lower yourself until your glutes lightly touch the box or bench. Ensure your knees track over your toes and do not cave inward.
Push through your heels to stand back up to the starting position, extending your hips and knees fully. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your knees track over your toes to prevent knee injuries and ensure proper form.
Lower your body slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you push up and inhaling as you lower down.
ex_R35D4D.description: Barbell Box Squat is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Lower Back.

ex_DAJ7JU.name: Barbell Bulgarian Split Squat
instructions: Stand with your back turned to a bench, holding a barbell across your upper back. Grip the bar with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Place one foot behind you on the bench, ensuring the top of your foot is resting on the bench.
Keep your chest up, and maintain a neutral spine. Begin the squat by bending your front knee and lowering your body until your back knee nearly touches the floor.
Push through the heel of your front foot to return to the starting position, extending your hip and knee fully. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
tips: Ensure your front knee tracks over your toes to prevent knee injuries and ensure proper form.
Lower your body slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you push up and inhaling as you lower down.
ex_DAJ7JU.description: Barbell Bulgarian Split Squat is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Lower Back.

ex_YXVGJH.name: Barbell Calf Jump
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart and a barbell placed securely across your upper back. Keep your torso upright.
Bend your knees to preload tension, keeping your heels grounded.
Extend your knees and drive through your forefeet to raise your heels explosively, lifting your body upward without jumping off the ground.
Slowly lower your heels back to the floor and repeat.
tips: Focus on pushing through your forefeet to maximize calf activation.
Control the descent to avoid bouncing or slamming your heels.
Keep your knees soft and slightly bent throughout the movement.
ex_YXVGJH.description: Barbell Calf Jump is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Hamstrings, Glutes.

ex_DHQ6PH.name: Barbell Clean Grip Front Squat
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with a clean grip (palms facing up, elbows pointing forward). The barbell should rest on the front of your shoulders, and your fingers should be under the bar to support it.
Begin the squat by pushing your hips back and bending your knees, lowering your body until your thighs are parallel to the floor or slightly below.
Push through your heels to return to the starting position, extending your hips and knees fully. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your elbows stay high throughout the movement to keep the barbell in place.
Lower your body slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you push up and inhaling as you lower down.
ex_DHQ6PH.description: Barbell Clean Grip Front Squat is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Lower Back.

ex_GHBANI.name: Barbell Curtsy Lunge
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell across your upper back. Grip the bar with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step your right leg behind and across your left leg, lowering your hips until your left thigh is parallel to the floor, and your right knee nearly touches the floor in a curtsy position.

Push through your front heel to return to the starting position. Repeat on the other side by stepping your left leg behind and across your right leg. Continue alternating legs for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your front knee tracks over your toes to prevent knee injuries and ensure proper form.
Lower your body slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Keep your chest up and back straight throughout the movement to maintain proper alignment.
ex_GHBANI.description: Barbell Curtsy Lunge is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Adductors.

ex_EBS3F7.name: Barbell Feet Elevated Figure Four Glute Bridge
instructions: Lie on your back with your arms to the floor. Place one foot on a box and cross the opposite ankle over your working leg, forming a figure-four shape. Position the barbell evenly across your hips, holding it securely with both hands.
Push through your elevated heel to lift your hips upward until your torso forms a straight line from shoulders to knee.
At the peak of the movement, squeeze your glutes. Slowly lower your hips down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired repetitions, and then switch legs and repeat.
tips: Ensure the barbell is comfortably cushioned or padded to prevent pressure on your hips.
Engage your core to prevent arching your back or overextending.
Exhale as you thrust up, and inhale as you return to the starting position.
ex_EBS3F7.description: Barbell Feet Elevated Figure Four Glute Bridge is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Lower Back, Core.

ex_2CHRSL.name: Barbell Feet Elevated Glute Bridge
instructions: Lie on your back with your feet placed on an elevated surface, knees bent. Rest a barbell across your hips, gripping it securely with both hands for stability.
Push through your elevated heels to lift your hips upward until your torso forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
At the peak of the movement, squeeze your glutes. Slowly lower your hips down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you lift your hips and inhale as you lower them.
Ensure your knees remain aligned with your feet; don’t let them collapse inward or flare outward.
Avoid excessive momentum; focus on a controlled, glute-driven motion.
ex_2CHRSL.description: Barbell Feet Elevated Glute Bridge is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Lower Back, Core.

ex_OMH367.name: Barbell Feet Elevated Single Leg Glute Bridge
instructions: Lie on your back with your arms to the floor. Place one foot on a box while the opposite leg is extended straight up. Position the barbell evenly across your hips, holding it securely with both hands.
Push through your elevated heel to lift your hips upward until your torso forms a straight line from shoulders to knee.
At the peak of the movement, squeeze your glutes. Slowly lower your hips down to the starting position.

ex_OMH367.description: Barbell Feet Elevated Single Leg Glute Bridge is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Lower Back, Core.

instructions: Lie on your back with your feet elevated on a box. Place one foot slightly forward and the other slightly backward (staggered stance). Rest a barbell across your hips, gripping it securely with both hands for stability.
Push through your elevated heels to lift your hips upward until your torso forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.

Begin the squat by pushing your hips back and bending your knees, lowering your body until you sit down on the bench.
Push through your heels to stand back up to the starting position, extending your hips and knees fully. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Engage your core to support your lower back and maintain proper posture.
Lower your body slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
ex_OEKPIP.description: Barbell Front Bench Squat is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Lower Back.

instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and position a barbell on the front of your shoulders. Cross your arms over the barbell, with your elbows pointing forward and your upper arms parallel to the floor, holding the barbell tightly.
Lower your body into a squat position by bending your knees and pushing your hips back, keeping your weight on your heels.
Continue lowering until your thighs are parallel to the floor and then push through your heels to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you stand up from the squat and inhale as you lower into the squat.
Keep your chest up and avoid leaning forward excessively.
Focus on engaging your quadriceps and glutes throughout the movement.
ex_GW4TSM.description: Barbell Front Squat is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves, Core.

ex_YTCHLK.name: Barbell Full Zercher Squat
instructions: Position a barbell in a squat rack at about waist height. Stand close to the barbell and hook your arms under it, holding the bar in the crook of your elbows with your hands close in front of your chest.
Lift the barbell off the rack by standing up straight. Step back and stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly pointed out.
Maintain a neutral spine as you begin the squat by pushing your hips back and bending your knees, lowering your body until your thighs are parallel to the floor or slightly below.
Push through your heels to return to the starting position, extending your hips and knees until you are fully upright. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Move slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you push up and inhaling as you lower down.
