ex_F2GVIK.name: Barbell Glute Bridge (Hands on Bar)
instructions: Lie on your back on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, shoulder-width apart. Place a barbell across your hips, holding it securely with both hands.
Push through your heels to lift your hips off the floor until your body forms a straight line from your shoulders to your knees.
Squeeze your glutes at the top of the movement and hold for a brief moment.
Lower your hips back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Drive through your heels to engage your glutes and hamstrings effectively.
Ensure your knees stay in line with your toes and do not flare out or cave inward.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you lift your hips and inhaling as you lower them back down.
Use a pad or towel on the barbell for added comfort on your hips.
ex_F2GVIK.description: Barbell Glute Bridge (Hands on Bar) is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Lower Back.

ex_XQV2D2.name: Barbell Hip Thrust
instructions: Sit on the floor with your upper back resting against a bench, knees bent, and feet flat on the floor. Roll a barbell over your hips, holding it securely with both hands.
Push through your heels to lift your hips off the floor until your body forms a straight line from your shoulders to your knees.
Squeeze your glutes at the top of the movement and hold for a brief moment, ensuring your hips are fully extended.
Lower your hips back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

ex_CAFYDH.name: Barbell Jefferson Squat
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, positioning yourself so that the barbell is between your legs. Grip the barbell with one hand in front of you and one hand behind you, using an overhand grip for the front hand and an underhand grip for the back hand.
Begin the squat by pushing your hips back and bending your knees, lowering your body until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Push through your heels to return to the starting position, extending your hips and knees fully. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on even weight distribution between both legs to ensure balanced muscle activation.

Keep your grip firm but relaxed to prevent unnecessary tension in your arms and shoulders.
ex_CAFYDH.description: Barbell Jefferson Squat is an advanced multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Lower Back.

ex_BCIL7D.name: Barbell Jump Squat
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell across your upper back. Grip the bar with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Begin the squat by pushing your hips back and bending your knees, lowering your body until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Explosively push through your heels to jump straight up, extending your hips and knees fully to jump.
Land softly on your forefeet, immediately bending your knees and hips to absorb the impact and lower back into the squat position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure the barbell remains steady on your back to prevent it from shifting during the exercise.

Squeeze your glutes at the top of the movement and hold for a brief moment, ensuring your hips are fully extended.

ex_VGH3FO.description: Dumbbell Single Leg Hip Thrust is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Core, Obliques.

ex_HXRX62.name: Dumbbell Single Leg Single Arm Deadlift
instructions: Stand upright with your feet together and hold a dumbbell by your side using a neutral grip. Shift your weight onto the leg opposite the dumbbell and slightly bend your supporting knee.
Lift the leg on the dumbbell side behind you with your knee bent as you push your hips back and hinge your torso forward.
Lower the dumbbell toward the floor beside your supporting leg until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor, keeping your back straight and your hips level.
Press through your supporting foot and drive your hips forward to return upright, then repeat before switching sides.
tips: Lower the dumbbell close to your supporting leg instead of reaching it forward.
Keep your supporting knee aligned with your toes and balance over the middle of your foot.
Keep your hips level and avoid rotating your torso toward either side.
Inhale as you hinge forward and exhale as you return to standing.
ex_HXRX62.description: Dumbbell Single Leg Single Arm Deadlift is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Core, Obliques, Lower Back.

ex_NEA3MY.name: Dumbbell Staggered Deadlift
instructions: Stand with one foot fully planted and place the opposite foot a short step behind, resting on the ball of the foot with the heel raised. Hold a dumbbell in each hand using an overhand grip.
Shift most of your weight onto the front leg, slightly bend both knees, and push your hips backward as you hinge your torso forward.
Lower the dumbbells in front of your shins while keeping your back straight and the weights close to your legs.
Press through your front foot and drive your hips forward to return upright, then complete the repetitions before switching your stance.
tips: Keep most of your body weight on the front leg and use the rear foot mainly for balance.
Push your hips backward rather than lowering into a squat.
Stop lowering when you feel a controlled stretch without rounding your back.
Inhale as you hinge forward and exhale as you return to standing.
ex_NEA3MY.description: Dumbbell Staggered Deadlift is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Lower Back, Core.

ex_4NGYTH.name: Dumbbell Staggered Glute Bridge
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and hold a dumbbell securely across your hips. Plant one foot close to your hips and place the opposite heel slightly farther forward with the toes raised.
Press primarily through the foot closest to your hips while using the forward heel lightly for balance.
Lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from your shoulders to your knees, keeping your hips level.
Pause and squeeze your glutes, then lower your hips with control and complete the repetitions before switching to the other side.
tips: Keep the foot closest to your hips firmly planted throughout the movement.
Use the forward heel mainly for balance rather than pushing equally through both legs.
Drive through the heel and middle of your working foot rather than your toes.
Inhale as you lower your hips and exhale as you lift them.
ex_4NGYTH.description: Dumbbell Staggered Glute Bridge is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Core, Lower Back.

ex_WGMISM.name: Dumbbell Staggered Hip Thrust
instructions: Sit with your upper back against the edge of a flat bench and hold a dumbbell securely across your hips. Plant one foot close to your hips and place the opposite heel slightly farther forward with the toes raised.
Press primarily through the foot closest to your hips and lift your hips toward the ceiling while using the forward heel lightly for balance.
Continue lifting until your torso and working thigh form a straight line, keeping your hips level and squeezing your glutes at the top.
Lower your hips with control, then repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching to the other side.
tips: Place most of your weight through the foot closest to your hips.
Use the farther heel mainly for balance rather than driving equally through both legs.
Stop at full hip extension without arching your lower back.
Inhale as you lower your hips and exhale as you press them upward.
ex_WGMISM.description: Dumbbell Staggered Hip Thrust is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Core, Calves.

ex_SMGP4S.name: Dumbbell Standing Hip Abduction
instructions: Stand upright with your feet together and hold a dumbbell against the outside of one thigh with the same-side hand.
Shift your weight onto the opposite leg, engage your core, and keep your supporting knee slightly bent.
Keep your working leg straight and lift it out and upward to the side while maintaining an upright torso and keeping your toes facing forward.
Pause briefly at the top, then lower your leg with control and repeat before switching sides.
tips: Keep your supporting foot firmly planted and distribute your weight across the entire foot.
Keep your hips level and avoid leaning away from the working leg.
Avoid swinging your leg or using momentum to raise the dumbbell.
Exhale as you lift your leg and inhale as you lower it.
ex_SMGP4S.description: Dumbbell Standing Hip Abduction is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Core, Obliques.

ex_LVCRYC.name: Frog Jumps
instructions: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder width apart and your toes turned slightly outward. Lower into a deep squat and reach both hands toward the floor between your feet.
Push through your feet and jump straight upward, extending your hips and knees.
Land softly in the same wide stance and immediately bend your knees.
Lower back into the squat, reach toward the floor, and continue repeating the movement.
tips: Keep your chest lifted and avoid rounding your lower back in the squat.
Bend your knees immediately upon landing to absorb the impact.
Fully extend your hips and knees at the top of each jump.
Inhale as you lower and exhale as you jump upward.
ex_LVCRYC.description: Frog Jumps is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Core, Adductors.

ex_ZJL2FE.name: Glute Bridge Bodyweight
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent, feet flat and hip-width apart.
Brace your core and press through your heels.
Lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower and repeat.
tips: Don't arch your lower back at the top.
Keep your knees in line with your feet.
ex_ZJL2FE.description: Glute Bridge Bodyweight is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Core.

ex_TVO5OD.name: Glute Bridge With Abduction Bodyweight
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart. Place your arms at your sides with palms facing down.
Engage your core and glutes and lift your hips towards the ceiling until your body forms a straight line from your shoulders to your knees.
While holding the bridge position, spread your knees apart as far as comfortable, keeping your feet flat on the floor.
Bring your knees back together, then lower your hips back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your hips remain lifted and in line with your body during the abduction movement.
Avoid letting your knees collapse inward; maintain control during the abduction movement.
Focus on steady breathing, exhaling as you lift your hips and spread your knees, and inhaling as you lower your hips.
ex_TVO5OD.description: Glute Bridge With Abduction Bodyweight is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings.

ex_DSL5SI.name: Good Mornings
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart, bend your knees slightly, and place your hands beside your head with your elbows pointing outward.
Push your hips back and hinge your torso forward while keeping your back straight.
Lower your torso until it is nearly parallel to the floor or until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
Drive your hips forward to return upright, then repeat.
tips: Keep your weight balanced over your heels and midfoot.
Lower only as far as you can without rounding your back.
Push your hips backward instead of lowering into a squat.
Inhale as you hinge forward and exhale as you stand upright.
ex_DSL5SI.description: Good Mornings is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Core.

ex_IU2JKY.name: Hack Squat Machine
instructions: Position yourself on the hack squat machine with your shoulders under the pads and your feet shoulder-width apart on the foot platform. Keep your back pressed against the backrest.
Release the safety handles and slowly lower your body by bending your knees until your thighs are parallel to the foot platform.
Push through your heels to extend your legs and return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back pressed against the backrest throughout the exercise.
Focus on keeping your knees aligned with your toes to avoid straining your joints.
Exhale as you push up and inhale as you lower your body.
ex_IU2JKY.description: Hack Squat Machine is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Hamstrings.

ex_TDV2L4.name: Hammer Strength Iso-Lateral Leg Curl Alternating Legs
instructions: Lie face down on the Hammer Strength Iso-Lateral Leg Curl machine, placing your ankles under the leg pads and holding the handles on the sides of the machine for stability. Start with both legs fully extended.
Curl one leg by bending your knee and pulling your ankle towards your glutes, keeping the other leg extended.
Squeeze your hamstrings at the top of the movement and slowly lower your leg back to the starting position with control.
Repeat with the other leg, alternating legs for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your hips pressed against the bench throughout the exercise.
Focus on engaging your hamstrings throughout the movement.
Exhale as you curl your leg and inhale as you lower it back down.
ex_TDV2L4.description: Hammer Strength Iso-Lateral Leg Curl Alternating Legs is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes.

ex_EGEHFT.name: Hammer Strength Iso-Lateral Leg Curl Single Leg
instructions: Lie face down on the Hammer Strength Iso-Lateral Leg Curl machine, placing your ankles under the leg pads and holding the handles on the sides of the machine for stability. Start with both legs fully extended.
Curl your right leg by bending your knee and pulling your ankle towards your glutes, keeping the other leg extended.
Squeeze your hamstring at the top of the movement and slowly lower your leg back to the starting position with control.
Repeat with the same leg for the desired number of repetitions and then switch to your left leg and repeat.
tips: Keep your hips pressed against the bench throughout the exercise.
Focus on engaging your hamstrings throughout the movement.
Exhale as you curl your leg and inhale as you lower it back down.
ex_EGEHFT.description: Hammer Strength Iso-Lateral Leg Curl Single Leg is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes.

ex_OOBHE5.name: Hammer Strength Iso-Lateral Leg Curl Both Legs
instructions: Lie face down on the Hammer Strength Iso-Lateral Leg Curl machine, placing your ankles under the leg pads and holding the handles on the sides of the machine for stability. Start with both legs fully extended.
Curl both legs by bending your knees and pulling your ankles towards your glutes.
Squeeze your hamstrings at the top of the movement and slowly lower your legs back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your hips pressed against the bench throughout the exercise.
Focus on engaging your hamstrings throughout the movement.
Exhale as you curl your leg and inhale as you lower it back down.
ex_OOBHE5.description: Hammer Strength Iso-Lateral Leg Curl Both Legs is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes.

ex_FCYU6R.name: Hip-Thrust in Smith Machine
instructions: Sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench and the Smith bar over your hips, with a pad.
Plant your feet flat and hip-width apart.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Squeeze your glutes, then lower and repeat.
tips: Tuck your chin and keep your ribs down.
Use a bar pad for comfort.
ex_FCYU6R.description: Hip-Thrust in Smith Machine is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a smith machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Quadriceps.

ex_2IVYK4.name: Horizontal Leg Press Calf Raise Single Leg
instructions: Sit on the leg press and place the ball of one foot on the bottom edge of the platform.
Extend the leg with a soft knee bend.
Push the platform away by pointing your toes.
Lower with control and repeat, then switch legs.
tips: Use a lighter weight than with two legs.
Pause at the top.
ex_2IVYK4.description: Horizontal Leg Press Calf Raise Single Leg is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category.

ex_ICLBXV.name: Horizontal Leg Press Calf Raise
instructions: Sit on the leg press and place the balls of your feet on the bottom edge of the platform.
Extend your legs with a soft knee bend.
Push the platform away by pointing your toes.
Let your heels come back for a stretch and repeat.
tips: Keep your knees still.
Use a full range of motion.
ex_ICLBXV.description: Horizontal Leg Press Calf Raise is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category.

ex_6NQ752.name: Horizontal Leg Press Single Leg
instructions: Sit on the leg press and place one foot in the centre of the platform.
Bend the knee to bring the weight toward you.
Lower until your knee is at about 90 degrees.
Press back out without locking the knee, then switch legs.
tips: Keep your knee in line with your toes.
Use a light weight to begin.
ex_6NQ752.description: Horizontal Leg Press Single Leg is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Hamstrings.

ex_X6C7GQ.name: Horizontal Leg Press
instructions: Sit on the machine with your back against the pad and your feet hip-width apart on the platform.
Release the safety and bend your knees to bring the weight toward you.
Lower until your knees are about 90 degrees.
Press through your feet to extend your legs without locking them, and repeat.
tips: Keep your lower back on the pad.
Keep your knees in line with your toes.
ex_X6C7GQ.description: Horizontal Leg Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Hamstrings.

ex_KAIT2V.name: In and Out Squats
instructions: Stand tall with your back straight, feet shoulder-width apart, and clasp your hands in front of your chest.
Lower your hips, jump up and land into a squat position with your knees bent, thighs parallel to the floor, and feet placed wider than your shoulder width.
Then lower your hips again, jump up, and land into a squat position with your knees bent, thighs parallel to the floor, and feet placed hip-width apart this time.
Repeat by jumping in and out alternately.
tips: Land softly on your forefeet to reduce impact on your joints.
Ensure your knees are aligned with your toes when you squat to avoid strain.
Move quickly but with control to maximize the effectiveness of the exercise and prevent injury.
ex_KAIT2V.description: In and Out Squats is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

ex_6ANGQE.name: Jumping Lunge
instructions: Stand in a split stance with one foot forward and clasp your hands in front of your chest.
Bend both knees and lower into a lunge until your back knee is just above the floor.
Jump straight upward, switch your legs in the air, and land with the opposite foot forward.
Lower into the next lunge and continue alternating sides.
tips: Keep your torso upright throughout the movement.
Lower your back knee toward the floor without touching it.
Land softly and bend both knees to absorb the impact.
Exhale as you jump and inhale as you lower into the lunge.
ex_6ANGQE.description: Jumping Lunge is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves, Core.

ex_UXYEM5.name: Jumping Pistol Squat
instructions: Stand on one leg with your hands on your hips and extend your opposite leg slightly forward.
Bend your supporting knee and lower into a single-leg squat while keeping your opposite leg extended in front of you.
Push forcefully through your supporting foot and jump straight upward.
Land softly on the same leg, lower into the next squat, and repeat for the desired number of repetitions then switch sides.
tips: Keep your extended leg off the floor throughout the movement.
Land softly and bend your knee to absorb the impact.
Maintain an upright chest as you lower.
Inhale as you lower and exhale as you jump.
ex_UXYEM5.description: Jumping Pistol Squat is an advanced multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Hip Flexors, Core.

ex_OUMB72.name: Kettlebell Calf Raise
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and hold a kettlebell in each hand by your sides.
Press through the balls of your feet and raise both heels as high as you can.
Pause briefly at the top while keeping your legs straight and your body upright.
Lower your heels to the floor with control, then repeat.
tips: Keep your knees straight without locking them.
Raise your heels without leaning forward.
Lower your heels slowly through the full range of motion.
Exhale as you rise and inhale as you lower.
ex_OUMB72.description: Kettlebell Calf Raise is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

ex_JXK75M.name: Kettlebell Glute Bridge

Press through your feet and lift your hips toward the ceiling.
Continue lifting until your body forms a straight line from your shoulders to your knees, holding at the top.
Lower your hips back to the floor with control, then repeat.

Squeeze your glutes at the top without arching your lower back.

ex_JXK75M.description: Kettlebell Glute Bridge is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Adductors, Core.

ex_JALHXC.name: Kettlebell Hip Thrust With Bench
instructions: Sit on the floor with your upper back resting against the edge of a bench, your knees bent, and your feet flat on the floor. Hold a kettlebell securely across your hips with both hands.
Press through your feet and lift your hips upward while keeping your upper back supported on the bench.
Continue lifting until your torso and thighs form a straight line, then squeeze your glutes at the top.
Lower your hips with control to the starting position, then repeat.

Fully extend your hips without arching your lower back.

ex_JALHXC.description: Kettlebell Hip Thrust With Bench is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Core.

ex_ELNYMU.name: Kettlebell Hip Thrust
instructions: Sit on the floor with your upper back resting against the edge of a bench, your knees bent, and your feet flat on the floor. Hold a kettlebell securely across your hips with both hands.
Press through your feet and lift your hips upward while keeping your upper back supported on the bench.
Continue lifting until your torso and thighs form a straight line, then squeeze your glutes at the top.
Lower your hips with control to the starting position, then repeat.
tips: Keep your upper back firmly supported on the bench throughout the movement.
Press through your heels and midfoot as you lift.
Fully extend your hips without arching your lower back.
Exhale as you lift your hips and inhale as you lower them.
ex_ELNYMU.description: Kettlebell Hip Thrust is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Core.

ex_U3LVBQ.name: Kettlebell Lateral Lunge
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width apart. Hold a kettlebell in each hand with an overhand grip in front of your thighs.
Step one foot out to the side, bend that knee, and push your hips back while keeping your opposite leg straight.
Lean your torso slightly forward and lower the kettlebells toward the floor between your legs.
Push through your bent leg to return to the starting position, then repeat.

Keep your back straight as your torso leans forward.
Keep the knee of your bent leg aligned with your toes.
Inhale as you lower and exhale as you return to standing.
ex_U3LVBQ.description: Kettlebell Lateral Lunge is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Core, Forearms.

ex_3DDDLD.name: Kettlebell Reverse Lunge
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder width apart and hold a kettlebell in each hand by your sides using a neutral grip.
Step one foot backward and lower your back knee toward the floor while bending your front knee.
Push through your front foot to rise and bring your back foot forward to the starting position.

ex_3DDDLD.description: Kettlebell Reverse Lunge is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Core, Forearms.

ex_CERI66.name: Kettlebell Seated Calf Raise
instructions: Sit upright on a bench with your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor. Rest a kettlebell on your thighs just above your knees and hold it securely with both hands.
Keep the balls of your feet on the floor and raise both heels as high as you can.
Pause briefly at the top and squeeze your calves.
Lower your heels back to the floor with control, then repeat.

Avoid bouncing at the bottom of the movement.
Lower your heels slowly through the full range of motion.

ex_CERI66.description: Kettlebell Seated Calf Raise is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category.

ex_CWPUEI.name: Kettlebell Single Leg Calf Raise
instructions: Stand on your left leg and hold a kettlebell in your left hand using a neutral grip. Bend your right knee and keep your right foot raised behind you.

Lower your left heel to the floor with control, then repeat before switching sides.

Keep your raised foot off the floor throughout the movement.

Exhale as you raise your heel and inhale as you lower it.
ex_CWPUEI.description: Kettlebell Single Leg Calf Raise is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms, Core.

ex_JFZ6G7.name: Kettlebell Single Leg Deadlift
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder width apart and hold a kettlebell in your left hand using an overhand grip. Keep a slight bend in your right knee and lift your left foot slightly off the floor.
Shift your weight toward the right leg, push your hips back and lean your torso forward as you extend your left leg straight behind you.
Lower the kettlebell toward the floor beside your right leg while keeping your back straight and your hips level.
Press through your right foot and bring your hips forward to return upright, then repeat before switching sides.

ex_JFZ6G7.description: Kettlebell Single Leg Deadlift is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Core, Forearms.

ex_2OCXJK.name: Kettlebell Single Leg Glute Bridge

Press through the heel of the planted foot to lift your hips.

ex_4VKHE7.name: Kettlebell Single Leg Hip Thrust

Drive through the planted heel to lift your hips until your thigh is parallel to the floor.

Hold the bell steady with both hands.
ex_4VKHE7.description: Kettlebell Single Leg Hip Thrust is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Quadriceps.

ex_H2KHCW.name: Kettlebell Single Leg Romanian Deadlifts

Hinge at your hips and extend your free leg straight behind you.
Lower the bell toward the floor with a flat back.

tips: Keep your hips square to the floor.
Keep a slight bend in the standing knee.
ex_H2KHCW.description: Kettlebell Single Leg Romanian Deadlifts is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Core.

ex_TCEYOQ.name: Kettlebell Staggered Deadlift
instructions: Stand with one foot slightly behind the other and hold a kettlebell in front of you.
Keep most of your weight on the front leg.
Hinge at your hips to lower the bell toward the floor with a flat back.
Drive your hips forward to stand, then switch the front leg.

ex_TCEYOQ.description: Kettlebell Staggered Deadlift is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back.

ex_WIG5CY.name: Kettlebell Step Up
instructions: Stand facing a bench, holding a kettlebell in each hand with your arms hanging at your sides.
Step up onto the bench with your right foot, pressing through your heel to lift your body up. Bring your left foot up to meet your right foot on the bench.
Step down with your left foot first, followed by your right foot, returning to the starting position.

ex_WIG5CY.description: Kettlebell Step Up is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

ex_3I54KF.name: Landmine Calf Raise

Rise onto the balls of your feet as high as possible.
Pause at the top.
Lower your heels slowly and repeat.

Keep your knees straight.
ex_3I54KF.description: Landmine Calf Raise is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category.

ex_625LFV.name: Landmine Curtsy Lunge

Step one leg behind and across your body into a curtsy position.
Lower until your front thigh is about parallel to the floor.
Push through the front foot to return to standing, then switch legs.
tips: Keep your torso upright.
Keep your front knee over your foot.
ex_625LFV.description: Landmine Curtsy Lunge is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Adductors, Abductors, Hamstrings.

ex_ANQFZY.name: Landmine Glute Kick Back
instructions: Place one foot under the sleeve of the landmine bar on all fours, or stand bent over with the bar behind your foot.
Brace your core.
Kick your leg back and up, lifting the bar with your heel.
Lower with control and repeat, then switch legs.

instructions: Lie flat on your back with your arms by your sides and a loop resistance band around your thighs, just above your knees. Keep your legs extended and together.
Engage your core to lift your right leg straight up towards the ceiling, keeping the resistance band taut and your left leg flat on the floor.
Slowly lower your leg back down with control, stopping just before your heel touches the floor.

ex_3EXNGA.name: Resistance Band One Leg Glute Bridge
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart. Place a loop resistance band around your right thigh, just above your knee, and loop it under your right forefoot.

Engage your core and glutes, then lift your legs upward, squeezing your glutes and keeping your legs straight.

ex_WNQ3SO.name: Resistance Band Seated Bent Knee Abduction
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs bent at a 90-degree angle and your feet flat on the floor. Place a loop resistance band around your thighs, just above your knees.
Engage your core, lean slightly back, and place your hands on the floor behind you for support.
Press your knees outward against the resistance of the band, spreading your legs as wide as possible while keeping your feet flat on the floor.

ex_X4D75R.name: Resistance Band Seated Hip Abduction
instructions: Sit on a bench with your legs bent at a 90-degree angle, feet slightly off the floor, and a loop resistance band around your thighs, just above your knees. Place your hands on the bench for support.

ex_ULMOIR.name: Resistance Band Side Plank Glute Raise
instructions: Place a loop resistance band around your thighs, just above your knees. Begin by lying on your left side with your legs bent at 90 degrees and stacked on top of each other.
Prop yourself up on your left forearm, ensuring your elbow is directly under your shoulder. Engage your core and lift your hips slightly off the floor.

Keeping your legs bent, lift your top leg upwards against the resistance of the band while also raising your hips until your torso is parallel to the floor, squeezing your glutes at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower your leg and hips back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other side.
tips: Focus on engaging your glutes and hip abductors throughout the movement.

ex_B3TV5L.name: Resistance Band Squat Jump
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and place a loop resistance band around your thighs, just above your knees. Keep your chest up and bring both hands close to your chest.
Lower your body into a squat position by bending your knees and pushing your hips back as if you are sitting in a chair.
Explosively jump up by pushing through your heels extending your legs fully and reaching your arms upward.
Land softly back into the squat position, absorbing the impact through your legs. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

ex_WRTEYR.name: Resistance Band Squat
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and place a loop resistance band around your thighs, just above your knees. Keep your chest up and bring both hands close to your chest.

Keeping your right leg straight, kick it back and upward against the band's resistance, squeezing your glutes at the top of the movement.

instructions: Sit down on the hip abduction machine and place your feet flat on the footrests while positioning your outer thighs against the padded levers.

ex_2XXWHX.name: Seated Leg Extension Single Leg

Extend your right leg by pushing the padded lever upward, straightening your knee, then slowly lower the lever to the starting position.

ex_JETUVB.name: Sissy Squat Bodyweight
instructions: Stand tall holding a support for balance, feet hip-width apart.

Lower until you feel a strong stretch in your quadriceps, keeping hips and torso in a straight line.

ex_5QF3QD.name: Smith Machine Narrow Stance Heels Elevated Squats

ex_CR7XF7.name: Standing Cable Hip Flexion
instructions: Attach an ankle strap to a low cable and fasten it to one ankle, facing away from the machine.

ex_EZTX2L.name: Suspension Trainer With Grips Hip Bridge

ex_TFLZI3.name: Barbell Clean Deadlift
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly pointed out, with a barbell on the floor in front of you. Bend at your hips and knees to grip the barbell with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core, keep your back straight, and your chest up. Begin the lift by pushing through your heels, extending your hips and knees to lift the barbell off the floor.
As the barbell passes your knees, explosively extend your hips and knees while shrugging your shoulders to bring the barbell to your upper thighs.
Reverse the movement by lowering the barbell back to the floor with control, maintaining a straight back and engaged core. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Maintain a neutral spine to avoid rounding your back and prevent injury.

ex_WQ3RQG.name: Barbell Clean Pull

Begin the lift by pushing through your heels, extending your hips and knees to lift the barbell off the floor.
As the barbell passes your knees, explosively extend your hips and knees while shrugging your shoulders and pulling the barbell to your midsection and up to chest level.
Lower the barbell back to the floor with control, maintaining a straight back and engaged core. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on leg drive to generate power from your lower body during the lift.
Maintain a neutral spine to avoid rounding your back and prevent injury.
Use your legs and hips to drive the barbell up, minimizing the strain on your lower back.

ex_ALJRKT.name: Barbell Clean and Jerk
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, gripping the barbell with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Bend your knees and hinge at your hips to lower your body and grasp the barbell.

Explosively extend your hips and knees to lift the barbell off the floor, pulling it up to your shoulders while keeping it close to your body. Rotate your elbows under the bar as you catch it in a front rack position.
Dip by bending your knees, then explosively extend your hips and knees to drive the barbell overhead. Simultaneously, split your legs into a lunge position to stabilize the weight overhead.

Fully extend your arms and legs to complete the lift. Carefully bring your feet back together and lower the barbell to your shoulders, then back to the floor. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Perform the movement with control to maximize muscle activation and reduce injury risk.
Keep the barbell close to your body during the clean phase to maintain proper form.

ex_AWI2PA.name: Barbell Full Clean
instructions: Bend at your hips and knees to grip the barbell with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Begin the lift by pushing through your heels, extending your hips and knees to lift the barbell off the floor.

As the barbell passes your knees, explosively extend your hips and knees, lightly jumping, while shrugging your shoulders and pulling the barbell up to your chest level. Rotate your elbows under the bar to catch it in a front squat position.

ex_6RELOP.name: Barbell Hang Clean
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, bend at your hips and knees to grip the barbell with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Hold the barbell against your thighs.

Begin the exercise by hinging at the hips, lowering the barbell to knee level, then explosively extend your hips and knees, lightly jumping, while shrugging your shoulders and pulling the barbell up to your chest level.
Swiftly rotate your elbows underneath the bar and catch it across the front of your shoulders in a partial squat.
Lower the barbell back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep the barbell close to your body throughout the entire movement.
Generate power from your hips and legs rather than pulling with your arms, landing on soft knees during the catch.
Engage your core to support your lower back and maintain stability throughout the movement.
Exhale during the explosive pull and inhale as you reset for the next repetition.
ex_6RELOP.description: Barbell Hang Clean is an advanced multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Quadriceps, Hamstrings.

ex_IMWVTU.name: Barbell Muscle Clean
instructions: Begin in a squatted position with your feet hip-width apart, holding a barbell with an overhand grip (palms facing your body), hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. The barbell should be resting on the floor.

Explosively extend your hips and knees while pulling the barbell up towards your chest, keeping it close to your body. As the barbell passes your knees, shrug your shoulders and continue to pull the barbell upward.
Quickly rotate your elbows under the bar and catch it in a front rack position with your elbows pointing forward. Stand up straight to complete the lift.
Lower the barbell back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep the barbell close to your body to ensure an efficient and powerful lift.
Focus on an explosive hip extension to generate the necessary force for the clean.
Engage your shoulders and traps during the shrug to assist in lifting the barbell.
Use your legs and hips rather than relying solely on your arms to lift the barbell.
ex_IMWVTU.description: Barbell Muscle Clean is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms, Biceps.

ex_CCMPLJ.name: Barbell Press Under
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and hold the barbell across the back of your shoulders with a wide grip.
Press the barbell overhead until your arms are fully extended.
Lower your body into a squat while keeping the barbell locked out overhead, pause for 1-2 seconds.
Return to the starting position by pressing through your heels. Reset and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your arms fully extended while the barbell is overhead.
Keep your chest up and your core engaged throughout the movement for stability.
Keep your heels flat on the floor throughout the squat.
Inhale deeply before moving into the squat and exhale as you stand back up.
ex_CCMPLJ.description: Barbell Press Under is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Hamstrings, Core.

ex_E2T2K4.name: Plate Clean and Press
instructions: Grip a weight plate on the floor and hinge at your hips.
Drive your hips forward to clean the plate up to your chest.
Press the plate straight overhead until your arms are locked out.
Lower it to your chest, then to the floor, and repeat.
tips: Brace your core before the press.
Keep your back flat when lowering.
ex_E2T2K4.description: Plate Clean and Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Triceps, Traps.

ex_KR2RJO.name: Plate Clean
instructions: Stand with a weight plate on the floor in front of you and grip it by its sides.
Hinge at your hips with a flat back.
Drive your hips forward explosively and pull the plate up.
Catch it at your chest with your elbows under it, then lower and repeat.
tips: The power comes from your hips, not your arms.
Keep the plate close to your body.
ex_KR2RJO.description: Plate Clean is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Traps, Shoulders, Quadriceps.

ex_ZT56XX.name: Plate Thruster
instructions: Hold a weight plate at your chest.
Squat down until your thighs are about parallel to the floor.
Drive up explosively and press the plate overhead in one movement.
Lower the plate to your chest as you go into the next squat.
tips: Use the momentum from your legs to help the press.
Keep your heels down in the squat.
ex_ZT56XX.description: Plate Thruster is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Triceps, Core.

ex_ZLC4FB.name: Sandbag Cleans
instructions: Stand over a sandbag with your feet hip-width apart.
Hinge at your hips and grab the sandbag by its sides or handles.
Drive your hips forward explosively and pull the bag up to your chest.
Catch it close to your body, lower it and repeat.
tips: Keep your back flat at the start.
Pull the bag up close to your body.
ex_ZLC4FB.description: Sandbag Cleans is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Traps, Biceps, Core.

ex_JKKGFX.name: Arm Tuck Side Bend
instructions: Stand with your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, with your right arm extended straight out to the side at shoulder height and palm facing upwards and your left hand resting on your hip.
Bend your right arm at the elbow, bringing your hand down towards your lower back.
Return your right arm to the extended position.
Continue the movement with the same arm for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on keeping your shoulder relaxed to avoid tension in your neck and upper back.
Maintain a steady rhythm to ensure consistent movement and effective muscle engagement.
Use a mirror, if available, to check your form.
ex_JKKGFX.description: Arm Tuck Side Bend is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_3MMXVJ.name: Backhand Raise
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, knees bent and lean forward at the hips until your torso is halfway parallel to the floor. Keep your back straight.
Extend your arms straight back parallel to your torso with your palms facing backwards.
Raise your arms upwards, keeping them straight, until they are over your back.
Lower your arms back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
tips: Engage your core to maintain stability and support your lower back throughout the exercise.
Keep your movements slow and controlled to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement to enhance upper back activation.
ex_3MMXVJ.description: Backhand Raise is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Back, Arms.

ex_DIMBLD.name: Band Behind Neck Shoulder Press
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and place the resistance band under your feet. Hold one handle of the band in each hand and bring them up to shoulder height with the band extending behind your body.
Press the handles upward until your arms are fully extended overhead.
Slowly lower the handles back to shoulder height with control, maintaining tension in the band.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure the resistance band is securely placed under your feet to avoid slipping.
Exhale as you press the band overhead and inhale as you lower it back down.
Perform the exercise slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement.
ex_DIMBLD.description: Band Behind Neck Shoulder Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Upper Back.

ex_TRSDJT.name: Band Close Grip Row
instructions: Secure the middle of the resistance band to a sturdy anchor point at chest height. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding one handle of the band in each hand with your palms facing each other and kept close together. Extend your arms in front of your chest, ensuring the band is taut.
Pull the handles towards your chest until your hands are close to your chest, bending your elbows and keeping them pointing outward.
Slowly extend your arms back to the starting position with control, maintaining tension in the band. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure the resistance band is securely anchored to avoid slipping.
Exhale as you pull the handles towards your chest and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Use a resistance band with appropriate tension to ensure you can perform the exercise with good form.
ex_TRSDJT.description: Band Close Grip Row is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps.

ex_KYL7IA.name: Band Face Pull
instructions: Secure the middle of the resistance band to a sturdy anchor point at head height. Stand facing the anchor point with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding one handle of the band in each hand with your arms extended straight in front of you, palms facing down.
Pull the handles towards your face, bending your elbows and flaring them out to the sides until your hands are at your face sides.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end of the movement, keeping your upper arms parallel to the floor.
Slowly extend your arms back to the starting position with control, maintaining tension in the band. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure the resistance band is securely anchored to avoid slipping.
Exhale as you pull the band towards your face and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Maintain a slight bend in your knees for better balance and support.
ex_KYL7IA.description: Band Face Pull is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps.

ex_ZDCZFS.name: Band Front Face Pull
instructions: Secure the middle of the resistance band to a sturdy anchor point at head height. Stand facing the anchor point with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding one handle of the band in each hand with your arms extended straight in front of you, palms facing down.
Pull the handles towards your face, bending your elbows and flaring them out to the sides until your hands are in front of your face.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end of the movement, keeping your upper arms parallel to the floor.
Slowly extend your arms back to the starting position with control, maintaining tension in the band. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure the resistance band is securely anchored to avoid slipping.
Exhale as you pull the band towards your face and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Maintain a slight bend in your knees for better balance and support.
ex_ZDCZFS.description: Band Front Face Pull is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps.

ex_KZZVAH.name: Band Front Raise
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and place the resistance band under both feet, holding one handle of the band in each hand with your arms extended straight down, palms facing your thighs.
Raise both handles straight in front of you to shoulder height, keeping your arms straight and palms facing down.
Slowly lower the handles back to the starting position with control, maintaining tension in the band.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure the resistance band is securely placed under your feet to avoid slipping.
Exhale as you raise the band handles and inhale as you lower them back down.
Avoid swinging your arms; use controlled movements.
ex_KZZVAH.description: Band Front Raise is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Chest, Upper Back.

ex_FYEZ2Z.name: Band Horizontal Shrug
instructions: Attach one end of a loop resistance band to a sturdy anchor point at head height. Stand facing the band with your feet shoulder-width apart. Hold the other end of the band with your arms extended straight forward.
Pull your shoulders backward in a horizontal shrugging motion, squeezing your shoulder blades together at the peak of the movement.
Slowly release the tension in the band, returning to the starting position.
Repeat the movement for the desired repetitions
tips: Focus on using your upper back and shoulders for the shrugging motion, avoiding any arm bending.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you shrug and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
Use a controlled motion to ensure proper form and maximize muscle activation.
ex_FYEZ2Z.description: Band Horizontal Shrug is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the traps (back). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

ex_HCJESJ.name: Band Incline Row
instructions: Lie chest-first on an incline bench set at a 45-degree angle, holding one handle of the resistance band in each hand with your arms fully extended down, palms facing back. Your feet should be firm on the floor, and the resistance band should be secured under the bench.
Pull the handles towards your chest, bending your elbows and keeping them away from your body until your hands are near by your chest sides.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the handles back to the starting position with control.
Repeat the rowing motion for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure the resistance band is secure to prevent any sudden slips.
Focus on squeezing your back muscles at the peak of the movement.
Perform each rep with controlled, deliberate movements for maximum benefit.
ex_HCJESJ.description: Band Incline Row is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Biceps.

ex_YQMDS7.name: Band Incline T Raise
instructions: Lie chest-first on an incline bench set at a 45-degree angle, holding one handle of the resistance band in each hand with your arms fully extended down, palms facing forward. Keep your feet firm on the floor and the resistance band secured under the bench.
Lift your arms out to the sides until they reach shoulder height, forming a "T" shape with your body.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring your arms are parallel and your torso is stable against the bench.
Lower your arms back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you lift your arms and inhale as you lower them back down.
Perform the exercise slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement.
Keep your neck in a neutral position by looking at the bench, not forward or down.
ex_YQMDS7.description: Band Incline T Raise is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_Q64MS2.name: Band Incline Y Raise
instructions: Lie chest-first on an incline bench set at a 45-degree angle, holding one handle of the resistance band in each hand with your arms hanging down and palms facing back. Ensure the resistance band is secured under the bench.
Lift your arms diagonally in a "Y" shape until they are in line with your body, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Lower your arms back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you lift your arms and inhale as you lower them back down.
Use a resistance band with appropriate tension to ensure you can perform the exercise with good form.
Maintain a slight bend in your elbows to protect your shoulder joints.
ex_Q64MS2.description: Band Incline Y Raise is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_4TFGE3.name: Band Reverse Fly
instructions: Lie chest-first on an incline bench, with your feet firmly planted on the floor. Hold the ends of a resistance band anchored below the bench with your arms extended downward and slightly bent at the elbows, palms facing each other.
Raise your arms out to the sides in a wide arc motion until they are in line with your shoulders, squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
Slowly return to the starting position, controlling the resistance band as you lower your arms.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your elbows slightly bent to avoid joint strain and focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Ensure the bench is stable and at an appropriate incline angle to effectively target the upper back muscles.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you raise the band and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
ex_4TFGE3.description: Band Reverse Fly is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_KXKQF2.name: Band Seated Lateral Raise
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor, holding the ends of a resistance band anchored under the bench with your arms hanging at your sides, palms facing inward, and a slight bend in your elbows.
Raise your arms out to the sides until they are parallel to the floor, keeping your elbows slightly bent and leading with your elbows.
Slowly return to the starting position, controlling the resistance band as you lower your arms.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Use an appropriate resistance band that challenges you without compromising your form.
Ensure the band is securely anchored under the bench to prevent slipping.
Keep your elbows slightly bent to avoid joint strain and focus on lifting with your shoulders.
ex_KXKQF2.description: Band Seated Lateral Raise is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_2TJBOE.name: Band Seated Neutral Grip Shoulders Press
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor, holding the ends of a resistance band anchored under the bench, with your arms bent, hands at shoulder level, and palms facing each other (neutral grip).
Press the handles of the band upwards until your arms are fully extended above your head, keeping your palms facing each other.
Slowly lower your hands back to shoulder level, controlling the resistance band as you lower your arms.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Perform the exercise slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and reduce the risk of injury.
Use an appropriate resistance band that challenges you without compromising your form.
Ensure the band is securely anchored under the bench to prevent slipping.
ex_2TJBOE.description: Band Seated Neutral Grip Shoulders Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Upper Back.

ex_SFSMAG.name: Band Seated Shoulder Press
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor, holding the ends of a resistance band anchored under the bench, with your arms bent, hands at shoulder level, and palms facing forward.
Press the handles of the band upwards until your arms are fully extended above your head, keeping your palms facing forward.
Slowly lower your hands back to shoulder level, controlling the resistance band as you lower your arms.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Perform the exercise slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and reduce the risk of injury.
Use an appropriate resistance band that challenges you without compromising your form.
Ensure the band is securely anchored under the bench to prevent slipping.
ex_SFSMAG.description: Band Seated Shoulder Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Upper Back.

ex_62PMVK.name: Band Single Arm Overhead Press
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and place one end of the resistance band securely under your foot of the working side. Hold the other end of the band in your working hand at shoulder height, palm facing inward.
Press the band overhead by fully extending your arm, keeping your wrist straight and elbow slightly bent at the top.
Slowly lower the band back to the starting position, maintaining control.
Repeat the movement for the desired repetitions, then switch sides.
tips: Use a controlled motion to press and lower the band to maximize muscle activation.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you press the band up and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
Ensure the band is securely anchored under your foot to prevent slipping.
ex_62PMVK.description: Band Single Arm Overhead Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Upper Back, Core.

ex_RYS3RK.name: Band Standing Rear Delt Row
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the ends of a resistance band anchored at head height in front of you. Keep your arms extended straight forward just higher than shoulder height with palms facing down.
Pull the band towards your chin by bending your elbows out to the sides, focusing on squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Slowly return to the starting position, extending your arms back to shoulder height.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily, exhaling as you pull the band towards your chin and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement to maximize rear delt engagement.
Adjust the band’s resistance by stepping on it closer to or farther from the anchor point.
ex_RYS3RK.description: Band Standing Rear Delt Row is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Biceps.

ex_CGNYSE.name: Band Y Raise
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the ends of two crossed resistance bands anchored at a low point on a sturdy equipment. Start with your arms hanging in front of your torso, palms facing your hips.
Raise your arms upward and outward to form a "Y" shape until your arms are in line with your shoulders.
Slowly return to the starting position, controlling the resistance band as you lower your arms.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily, exhaling as you raise your arms and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
Keep your elbows slightly bent to avoid joint strain and focus on lifting with your shoulders.
Use an appropriate resistance band that challenges you without compromising your form.
ex_CGNYSE.description: Band Y Raise is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_VOKKUS.name: Barbell Back Wide Shrug
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with both hands behind your back. Your palms should face away from your body with a wide grip.
Keep your shoulders back and chest up. Slowly lift your shoulders towards your ears in a shrugging motion.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement, holding the contraction for a moment.
Slowly lower your shoulders back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid rotating your shoulders; lift them straight up and down to prevent strain.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you lift your shoulders and inhaling as you lower them.
Keep your arms straight throughout the exercise to focus the movement on your shoulders.
ex_VOKKUS.description: Barbell Back Wide Shrug is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the traps (back). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

ex_3EUUOB.name: Barbell Behind the Back Push Press Single Arm Balance
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with one hand behind your back. Your hand should be slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, with the barbell resting on your upper back and shoulder.
Slightly bend your knees, preparing to use your legs to generate power.

Push through your heels and extend your knees and hips explosively, pressing the barbell overhead with one arm until your arm is fully extended. Keep the bar slightly behind your head at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position behind your shoulder with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.
tips: Maintain balance by focusing on a fixed point in front of you and keeping your core engaged.
Exhale forcefully as you press the barbell overhead and inhale as you bring it back down.
Ensure a smooth and controlled descent to maintain proper form and prevent injury.
ex_3EUUOB.description: Barbell Behind the Back Push Press Single Arm Balance is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the balance category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Triceps.

ex_C7VBF4.name: Barbell Bent Over Reverse Raise (Skier)
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell behind your glutes with both hands, palms facing backward. Bend your knees and hinge at your hips, keeping your back straight and your core engaged.
Lower your torso until it is parallel to the floor, letting the barbell hang down under your hamstrings with your arms extended.
Keeping your arms straight, lift the barbell backward in a reverse raise motion until both arms are parallel to the floor.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you lift the barbell and inhale as you lower it back down.
Use a weight that provides enough resistance to challenge your muscles without compromising form.
Focus on engaging your upper back and shoulder muscles throughout the movement.
ex_C7VBF4.description: Barbell Bent Over Reverse Raise (Skier) is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Core.

ex_CH2EB4.name: Barbell Decline Shrug
instructions: Position a decline bench at a 45-degree angle. Lie face down on the bench with your forefeet firmly on the floor. Have a barbell placed on the floor underneath the bench within reach.
Grip the barbell with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Shrug your shoulders towards your ears, lifting the barbell straight up.
Slowly lower the barbell to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on squeezing your trapezius muscles at the top of the movement.
Avoid using your arms to lift the weight; the movement should come from your shoulders.
Keep your neck neutral and avoid looking up or down excessively.
ex_CH2EB4.description: Barbell Decline Shrug is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the traps (back). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_CZECCL.name: Barbell Incline Shoulders Press (Inside Squat Cage)
instructions: Set an adjustable bench to a 45-degree incline and position it inside a squat cage. Sit on the bench with your feet flat on the floor. Grasp the barbell with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and press your back firmly against the bench. Lift the barbell off the rack and hold it at shoulder level with your elbows bent and pointing down.
Press the barbell overhead until your arms are fully extended, keeping your wrists straight and elbows slightly bent at the top.
Slowly lower the barbell back to shoulder level with control, maintaining tension in your shoulders. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your core engaged to maintain stability and prevent lower back strain.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and reduce injury risk.
Exhale as you press the barbell overhead and inhale as you lower it back down.
ex_CZECCL.description: Barbell Incline Shoulders Press (Inside Squat Cage) is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Chest, Triceps, Upper Back.

ex_UNVEZA.name: Barbell Incline Shoulders Press
instructions: Set an adjustable bench to a 45-degree incline. Sit on the bench with your feet flat on the floor. Grasp the barbell with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and press your back firmly against the bench. Hold the barbell at shoulder level with your elbows bent and pointing down.
Press the barbell overhead until your arms are fully extended, keeping your wrists straight and elbows slightly bent at the top.
Slowly lower the barbell back to shoulder level with control, maintaining tension in your shoulders. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your core engaged to maintain stability and prevent lower back strain.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and reduce injury risk.
Exhale as you press the barbell overhead and inhale as you lower it back down.
ex_UNVEZA.description: Barbell Incline Shoulders Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Chest, Triceps, Upper Back.

ex_I37FO2.name: Barbell Silverback Shrug
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with both hands using an overhand grip (palms down). Your hands should be shoulder-width apart. Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and your torso at 45 degrees to the ground.
Start with your arms fully extended, letting the barbell hang directly below your shoulders.
Shrug your shoulders upward to your ears. Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower your shoulders back to the starting position. Repeat the movement for the desired repetitions.
tips: Maintain a neutral spine and avoid rounding your back during the exercise to prevent injury.
Engage your core to stabilize your torso and maintain balance throughout the movement.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you shrug your shoulders upward and inhaling as you lower them back down.
ex_I37FO2.description: Barbell Silverback Shrug is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the traps (back). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

ex_A463TS.name: Barbell Z Press
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended and your feet slightly apart. Hold the barbell at shoulder height using an overhand grip (palms facing forward), slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Keep your back straight, engage your core, and ensure your chest is upright.
Press the barbell overhead by extending your arms fully, keeping your head neutral and looking forward.
Slowly lower the barbell back to shoulder height. Repeat the movement for the desired repetitions.
tips: Engage your core to stabilize your torso and maintain an upright posture.
Use a controlled motion to lift and lower the barbell to maximize shoulder engagement.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you press the bar up and inhaling as you lower it back down.
ex_A463TS.description: Barbell Z Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Triceps, Core.

ex_WUNFO4.name: Cable 30 Degree Shrug
instructions: Stand upright between two low cable pulleys and hold the handles at your sides with a neutral grip and your arms fully extended.
Elevate your shoulders toward your ears while keeping your arms straight and your torso still.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement while squeezing your upper back muscles.
Lower your shoulders slowly to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your arms fully extended throughout the exercise.
Squeeze your upper trapezius at the top of each repetition.
Keep your neck in a neutral position and look straight ahead.
Inhale as you lower your shoulders and exhale as you shrug upward.
ex_WUNFO4.description: Cable 30 Degree Shrug is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the traps (back). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Shoulders, Forearms.

ex_2O5T2A.name: Cable Face Pull With Rope
instructions: Set a cable pulley at upper chest height and attach a rope.
Hold the rope ends with an overhand grip and step back until your arms are straight.
Pull the rope toward your face, separating the ends and driving your elbows out and back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades, then return slowly and repeat.
