ex_2O5T2A.description: Cable Face Pull With Rope is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Traps, Rotator Cuff.

ex_2TE5HA.name: Cable Single Arm Reverse Fly
instructions: Stand sideways to a cable machine with the pulley set at shoulder height and hold the handle with the arm farthest from the machine. Extend your arm across the front of your body with a slight bend in your elbow.
Pull the handle outward and backward in a wide horizontal arc until your arm is in line with your shoulder.
Pause briefly while squeezing your posterior deltoid.
Slowly return the handle along the same arc to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching sides.
tips: Maintain a slight bend in your elbow throughout the exercise.
Keep your torso upright and avoid rotating as you pull.
Control the return phase to maintain constant muscle tension.
Inhale as you return to the starting position and exhale as you pull the handle outward.
ex_2TE5HA.description: Cable Single Arm Reverse Fly is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Middle Back, Forearms.

ex_BORKNT.name: Dumbbell Alternating Arnold Press
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder width apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height with your palms facing your body and your elbows bent.
Press one dumbbell overhead while rotating your hand until your palm faces forward as your arm reaches full extension.
Lower the dumbbell back to shoulder height while rotating your hand until your palm faces your body again.
Repeat the movement with the opposite arm, alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep the non-working dumbbell at shoulder height while pressing the opposite arm.
Rotate your hand smoothly throughout the press instead of turning it all at once.
Press the dumbbell directly overhead without letting your elbow flare excessively.
Inhale as you lower the dumbbell and exhale as you press it overhead.
ex_BORKNT.description: Dumbbell Alternating Arnold Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Shoulders, Core.

ex_YHMCMN.name: Dumbbell Chest Supported Y Raise
instructions: Lie face down on an incline bench with your chest fully supported. Hold a dumbbell in each hand, in a neutral grip and allow your arms to hang straight toward the floor with a slight bend in your elbows.
Raise both dumbbells diagonally upward and outward, while rotating the weight until your arms form a Y shape with your body, finishing the movement with palms facing down.
Pause briefly at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your chest in contact with the bench throughout the exercise.
Use light weights to maintain proper technique and a full range of motion.
Avoid swinging the dumbbells or using momentum.
Inhale as you lower the dumbbells and exhale as you raise them.
ex_YHMCMN.description: Dumbbell Chest Supported Y Raise is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Rotator Cuff, Shoulders, Core.

ex_QTPCQN.name: Dumbbell Laying 30 Degree Shrug
instructions: Lie on your right side on a 30 degree incline bench with your knees bent. Hold a dumbbell in your right hand using a neutral grip and let your arm hang straight toward the floor.
Keep your arm straight and raise your working shoulder toward your ear, lifting the dumbbell slightly upward.
Pause briefly at the top and squeeze your upper back while keeping your torso still.
Slowly lower your shoulder until your arm hangs fully extended, then repeat before switching sides.

Exhale as you raise your shoulder and inhale as you lower it.
ex_QTPCQN.description: Dumbbell Laying 30 Degree Shrug is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the traps (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms, Shoulders, Core.

ex_OFAU3E.name: Dumbbell Laying Silverback Shrug
instructions: Lie face down on an incline bench with your chest supported, your legs extended, and your feet firmly on the floor. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip and let your arms hang straight below your shoulders.
Shrug your shoulders toward your ears and slightly backward while keeping your arms straight and your chest against the bench.
Pause briefly at the top and squeeze your upper back muscles.
Slowly lower your shoulders to the starting position, allowing them to fully relax before repeating.
tips: Keep your chest firmly supported on the bench throughout the exercise.
Move your shoulders upward and slightly backward without rolling them.
Avoid swinging the dumbbells or using momentum to lift them.
Exhale as you raise your shoulders and inhale as you lower them.
ex_OFAU3E.description: Dumbbell Laying Silverback Shrug is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the traps (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Shoulders, Forearms.

ex_NEY7IB.name: Dumbbell Plank Pullthrough
instructions: Begin in a high plank with your hands directly below your shoulders, your feet slightly apart, and a dumbbell positioned on the floor beside one hand.
Shift your weight onto one hand and reach your opposite hand underneath your torso to grasp the dumbbell.
Drag the dumbbell across the floor to the opposite side while keeping your shoulders and hips facing the floor.
Place your hand back on the floor, repeat the pull with the opposite arm, and continue alternating sides.
tips: Keep your hips level and avoid rotating your torso as you reach underneath.
Transfer your weight smoothly without collapsing into your supporting shoulder.
Drag the dumbbell across the floor instead of lifting it upward.
Exhale as you pull the dumbbell across and inhale as you return your hand to the floor.
ex_NEY7IB.description: Dumbbell Plank Pullthrough is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Middle Back, Chest, Triceps.

ex_OPQU6Y.name: Dumbbell Shoulder Extension
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand using a neutral grip. Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor, allowing your arms to hang below your shoulders.
Keep your elbows slightly bent and raise both dumbbells backward by extending your arms behind your hips.
Pause briefly at the top and squeeze the backs of your shoulders while keeping your torso still.
Slowly lower the dumbbells until they hang below your shoulders, then repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep the bend in your elbows fixed without turning the exercise into a row.
Move your arms backward from your shoulders rather than swinging the dumbbells.
Keep your torso still and avoid rising as you lift the weights.
Exhale as you raise the dumbbells and inhale as you lower them.
ex_OPQU6Y.description: Dumbbell Shoulder Extension is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Upper Back, Core.

ex_YB5AGZ.name: Dumbbell Silverback Shrug
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand using an overhand grip. Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward while keeping your back straight and your arms hanging below your shoulders.

Pause briefly at the top and squeeze your upper back without lifting your torso.
Slowly lower your shoulders until your arms hang fully extended, then repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Exhale as you raise your shoulders and inhale as you lower them.
ex_YB5AGZ.description: Dumbbell Silverback Shrug is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the traps (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Shoulders, Forearms.

ex_WAWFID.name: Dumbbell Single Arm Upright Row
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder width apart and hold a dumbbell in front of your thigh using an overhand grip. Keep your free arm relaxed by your side.
Pull the dumbbell upward close to your torso by leading with your elbow and moving it outward and upward.
Raise the dumbbell toward your upper chest until your elbow is higher than your wrist.
Slowly lower the dumbbell along the same path until your arm is fully extended, then repeat before switching sides.

Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning backward as the dumbbell rises.

ex_WAWFID.description: Dumbbell Single Arm Upright Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Forearms, Core.

ex_WNARFC.name: Elevated Pike Shoulder Shrug
instructions: Place the balls of both feet on an elevated platform and position your hands shoulder width apart on the floor. Straighten your arms and legs, then lift your hips until your body forms an inverted V shape.
Keep your elbows fixed with a slight bend, lowering your upper body slightly between your arms.
Press firmly through your palms and shrug your shoulders upwards, raising your upper body without bending your elbows.
Lower your shoulders with control to return to the starting position, then repeat while keeping your feet fixed and your hips elevated.
tips: Keep your hands shoulder width apart and spread your fingers for stability.
Keep your elbows fixed with a slight bend so the movement occurs through your shoulder blades.
Keep your legs extended and the balls of your feet firmly supported on the platform.

ex_WNARFC.description: Elevated Pike Shoulder Shrug is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the traps (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Core, Forearms.

ex_SHU7T7.name: Iso Lateral Shoulder Press Alternate Arms
instructions: Sit on the Iso-Lateral Shoulder Press machine, back pressed against the backrest and feet flat on the floor. Grasp the handles with both hands, palms facing forward.

ex_NJ4HKX.name: Iso Lateral Shoulder Press Single Arm

ex_GXMEIJ.name: Jump Rope Face Pull
instructions: Loop the jump rope over a vertical bar or similar stable structure, ensuring the rope is at about hip height. Stand facing the bar with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handles of the jump rope with both hands.
Step back slightly to create tension in the rope, keeping your core engaged and your back straight.
Pull the rope towards your face by bending your elbows and bringing your hands towards your ears, engaging your upper back and shoulder muscles.
Extend your arms back out to the starting position with control. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.

Ensure the vertical bar or structure is stable and can support the tension in the rope to prevent slipping or injury.
ex_GXMEIJ.description: Jump Rope Face Pull is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a rope, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Biceps.

ex_XUHYLY.name: Kettlebell Front Raise
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and hold a kettlebell by the handle with both hands in front of you, keeping your arms extended.

Raise and lower the weight smoothly without using momentum.

ex_FM6LUW.name: Kettlebell Rear Delt Row
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart, bend your knees slightly, and hinge forward with a straight back. Hold a kettlebell with both hands, in an overhand grip, and let it hang between your legs.

ex_7BWTV3.name: Kettlebell Shoulder Extension

Lower the kettlebell with control until your arm returns toward the floor, then repeat before switching sides.

Move your arm from the shoulder instead of turning the movement into a row.
Raise the kettlebell straight backward rather than out to the side.

ex_EWCTDD.description: Plate Full Front Raise is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Chest, Traps.

ex_2BHIY2.name: Plate Halo
instructions: Hold a weight plate by its sides in front of your chest.
Move the plate around your head in a circle, close to your head.
Bring it back to the front.
Repeat in one direction, then switch direction.
tips: Keep your core braced and hips still.
Keep the plate close to your head.
ex_2BHIY2.description: Plate Halo is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Upper Back, Core.

ex_TV6BSP.name: Plate Internally Rotated Rear Delt Fly
instructions: Hinge forward with a flat back, holding a light plate in each hand, thumbs turned in.
Let your arms hang below your shoulders.
Raise your arms out to the sides, leading with your elbows.
Lower slowly and repeat.
tips: Use light plates.
Squeeze your rear shoulders at the top.
ex_TV6BSP.description: Plate Internally Rotated Rear Delt Fly is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Traps.

ex_LLSC2T.name: Plate Lateral Raise
instructions: Stand holding a light weight plate in each hand at your sides.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows.
Raise your arms out to the sides until they reach shoulder height.
Lower slowly and repeat.
tips: Lead with your elbows.
Don't shrug your shoulders.
ex_LLSC2T.description: Plate Lateral Raise is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Traps.

ex_ZNRZO6.name: Plate Overhead Press to Tricep Extension
instructions: Hold a weight plate at your chest and press it overhead.
With your upper arms by your ears, lower the plate behind your head by bending your elbows.
Extend your elbows to bring the plate back overhead.
Lower the plate to your chest and repeat.
tips: Keep your elbows pointing forward during the extension.
Brace your core.
ex_ZNRZO6.description: Plate Overhead Press to Tricep Extension is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Core.

ex_LIGPOE.name: Plate Overhead Shrug
instructions: Press a weight plate overhead with your arms locked out.

Lower your shoulders with control and repeat.
tips: Keep your arms locked.
Good for overhead stability.
ex_LIGPOE.description: Plate Overhead Shrug is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the traps (back). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Serratus Anterior.

ex_IZZ4Z4.name: Plate Reach
instructions: Stand holding a weight plate at your chest.
Press the plate straight out in front of you.
Hold it briefly at arm's length.
Bring it back to your chest and repeat.
tips: Keep your core braced.
Don't let your shoulders shrug.
ex_IZZ4Z4.description: Plate Reach is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Core, Chest.

ex_WG7O34.name: Plate Rear Delt Fly
instructions: Hinge forward with a flat back, holding a light plate in each hand.
Let your arms hang below your shoulders with a slight bend in your elbows.
Raise your arms out to the sides until they are level with your shoulders.
Lower slowly and repeat.
tips: Keep your neck in line with your spine.
Use a light weight.
ex_WG7O34.description: Plate Rear Delt Fly is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Traps.

ex_ZL4TSI.name: Reverse Machine Fly
instructions: Sit on a stool with your back straight, knees bent, and feet on the floor.
Extend your arms forward and grab the handles of the machine with your palms facing down.
Pull the handles by opening your arms wide to your sides.
As your arms are aligned with the shoulders, return to the initial position and repeat.
tips: Exhale as you pull the handles outward and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Keep your elbows slightly bent to reduce strain on your joints.
Focus on engaging your upper back and shoulder muscles throughout the movement.
ex_ZL4TSI.description: Reverse Machine Fly is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_WCFETK.name: Seated Dumbbell Neutral Grip Front Raises
instructions: Sit tall on a bench holding a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other.
Raise the dumbbells in front of you to shoulder height.
Pause briefly.
Lower slowly and repeat.
tips: Don't swing the weights.
Keep your back against the pad if there is one.
ex_WCFETK.description: Seated Dumbbell Neutral Grip Front Raises is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Chest.

ex_BVITF4.name: Seated Dumbbell Neutral Grip Side Raises
instructions: Sit tall holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing in.
Raise the dumbbells out to the sides to shoulder height.
Pause briefly.
Lower slowly and repeat.
tips: Keep a slight bend in your elbows.
Don't shrug.
ex_BVITF4.description: Seated Dumbbell Neutral Grip Side Raises is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Traps.

ex_TR7J7C.name: Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Shrugs
instructions: Sit tall holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Shrug your shoulders straight up toward your ears.
Hold briefly at the top.
Lower slowly and repeat.
tips: Don't roll your shoulders.
Keep your arms straight.
ex_TR7J7C.description: Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Shrugs is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the traps (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

ex_JEXHJ4.name: Seated Plate Bus Drivers
instructions: Sit tall holding a weight plate at the 3 and 9 o'clock positions, arms extended at shoulder height.
Turn the plate to one side like a steering wheel.
Return to the centre and turn it to the other side.
Keep alternating with your arms at shoulder height.
tips: Keep your arms straight.
Sit tall without leaning back.
ex_JEXHJ4.description: Seated Plate Bus Drivers is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms, Core.

ex_ROCA5B.name: Seated Plate Front Raises
instructions: Sit tall holding a weight plate at its sides in front of your thighs.
Raise the plate in front of you to shoulder height with straight arms.
Pause briefly.
Lower slowly and repeat.
tips: Don't lean back.
Use a light plate.
ex_ROCA5B.description: Seated Plate Front Raises is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Chest.

ex_PPZIEP.name: Seated Plate Side Raises
instructions: Sit tall holding a light plate in each hand at your sides.
Raise your arms out to the sides to shoulder height.
Pause briefly.
Lower slowly and repeat.
tips: Lead with your elbows.
Don't shrug.
ex_PPZIEP.description: Seated Plate Side Raises is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a weighted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Traps.

ex_JTIBYB.name: Suspension Trainer With Grips Face Pull
instructions: Adjust the suspension trainer handles to about chest height. Stand facing the handles with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handles with your arms extended straight in front of you and palms facing each other.
Engage your core and lean back slightly, keeping your body straight from head to heels.
Pull the handles towards your face, bending your elbows and flaring them out to the sides until your hands are at face level.
Slowly extend your arms back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily: exhale as you pull the handles towards your face and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Focus on using your upper back and shoulder muscles to perform the pull, avoiding excessive use of your arms.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid shrugging them towards your ears.
ex_JTIBYB.description: Suspension Trainer With Grips Face Pull is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a suspension trainer, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

ex_ZMFZTU.name: Suspension Trainer With Grips Front Raise
instructions: Adjust the suspension trainer handles to about chest height. Stand facing the handles with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handles with your arms extended straight in front of you and palms facing down.
Engage your core and lean back slightly, keeping your body straight from head to heels.
Keeping your arms straight, raise the handles upward until your arms are fully extended above your head, forming a straight line with your body.
Slowly lower the handles back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep tension in the suspension trainer straps throughout the exercise.
Avoid letting your hips sag to maintain proper body alignment.
If you feel strain in your lower back, readjust your position and ensure your core is engaged.
ex_ZMFZTU.description: Suspension Trainer With Grips Front Raise is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a suspension trainer, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Core.

ex_MEPICW.name: Suspension Trainer With Grips Rear Delt Row
instructions: Adjust the suspension trainer handles to about chest height. Stand facing the anchor point with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handles with a neutral grip (palms facing each other), and lean back slightly with your arms extended.
Engage your upper back and pull your chest towards the handles by bending your elbows and driving them out to the sides, focusing on squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Continue pulling until your upper arms are parallel to the floor and your elbows are bent at a 90-degree angle.
Slowly extend your arms back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily: exhale as you pull your chest towards the handles and inhale as you extend your arms back.
Keep your core tight to maintain stability and prevent your hips from sagging.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid shrugging them towards your ears.
ex_MEPICW.description: Suspension Trainer With Grips Rear Delt Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a suspension trainer, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Forearms.

ex_B45FGP.name: Suspension Trainer With Grips Single Arm Rear Delt Row
instructions: Adjust the suspension trainer handle to about chest height. Stand facing the handle, holding one handle with an overhand grip (palm facing down), and lean back slightly with your arm extended and feet shoulder-width apart.
Engage your arm and pull your chest towards the handle by bending your elbow and driving it out to the side, focusing on squeezing your shoulder blade towards your spine.
Continue pulling until your upper arm is parallel to the floor and your elbow is bent at a 90-degree angle.
Slowly extend your arm back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms.
tips: Focus on using your rear deltoid and upper back muscles to perform the row, avoiding excessive use of your arm.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid shrugging them towards your ears.
Breathe steadily: exhale as you pull your chest towards the handle and inhale as you extend your arm back.
ex_B45FGP.description: Suspension Trainer With Grips Single Arm Rear Delt Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a suspension trainer, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Forearms.

ex_PCZFB5.name: Suspension Trainer With Grips Split Fly
instructions: Adjust the suspension trainer handles to about chest height. Stand facing the handles with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a handle in each hand with an overhand grip (palm facing down) with the left hand and an underhand with the right (palm facing up).
Engage your core and lean back slightly with your arm extended, keeping your body straight from head to heels and your arms extended in front of you at shoulder height.
Spread your arms in front of you, bringing your left arm overhead and the right arm by your hip, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Slowly bring your arms back together to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Start with a smaller range of motion and gradually increase as your strength and flexibility improve.
Ensure your wrists are straight and not bending during the movement.
Breathe steadily: exhale as you open your arms and inhale as you bring them back together.
ex_PCZFB5.description: Suspension Trainer With Grips Split Fly is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a suspension trainer, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_V6QVU7.name: Trap Bar Shrug
instructions: Stand in the center of a trap bar with your feet shoulder-width apart. Bend your knees and hips to lower your body, and grasp the handles of the trap bar with a neutral grip (palms facing in).
Stand up straight with the trap bar at arm's length by your sides, keeping your core engaged and back straight.
Lift your shoulders towards your ears, squeezing your traps at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower your shoulders back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily: exhale as you shrug your shoulders and inhale as you lower them.
Keep your neck relaxed and avoid straining it during the movement.
Ensure your back remains straight and avoid leaning forward or backward.
ex_V6QVU7.description: Trap Bar Shrug is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the traps (back). Performed with a trap bar, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Forearms.

ex_YJ3GLB.name: 5 Sec Fist Against Chin
instructions: Sit or stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart, maintaining good posture. Make a fist with both hands and place them under your chin.
Apply gentle upward pressure with your fist against your chin, resisting with your neck muscles. Hold this position for 5 seconds.
Keep your neck and head steady, avoiding any movement while maintaining the pressure.
Release the pressure after 5 seconds and relax. Repeat the exercise for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your jaw relaxed, avoiding clenching your teeth.
Focus on the resistance created by your fist and neck muscles rather than the amount of force applied.
Breathe normally throughout the exercise, avoiding holding your breath.
ex_YJ3GLB.description: 5 Sec Fist Against Chin is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the levator scapulae (neck). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category.

ex_DR7ILG.name: 90 to 90 Stretch
instructions: Sit on the floor with both legs bent at 90 degrees. Position one leg in front of your body with your thigh and shin at a 90-degree angle, and the other leg to the side with your thigh and shin at a 90-degree angle with foot extending backwards.
Lean lightly forward keeping your arms on the floor and holding the stretch for a few seconds.
Switch the position of your legs to perform the stretch on the opposite side.
tips: Keep your back straight as you lean forward to maximize the stretch and avoid straining your lower back.
Breathe deeply and steadily throughout the stretch to help relax your muscles.
Perform the stretch slowly and avoid bouncing or jerking movements to reduce the risk of injury.
ex_DR7ILG.description: 90 to 90 Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors, Glutes.

ex_M6ZHX5.name: Abdominal Stretch ( Version2 )
instructions: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and drawn towards your chest.
Place your hands on your knees keeping them set and lean your chest to your knees to stretch.
Hold the stretch in this position, allowing your back to round slightly and your head to relax forward.
After holding the stretch for the desired amount of time, release your arms and return to a neutral sitting position.
tips: Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid hunching them up towards your ears.
Breathe deeply and steadily throughout the stretch to help relax your muscles.
Perform the stretch slowly and avoid any sudden movements to prevent strain.
ex_M6ZHX5.description: Abdominal Stretch ( Version2 ) is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors, Lower Back.

ex_4FI2J5.name: Abdominal Stretch
instructions: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and drawn towards your chest.
Wrap your arms around your knees, hugging them tightly.
Hold the stretch in this position, allowing your back to round slightly and your head to relax forward.
After holding the stretch for the desired amount of time, release your arms and return to a neutral sitting position.
tips: Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid hunching them up towards your ears.
Breathe deeply and steadily throughout the stretch to help relax your muscles.
Perform the stretch slowly and avoid any sudden movements to prevent strain.
ex_4FI2J5.description: Abdominal Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors, Lower Back.

ex_B3CBME.name: Above Head Chest Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your back straight. Raise your arms overhead and clasp your hands together with elbows bent.
Keeping your hands clasped, bring your elbows backward to stretch.
Hold the stretch in this position, keeping your back straight and core engaged.
After holding the stretch for the desired amount of time, return to the starting position.
tips: Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid hunching them up towards your ears.
Breathe deeply and steadily throughout the stretch to help relax your muscles.
Maintain a straight back and engaged core to ensure proper form and maximize the stretch.
ex_B3CBME.description: Above Head Chest Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_SJ2ICV.name: Across Chest Shoulder Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your back straight. Raise one arm to shoulder height and bring it across your chest.
Use your opposite hand to grasp your upper arm and gently pull it towards your chest, stretching your shoulder.
Hold the stretch in this position.
Release your arm and repeat the movement on the other side.
tips: Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid hunching them up towards your ears.
Breathe deeply and steadily throughout the stretch to help relax your muscles.
Maintain a straight back and avoid twisting your torso to ensure proper form.
ex_SJ2ICV.description: Across Chest Shoulder Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_DGO6DL.name: Adductor Dynamic Stretch
instructions: Lie on your back on a mat with both legs extended upwards.
Open your legs wide apart, stretching your inner thighs.
Bring your legs back together to the starting position.
Continue the movement in a dynamic manner, opening and closing your legs.
tips: Keep your core engaged to maintain stability and control throughout the movement.
Perform the movement with controlled and smooth transitions to maximize the stretch and prevent injury.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you open your legs and inhaling as you bring them back together.
ex_DGO6DL.description: Adductor Dynamic Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the adductors (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors, Quadriceps.

ex_YKLGJN.name: Adductor Stretch Side Standing
instructions: Stand tall with your back straight and feet shoulder-width apart while keeping your hands together in front of your chest.
Take a step to the left while keeping your right foot in place.
Bend the left knee unless your right thigh becomes parallel to the floor.
Hold for a few seconds, return to the initial position, and repeat.
tips: Keep your core engaged to maintain balance and stability throughout the stretch.
Ensure your bent knee does not extend past your toes to avoid strain on your knee joint.
Perform the stretch slowly and avoid any sudden movements to prevent strain.
ex_YKLGJN.description: Adductor Stretch Side Standing is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the adductors (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Glutes.

ex_KVS4DE.name: Adductor Stretch
instructions: Lie on your back on a mat with both legs extended upwards.
Open your legs wide apart, stretching your inner thighs.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, or as needed.
tips: Keep your core engaged to maintain stability and control throughout the stretch.
Focus on maintaining a steady breathing pattern, inhaling deeply through your nose and exhaling through your mouth while holding the stretch.
Perform the stretch slowly and avoid any sudden movements to prevent strain.
ex_KVS4DE.description: Adductor Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the adductors (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors, Quadriceps.

ex_DNVBGW.name: All Fours Quad Stretch
instructions: Start in an all-fours position on a mat, with your hands directly under your shoulders and your knees under your hips.
Reach back with your right hand to grasp the ankle of your right leg.
Gently pull your ankle towards your glutes, stretching your quadriceps, and hold the stretch in this position for 20-30 seconds.
Release your ankle and switch sides, repeating the stretch.
tips: Keep your core engaged to maintain balance and stability throughout the stretch.
Avoid arching your back; maintain a neutral spine to protect your lower back.
Breathe deeply and steadily throughout the stretch to help relax your muscles.
ex_DNVBGW.description: All Fours Quad Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

ex_P7WRLU.name: Armless Prayer Stretch
instructions: Begin on your knees, spread wide and feet touching, with your elbows on the floor, directly under your shoulders.
Place your hands on your shoulders, with your head positioned between your elbows close to the floor.
Gently lower your chest towards the floor, keeping your hips over your knees and your back straight.
Hold the stretch briefly, then return to the starting position. Repeat the movement.
tips: Engage your core to maintain stability and support your lower back throughout the exercise.
Focus on lowering your chest towards the floor to maximize the stretch in your shoulders and upper back.
Keep the stretch at least between 15-20 seconds to make the most out of it.
ex_P7WRLU.description: Armless Prayer Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Chest.

ex_EZ5PXP.name: Arms Behind Back Chest Stretch
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder width apart and clasp your hands behind your lower back.
Lift your chest up while rolling your shoulders back and downward.
Hold the stretch while breathing steadily.
tips: Maintain an upright posture without arching your lower back excessively.
Breathe slowly and deeply throughout the stretch, keeping your chest up.
Stretch only until you feel gentle tension, not pain.
Keep your neck relaxed and your head in a neutral position.
ex_EZ5PXP.description: Arms Behind Back Chest Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_BSYI3P.name: Arms Wide Chest Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and extend your arms straight out to your sides at shoulder height.
Rotate your arms so that your palms face forward.
Move both your arms backward, as for as you can.
Hold the stretch for 20 - 30seconds, while breathing steadily.
tips: Pull your shoulder blades down and back.
Stretch only until you feel mild tension in your chest, not pain.
Breathe slowly and rhythmically, focusing on the stretch.
ex_BSYI3P.description: Arms Wide Chest Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Arms, Upper Back.

ex_RDTKVV.name: Back Slaps Wrap Around Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Swing your arms out to the sides, keeping them lightly bent.
Cross your arms in front of your body, wrapping them around yourself as if giving yourself a hug.
Continue the swinging motion, alternating which arm crosses on top with each repetition.
tips: Keep your movements fluid to promote relaxation and prevent stiffness.
Focus on extending your arms fully to each side to maximize the stretch in your chest and shoulders.
Maintain a steady pace to ensure you are not rushing through the movement and to allow a thorough stretch.
ex_RDTKVV.description: Back Slaps Wrap Around Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Arms.

ex_XGRFQD.name: Back and Shoulder Stretch
instructions: Sit on a block with your back straight, feet shoulder-width apart and raise your right arm overhead.
Bend your right elbow and reach down your back. Use your left hand to gently pull on your right elbow, enhancing the stretch.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds.
Switch arms and repeat the stretch on the left side.
tips: Keep your core engaged to maintain balance and proper posture throughout the stretch.
Avoid pulling too hard on your elbow; the stretch should be gentle and not cause pain.
Breathe deeply and steadily to help relax your muscles and enhance the stretch.
ex_XGRFQD.description: Back and Shoulder Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Lats.

ex_A6PMJJ.name: Backward Forward Turn to Side Neck Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your head in a neutral position.
Tilt your head backward, stretching the front of your neck.
Return to the neutral position, then tilt your head forward to stretch the back of your neck.
Turn your head to one side, holding briefly, and then return to the neutral position. Repeat on the other side.
tips: Perform the movements slowly and gently to avoid straining your neck muscles.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and down to prevent tension in your upper back and shoulders.
Breathe deeply and steadily to help relax your muscles and enhance the stretch.
ex_A6PMJJ.description: Backward Forward Turn to Side Neck Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the levator scapulae (neck). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_IVKJHL.name: Band Warm Up Shoulder Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the resistance band with both hands in front of you. Your arms should be straight, and hands shoulder-width apart.
Slowly lift the band overhead while slightly spreading your hands to stretch the band.
Hold this position for a few seconds and slowly return to the starting position with the band in front of you.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your arms straight but not locked to avoid joint strain.
Ensure the resistance band has appropriate tension to provide an effective stretch without causing discomfort.
Perform the stretch slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and reduce the risk of injury.
ex_IVKJHL.description: Band Warm Up Shoulder Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_W4I7FX.name: Both Arms Behind on Wall Biceps Stretch
instructions: Stand upright facing away from a wall and place both palms facing upward against it behind your body with your arms fully extended.
Bend your knees slowly while keeping your hands against the wall until you feel a gentle stretch in your upper arms and shoulders.
Keep your elbows fully extended, your chest up, and hold the stretch for the desired duration.
Return to starting position to release tension.
tips: Keep both elbows fully extended throughout the stretch.
Stand tall and avoid leaning your torso forward.
Bend your knees gradually, reaching a comfortable stretch without feeling pain.
Breathe slowly and evenly while holding the stretch.
ex_W4I7FX.description: Both Arms Behind on Wall Biceps Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Forearms.

ex_ZJQBWX.name: Bulgarian Split Squat Stretch
instructions: Place your front foot flat on the floor and keep your torso upright.
Kneel in a split stance with your rear knee on the floor and the top of your rear foot resting against a wall behind you.
Gently shift your hips backward until you feel a comfortable stretch through the front of your rear thigh and hip.
Hold the stretch for the desired duration, then return to the starting position and repeat on the opposite side.
tips: Keep your torso upright throughout the stretch.
Keep your hips facing forward and avoid twisting your pelvis.
Shift your hips backward gradually until you feel a gentle stretch without pain.
Breathe slowly and evenly while holding the stretch.
ex_ZJQBWX.description: Bulgarian Split Squat Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Hamstrings, Core.

ex_3D4VG2.name: Calve Stretch Foot on Wall
instructions: Stand facing a wall and place both hands against it for support. Position the ball of one foot against the wall with your heel off the wall, while your opposite foot remains behind you for balance.
Keep your stretching leg straight and slowly lean your body toward the wall until you feel a stretch in your calf.
Hold the stretch while keeping your heel firmly in contact with the floor.
Return to the starting position with control and repeat before switching legs.
tips: Lean forward gradually until you feel a comfortable stretch without pain.
Keep both hips facing the wall to maintain proper alignment.
Inhale as you prepare and exhale as you lean into the stretch.
ex_3D4VG2.description: Calve Stretch Foot on Wall is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings.

ex_VIXZSM.name: Calve Stretch From Wall to Floor
instructions: Stand facing a wall and place both hands against it for support. Step one foot forward near the wall and extend your opposite leg straight behind you.
Slowly lean your body toward the wall, bending your front leg at the knee joint , while straightening your back leg.
Hold the stretch when you feel it in the calf of your back leg, keeping your heel as on the floor.
Return to the starting position with control and repeat before switching legs.
tips: Keep your back leg straight throughout the stretch.
Lean forward gradually until you feel a comfortable stretch.
Inhale before leaning forward and exhale as you deepen the stretch.
ex_VIXZSM.description: Calve Stretch From Wall to Floor is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings.

ex_US4U5H.name: Calves Stretch on Step
instructions: Stand on the edge of a step with the balls of both feet on the platform and your heels hanging off the edge. Place both hands against a wall for support.
Keep your legs straight and slowly lower your heels below the level of the step until you feel a stretch in your calves.
Hold the stretch while keeping your movements relaxed and controlled.
Raise your heels back to the starting position with control and repeat for the desired number of repetitions or hold time.
tips: Lower your heels slowly to deepen the stretch without bouncing.
Keep the balls of your feet firmly on the edge of the step.
Stretch only until you feel a comfortable pull in your calves, not pain.
Inhale before lowering your heels and exhale as you deepen the stretch.
ex_US4U5H.description: Calves Stretch on Step is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings.

ex_2ZWCRH.name: Child Pose Lower Back Stretch
instructions: Kneel on the floor with your big toes together and knees apart.
Sit your hips back toward your heels.
Reach your arms forward and lower your chest toward the floor.
Rest your forehead down and breathe deeply into your lower back.
tips: Keep your knees closer together for a deeper back stretch.
Relax your shoulders.
ex_2ZWCRH.description: Child Pose Lower Back Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Lats, Glutes.

ex_U7FZCY.name: Cobra Stretch
instructions: Lie face down with your legs extended and the tops of your feet resting on the floor. Place your hands beneath your shoulders with your elbows close to your body.
Press through your hands to slowly lift your chest while extending your arms and keeping your hips in contact with the floor.
Raise your chest until you feel a comfortable stretch through your lower back and abdomen while keeping your shoulders relaxed.
Hold the stretch briefly, then slowly lower your chest back to the starting position with control.
tips: Keep your hips and legs in contact with the floor throughout the stretch.
Press up gradually and avoid forcing your lower back into excessive extension.
Keep your elbows close to your body as you lift your chest.
Exhale as you lift your chest and inhale as you lower back down.
ex_U7FZCY.description: Cobra Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Shoulders, Lower Back.

ex_UADLSS.name: Crescent Moon Pose Quad Stretch With Block
instructions: Begin in a lunge position with one foot forward and your back knee resting on the floor. Bend your back knee and reach behind you to grasp your back foot with both hands.
Gently draw your back heel toward your glutes while keeping your chest lifted and your hips facing forward.
Hold the stretch until you feel a comfortable stretch along the front of your back thigh and hip.
Release your foot with control, return to the starting position, and repeat on the opposite side.
tips: Keep your front knee directly above your ankle.
Engage your core to help maintain balance and alignment.
Keep your chest lifted and avoid leaning excessively forward.
Inhale before deepening the stretch and exhale as you gently pull your foot closer.
ex_UADLSS.description: Crescent Moon Pose Quad Stretch With Block is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors, Glutes, Core.

ex_R5NLPK.name: Cross Body Elbow Pull Shoulder Stretch
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder width apart and your arms relaxed by your sides. Bend one arm behind your lower back with your elbow pointing outward.
Reach across your body with your opposite hand and grasp the elbow of your bent arm.
Gently pull the elbow across your body until you feel a comfortable stretch in the your shoulder.
Hold the stretch, then slowly release and repeat on the opposite side.
tips: Pull your elbow gently without forcing it beyond a comfortable range.
Maintain a slow, steady pull rather than using quick movements.
Keep your neck relaxed and your shoulders away from your ears.
Inhale before applying the stretch and exhale as you gently deepen it.
ex_R5NLPK.description: Cross Body Elbow Pull Shoulder Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Rotator Cuff, Upper Back, Chest.

ex_GUHHB2.name: Cross Body Shoulder Stretch
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder width apart and your arms relaxed by your sides.
Raise one arm straight across the front of your chest at shoulder height.
Grasp your upper arm just above the elbow with your opposite hand and gently pull it closer to your chest while keeping your shoulders relaxed.
Hold the stretch, then slowly release and repeat on the opposite side.
tips: Pull from your upper arm rather than your forearm or wrist.
Keep your shoulders level and avoid shrugging them toward your ears.
Stretch only until you feel a comfortable pull in the back of your shoulder.
Inhale before applying the stretch and exhale as you gently pull your arm closer.
ex_GUHHB2.description: Cross Body Shoulder Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Rotator Cuff.

ex_ZMHGFN.name: Foam Roller Back
instructions: Sit on the floor with a foam roller behind you and lie back so it is under your upper back.
Support your head with your hands and lift your hips slightly.
Roll slowly up and down from the bottom of your shoulder blades to the top of your back.
Pause on tight spots and breathe.
tips: Don't roll your lower back directly.
Move slowly.
ex_ZMHGFN.description: Foam Roller Back is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a roller, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Middle Back.

ex_GYYVUM.name: Foam Roller Calves
instructions: Sit with your legs straight and a foam roller under your calves.
Lift your hips with your hands on the floor.
Roll slowly from your ankles to just below your knees.
Turn your legs in and out to reach the sides of your calves.
tips: Cross one leg over the other for more pressure.
Pause on tight spots.
ex_GYYVUM.description: Foam Roller Calves is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with a roller, it falls under the flexibility category.

ex_PLDOZT.name: Foam Roller Lateral Quads
instructions: Lie on your side with a foam roller under the outside of your thigh.
Support yourself on your forearm and your top foot.
Roll slowly between your hip and your knee.
Pause on tender areas and breathe, then switch sides.
tips: Take weight through your top foot if it is too intense.
Don't roll over your knee.
ex_PLDOZT.description: Foam Roller Lateral Quads is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a roller, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Abductors.

ex_A76CR4.name: Foam Roller Quads
instructions: Lie face down with a foam roller under the front of your thighs.
Support yourself on your forearms.
Roll slowly from your hips to just above your knees.
Pause on tight spots and breathe.
tips: Roll one leg at a time for more pressure.
Keep your core tight.
ex_A76CR4.description: Foam Roller Quads is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a roller, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

ex_TMIPLX.name: Forearms Pull With Opposite Hand Stretch
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder width apart and extend your right arm straight in front of your chest with your palm facing down.
Place your left hand over your right hand while keeping the working elbow straight and your shoulder relaxed.
Gently pull your right hand downward and toward your body until you feel a comfortable stretch along the top of your forearm.
Hold the stretch briefly, release your hand with control, and repeat for the desired duration before switching arms.
tips: Keep the elbow of your stretching arm fully extended throughout the movement.
Pull through the fingers rather than pressing directly against the wrist joint.
Stop if you feel sharp pain, tingling, or numbness in your wrist or hand.
Inhale before applying the stretch and exhale as you gently pull your fingers downward.
ex_TMIPLX.description: Forearms Pull With Opposite Hand Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Shoulders.

ex_MW5LZ4.name: Forearms Stretch on Wall Fingers Facing Down
instructions: Stand facing a wall and place the fingers of your right hand against it at shoulder height, pointing them downward. Keep your palm slightly away from the wall and maintain a small bend in your elbow.
Keep your fingers in contact with the wall as you slowly shift your body weight forward.
Gently press your right palm into the wall until you feel a comfortable stretch in your forearm.
Shift your weight backward and lift your palm away from the wall while keeping your fingers in contact, then repeat before switching to your left hand.
tips: Keep your fingers in contact with the wall throughout every repetition.
Maintain a small bend in your elbow instead of locking your arm.
Use a comfortable range of motion and stop if you feel pain, tingling, or numbness.
Inhale as you move your palm away and exhale as you press it into the wall.
ex_MW5LZ4.description: Forearms Stretch on Wall Fingers Facing Down is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Forearms, Biceps.

ex_L72ELI.name: Forearms Stretch on Wall
instructions: Stand with your right side beside a wall and place your right palm flat against it at shoulder height.
Keep your right hand against the wall, with a bend in your elbow and your shoulder relaxed.
Slowly shift your weight forward until you feel a stretch along your right forearm.
Hold the stretch, then release and repeat with your left arm.
tips: Keep your palm and fingers flat against the wall.
Keep your stretching arm straight throughout the stretch.
Stop if you feel pain, tingling, or numbness.
Inhale before turning and exhale as you deepen the stretch.
ex_L72ELI.description: Forearms Stretch on Wall is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Chest, Shoulders.

ex_LSHRTH.name: Half Neck Rolls
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder width apart and cross your arms over your chest.
Lower your chin toward your chest and slowly roll your head from the left side toward the right side.
Reverse the movement and roll your head back toward the left, keeping your chin moving across the front of your chest.
Continue moving slowly from side to side for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your shoulders relaxed and away from your ears.
Do not roll your head backward or drop it behind your shoulders.
Stop if you feel pain, dizziness, or tingling.
Inhale as you reach one side and exhale as your chin moves across your chest.
ex_LSHRTH.description: Half Neck Rolls is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the levator scapulae (neck). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

ex_GWZN6U.name: Hands Clapped Forearms Stretch
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder width apart and press your palms together in front of your chest with your fingers pointing upward.
Keep your palms together and your elbows lifted as you rotate your hands until your fingers point downward.
Gently lower your joined hands toward your abdomen until you feel a stretch through your wrists and forearms.
Reverse the movement, return your fingers upward, then lower your arms to the starting position.
tips: Rotate your hands slowly without separating them.
Lower your hands only as far as your wrists remain comfortable.
Stop if you feel pain, tingling, or numbness.
Inhale as your fingers point upward and exhale as you lower your hands.
ex_GWZN6U.description: Hands Clapped Forearms Stretch is an advanced single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Shoulders.

ex_2PRHQH.name: Kneeling Forearm Flexor Stretch
instructions: Kneel on the floor and place your palms on the floor with your fingers pointing back toward your knees.
Keep your arms straight.
Gently sit back until you feel a stretch along the inside of your forearms.
Hold, breathing steadily, then release.
tips: Go gently; wrists are sensitive.
Keep your palms flat.
ex_2PRHQH.description: Kneeling Forearm Flexor Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category.

ex_VOQREB.name: Lats Stretch Elbow on Wall
instructions: Stand facing a wall and place one elbow on it above your head.
Step back slightly and lower your chest toward the floor.
Push your hips back until you feel a stretch along the side of your back.
Hold, then switch sides.
tips: Keep your back flat.
Breathe into the stretch.
ex_VOQREB.description: Lats Stretch Elbow on Wall is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Shoulders.

ex_CONPPC.name: Lats Stretch on Wall
instructions: Stand facing a wall and place both hands on it at shoulder height or higher.
Walk your feet back and hinge at your hips.
Lower your chest toward the floor until you feel a stretch under your arms.
Hold and breathe.
tips: Keep your arms straight.
Push your hips back.
ex_CONPPC.description: Lats Stretch on Wall is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Chest.

ex_PYKVMB.name: Lying Bent Knee Cross Glutes Stretch
instructions: Lie on your back with both knees bent and feet flat.
Cross one ankle over the opposite knee.
Pull the lower leg toward your chest until you feel a stretch in the glute of the crossed leg.
Hold, then switch sides.
tips: Keep your head and shoulders relaxed on the floor.
Push the crossed knee away gently for more stretch.
ex_PYKVMB.description: Lying Bent Knee Cross Glutes Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

ex_KJ7BTP.name: Lying Face Down Quadriceps Stretch
instructions: Lie face down on the floor.
Bend one knee and reach back to hold your ankle or foot.
Gently pull your heel toward your glute until you feel a stretch in the front of your thigh.
Hold, then switch sides.
tips: Keep your hips pressed into the floor.
Use a strap if you can't reach your foot.
ex_KJ7BTP.description: Lying Face Down Quadriceps Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

ex_K4VP5Q.name: Lying Knee Hugs Lower Back Stretch
instructions: Lie on your back.
Pull both knees toward your chest.
Wrap your arms around your shins and hug them in.
Hold, breathing slowly, and relax your lower back into the floor.
tips: Rock gently side to side for a light massage.
Keep your head on the floor.
ex_K4VP5Q.description: Lying Knee Hugs Lower Back Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Glutes.

ex_CB3HCW.name: Lying Knee Pull Glutes Stretch
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs straight.
Bend one knee and pull it toward the opposite shoulder.
Hold until you feel a stretch in your glute.
Release and switch sides.
tips: Keep the other leg relaxed on the floor.
Breathe deeply.
ex_CB3HCW.description: Lying Knee Pull Glutes Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back.

ex_4ZTVIW.name: Lying Knees to Floor Lower Back Stretch
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and arms out to the sides.
Keeping your shoulders on the floor, lower both knees to one side.
Hold, feeling a stretch in your lower back and side.
Bring your knees back to the centre and lower them to the other side.
tips: Turn your head away from your knees for a deeper stretch.
Move slowly.
ex_4ZTVIW.description: Lying Knees to Floor Lower Back Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Glutes.

ex_5V735Q.name: Lying Single Leg Extended on Wall Hamstrings Stretch
instructions: Lie on your back in a doorway or next to a wall.
Place one leg straight up against the wall, the other flat on the floor.
Move closer to the wall until you feel a stretch in the back of the raised leg.
Hold, then switch legs.
tips: Keep both legs straight.
Relax your shoulders and neck.
ex_5V735Q.description: Lying Single Leg Extended on Wall Hamstrings Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Calves.

ex_AYRJBW.name: Resistance Band Assisted Front Rack Stretch
instructions: Stand in the middle of a weight cage with a horizontal bar at chest level. Place the resistance band under your left foot and hold the other end of the band with your left hand.
Bring your left elbow up and rest it on the horizontal bar, allowing your forearm to lean backward. The band should extend down by your shoulder, creating tension.
Slowly allow your forearm to lean back to increase the stretch in your shoulder, keeping your hand close to your shoulder.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, then slowly release the tension and switch to the other arm.
tips: Keep your elbow securely on the bar to ensure proper stretch.
Allow your forearm to naturally lean back without forcing the movement.
Keep a relaxed grip on the band to avoid unnecessary tension.
ex_AYRJBW.description: Resistance Band Assisted Front Rack Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Biceps.

ex_2UFLOU.name: Revolved Head to Knee
instructions: Sit with one leg extended to the side and the other bent, foot against the inside of the extended thigh.
Turn your torso toward the bent knee.
Side-bend over the extended leg and reach your top arm overhead toward the foot.
Hold, breathing into the side of your body, then switch sides.
tips: Keep your chest open toward the ceiling.
Bend the extended knee slightly if your hamstrings are tight.
ex_2UFLOU.description: Revolved Head to Knee is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Lats, Adductors.

ex_WVCAVH.name: Seated Figure Four With Twist Glute Stretch
instructions: Sit tall with your legs extended.
Cross one ankle over the opposite knee and draw that foot in.
Twist your torso toward the bent knee, placing your opposite elbow against it.
Hold, then switch sides.
tips: Sit tall; don't round your back.
Breathe and deepen the twist slowly.
ex_WVCAVH.description: Seated Figure Four With Twist Glute Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Obliques, Lower Back.

ex_VOWPFO.name: Seated Forward Bend
instructions: Sit with your legs extended straight in front of you.
Sit tall and inhale, reaching your arms up.
Exhale and hinge forward from your hips, reaching toward your feet.
Hold, breathing slowly.
tips: Lead with your chest, not your head.
Bend your knees if your hamstrings are tight.
ex_VOWPFO.description: Seated Forward Bend is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Calves.

ex_J4IB4B.name: Seated Side Bend Pose
instructions: Sit cross-legged with a tall spine.
Place one hand on the floor beside you.
Reach the other arm overhead and lean toward the hand on the floor.
Hold, then switch sides.
tips: Keep both hips on the floor.
Breathe into the side of your ribs.
ex_J4IB4B.description: Seated Side Bend Pose is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

ex_55W5VR.name: Seated Single Leg Toe Touch Hamstring Stretch
instructions: Sit with one leg extended and the other bent, foot against the inner thigh.
Sit tall and face the extended leg.
Hinge forward from your hips and reach toward your toes.
Hold, then switch sides.
tips: Keep your back long.
Don't bounce.
ex_55W5VR.description: Seated Single Leg Toe Touch Hamstring Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Lower Back.

ex_ZNALT3.name: Seated Toe Touch Hamstrings Stretch
instructions: Sit with both legs extended in front of you.
Sit tall and reach your arms forward.
Hinge from your hips and reach toward your toes.
Hold, breathing slowly.
tips: Bend your knees slightly if needed.
Relax your neck.
ex_ZNALT3.description: Seated Toe Touch Hamstrings Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Lower Back.

ex_CJCRU3.name: Seated Twist
instructions: Sit tall with your legs extended.
Bend one knee and place that foot outside the opposite knee.
Twist toward the bent knee, using your opposite arm against the knee to deepen the twist.
Hold, then switch sides.
tips: Lengthen your spine on each inhale.
Twist a little further on each exhale.
ex_CJCRU3.description: Seated Twist is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Glutes.

ex_2GKGNS.name: Side Bend Standing Lats Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart.
Reach one arm overhead.
Lean to the opposite side until you feel a stretch along your side.
Hold, then switch sides.
tips: Keep your hips centred.
Don't lean forward or back.
ex_2GKGNS.description: Side Bend Standing Lats Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

ex_4MB2IK.name: Side Chest Stretch on Wall
instructions: Stand beside a wall and place your forearm and palm against it at shoulder height.
Step forward with the leg nearest the wall.
Gently turn your body away from the wall until you feel a stretch across your chest.
Hold, then switch sides.
tips: Change the height of your arm to stretch different parts of the chest.
Don't force the stretch.
ex_4MB2IK.description: Side Chest Stretch on Wall is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Front Shoulders, Biceps.

ex_NZVX4Y.name: Single Arm Extended Pull Downwards Biceps Stretch
instructions: Extend one arm in front of you, palm facing up.
With your other hand, gently pull your fingers down toward the floor.
Keep your arm straight until you feel a stretch in your biceps and forearm.
Hold, then switch arms.
tips: Keep your elbow straight.
Pull gently.
ex_NZVX4Y.description: Single Arm Extended Pull Downwards Biceps Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

ex_LNMH4X.name: Single Arm Palm Down on Wall Biceps Stretch
instructions: Stand side-on to a wall and place your palm flat on it behind you at shoulder height, fingers pointing back.
Keep your arm straight.
Slowly turn your body away from the wall until you feel a stretch in your biceps.
Hold, then switch arms.
tips: Move slowly into the stretch.
Keep your shoulder down.
ex_LNMH4X.description: Single Arm Palm Down on Wall Biceps Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Front Shoulders.

ex_UX5Y23.name: Single Arm on Wall Side Biceps Stretch
instructions: Stand beside a wall and place your hand on it at shoulder height with your arm straight.
Rotate your thumb downward.
Turn your body gently away from the wall until you feel a stretch in your biceps.
Hold, then switch arms.
tips: Keep your arm straight.
Breathe steadily.
ex_UX5Y23.description: Single Arm on Wall Side Biceps Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Front Shoulders, Chest.

ex_CWLQWA.name: Standing Quadriceps Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and find a stable surface to hold onto for balance if needed.
Bend your right knee and bring your heel towards your glutes. Grasp your right ankle with your right hand.
Keep your knees close together and lightly pull your right ankle upward, feeling a stretch along the front of your right thigh.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, then release your right ankle and return to the starting position. Repeat the stretch on the left leg.
tips: Perform the stretch slowly and with control to maximize muscle flexibility and reduce injury risk.
Ensure your supporting leg remains slightly bent to maintain balance.
Focus on keeping your torso upright and avoid leaning forward or backward.
ex_CWLQWA.description: Standing Quadriceps Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

ex_M3PKJW.name: Standing Straight-Leg Hamstring Stretch
instructions: Stand tall and place the heel of one foot on a low step or out in front of you with the leg straight.
Keep your back flat.
Hinge forward from your hips until you feel a stretch in the back of that leg.
Hold, then switch legs.
tips: Keep the standing knee soft.
Lead with your chest.
ex_M3PKJW.description: Standing Straight-Leg Hamstring Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Calves.

ex_OPBCSS.name: Band Bent Over One Arm Kickback
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and place one end of the resistance band under your feet. Hold the other end of the band in your right hand and bend your torso forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and your knees bent.
Position your right upper arm almost parallel to the floor with your elbow bent at a 90-degree angle, keeping your upper arm close to your body.
Extend your right arm straight back, squeezing your triceps at the top of the movement.
Slowly return your right arm to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the left arm.
tips: Ensure the resistance band is securely placed under your feet to avoid slipping.
Exhale as you extend your arm back and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Perform the exercise slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement.
ex_OPBCSS.description: Band Bent Over One Arm Kickback is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

ex_Y6ZFIV.name: Band Incline Triceps Extension
instructions: Lie on an incline bench set at a 45-degree angle. Place the resistance band under the bench and hold one handle of the band in each hand with your arms extended straight above your head, palms facing forward.
Lower the handles behind your head by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, ensuring your forearms are parallel to the floor and your upper arms remain still.
Extend your arms back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure the resistance band is securely anchored under the bench to avoid slipping.
Maintain a neutral wrist position to reduce strain on your joints. 3 .Focus on squeezing your triceps at the top of the movement.
ex_Y6ZFIV.description: Band Incline Triceps Extension is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category.

ex_4P63XX.name: Band Lying Press Down
instructions: Attach a resistance band at the bottom of a piece of sturdy equipment.
Lie on your back with your knees bent, feet flat on the floor. Hold onto the resistance bands with your hands above your forehead, elbows bent and facing upward.
Push the band up to the ceiling, squeezing your triceps hard at the top of the movement.
Slowly return your arms to the starting position with control and repeat.
tips: Keep your lower back in a neutral position throughout the exercise.
Keep your arms perpendicular to the ground and elbows tucked in.
Keep the movement controlled and avoid letting the band pull your arms back quickly.
Exhale as you extend the band upward using your triceps and inhale as you return.
ex_4P63XX.description: Band Lying Press Down is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms, Shoulders.

ex_2LG3JS.name: Band Triceps Pushdown Single Arm
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and a slight bend in the knees, facing the anchored resistance band.
Using an overhand grip, grasp the other end of the band, keeping your elbow bent and tucked close to your side.
Press downward by squeezing your triceps, extending your arm at the elbow joint. Pause briefly at the bottom of the exercise.
Slowly return to the starting position. Repeat for the desired amount of repetitions and switch arms.
tips: Keep your elbow close to your torso throughout the movement and upper arm stationary, moving only at the elbow joint.
Fully extend your arm without forcefully locking your elbow. Control the return phase to maintain constant tension on the band.
Stand tall with your chest up and core engaged to prevent body sway.
Exhale as you press downward and inhale as you return.
ex_2LG3JS.description: Band Triceps Pushdown Single Arm is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms, Shoulders, Core.

ex_4C7SNB.name: Barbell Lying Extension
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor, holding a barbell with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart. Your arms should be fully extended above your chest.
Slowly lower the barbell by bending your elbows, bringing the barbell towards over your forehead.
